`AGENTS.md`:

```md
# AGENTS.md

Instructions for AI coding agents working in this repository. Read
[docs/developer/architecture.md](docs/developer/architecture.md) for how the code fits
together and [docs/developer/ROADMAP.md](docs/developer/ROADMAP.md) for what is done and
what is open. This file holds the house rules and the facts you must not relearn the hard
way.

## What this is

USB Arsenal is a root tool, written in C, that builds a **composite USB gadget** through
configfs on Android and Linux. It provides mass storage (ISOs as a disk or CD-ROM,
writable drives), tethering (NCM/RNDIS with DHCP and NAT, or an OpenWrt gateway), and HID
nodes, all at once. It only drives the kernel's gadget subsystem: create functions, set
attributes, link, bind, raise the pullup, and always hand the controller back so the
phone's own USB (ADB/MTP) returns.

There is no daemon: every copy of the binary acts itself, as root, and exits (only `tether`
leaves its network process running). A privileged container runs the binary directly
([docs/containers.md](docs/containers.md)); the daemon that relayed for containers was
removed because it let its group make root open any file.

## Build

- `make native`, `make aarch64`, `make armhf`, `make x86_64`, `make x86`: static musl
  builds into `output/usb-arsenal`. Toolchains are found as `<triplet>-gcc` in
  `$MUSL_CROSS`, `~/toolchains/<triplet>-cross/bin`, `PATH` or `/opt/cross/bin`.
- `make module`: every architecture in a KernelSU/Magisk zip (`module/`).
- `make format`: clang-format over `src/`. Bare `make` prints help.
- **Version:** `UA_VERSION` in `usbarsenal.h` is the only source. `make bump NEW=x.y.z`
  rewrites it and `module/module.prop`; commit that alone as `usb-arsenal: bump vX.Y.Z`.
  The built versionCode, in the module zip and the APK alike, is
  (major*1000 + minor*100 + patch*10) * 10000 + the commit count, as Droidspaces does, so
  every commit's build updates the last; CI checks out the full history for it.
- **CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): every push
  and pull request builds the module zip with Droidspaces' published musl toolchains,
  cached between runs, and the app's release APK.
  Pushing a `vX.Y.Z` tag (or a manual run with `tag_name`) also publishes a release with
  the zip, the APK, `SHA256SUMS` and generated notes. The tag must equal `UA_VERSION`, so bump
  first: `make bump NEW=X.Y.Z`, commit, then `git tag vX.Y.Z && git push --tags`.
- **The app's signing key** is Droidspaces': `droidspaces.keystore` at the repo root and its
  passwords in `Android/local.properties` (see `local.properties.example`), both gitignored;
  CI takes them from the `RELEASE_KEYSTORE` (base64), `KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `KEY_ALIAS` and
  `KEY_PASSWORD` secrets. Without them a release is signed with the debug key. Releases are
  shrunk with R8.
- **No wildcard SRCS**: add each new `.c` to the list in the Makefile.
- Header dependencies are tracked (`-MMD`), so a header edit rebuilds what includes it.
- clangd reads `compile_flags.txt`.

## Layout

| Path | What lives there |
|---|---|
| `src/include/usbarsenal.h` | the only header a `.c` includes (plus `src/net/net.h` for networking) |
| `src/gadget.c` | the core every command goes through: open, begin, add, commit, teardown |
| `src/gadgets/` | the commands: storage, hid, tether |
| `src/config.c` | identity profiles |
| `src/check.c` | capability probing |
| `src/net/` | lifted from Droidspaces; keep its `ds_` names so it can be re-synced |
| `kernel-patches/<kernel-version>/` | `git format-patch` exports of kernel fixes, and the `README.md` that lists them (the rule below) |
| `DESIGN.md` | the Android app's design language: tokens, components, copy rules |
| `docs/developer/design/` | the reference screens and `lcd.css`, the shared stylesheet |

Two more facts:
- **The workspace** is `/data/local/USB-Arsenal` on Android and `/var/lib/USB-Arsenal` on
  Linux and in containers. Use `ua_ws_path()`; never invent another state path.
- **Never assume Android from `/system`.** Whether Android owns the controller is decided
  from the kernel (`g1` plus `/sys/class/android_usb`), so the tool also works inside a
  container.

## Kernel traps that panicked a phone: never regress these

Both are in kernel code that a plain configfs or sysfs write reaches. Details are in
[docs/developer/research/01-kernel-survey.md](docs/developer/research/01-kernel-survey.md).

- **Never write `connect` to `soft_connect` unless the UDC `state` is still "not
  attached", and then only as `disconnect` followed by `connect`.** On 4.14 cores
  "connect" starts the controller unconditionally. A started dwc3 then frees its own IRQ
  while in use, and the next unbind panics.
- **Never create an NCM function, not even to probe, when
  `/sys/class/android_usb/android0/terminal_version` exists without `ncm_instances`.**
  Samsung's f_ncm then destroys the shared `android0` and the kernel BUGs. Use RNDIS.
  `ua_ncm_unsafe()` is the one place that decides.
- **Never remove a gadget directory (ours or a probe) while `/sys/class/android_usb`
  exists.** Every `androidN` device has devt 0 and `android_device_destroy()` finds its
  device by devt, so any `rmdir` of a gadget destroys `android0`, which is `g1`'s. Android
  then hears no USB state until a reboot: no USB notification, tethering greyed out.
  `keep_gadget()` in `src/gadget.c` keeps ours, unbound and empty. `kernel-patches/`
  fixes the kernel for 4.9 to 6.6 (on 6.6 in `android_configfs_uevent.c`). Seen on the
  a166p (5.15).
- **Never write `dev_addr`, `host_addr` or `qmult` to a network function without
  reading `dev_addr` first.** Samsung's f_ncm has no netdev before bind, and its stores
  dereference that NULL. The read is safe everywhere, and failing means skip
  (the f_ncm patch in `kernel-patches/` for 4.9, 4.14 and 4.19 fixes the kernel).

## Testing on a device

- **Run `adb devices` first, every time.** If no line ends in `device`, stop and say so.
- **ADB drops while the gadget holds the port, wireless ADB too:** taking the port sets
  `sys.usb.config none`, which stops `adbd` (seen on the a166p), and handing it back restarts
  it. Run each test as one background `nohup` script that ends in `usb-arsenal stop` and logs
  to a file (`screencap` and `input tap` work from it), and read the file afterwards over USB
  ADB, which is back once Android holds the port again.
- **Check `dmesg` after every step**, not only at the end. The warnings come before the
  panic.
- **After a panic, read `/proc/last_kmsg` and `/sys/fs/pstore/*` before anything else,**
  then read the kernel source at the call trace. Never guess.
- **`usb-arsenal stop` is the recovery path.** A test that cannot end in a working
  `stop` is not finished.
- **Keep the test PC's own connection off the USB link** (a `never-default` profile), or
  a gateway test stalls the machine running it.
- Without a phone: `sudo tests/dummy_hcd.sh`. More in
  [docs/developer/testing.md](docs/developer/testing.md).

## Commits

- Run `make format` before committing any change to a `.c` or `.h` file.
- Sign off every commit: `git commit -s`.
- **Never add a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer for an AI agent** in this repository. Human
  co-authors are fine.
- Prefixes, matching the style Droidspaces uses: `fix:`, `refactor:`, `feat:`, `docs:`,
  or a subsystem name (`gadget:`, `storage:`, `net:`, `hid:`, `check:`). Use
  `fix(security):` for anything security related.

## Style

Four rules. They apply to code, comments, commit messages, and documentation.

**No em-dashes.** Use a comma, a full stop, or rewrite the sentence.

**No ASCII banner comments.** No rows of `-----`, no `=====`, no boxed section headers.
An SPDX licence block at the top of each file is fine.

**Comments sound like a person.** Say why the code does something, or what breaks if it
does not. Skip comments that restate the line below them.

```c
/* Bad: write 1 to the UDC */
echo_udc(udc);

/* Good: Android's bind HACK leaves D+ down, so assert the pullup ourselves after bind */
udc_soft_connect(udc);
```

**Ten lines that work beat a hundred that do the same thing.** Delete before you add.
A smaller diff in the right place is the goal, not a smaller diff anywhere.

## Before you write it at all

Work down this list and stop at the first answer that holds.

1. Does this need to exist? A flag nobody asked for, a knob for a value that never
   changes, an abstraction with one implementation: skip it and say so in one line.
2. Does it already exist here? Grep first.
3. **Does the kernel already do it?** This is the big one for USB Arsenal. The gadget
   subsystem, configfs, `f_mass_storage`, `f_hid` and `f_ncm`/`f_rndis` already
   implement the hard parts. Use the kernel's interface; do not reimplement a protocol in
   userspace. Read the kernel sources (the trees in
   [research/01](docs/developer/research/01-kernel-survey.md) are a start) before writing a
   line.
4. Does an installed dependency or libc cover it? Never add a dependency for a few lines.
5. Can it be one line? Then it is one line.
6. Only then write the smallest thing that works.

Two answers work? Take the higher one and move on.

The list shortens the solution, never the reading. Trace the flow the change touches
before you pick a rung. A small diff in the wrong place is a second bug, not a lazy fix.

Never simplify away input validation at a trust boundary, a fail-closed check, error
handling that would leave the phone's USB broken, or anything the requester asked for by
name.

## Hard constraints

- **The kernel floor is 3.18 built with `CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS`.** Stock 3.18 ships the
  legacy android gadget instead, and `check` refuses it with the reason. The top end is
  the latest GKI. Detect capabilities at runtime (which functions the kernel built, the
  UDC, patched or stock configfs); never hardcode a kernel-specific path.
- **Never hardcode the UDC name.** Read it from `/sys/class/udc`; require `--udc` when
  there is more than one.
- **Teardown must always restore the previous owner.** A crash or error path that leaves
  the UDC unbound kills ADB and MTP. The hand-back record stays until Android's gadget
  is really bound again. This is the one thing that must never break.
- **Never unbind someone else's gadget off Android.** Name it and refuse.
- **Root is required.** Fail closed and loud when a configfs path, a permission or the
  workspace is wrong.

## Documentation

- **User pages** live in `docs/` (installation, usage, tethering, containers, identity,
  troubleshooting); the kernel page is `kernel-patches/README.md`, beside the patches.
- **Developer material** lives in `docs/developer/`: architecture, testing, research
  notes, references and the roadmap.
- **Record findings and decisions there as you make them,** not in your head. Tick
  `docs/developer/ROADMAP.md` and add a dated line to its status log.
- **The README stays under 150 lines and claims nothing that was not verified on
  hardware.**
- **`kernel-patches/README.md` stays brief:** the options a feature needs, and the patches a
  feature needs on which kernel versions. No device names, no links to kernel trees, no test
  history. A new patch folder adds its row there in the same commit.

## Designing the app

- **[DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) is the law** for anything the app shows. Read it before any UI
  work and again before you call it finished. Closed world: two colours (`lcd`, `ink`),
  three faces (Jersey 10, Silkscreen, VT323), four sizes (104, 72, 22, 16), square corners,
  stepped motion. If a value is not in the file, the file is telling you not to want it.
- **Start from what exists.** Take the rules from `docs/developer/design/lcd.css` and the
  closest screen in `docs/developer/design/`. Never restyle a component that already has a
  class there.
- **Show only what the backend does.** Before a control, a status line or a number goes on
  a screen, grep `src/` for the command or flag behind it. If the app does it on its own
  (the image folder, Create, HID input), it is app-side; say so in DESIGN.md's Backend truth
  table. No UVC, pending queue, host port, lease countdown or uptime until the C side has it.
- **Say it once.** A fact appears once per screen. No status line that repeats what an
  element shows (`host sees dvd`, `serving`, `configured`), no note beside a title that
  echoes the box below it, no `by arsenal`, no subtitle explaining a control, nothing in the
  top bar beside `< BACK`. Helper text only prevents a mistake; warnings only state a
  consequence.
- **Research before using a platform API.** Read the Android developer docs for any
  animation, haptics, focus or input API before writing it, and record its API level and
  fallback in DESIGN.md. Never guess a constant's API level.
- **Motion and haptics come from DESIGN.md's tables.** Stepped easing on the 40ms frame
  clock, the event map for haptics, the device tiers for rich effects. Never use
  `createOneShot` or a hand-made waveform for touch feedback. With reduced motion, every loop
  shows its resting frame.
- **Fast work is paced so it can be read.** Nothing appears in a single frame: titles type,
  shells play their session (DESIGN.md's Shell session row: Root, Check, Backend).
  The pacing comes from the beat between lines, not from slow typing, and the keys never run
  ahead of what the screen says. Check a change frame by frame in a `screenrecord`, not by eye.
- **A screen never re-lays itself out when work finishes.** It shows its final layout from
  the start (a disabled key where a key will be, an idle prompt where output will go), and a
  line already drawn never moves.
- **Never ask root for what the app knows itself** (its own version, the phone's codename),
  and never ask twice: every read is cached across launches with the boot id it was read in
  (`backend/Cache.kt`), the first frame draws from the cache, one live read per launch corrects
  it, and Back never re-runs a probe; only Recheck, Reinstall, a controller change or an identity
  command does. The activity handles configuration changes itself, so a rotation or a gamepad
  connecting never cancels a su request.
- **The setup is the backend's.** What each function starts with lives in
  `Gadget/setup.conf`, what runs in `Gadget/running.conf`, both written by the C side
  (`src/setup.c`); the app edits the setup through `setup set`, starts with a bare `start`, applies
  with `<function> apply`, and reads everything back in one `status --json`. Never keep a setup
  or a "what runs" record in the app: `docs/developer/research/06-app-state.md` is why.
- **One status loop,** in `App()`, with ordered reads: a read begun while a command runs is
  skipped, and a result is dropped when a newer one was applied or a command finished since it
  began. A failed read keeps the last status; after three the bar says `no answer from usb-arsenal`.
- **Every screen works without touch.** Before a screen is done, walk it with
  `adb shell input keyevent` (`KEYCODE_DPAD_*`, `KEYCODE_ENTER`, `KEYCODE_BUTTON_A`,
  `KEYCODE_BUTTON_B`, `KEYCODE_TAB`) and confirm every control is reachable and the focus
  cursor is visible.
- **Done means:** `npx @google/design.md lint DESIGN.md` reports no errors, every screen
  renders at 390x844 with nothing clipped and the bottom 48px empty, and a grep for the em
  dash finds nothing. A change to the language goes into DESIGN.md and `lcd.css` in the
  same commit.

## Android app

- **Where and what:** `Android/`, a Kotlin and Jetpack Compose app, package
  `com.usbarsenal.app`, minSdk 26. Compose foundation only: no Material component is
  visible, every widget is ours and follows DESIGN.md. The version comes from `UA_VERSION`.
- **Never run root commands through one shared shell.** One stuck command would freeze every
  other one behind it. Each operation runs in its own short-lived root shell with a timeout,
  and the shell is killed (not just abandoned) on timeout or cancel. Commands that change the
  gadget go through one ordered lane, so two never race; a timeout kills that command's shell
  and frees the lane, so the lane cannot stall. Reads (`status --json`, `check --json`, log
  tails) use their own shells and never wait on the lane.
- **The installer is ported from Droidspaces** (`BinaryInstaller`, `ModuleInstaller`,
  `DeviceArch`, the backend checker), restyled to DESIGN.md. The boot module is `module/`.
  The binary lives in the workspace (`/data/local/USB-Arsenal/bin/usb-arsenal`); the module
  holds `sepolicy.rule`, the uninstall hand-back and the PATH link, nothing that runs at boot. `/data/adb/modules/usb-arsenal/system/bin/usb-arsenal` is a link to it, there
  only while the user wants `usb-arsenal` on PATH (Droidspaces' `SymlinkInstaller`; the zip
  makes it, the app's Settings switch makes or removes it). The install is the binary,
  then the module, and every step's real output goes to the screen.
- **Never patch the live SELinux policy** (`ksud sepolicy patch`, `magiskpolicy --live`): root
  detectors watch for it. `sepolicy.rule` loads at boot; when the module had none before an
  install, the install says to reboot.
- **Test over wireless ADB** while nothing is bound; a test that binds the gadget runs as the
  background script above, since `adbd` stops for as long as the gadget holds the port.
- **Test haptics on more than one phone:** one with rich haptics, one midrange, and once with
  touch feedback switched off.

`Android/app/build.gradle.kts`:

```kts
import java.util.Properties

plugins {
    id("com.android.application")
    id("org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose")
}

// The signing key's passwords, as Droidspaces keeps them: local.properties (never committed),
// then a -P property, then the environment (CI's secrets). An unset GitHub secret arrives as an
// empty string, so a blank counts as missing
val local = Properties().apply {
    rootProject.file("local.properties").takeIf { it.exists() }?.inputStream()?.use(::load)
}
fun secret(name: String): String? =
    sequenceOf(local.getProperty(name), providers.gradleProperty(name).orNull, System.getenv(name))
        .firstOrNull { !it.isNullOrBlank() }

// UA_VERSION is the only version source; versionCode matches the module.prop `make module` writes
val uaVersion = Regex("""#define\s+UA_VERSION\s+"(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)"""")
    .find(rootProject.file("../src/include/usbarsenal.h").readText())
    ?.groupValues?.drop(1)?.map(String::toInt)
    ?: error("UA_VERSION x.y.z not found in src/include/usbarsenal.h")

// Every commit gets its own versionCode, as the Makefile gives module.prop, so CI builds
// between bumps install over each other. A shallow clone counts 1, a tarball 0
val commits = runCatching {
    providers.exec { commandLine("git", "rev-list", "--count", "HEAD") }.standardOutput.asText.get().trim().toInt()
}.getOrDefault(0)

android {
    namespace = "com.usbarsenal.app"
    compileSdk = 37

    defaultConfig {
        applicationId = "com.usbarsenal.app"
        minSdk = 26
        targetSdk = 37
        versionName = uaVersion.joinToString(".")
        // ponytail: 10000 commits per release before the count spills into the next version's codes
        versionCode = (uaVersion[0] * 1000 + uaVersion[1] * 100 + uaVersion[2] * 10) * 10000 + commits
    }

    // Droidspaces' key at the repo root, gitignored. Without it (a fork, or CI with no secrets) the
    // release is signed with the debug key, so it still builds and installs. With it, debug builds
    // carry it too, as in Droidspaces: one signature, so either installs over the other
    val keystore = rootProject.file("../droidspaces.keystore")
    val password = secret("KEYSTORE_PASSWORD")
    val signed = keystore.exists() && !password.isNullOrEmpty()
    signingConfigs {
        if (signed) {
            val alias = secret("KEY_ALIAS") ?: "droidspaces"
            val keyPassword = secret("KEY_PASSWORD") ?: password
            listOf(getByName("debug"), create("release")).forEach {
                it.storeFile = keystore
                it.storePassword = password
                it.keyAlias = alias
                it.keyPassword = keyPassword
                it.enableV2Signing = true
                it.enableV3Signing = true
                it.enableV4Signing = true
            }
        }
    }

    buildTypes {
        release {
            isMinifyEnabled = true
            isShrinkResources = true
            proguardFiles(getDefaultProguardFile("proguard-android-optimize.txt"), "proguard-rules.pro")
            signingConfig = signingConfigs.getByName(if (signed) "release" else "debug")
        }
    }

    compileOptions {
        sourceCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_17
        targetCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_17
    }

    buildFeatures {
        compose = true
        buildConfig = true
    }
}

// The backend the app installs: `make module` builds the four binaries and the boot module
val repo = rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("..")
val buildBackend = tasks.register<Exec>("buildBackend") {
    workingDir(repo)
    commandLine("make", "module")
    inputs.dir(repo.dir("src"))
    inputs.dir(repo.dir("module"))
    inputs.file(repo.file("Makefile"))
    outputs.dir(repo.dir("output/module"))
}

// assets/binaries/usb-arsenal-<arch> and assets/boot-module/, generated so they never show up as a diff.
// customize.sh stays behind: the app does its job itself when it installs the module
abstract class BackendAssets : DefaultTask() {
    @get:InputFiles
    abstract val module: ConfigurableFileCollection

    @get:OutputDirectory
    abstract val outputDir: DirectoryProperty

    @get:Inject
    abstract val fs: FileSystemOperations

    @TaskAction
    fun copy() {
        val dir = module.singleFile
        fs.sync {
            from(dir.resolve("bin")) { into("binaries") }
            from(dir) {
                include("module.prop", "uninstall.sh", "sepolicy.rule")
                into("boot-module")
            }
            into(outputDir)
        }
    }
}

val backendAssets = tasks.register<BackendAssets>("backendAssets") {
    module.from(buildBackend)
}

androidComponents {
    onVariants { variant ->
        variant.sources.assets?.addGeneratedSourceDirectory(backendAssets, BackendAssets::outputDir)
    }
}

dependencies {
    implementation(platform("androidx.compose:compose-bom:2026.09.00"))
    implementation("androidx.compose.foundation:foundation")
    implementation("androidx.activity:activity-compose:1.13.0")

    testImplementation("junit:junit:4.13.2")
    // android.jar's org.json is a stub on the JVM; the real one runs the parser tests
    testImplementation("org.json:json:20260814")
}

```

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android">

    <!-- Rich haptics (the bind sequence) go through Vibrator, which needs it -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.VIBRATE" />

    <application
        android:label="USB Arsenal"
        android:icon="@mipmap/ic_launcher"
        android:theme="@style/Lcd">
        <!-- Compose redraws for every one of these itself. Recreating the activity would cancel a
             su request mid-dialog and ask again, and replay every typed session; a gamepad or
             keyboard connecting is one of them, and this app is meant to be driven by one.
             adjustResize: Screen pads for the keyboard itself; a window the system also pans
             or resizes leaves a gap the keyboard's height above it -->
        <activity
            android:name=".MainActivity"
            android:windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize"
            android:configChanges="orientation|screenSize|screenLayout|smallestScreenSize|density|fontScale|fontWeightAdjustment|uiMode|colorMode|keyboard|keyboardHidden|navigation|touchscreen|locale|layoutDirection|mcc|mnc"
            android:exported="true">
            <intent-filter>
                <action android:name="android.intent.action.MAIN" />
                <category android:name="android.intent.category.LAUNCHER" />
            </intent-filter>
        </activity>
    </application>

</manifest>

`Android/app/src/main/java/com/usbarsenal/app/MainActivity.kt`:

```kt
package com.usbarsenal.app

import android.annotation.SuppressLint
import android.os.Build
import android.os.Bundle
import android.graphics.Color
import androidx.activity.ComponentActivity
import androidx.activity.SystemBarStyle
import androidx.activity.compose.setContent
import com.usbarsenal.app.backend.Cache
import com.usbarsenal.app.ui.HidSetup
import androidx.activity.enableEdgeToEdge
import com.usbarsenal.app.lcd.LcdTheme
import com.usbarsenal.app.lcd.Switches
import android.view.InputDevice
import android.view.KeyEvent
import android.view.MotionEvent
import com.usbarsenal.app.ui.App
import com.usbarsenal.app.ui.Stick

class MainActivity : ComponentActivity() {
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        // The splash leaves in one cut, as an LCD would, not the system's fade
        if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S) splashScreen.setOnExitAnimationListener { it.remove() }
        // The bars are see-through; LcdTheme sets their icons' colour, as the theme, not the system, decides it
        val bars = SystemBarStyle.light(Color.TRANSPARENT, Color.TRANSPARENT)
        enableEdgeToEdge(bars, bars)
        val switches = Switches(applicationContext)
        // The last reads and the trackpad's settings, so the first frame draws from them
        Cache.init(applicationContext)
        HidSetup.init(applicationContext)
        // The launch window's Pin (Android 8 to 11's splash) has done its job once Compose draws: LcdTheme replaces it
        setContent { LcdTheme(switches) { App() } }
    }

    /*
     * Back and Escape mean back, focused or not, so they go to the back dispatcher before any
     * view: Compose takes both as a focus exit while anything is focused, and Escape has no
     * fallback to BACK in every key map (the S10's has none). BUTTON_B falls back to BACK.
     * Activity.dispatchKeyEvent is public; lint flags it for androidx's own @RestrictTo override.
     * Only a press whose down came here counts: one let go after a dialog or su's prompt closed is not ours.
     */
    private var backDown = false

    @SuppressLint("RestrictedApi")
    override fun dispatchKeyEvent(event: KeyEvent): Boolean {
        if (event.keyCode != KeyEvent.KEYCODE_ESCAPE && event.keyCode != KeyEvent.KEYCODE_BACK) return super.dispatchKeyEvent(event)
        if (event.action == KeyEvent.ACTION_DOWN && event.repeatCount == 0) backDown = true
        if (event.action == KeyEvent.ACTION_UP) {
            if (backDown && !event.isCanceled) onBackPressedDispatcher.onBackPressed()
            backDown = false
        }
        return true
    }

    private var hat = 0f to 0f

    // While Keys + mouse holds the left stick, it moves the host pointer, not focus. Most pads
    // send their D-pad as a hat on these same events: a hat that moved, pressed or let go, still
    // goes on, so Android turns it into the D-pad keys that move focus. It goes on with the stick
    // centred, or a deflected stick would start a repeating D-pad key of its own
    override fun dispatchGenericMotionEvent(ev: MotionEvent): Boolean {
        val sink = Stick.sink
        if (sink != null && ev.isFromSource(InputDevice.SOURCE_JOYSTICK) && ev.action == MotionEvent.ACTION_MOVE) {
            sink(ev.getAxisValue(MotionEvent.AXIS_X), ev.getAxisValue(MotionEvent.AXIS_Y))
            val now = ev.getAxisValue(MotionEvent.AXIS_HAT_X) to ev.getAxisValue(MotionEvent.AXIS_HAT_Y)
            val hatMoved = now != hat
            hat = now
            if (!hatMoved) return true
            val hatOnly = ev.withoutStick()
            return super.dispatchGenericMotionEvent(hatOnly).also { hatOnly.recycle() }
        }
        return super.dispatchGenericMotionEvent(ev)
    }
}

// The same event with the left stick's axes at rest
private fun MotionEvent.withoutStick(): MotionEvent {
    val props = Array(pointerCount) { i -> MotionEvent.PointerProperties().also { getPointerProperties(i, it) } }
    val coords = Array(pointerCount) { i ->
        MotionEvent.PointerCoords().also {
            getPointerCoords(i, it)
            it.setAxisValue(MotionEvent.AXIS_X, 0f)
            it.setAxisValue(MotionEvent.AXIS_Y, 0f)
        }
    }
    return MotionEvent.obtain(downTime, eventTime, action, pointerCount, props, coords, metaState, buttonState, xPrecision, yPrecision, deviceId, edgeFlags, source, flags)
}

`Android/app/src/main/java/com/usbarsenal/app/backend/Backend.kt`:

```kt
package com.usbarsenal.app.backend

import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import java.time.Instant
import java.time.ZoneId
import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter
import org.json.JSONArray
import org.json.JSONObject

// The one root runner every command goes through. The global mount namespace, as at boot: an image
// or the tether process started from here must see the mounts init sees, not the app's own view
val Root = RootExec { ProcessBuilder("su", "--mount-master", "-c", it).start() }

// ua_ws_path()'s workspace on Android; the binary lives in its bin/
const val WORKSPACE = "/data/local/USB-Arsenal"
const val UA = "$WORKSPACE/bin/usb-arsenal"

// Keys + mouse's writer for one node: reports of [size] bytes on stdin, each one write, never
// blocking on the node (hid.c's `hid write`)
suspend fun hidWrite(node: String, size: Int) = Root.stream("$UA hid write ${shellQuote(node)} $size")

// A USB device controller as /sys/class/udc lists it, and its state ("configured": a host is
// talking to it, "not attached": nothing is)
data class Udc(val name: String, val state: String)

// "<name> <state>" a line; a state can be several words
fun parseUdcs(lines: List<String>): List<Udc> = lines.mapNotNull { line ->
    val l = line.trim().ifEmpty { return@mapNotNull null }
    val gap = l.indexOf(' ')
    if (gap < 0) Udc(l, "") else Udc(l.substring(0, gap), l.substring(gap + 1).trim())
}.filterNot { it.name.startsWith("dummy_udc.") } // GKI's built-in dummy_hcd reaches no host; the backend skips it too

/*
 * The controller every command uses. With more than one, the backend reads the setup's `udc`
 * key, so the pick is set once (`setup set udc=NAME`) and no command carries a flag; with one
 * there is no pick. The app only mirrors the key, from the last status read.
 */
object Controller {
    var picked by mutableStateOf<String?>(Cache.status?.setup?.get("udc")?.ifEmpty { null })
        private set

    // What /sys/class/udc listed last, from the cache first
    var udcs by mutableStateOf<List<Udc>?>(Cache.udcs)

    // The setup says, after a status read
    fun mirror(setup: Map<String, String>) {
        picked = setup["udc"]?.ifEmpty { null }
    }

    /*
     * Writes the pick into the setup through [binary] (the staged one before the backend is
     * installed, since Check runs it), and shows it at once. A pick is never cleared by the app:
     * a controller gone to host mode comes back, and the user picks another in Settings.
     */
    suspend fun set(name: String, binary: String = UA): RootResult {
        val r = Root.change("${shellQuote(binary)} setup set ${shellQuote("udc=$name")}")
        if (r.ok) picked = name
        return r
    }

    // Reads the controllers; whether the user has to pick one now comes back. A failed read
    // keeps the last list and asks nothing
    suspend fun refresh(): Boolean {
        val found = Root.read("""for u in /sys/class/udc/*; do [ -e "${'$'}u" ] && echo "${'$'}{u##*/} ${'$'}(cat "${'$'}u/state" 2>/dev/null)"; done; true""")
            .takeIf { it.ok }?.let { parseUdcs(it.out) } ?: return false
        udcs = found
        Cache.udcs = found
        return found.size > 1 && picked == null
    }
}

// check probes by creating functions in configfs, so once the gadget may be live it goes through
// the change lane and never races a command
suspend fun readCheck(): Result<Capabilities> = Root.change("$UA check --json").json(::parseCheck)

// The C side colours its [+] lines even through a pipe
private val ANSI = Regex("\u001B\\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]")

fun plain(line: String) = line.replace(ANSI, "")

// What a shell shows of check's report: no colour (it always colours), no indent, and its marks
// as the installer's [+] and [-], since VT323 has no check mark or cross. The blank lines that
// part its sections stay
private const val REPORT_END = "@@check-json"

// The report and the --json lines of one readCheckReport; a report cut short (a timeout before the
// marker) keeps what it printed, which is where it stalled
fun splitCheck(out: List<String>): Pair<List<String>, List<String>> {
    val end = out.indexOf(REPORT_END)
    val report = (if (end < 0) out else out.take(end))
        .map { plain(it).trim().replace("[✓]", "[+]").replace("[✗]", "[-]") }
        .dropWhile { it.isEmpty() }
        .dropLastWhile { it.isEmpty() }
    return report to if (end < 0) emptyList() else out.drop(end + 1)
}

/*
 * Check's shell: the report check prints, then its --json from the same root shell, for the
 * app's own use. Both run the binary Check stages, with the controller picked. The report
 * comes back even when the JSON does not.
 * ponytail: check probes twice, once per format; one run that prints both if a kernel ever minds
 */
suspend fun readCheckReport(binary: String): Pair<List<String>, Result<Capabilities>> {
    val check = "${shellQuote(binary)} check"
    val r = Root.read("$check 2>&1; echo $REPORT_END; $check --json", timeoutMs = 30_000)
    val (report, json) = splitCheck(r.out)
    return report to r.copy(out = json).json(::parseCheck)
}

/*
 * identity show --json: the keys in force (a derived one empty, so left out), with "profile"
 * (the file, empty for the built-in defaults) and "missing" (a link to a file that is gone, whose
 * host gets the defaults). Empty when it could not be read.
 */
suspend fun readProfile(): Map<String, String> = parseProfile(Root.read("$UA identity show --json").out.joinToString("\n"))

fun parseProfile(json: String): Map<String, String> = runCatching {
    val o = JSONObject(json)
    o.getJSONObject("keys").strings().filterValues { it.isNotEmpty() } +
        mapOf("profile" to o.getString("profile"), "missing" to o.optString("missing"))
}.getOrDefault(emptyMap())

// Whether Droidspaces is installed, and its running containers by name, which tether --gateway
// takes; [running] is null when they could not be read, which is not the same as none
data class Droidspaces(val installed: Boolean, val running: List<String>?)

suspend fun readDroidspaces(): Droidspaces {
    // A Droidspaces from before --json ignores the flag and prints its table; its JSON was --format
    val r = Root.read("d=$DROIDSPACES; [ -x \$d ] || exit 3; o=\$(\$d show --json); case \"\$o\" in \"{\"*) echo \"\$o\" ;; *) \$d show --format ;; esac")
    if (r.code == 3) return Droidspaces(false, null)
    return Droidspaces(true, if (r.ok) runCatching { parseContainers(r.out.joinToString("\n")) }.getOrNull() else null)
}

const val LOG = "$WORKSPACE/Logs/usb-arsenal.log"

// A line of the backend's log, "2026-10-25T18:21:03.123Z tether[1234] [+] NCM is up on usb0",
// as the screen shows it: "23:51:03: tether [+]: NCM is up on usb0", the time the phone's. A
// command line drops the command the process is named after ("hid [$]: start"). Null for a
// tagged chatter line ("[*] [DEBUG] ...", "[+] [NET] ..."), which the terminal shows only with
// -v; a tagged warning or error stays, it says why something did not work
private val LOG_LINE = Regex("""^(\S+Z) (\S+)\[\d+\] \[(.)\] (.*)$""")
private val CLOCK = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm:ss")
fun logView(line: String, zone: ZoneId = ZoneId.systemDefault()): String? {
    val (at, who, glyph, msg) = LOG_LINE.matchEntire(line)?.destructured ?: return line
    if (glyph !in "!-" && msg.startsWith("[")) return null
    val time = runCatching { Instant.parse(at).atZone(zone).format(CLOCK) }.getOrNull() ?: return line
    val said = if (glyph == "$") msg.removePrefix("$who ") else msg
    return "$time: $who [$glyph]: $said"
}

// The log past byte [from]: the lines since, and where they end, which is where the next read
// starts (every backend write is one whole line, so the bytes read are the offset; a size read
// beside the tail would miss a line landing in between and show it twice). From 0 it is the last
// [keep] lines, the file's start being the oldest and the least worth a read. The file's size
// comes last, after the tail: below the offset, the file was emptied or stepped aside. Null when
// the file could not be read
suspend fun readLog(from: Long, keep: Int): LogTail? {
    val since = if (from > 0) "tail -c +${from + 1}" else "tail -n $keep"
    val r = Root.read("f=$LOG; [ -e \"\$f\" ] || exit 0; $since \"\$f\"; echo \"$LOG_SIZE \$(wc -c < \"\$f\")\"")
    if (!r.ok) return null
    val size = r.out.lastOrNull()?.takeIf { it.startsWith(LOG_SIZE) }?.substringAfter(' ')?.trim()?.toLongOrNull() ?: return LogTail(emptyList(), 0, 0)
    val lines = r.out.dropLast(1)
    val bytes = lines.sumOf { it.toByteArray().size + 1L }
    // From the start, the tail's end is the file's end
    return LogTail(lines.map(::plain), if (from > 0) from + bytes else size, size)
}

data class LogTail(val lines: List<String>, val end: Long, val size: Long)

private const val LOG_SIZE = "__size__"

// The interfaces a default route leaves by, in any table: the phone's uplinks (Droidspaces' rule);
// null when they could not be read
suspend fun readUplinks(): List<String>? = Root.read("ip route show table all").takeIf { it.ok }?.out
    ?.filter { it.startsWith("default") }
    ?.mapNotNull { it.trim().split(Regex("\\s+")).zipWithNext().firstOrNull { (k, _) -> k == "dev" }?.second }
    ?.filterNot { it.startsWith("ds-") || it.startsWith("dummy") }
    ?.distinct()?.sorted()

// The folder's files as `stat -c '%s %n'` prints them
fun parseImages(lines: List<String>): List<ImageFile> = lines.mapNotNull { line ->
    val bytes = line.substringBefore(' ').toLongOrNull() ?: return@mapNotNull null
    ImageFile(line.substringAfter(' '), bytes)
}.sortedBy { it.name.lowercase() }

const val DROIDSPACES = "/data/local/Droidspaces/bin/droidspaces"

fun parseContainers(json: String): List<String> =
    JSONObject(json).optJSONArray("running")?.let { a -> (0 until a.length()).map { a.getJSONObject(it).getString("name") } }.orEmpty()

suspend fun readStatus(): Result<GadgetStatus> = Root.read("$UA status --json").json(::parseStatus)

/*
 * What su -v prints, as it prints it: "3.3.0:KernelSU" on the a166p. A failure carries what a shell would have said. KernelSU hides su from an app it has not
 * granted, so a missing su reads as sh reports it; a su that ran and refused says so on stderr.
 */
suspend fun rootInfo(): Result<String> {
    val timeoutMs = 15_000L
    val r = Root.read("id -u; su -v", timeoutMs)
    // The uid decides: the exit code is su -v's, which a root shell without su on its PATH fails
    return when {
        // A root shell with no su on its PATH: what it said, or that there is none
        r.out.firstOrNull() == "0" -> Result.success(r.out.getOrNull(1) ?: r.err.lastOrNull()?.takeIf(String::isNotBlank) ?: "(no su)")
        r.code == NO_ROOT && r.out.isEmpty() -> Result.failure(SecurityException("su: inaccessible or not found"))
        r.timedOut -> Result.failure(SecurityException("su: no answer in ${timeoutMs / 1000}s"))
        else -> Result.failure(SecurityException(r.err.lastOrNull() ?: "su: permission denied"))
    }
}

// check exits 1 when a requirement is missing and still prints the report, so stdout decides
private inline fun <T> RootResult.json(parse: (String) -> T): Result<T> = runCatching {
    if (out.isEmpty()) error(err.joinToString("\n").ifEmpty { if (timedOut) "timed out" else "exit $code" })
    parse(out.joinToString("\n"))
}

// A check --json probe: 1 ok, 0 missing, -1 works with caveats
enum class Probe { OK, MISSING, CAVEAT }

data class Capabilities(
    val root: Probe,
    val configfs: Probe,
    val udc: Probe,
    val gadget: Probe,
    val massStorage: Probe,
    val cdrom: Probe,
    val hid: Probe,
    val ncm: Probe,
    val rndis: Probe,
    val nat: Probe,
    val nat6: Probe,
    val version: String,
    val udcName: String,
    val requirementsMet: Boolean,
    // Whether f_hid takes an interval; null from a backend older than the probe
    val hidInterval: Probe? = null,
    // The JSON it was parsed from, for the cache
    val raw: String = "",
)

// An ejected LUN has an empty file, mode and access
data class Lun(val lun: Int, val file: String, val mode: String, val access: String)

// [interval] is the poll interval exponent the function runs with: 0 for the kernel's default
// (1 ms), -1 where the kernel has no control for it (stock f_hid keeps 1 ms) or the backend is
// older
data class HidNode(val function: String, val node: String, val interval: Int = -1)

data class Tether(
    val function: String,
    val iface: String,
    val running: Boolean,
    val address: String,
    val ipv6: String,
    val upstream: String,
    val gateway: Boolean,
    val gatewayContainer: String,
    val gatewayIface: String,
    val gatewayWaiting: Boolean,
    // What the phone's end of the link has sent and received; -1 unread, or an older backend
    val txBytes: Long = -1,
    val rxBytes: Long = -1,
)

data class GadgetStatus(
    val version: String,
    val udc: String,
    val udcState: String,
    val bound: Boolean,
    val storage: List<Lun>,
    val hid: List<HidNode>,
    val tether: Tether?,
    // The boot this was read in, the setup (what each function starts with), what the last
    // successful start used, and whether they differ per function; empty from an older backend
    val bootId: String = "",
    val setup: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
    val running: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
    val pending: Map<String, Boolean> = emptyMap(),
    // The bus speed the host gave the gadget (full-speed, high-speed, super-speed); empty unbound
    val speed: String = "",
    val raw: String = "",
)

// The C side prints every key, so a missing one is a mismatched backend and throws
fun parseCheck(json: String): Capabilities = with(JSONObject(json)) {
    fun p(key: String) = when (getInt(key)) {
        1 -> Probe.OK
        -1 -> Probe.CAVEAT
        else -> Probe.MISSING
    }
    Capabilities(
        p("root"), p("configfs"), p("udc"), p("gadget"), p("mass_storage"), p("cdrom"), p("hid"),
        p("ncm"), p("rndis"), p("nat"), p("nat6"),
        getString("version"), getString("udc_name"), getInt("requirements_met") == 1,
        if (has("hid_interval")) p("hid_interval") else null,
        raw = json,
    )
}


fun parseStatus(json: String): GadgetStatus = with(JSONObject(json)) {
    GadgetStatus(
        version = getString("version"),
        udc = getString("udc"),
        udcState = getString("udc_state"),
        bound = getInt("bound") == 1,
        storage = getJSONArray("storage").objects().map {
            Lun(it.getInt("lun"), it.getString("file"), it.getString("mode"), it.getString("access"))
        },
        hid = getJSONArray("hid").objects().map { HidNode(it.getString("function"), it.getString("node"), it.optInt("interval", -1)) },
        tether = if (isNull("tether")) null else getJSONObject("tether").run {
            Tether(
                function = getString("function"),
                iface = getString("iface"),
                running = getInt("running") == 1,
                address = getString("address"),
                ipv6 = getString("ipv6"),
                upstream = getString("upstream"),
                gateway = getInt("gateway") == 1,
                gatewayContainer = getString("gateway_container"),
                gatewayIface = getString("gateway_iface"),
                gatewayWaiting = getInt("gateway_waiting") == 1,
                txBytes = optLong("tx_bytes", -1),
                rxBytes = optLong("rx_bytes", -1),
            )
        },
        bootId = optString("boot_id"),
        setup = optJSONObject("setup")?.strings().orEmpty(),
        running = optJSONObject("running")?.strings().orEmpty(),
        pending = optJSONObject("pending")?.let { o -> o.keys().asSequence().associateWith { o.getInt(it) == 1 } }.orEmpty(),
        speed = optString("speed"),
        raw = json,
    )
}

private fun JSONArray.objects() = (0 until length()).map(::getJSONObject)

`Android/app/src/main/java/com/usbarsenal/app/backend/Cache.kt`:

```kt
package com.usbarsenal.app.backend

import android.content.Context
import androidx.core.content.edit
import java.io.File
import org.json.JSONArray
import org.json.JSONObject

/*
 * The last of every read, kept in prefs purely as a cache (Droidspaces' cachedContainers and
 * cachedHostCapabilitiesBootId): the first frame of every screen draws from it, a live read
 * replaces it, a failed read leaves it. The truth is the backend's; wiping this loses nothing.
 * Each entry remembers the boot it was read in, so a gadget from before a reboot is never shown
 * as live; the setup, caps and profile outlive a reboot.
 */
object Cache {
    // Null until init, as in a unit test: then nothing is cached and nothing is saved
    private var prefs: android.content.SharedPreferences? = null

    // This boot, read by the app itself (no root): the same id the backend prints
    val bootId: String by lazy { runCatching { File("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id").readText().trim() }.getOrDefault("") }

    fun init(context: Context) {
        prefs = context.getSharedPreferences("cache", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
    }

    private fun text(key: String) = prefs?.getString(key, null)

    private fun put(key: String, value: String?) {
        prefs?.edit { if (value == null) remove(key) else putString(key, value) }
    }

    // The last status; its gadget part only while the boot it was read in is this one
    var status: GadgetStatus?
        get() = text("status")?.let { raw -> runCatching { parseStatus(raw) }.getOrNull() }?.let { s ->
            if (s.bootId.isNotEmpty() && s.bootId == bootId) s else s.copy(bound = false, storage = emptyList(), hid = emptyList(), tether = null, running = emptyMap(), pending = emptyMap())
        }
        set(v) = put("status", v?.raw)

    var caps: Capabilities?
        get() = text("caps")?.let { runCatching { parseCheck(it) }.getOrNull() }
        set(v) = put("caps", v?.raw)

    var profile: Map<String, String>
        get() = text("profile")?.let { runCatching { JSONObject(it).toMap() }.getOrNull() }.orEmpty()
        set(v) = put("profile", if (v.isEmpty()) null else JSONObject(v).toString())

    var backend: Backend?
        get() = text("backend")?.let { runCatching { JSONObject(it) }.getOrNull() }?.let { Backend(BackendState.valueOf(it.getString("state")), it.optString("installed").ifEmpty { null }) }
        set(v) = put("backend", v?.let { JSONObject().put("state", it.state.name).put("installed", it.installed ?: "").toString() })

    // Edits of the setup not yet sent to the backend, so a kill in the beat before they go loses none
    var edits: Map<String, String>
        get() = text("edits")?.let { runCatching { JSONObject(it).toMap() }.getOrNull() }.orEmpty()
        set(v) = put("edits", if (v.isEmpty()) null else JSONObject(v).toString())

    var droidspaces: Droidspaces?
        get() = text("droidspaces")?.let { runCatching { JSONObject(it) }.getOrNull() }?.let { o ->
            Droidspaces(o.getBoolean("installed"), o.optJSONArray("running")?.let { a -> (0 until a.length()).map(a::getString) })
        }
        set(v) = put("droidspaces", v?.let { JSONObject().put("installed", it.installed).put("running", it.running?.let(::JSONArray)).toString() })

    var udcs: List<Udc>?
        get() = text("udcs")?.let { parseUdcs(it.lines()) }
        set(v) = put("udcs", v?.joinToString("\n") { "${it.name} ${it.state}" })

    var pathLinked: Boolean?
        get() = text("linked")?.toBooleanStrictOrNull()
        set(v) = put("linked", v?.toString())

    // Storage's folder: its canonical path, its files as `<bytes> <path>` lines, and the free bytes
    var imagesDir: String?
        get() = text("imagesDir")
        set(v) = put("imagesDir", v)

    var images: List<ImageFile>?
        get() = text("images")?.let { parseImages(it.lines()) }
        set(v) = put("images", v?.joinToString("\n") { "${it.bytes} ${it.path}" })

    var uplinks: List<String>?
        get() = text("uplinks")?.lines()?.filter { it.isNotEmpty() }
        set(v) = put("uplinks", v?.joinToString("\n"))

    // The log's newest lines as last read, so the Log screen never opens empty
    var log: List<String>?
        get() = text("log")?.lines()?.filter { it.isNotEmpty() }
        set(v) = put("log", v?.joinToString("\n"))

    var free: Long?
        get() = text("free")?.toLongOrNull()
        set(v) = put("free", v?.toString())

    // Identity's folder, as `identity show --json FILE...` printed it
    var profiles: String?
        get() = text("profiles")
        set(v) = put("profiles", v)

    // The last install that ended, its phase and what it printed, until the next one starts
    var install: Pair<String, List<String>>?
        get() = text("install")?.lines()?.let { it.first() to it.drop(1) }
        set(v) = put("install", v?.let { (phase, log) -> (listOf(phase) + log).joinToString("\n") })

    private fun JSONObject.toMap() = keys().asSequence().associateWith { getString(it) }
}

`Android/app/src/main/java/com/usbarsenal/app/backend/Images.kt`:

```kt
package com.usbarsenal.app.backend

import android.annotation.SuppressLint
import android.content.Context
import android.net.Uri
import android.system.Os
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext

// The app's folder on shared storage, as root sees it in the global mount namespace, which is
// where every path here is opened; the app's own view of storage is not involved
@SuppressLint("SdCardPath")
const val FOLDER = "/sdcard/USB-Arsenal"

// The folder Storage lists and Create writes to
const val IMAGES = "$FOLDER/Disks"

// What Storage serves: an image by its name, as the folder lists it and the picker takes it.
// A name that is only the extension (.iso) is a hidden file with none
private val IMAGE_EXTS = setOf("iso", "img", "bin", "raw", "ima", "dd")

fun isImage(path: String): Boolean {
    val name = path.substringAfterLast('/')
    val ext = name.substringAfterLast('.', "")
    return ext.lowercase() in IMAGE_EXTS && name.length > ext.length + 1
}

const val NOT_IMAGE = "[-] Not a disk image or ISO (.iso .img .bin .raw .ima .dd)"

// An image the folder holds: where it is, and how big
data class ImageFile(val path: String, val bytes: Long) {
    val name get() = path.substringAfterLast('/')
}

// The folder, made if it is not there yet, by its canonical path (/storage/emulated/0/...): the
// form the kernel reports a LUN's file in, so a file and the LUN serving it compare equal
suspend fun imagesDir(): String = Root.read("mkdir -p $IMAGES && readlink -f $IMAGES").out.firstOrNull() ?: IMAGES

// The folder's images; stat prints "<bytes> <path>"
suspend fun listImages(dir: String): List<ImageFile> = parseImages(
    Root.read("for f in ${shellQuote(dir)}/*; do [ -f \"\$f\" ] && stat -c '%s %n' \"\$f\"; done; true").out,
).filter { isImage(it.path) }

// What the folder's filesystem has left for a new image
suspend fun freeBytes(): Long? = Root.read("stat -f -c '%a %S' $IMAGES").out.firstOrNull()?.split(' ')?.let { (a, s) ->
    (a.toLongOrNull() ?: return@let null) * (s.toLongOrNull() ?: return@let null)
}

const val NO_PATH = "[-] That picker gives no file path; copy the image into $IMAGES"

/*
 * The file a provider actually opened for [uri], as a path root can open: Droidspaces'
 * FilePickerUtils.realPath. Guessing paths from document IDs differs per provider; the kernel
 * already knows the answer. It comes back canonical (/storage/emulated/0/..., never
 * /mnt/user/0/...), the spelling the folder's files and the kernel's LUNs use, so they compare
 * equal. A failure is the fault to show: no path when the provider hands out a pipe (cloud
 * providers) or root sees a different file there, or root that could not be asked.
 */
suspend fun realPath(context: Context, uri: Uri): Result<String> = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
    val pfd = runCatching { context.contentResolver.openFileDescriptor(uri, "r") }.getOrNull()
        ?: return@withContext Result.failure(IllegalStateException("[-] Cannot open that file"))
    pfd.use {
        val path = runCatching { Os.readlink("/proc/self/fd/${it.fd}") }.getOrNull()?.takeIf { p -> p.startsWith("/") }
            ?: return@withContext Result.failure(IllegalStateException(NO_PATH))
        val st = Os.fstat(it.fileDescriptor)
        val q = shellQuote(path)
        val r = Root.read("stat -c '%d %i' $q && readlink -f $q")
        when {
            r.timedOut || r.code == NO_ROOT -> Result.failure(IllegalStateException("[-] Cannot ask root about that file: ${r.why}"))
            r.out.firstOrNull() != "${st.st_dev} ${st.st_ino}" -> Result.failure(IllegalStateException(NO_PATH))
            else -> Result.success(r.out.getOrNull(1) ?: path)
        }
    }
}

// A sparse image: the size is set, no block is written until the host writes one
suspend fun createSparse(path: String, bytes: Long) = Root.change("truncate -s $bytes ${shellQuote(path)}")

// A full image is written out in megabytes; its progress is the file's size as it grows
suspend fun createFull(path: String, megabytes: Long) =
    Root.stream("dd if=/dev/zero of=${shellQuote(path)} bs=1048576 count=$megabytes")

suspend fun fileBytes(path: String): Long? = Root.read("stat -c %s ${shellQuote(path)}").out.firstOrNull()?.toLongOrNull()

suspend fun removeFile(path: String) = Root.change("rm -f ${shellQuote(path)}")

`Android/app/src/main/java/com/usbarsenal/app/backend/Installer.kt`:

```kt
package com.usbarsenal.app.backend

import android.content.Context
import android.os.Build
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.NonCancellable
import kotlinx.coroutines.sync.Mutex
import kotlinx.coroutines.sync.withLock
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import java.io.File
import java.security.MessageDigest

// Ported from Droidspaces' BinaryInstaller, ModuleInstaller, DeviceArch and DroidspacesChecker
const val MODULE = "/data/adb/modules/usb-arsenal"

// The PATH link Droidspaces' SymlinkInstaller makes: the binary stays in the workspace, and this
// links to it only while the user has asked for it
private const val MODULE_LINK = "$MODULE/system/bin/usb-arsenal"
private val MODULE_FILES = listOf("module.prop", "uninstall.sh", "sepolicy.rule")

// The binary suffix for this device's primary ABI, or null when we ship none for it
fun deviceArch(): String? = when (Build.SUPPORTED_ABIS.firstOrNull()) {
    "arm64-v8a" -> "aarch64"
    "armeabi-v7a", "armeabi" -> "armhf"
    "x86_64" -> "x86_64"
    "x86" -> "x86"
    else -> null
}

// NO_ROOT: su is missing, denied, or its grant dialog is still open, so nothing could be checked
enum class BackendState { NO_ROOT, NOT_INSTALLED, MODULE_MISSING, CORRUPTED, UPDATE_AVAILABLE, READY }

// [installed] is the version the installed binary reports, when it runs
data class Backend(val state: BackendState, val installed: String?)

suspend fun backendState(context: Context): Backend {
    val r = Root.read(
        """
        echo root
        test -x $UA && echo bin
        test -f $MODULE/module.prop && echo module
        v=$($UA version 2>/dev/null) && echo "${'$'}v" | head -n 1 | sed 's/^/runs /'
        md5sum $UA 2>/dev/null
        """.trimIndent(),
    )
    // "runs usb-arsenal 1.2.0"
    val installed = r.out.firstOrNull { it.startsWith("runs ") }?.substringAfterLast(' ')?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }
    val md5 = r.out.firstNotNullOfOrNull { Regex("^([0-9a-f]{32}) ").find(it)?.groupValues?.get(1) }
    // A shell that never said `root` never ran: su denied it (Magisk exits 13 with nothing said)
    // or is missing, so nothing was checked. No binary bundled for this ABI is nothing to update to
    val asset = assetMd5(context)
    val state = when {
        "root" !in r.out -> BackendState.NO_ROOT
        "bin" !in r.out -> BackendState.NOT_INSTALLED
        "module" !in r.out -> BackendState.MODULE_MISSING
        installed == null -> BackendState.CORRUPTED
        asset != null && md5 != asset -> BackendState.UPDATE_AVAILABLE
        else -> BackendState.READY
    }
    return Backend(state, installed)
}

private suspend fun assetMd5(context: Context): String? {
    val arch = deviceArch() ?: return null
    return withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
        runCatching {
            context.assets.open("binaries/usb-arsenal-$arch").use { MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5").digest(it.readBytes()).toHexString() }
        }.getOrNull()
    }
}

/*
 * Droidspaces' install: the binary into the workspace, the module's three files beside it
 * (never customize.sh, which only the zip runs), each step reporting what it really printed.
 * The module zip's customize.sh lands the same files.
 */
suspend fun installBackend(context: Context, log: (String) -> Unit): Boolean =
    withContext(NonCancellable) { installing.withLock { install(context, log) } }

// One install at a time: a second one would rewrite the staged binary while the first copies it
private val installing = Mutex()

private suspend fun install(context: Context, log: (String) -> Unit): Boolean {
    val arch = deviceArch() ?: run {
        log("[-] No usb-arsenal binary for ${Build.SUPPORTED_ABIS.firstOrNull()}")
        return false
    }
    log("[+] Device architecture: $arch")

    // The manager loads sepolicy.rule at boot. The rule already in the module is in the policy
    // now; a new or changed one waits for a reboot. It is never patched into the live policy,
    // which root detectors watch for. Asked before anything is copied, as Droidspaces does
    val oldRule = Root.read("cat $MODULE/sepolicy.rule").takeIf { it.ok }?.out
    val newRule = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { context.assets.open("boot-module/sepolicy.rule").bufferedReader().readLines() }
    val ruleIsNew = oldRule != newRule.dropLastWhile(String::isEmpty)

    val staging = File(context.cacheDir, "backend")
    try {
        stageBinary(context, staging)
        withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
            for (f in MODULE_FILES) {
                context.assets.open("boot-module/$f").use { i -> File(staging, f).outputStream().use(i::copyTo) }
            }
        }
        val s = shellQuote(staging.absolutePath)

        log("[+] Installing the binary in $WORKSPACE/bin")
        // Copied beside the target and renamed over it, so a hard reboot leaves the old binary or
        // the new one, and a copy still running the old one is never written to (Droidspaces'
        // installFileDurably). It also replaces the link an older install left here
        val binary = Root.change(
            """
            mkdir -p $WORKSPACE/bin &&
            { cp $s/usb-arsenal $UA.new && chmod 755 $UA.new && sync && mv -f $UA.new $UA && sync; } ||
            { rm -f $UA.new; false; }
            """.trimIndent(),
        )
        if (!step(log, binary)) return false

        log("[+] Installing the boot module in $MODULE")
        // A remove or disable mark from the manager, or a zip still pending in modules_update,
        // would undo this at the next boot. An older install kept the binary itself in
        // system/bin; that goes, and a PATH link the user asked for stays
        val module = Root.change(
            """
            rm -rf $MODULE/remove $MODULE/disable /data/adb/modules_update/usb-arsenal &&
            { [ -L $MODULE_LINK ] || rm -rf $MODULE/system; } &&
            mkdir -p $MODULE &&
            for f in ${MODULE_FILES.joinToString(" ")}; do cp $s/${'$'}f $MODULE/${'$'}f || exit 1; done &&
            chmod 755 $MODULE/uninstall.sh &&
            chmod 644 $MODULE/module.prop $MODULE/sepolicy.rule
            """.trimIndent(),
        )
        if (!step(log, module)) return false
    } finally {
        // Check's copy of the binary too: once installed, nothing runs it again
        withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
            staging.deleteRecursively()
            File(context.cacheDir, "check").deleteRecursively()
        }
    }

    val ok = backendState(context).state == BackendState.READY
    log(if (ok) "[+] Installed" else "[-] Installed, but the check after it failed")
    if (ok && ruleIsNew) log("[!] Reboot to load the SELinux rule")
    return ok
}

// A step prints what it really printed, then, when it failed, why it stopped
private fun step(log: (String) -> Unit, r: RootResult): Boolean {
    (r.out + r.err).forEach(log)
    if (!r.ok) log(if (r.timedOut) "[-] Timed out" else "[-] Failed (exit ${r.code})")
    return r.ok
}

/*
 * The bundled binary for this device, copied into a fresh [dir] and made executable, so setup
 * can run it before anything is installed. Null when we ship none for this ABI.
 */
suspend fun stageBinary(context: Context, dir: File = File(context.cacheDir, "check")): File? {
    val arch = deviceArch() ?: return null
    return withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
        dir.deleteRecursively()
        dir.mkdirs()
        File(dir, "usb-arsenal").also { bin ->
            context.assets.open("binaries/usb-arsenal-$arch").use { i -> bin.outputStream().use(i::copyTo) }
            bin.setExecutable(true)
        }
    }
}

// Droidspaces' SymlinkInstaller: usb-arsenal on PATH is the module's system/bin link to the workspace binary
suspend fun pathLinked(): Boolean? = Root.read("test -L $MODULE_LINK && echo 1 || echo 0").takeIf { it.ok }?.out?.firstOrNull()?.let { it == "1" }

// Only into an installed module, to the binary there; off takes system/ away whole, as the installer does
suspend fun setPathLinked(on: Boolean) = Root.change(
    if (on) {
        "test -f $MODULE/module.prop -a -x $UA || { echo '[-] Install the backend first' >&2; exit 1; }; " +
            "mkdir -p $MODULE/system/bin && ln -sfn $UA $MODULE_LINK"
    } else {
        "rm -rf $MODULE/system"
    },
)

`Android/app/src/main/java/com/usbarsenal/app/backend/Profiles.kt`:

```kt
package com.usbarsenal.app.backend

import org.json.JSONArray
import org.json.JSONObject

// Identity's profiles, files `identity set` takes, kept beside the images' folder
const val PROFILES = "$FOLDER/Profiles"

/*
 * A profile as Identity shows and edits it: the keys the host sees by name. The file holds every
 * other key too, at the values `identity generate` gave it. [path] is empty for the built-in
 * defaults, which are no file.
 */
// An empty [serial] is the phone's own: config.c derives it from ro.serialno (or /etc/machine-id)
data class Profile(val path: String, val product: String, val maker: String, val vid: String, val pid: String, val power: Int, val serial: String = "") {
    val name get() = if (path.isEmpty()) "Built-in" else path.substringAfterLast('/').removeSuffix(".conf")
}

// config.c's defaults, which `identity unset` goes back to
val BUILT_IN = Profile("", "USB Arsenal", "USB Arsenal", "1d6b", "0104", 250)

// The folder by its canonical path, the form `identity show` names the active profile in
suspend fun profilesDir(): String = Root.read("mkdir -p $PROFILES && readlink -f $PROFILES").out.firstOrNull() ?: PROFILES

// The folder's profiles, each read by config.c's own loader (`identity show --json FILE...`), so
// the app reads a file exactly as `identity set` will; the JSON as printed, which the cache keeps
suspend fun listProfilesJson(dir: String): String? = Root.read(
    "set -- ${shellQuote(dir)}/*.conf; [ -e \"\$1\" ] || { echo '[]'; exit 0; }; $UA identity show --json \"\$@\"",
).out.joinToString("\n").takeIf { it.startsWith("[") }

// "0x18d1" as config.c prints an id: four lower-case hex digits, as the screen shows it
fun hex4(v: String) = v.trim().removePrefix("0x").removePrefix("0X").lowercase().padStart(4, '0')

// A profile from the keys config.c printed for it; a key it lacks is the built-in value
fun profileOf(path: String, keys: Map<String, String>) = Profile(
    path,
    keys["product"]?.ifEmpty { null } ?: BUILT_IN.product,
    keys["manufacturer"]?.ifEmpty { null } ?: BUILT_IN.maker,
    keys["id_vendor"]?.ifEmpty { null }?.let(::hex4) ?: BUILT_IN.vid,
    keys["id_product"]?.ifEmpty { null }?.let(::hex4) ?: BUILT_IN.pid,
    keys["max_power"]?.toIntOrNull() ?: BUILT_IN.power,
    keys["serial"].orEmpty(),
)

// `identity show --json FILE...`: one object per file, its path and its keys
fun parseProfiles(json: String): List<Profile> = runCatching {
    val a = JSONArray(json)
    (0 until a.length()).map { i ->
        val o = a.getJSONObject(i)
        profileOf(o.getString("path"), o.getJSONObject("keys").strings())
    }.sortedBy { it.name.lowercase() }
}.getOrDefault(emptyList())

internal fun JSONObject.strings() = keys().asSequence().associateWith { getString(it) }

// The template with this profile's keys put in, each as a plain `key=value` line; a key a
// hand-made file lacks is added at the end, so none of the six is ever left out
fun withKeys(template: List<String>, p: Profile): String {
    val set = mapOf(
        "product" to p.product,
        "manufacturer" to p.maker,
        "id_vendor" to "0x${p.vid}",
        "id_product" to "0x${p.pid}",
        "max_power" to "${p.power}",
        "serial" to p.serial,
    )
    val there = template.map { it.substringBefore('=', "").trim() }.toSet()
    val lines = template.map { line ->
        val key = line.substringBefore('=', "").trim()
        set[key]?.let { "$key=$it" } ?: line
    } + set.filterKeys { it !in there }.map { (k, v) -> "$k=$v" }
    return lines.joinToString("\n", postfix = "\n")
}

// What a profile's file holds now, to put back if an edit is discarded; null when unreadable
suspend fun profileText(path: String): String? =
    Root.read("cat ${shellQuote(path)}").takeIf { it.ok }?.out?.joinToString("\n", postfix = "\n")

/*
 * Writes [p] at its path. A new one starts from `identity generate`'s template, every key with
 * its comment; an edit starts from the file as it is, so the keys this screen does not show
 * (storage mode, the tether address, the HID group...) keep their values.
 */
suspend fun writeProfile(p: Profile, create: Boolean): RootResult {
    val template = if (create) {
        val tmp = shellQuote("${p.path}.new")
        Root.change("$UA identity generate $tmp --force >/dev/null && cat $tmp")
    } else {
        Root.read("cat ${shellQuote(p.path)}")
    }
    if (!template.ok) return template
    return writeText(p.path, withKeys(template.out, p), fresh = create)
}

/*
 * [text] into [path] through a file beside it and a rename, so a start that reads the profile
 * meanwhile sees the old file or the new one, never half of one. The text goes as one
 * shell-quoted word, so nothing in it can break the command. [fresh] refuses a file that is
 * already there: a new profile never overwrites another.
 */
suspend fun writeText(path: String, text: String, fresh: Boolean = false): RootResult {
    val f = shellQuote(path)
    val tmp = shellQuote("$path.new")
    val guard = if (fresh) "if [ -e $f ]; then rm -f $tmp; echo '[-] A profile by that name is already there' >&2; exit 1; fi; " else ""
    return Root.change("${guard}printf '%s' ${shellQuote(text)} > $tmp && mv -f $tmp $f")
}
