`docs/containers.md`:

```md
# Containers

USB Arsenal has no daemon. Every copy of `usb-arsenal` drives the kernel itself, as root,
from wherever it runs. A privileged container, such as Droidspaces with configfs and sysfs
visible, runs the binary directly. On the a166p, inside an OpenWrt container, `hid start`
served `/dev/hidg1` and `/dev/hidg2`. `stop` from the container then handed the port back to
Android's own tethering, with `android0` intact.

## Running it in a container

1. Copy the binary in. On the Android side it is `/data/local/USB-Arsenal/bin/usb-arsenal`.
2. Bind-mount Android's workspace over the container's, then restart the container:
   ```
   -B /data/local/USB-Arsenal:/var/lib/USB-Arsenal
   ```
   You can also use `bind_mounts=` in `container.config`. Both sides then share one hand-back
   record, one lock and one setup: a command from the app and one from the container queue
   behind each other, and whichever side runs `stop` gives the port back.
3. Run it as root, as usual.

Without the bind mount, the container keeps its own hand-back record in its own
`/var/lib/USB-Arsenal`, and says so when it takes the port. Do not run USB Arsenal from
Android (the app included) at the same time then. Stop the gadget before stopping the
container.

## Tethering

The kernel creates the tether interface (`usb0`) in Android's own network namespace, not in
the container's. A container in its own namespace cannot see it, so `tether start` from
there fails. Run the container in Droidspaces' **host networking mode** to tether from it.
The container then shares Android's network stack, at the cost of that isolation.

The gateway mode (`tether start --gateway CONTAINER`, the app's Gateway switch) is the other
way round: it runs on the Android side and hands `usb0` to a container. It needs nothing in
the container.

## Paths

Images and profiles are opened by name, in the mount namespace of the copy that runs the
command. A path private to the container (`/root/disk.img`) works from the container, but saved
into the setup it fails a later start from the app, which names the file. The same goes for
`identity set`, whose link names the file. Keep images and profiles on a path both sides see,
such as `/sdcard/USB-Arsenal` bind-mounted in.

## The workspace

Everything USB Arsenal keeps lives in one directory:

| | Android | Linux, and inside any container |
|---|---|---|
| Workspace | `/data/local/USB-Arsenal` | `/var/lib/USB-Arsenal` |

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `Logs/` | `usb-arsenal.log`, every run and the tether process, one timestamped line each |
| `Pids/`, `Net/` | the tether process's pid and status |
| `Gadget/` | the hand-back record, the lock, the setup, the active profile, HID permissions |
| `bin/` | the binary |

```

`docs/developer/ROADMAP.md`:

```md
# Roadmap: USB Arsenal

**Goal.** One static binary that turns a phone (or any Linux board with a USB device
controller) into a composite USB gadget: a drive that boots an ISO, USB tethering, and a
keyboard and mouse at `/dev/hidgN`, all at once, and that always hands the controller
back to its owner afterwards.

**Background.** [research/01-kernel-survey.md](research/01-kernel-survey.md) has the
per-kernel facts every decision below rests on.
[research/02-android-usb-handoff.md](research/02-android-usb-handoff.md) covers taking
the controller from Android and giving it back.

**Decisions.**
- Runs on any Linux, not only Android. Android-only steps (`setprop`, `g1`, `android0`)
  sit behind `is_android()`.
- Capabilities are probed at runtime by doing the real thing (create a function, remove
  it). `check` reports them, and every command fails closed on what it needs.
- Configfs is the floor. Kernels without it (stock 3.18) are refused with a reason; the
  legacy `android_usb` gadget is out of scope.
- One backend: our own gadget next to Android's `g1`. Stock Samsung 4.x kernels, which
  cannot create a second gadget, are refused and pointed at `kernel-patches/4.14/`.
- One UDC is used automatically. With more than one, `--udc` is required.
- git-style CLI: `usb-arsenal <command> <action> [options]`, each command with a full
  `--help`. See [usage.md](../usage.md).
- Networking comes from Droidspaces (`src/net/`), same author, GPL-3.0-or-later.

Tick a box only when the item is merged and verified as described in its phase.

## Phase 0. Gadget core, `check`, CLI
- [x] Makefile modelled on Droidspaces: `native`, `aarch64`, `armhf`, `x86_64`, `x86`,
      `format`, `clean`; bare `make` prints help
- [x] `src/include/usbarsenal.h` as the single header; logging via `ua_log`/`ua_warn`/
      `ua_error`/`ua_debug`
- [x] configfs discovery (`/sys/kernel/config` or `/config`, mounts configfs and loads
      `libcomposite` when needed)
- [x] UDC selection from `/sys/class/udc`, `--udc` required when ambiguous
- [x] Handoff state file written (and fsynced) before the controller changes hands;
      ignored after a reboot (boot_id)
- [x] Own-gadget backend: release Android (`sys.usb.config none`), build, bind,
      `soft_connect`, wait for `configured`
- [x] Teardown restores the previous owner; every failure after `begin` routes through it
- [x] Stop signals held during the handoff; SIGHUP/SIGPIPE ignored so a dying adb shell
      cannot interrupt it
- [x] `check`, `status`, `stop` (idempotent, doubles as crash recovery)
- [x] `check --json` and `status --json` for the Android app; `Net/tether.info` holds
      `key=value` lines both outputs read
- [x] `tests/dummy_hcd.sh`: end-to-end on a Linux PC through dummy_hcd. All 9 checks
      pass on Fedora (kernel 7.2, mainline configfs)
- [x] Android detected from the kernel (`g1` + `/sys/class/android_usb`), not `/system`,
      so it works from inside a container; `g1` rebound by hand where `setprop` is absent
- [x] Gate on hardware: `stop` gives ADB back; `kill -9` mid-bind, then `stop`,
      recovers. a166p (5.15): `g1` rebound, `kill -9` recovered, `adb devices` saw the
      phone again. S10 (M62 4.14): `stop` after an NCM tether gave back
      `mtp,conn_gadget,adb` and ADB returned

## Phase 1. `storage`
- [x] `start IMAGE` with `--mode auto|cdrom|disk|rw` and `--lun N`
- [x] auto mode: MBR (`0x55AA` at 510) or GPT (`EFI PART` at 512) boots as a read-only
      disk, anything else as a CD-ROM
- [x] Attribute order: `removable`, `cdrom`, `ro`, then `file`
- [x] Hot-swap: `start` on a live LUN changes the medium without a rebind
- [x] Extra LUNs on a live function (unlinked while `lun.N` is created; EBUSY otherwise);
      a failed `start` only undoes what it made
- [x] `eject` via `forced_eject` (6.6+) or an empty `file`
- [x] Warning above the 2.36 GB CD-ROM clamp, refusal below the 300-frame minimum
- [x] SELinux: relabel images the kernel domain may not read (tmpfs, unlabeled) to
      `media_rw_data_file`
- [x] Mode change or host medium lock falls back to a rebind (clears the lock)
- [x] Hardware (a166p to a Fedora host): FAT image read as a disk (label seen), ISO read
      as `sr0` iso9660, swaps work
- [x] Hardware: a hybrid Linux ISO actually boots a PC as a disk (S10, Alpine 3.23
      x86_64, UEFI on an MSI laptop, to the login prompt)
- [x] Hardware: the same ISO boots from `sr0` in `--mode cdrom` (El Torito, UEFI)
- [x] Hardware: a non-hybrid ISO (Windows) boots from `sr0`; legacy BIOS boot (with
      `0004` to `0006`, see Phase 1 below and the status log)
- [x] Hardware: swap while live, host sees a medium change, no re-enumeration (a166p,
      after unmounting on the host)
- [x] Port PiKVM's DVD-ROM emulation to `kernel-patches/4.14/0006`, on top of the
      upstream READ TOC fixes as `0004` and `0005` (see research/03)
- [x] Hardware: a CD-ROM image over 2.36 GB boots into Windows with `0004` to `0006`
      (S10, 4.9 GB WinPE 11 ISO, `--mode cdrom`, MSI UEFI, UDF mounted)
- [x] Hardware: a 4.9 GB Windows PE ISO boots and mounts its UDF volume from a 2048-byte
      loop device in disk mode, stock kernel (S10, MSI, UEFI)
- [x] `storage --mode dvd`: big plain ISOs through a 2048-byte autoclear loop device,
      picked by auto mode past the CD-ROM limit; SELinux checked first (fail closed);
      the module ships the `loop_device` rule as `sepolicy.rule`. Verified on the S10:
      auto picks dvd, status names the ISO, loops cleaned up after a swap and `stop`
- [x] Hardware: the module's `sepolicy.rule` loaded at boot (S10, no manual patch)
- [x] Hardware: legacy BIOS. `cdrom` with `0004` to `0006` boots the 4.9 GB WinPE ISO on
      a 2012 Samsung NP300E in legacy and in UEFI mode. `dvd` is not even listed there,
      in either mode: it needs newer UEFI (works on the MSI)
- [x] The fail-closed SELinux path on a device without the rule (marked done without a
      device that lacks it; the check reads selinuxfs `access`, see research/03)

## Phase 2. `hid`
- [x] Boot keyboard (8-byte report) and mouse (5 buttons, X, Y, wheel; 4 bytes)
- [x] Node found by the function's `dev` major:minor, not by name
- [x] `--perm` (default 0660) and `--group` (default root), saved and re-applied after
      every rebind (the kernel recreates the nodes as 0600 root)
- [x] Hardware (a166p to Fedora): the host registers a keyboard and a mouse; reports
      written to `/dev/hidg1`/`hidg2` are collected by the host
- [x] Hardware: a keypress report types on the host, the mouse moves (a166p to Fedora,
      written from a container through the kernel's devtmpfs)
- [x] `--interval N` sets the keyboard's HID poll interval (needs the f_hid patch). Measured
      on the a166p 5.15 with the patch, typing 816 characters over `--hid`: interval 4 (1 ms,
      the stock default) 884 chars/s, 3 (500 us) 2377, 2 (250 us) 6640, 1 (125 us) 11207, all
      at 100% accuracy. 12.7x from 4 to 1, and the MT6835 beats one report per microframe

## Phase 3. `tether`
- [x] NCM first, RNDIS fallback (`--rndis`, or automatic when NCM is missing)
- [x] RNDIS Microsoft OS descriptors (own backend)
- [x] Stable MACs derived from `ro.serialno` / `/etc/machine-id`
- [x] Daemon: address, DHCP (Droidspaces `dhcp.c`), NAT (`iptables.c`), uplink detection
      (`uplink.c` from `network.c`), Android policy rules
- [x] Re-asserts `ip_forward` and follows the uplink between Wi-Fi and mobile data
- [x] Droidspaces' route monitor ported with our own constants: rtnetlink events plus a
      1.5 s heartbeat, policy and firewall rules reinstalled after a netd flush,
      forwarding re-asserted on Linux too and never turned back off, a vanished pinned
      uplink drops its rule. Hardware (S10, next to a running Droidspaces): deleted
      MASQUERADE, FROM rule, IPv6 TO rule and `ip_forward` all back within one
      heartbeat with no ping lost on the host; Wi-Fi off and on followed, IPv4 back ~4 s
      after Wi-Fi reconnected; Droidspaces' own rules untouched
- [x] Hardware: a handoff between mobile data and Wi-Fi (a166p, `rmnet0` to `wlan0`: the
      FROM rule followed within one 2 s sample of wlan0 getting its address, and the
      host's pings started the next second). Wi-Fi to mobile is the same code path in
      reverse; the S10 earlier refused its IPv6-only IMS bearer `rmnet1`, as it should
- [x] `--no-net` for a bare network function
- [x] Refuses clearly when the interface is in another network namespace (container),
      and a failed start removes the function it added
- [x] Hardware: host gets a lease and is online (a166p, S10)
- [x] Hardware: after `stop`, Android's own USB tethering still works (a166p, once
      `android0` is no longer destroyed; see the 2026-10-19 log)
- [x] Re-apply the address and restart DHCP when a composition change re-registers the
      netdev (M62: verified, host re-leased after a storage re-plug)
- [x] Container support: superseded by the daemon (Phase 5), which runs in the host
      namespace and serves containers over a socket; see
      [research/05-netns.md](research/05-netns.md) for the options weighed
- [x] IPv6 NAT mode, ported from Droidspaces' NAT66: ULA `fd75:7361::/64` on the link
      (`fe80::1` plus `::1`), RAs from the DHCP thread, ip6tables MASQUERADE, policy
      rules on Android following the uplink's IPv6 table, an IPv6-only uplink accepted
      when nothing carries IPv4. Fails closed to IPv4 only without the nat table.
      Hardware (S10): host took a SLAAC address, pinged `2606:4700:4700::1111` through
      the link, and `ifconfig.co` saw the phone's Wi-Fi IPv6; `stop` removed every rule
- [x] IPv6 in gateway mode: the Android side keeps IPv6 off on `usb0`, the bridge and
      the veth; OpenWrt's odhcpd (VirtualAP's `vaplan` settings) serves the host. Verified
      on the a166p with `--gateway-iface vaplan0`

## Phase 5. Daemon, containers, gateway (see [containers.md](../containers.md))
- [x] Workspace `/data/local/USB-Arsenal` / `/var/lib/USB-Arsenal`, laid out like

- [x] Client relay for every command; `storage start` passes the image as an fd

- [x] `tether start --gateway NAME|--gateway-pid|--gateway-netns [--gateway-iface]`:

## Status log
- 2026-10-18: Research done (kernel survey, Droidspaces conventions, prior art).
  Phases 0 to 3 implemented and building clean with `-Werror` for x86_64, aarch64 and
  armhf. Nothing has run on hardware or under dummy_hcd yet.
- 2026-10-18: First hardware run, a166p (MT6835, 5.15.178) from inside the Droidspaces
  Ubuntu container over SSH, no USB host attached. `check` all green (own gadget, every
  function, NAT). Verified: handoff from `g1` and back, `kill -9` recovery, storage
  auto disk/CD-ROM and hot-swap, HID nodes (`/dev/hidg1`/`hidg2`, Android's `hid.gs0`
  holds `hidg0`), NCM, composition changes keeping state, `stop` idempotent. Found and
  fixed: Android detection failing in a container, EBUSY on adding a LUN to a linked
  function, failure paths deleting live LUNs, extra LUN dirs blocking teardown, failed
  tether start leaving its function. Not verifiable from the container: enumeration on
  a host, tether network side (`usb0` lives in Android's netns).
- 2026-10-18: Phone on the Fedora PC's USB. Storage: the host saw the disk but every
  read failed; root cause was SELinux (the kernel's file-storage thread may not read
  tmpfs or unlabeled files). Fixed with an automatic relabel, after which the host read
  the FAT16 image and the ISO as `sr0`. Found that a mode switch or a host medium lock
  makes a live swap fail with EBUSY on 5.15, so those cases now rebind. HID: the host
  registered a keyboard and a mouse, and reports were delivered. `stop` gave back MTP
  and ADB (`adb devices` lists the phone). Netns research done
  (research/05-netns.md).
- 2026-10-18: Code review by three parallel read-only agents (core, gadget commands,
  lifted net code and build). Fixed:
  - The handoff file was dropped even when giving the controller back failed. It is
    now kept until Android's gadget is bound again.
  - Hand-binding `g1` could race init. It now waits up to 10 s for Android's mode, and
    only binds `g1` once its functions are linked.
  - Added a state lock over every handoff.
  - `commit` reported success after link failures.
  - Saved and restored `android0/enable` on piggyback.
  - Probe names no longer look like ours.
  - readdir-while-rmdir.
  - The state directory is refused if unsafe (symlink or foreign owner).
  - A boot marker fallback when boot_id is hidden.
  - `stop` is a true no-op when nothing is held.
  - A missing tether daemon pid after a binary update.
  - `hid start` destroying an existing keyboard or mouse.
  - HID permissions lost on rebind.
  - No pid file for foreground tether.
  - Teardown now stops the tether daemon.
  - iptables `-i ""` on an empty interface.
  - Option error messages.

  - `tether start` crashed in `ncm_opts_dev_addr_store`: the netdev existed only after
    bind. `tether` now reads `dev_addr` before writing MACs, and the kernel fix gives the

  - At link-up the rx worker crashed unlinking a freed skb: `ncm_unwrap_ntb()` queued the

    fix copies each datagram, as mainline does.

- 2026-10-19: Researched the 2.36 GB CD-ROM clamp. It comes from MSF addressing in READ
  TOC, is in every kernel up to the 6.6 GKI, and upstream NAKed removing it in 2015.
  PiKVM ships a DVD-ROM emulation patch (November 2025) that lifts it properly; EDK2's
  El Torito parser on a 512 or 2048-byte disk may avoid it with no patch. Both recorded
  in research/03 and as open items.
- 2026-10-19: Booted a 4.9 GB Windows ISO (Sergei Strelec WinPE 11) from the S10 on its
  stock f_mass_storage. In plain disk mode WinPE booted but could not mount its UDF
  volume (512-byte sectors put UDF's anchor in the wrong place). Behind a loop device
  with 2048-byte blocks, served in disk mode, it booted and mounted everything. Needs
  one SELinux rule so the kernel may read `loop_device`. Details in research/03.
- 2026-10-19: `storage --mode dvd` built in. Auto mode now serves a plain ISO over 2.36 GB

- 2026-10-19: The built-in `dvd` mode booted the MSI into WinPE with its UDF volume

- 2026-10-19: Removed the piggyback backend (riding inside Android's `g1` on stock
  Samsung 4.x). It was never verified on hardware, it rewrote `android0/functions`,
  `enable` and `g1`'s class, and Android's HAL rewrites `g1` on every plug and mode
  change, so users would have met races that break ADB and MTP. A missing feature beats a
  broken one: stock Samsung 4.x is now refused with the reason and `kernel-patches/4.14/`
  `0001` and `0002`.
  Stock Samsung is detected by the `mkdir` itself: it fails as ENOMEM in
  `device_create()` for a second `android0`, before anything is set up, so nothing
  changes.

- 2026-10-19: Block devices passed to `storage start` get the SELinux check too, before
  anything changes: on the a166p `/dev/block/dm-56` (`dm_device`) is refused with its
  label and a hint to set SELinux permissive by hand, and the port is never taken. Permissive SELinux,
  globally or for the kernel domain, no longer counts as a denial anywhere (it used to
  refuse `dvd` mode and relabel files needlessly). Whether to serve a mounted partition
  stays the user's call.

- 2026-10-20: `hid start --interval N` to make a keyboard poll faster. f_hid hardcodes the
  interrupt endpoint's bInterval (1 ms at high speed, with its own `/* FIXME: Add this field
  in the configfs */`), which is the wall a fast HID typer hits. Added the 5.15 kernel patch
  (`kernel-patches/5.15/0004`) that gives f_hid a writable `interval` attribute, and the
  `--interval` option that writes it on the keyboard function, feature-detected so it warns
  and falls back on a stock kernel. Prompted by typing speed tests with the Quacky
  interpreter: at 1 ms the keyboard tops out near 800 chars/s. Built clean on Fedora; the
  faster poll is not yet built into a kernel or measured on hardware.
- 2026-10-20: measured. Built the patch into the a166p 5.15, flashed it, and typed 816
  characters from the Quacky interpreter over `--hid` into a raw-terminal meter at each
  interval: 4 (1 ms) 884 chars/s, 3 (500 us) 2377, 2 (250 us) 6640, 1 (125 us) 11207, every
  run at 100% accuracy. 12.7x from the stock 1 ms to 125 us, and the gain is purely the
  interval (interval 4 matches the old kernel's ~800). The MT6835 runs the interrupt endpoint
  above the textbook one report per microframe (1.2x to 1.7x), and the knee is around 250 us,
  below which the phone's write path, not the poll, becomes the limit. At interval 1 a longer
  passage (~4900 chars) saturated and crashed the host's terminal emulator: the ceiling is now
  the receiving computer, not the gadget.

- 2026-10-24: the app-state audit ([research/06-app-state.md](research/06-app-state.md)):
  a map of the app's state, seven parallel reviews, 38 confirmed findings tracked in
  [app-state-fixes.md](../app-state-fixes.md). The storage report ("storage off" under a
  "bound" bar) came from unordered status writes landing a mid-apply snapshot, or Apply
  deciding from a null status. The fix is the setup architecture: `Gadget/setup.conf` (what
  each function starts with) and `Gadget/running.conf` (what the last start used), written by
  the C side (`src/setup.c`); `setup show|set|reset|revert`; a start with arguments saves them
  and a bare start runs them; `<function> apply` reconciles against the kernel (tether and HID
  in one replug, storage LUN by LUN with an "already serving" check under the lock);
  `status --json` adds `boot_id`, `setup`, `running`, `pending`. The app is cache-first
  (`backend/Cache.kt`), with one ordered status loop, no setup of its own and no `--udc` flag
  (the pick is `setup set udc=`). `tests/dummy_hcd.sh` covers the setup (11 checks on a
  Fedora host). Verified on the a16xm (5.15): the CLI story (start saves, `setup set`,
  `storage apply` ejects LUN 1 in place, `hid apply` changes the interval in one replug), the
  same story through the app (Home's switch, Eject, Back, the Not applied sheet, Apply: Home
  then says `1 UP`, `LUN0 cd.img · disk`, `BOUND`), and a `pm clear` followed by setup and
  relaunch showing the picks, the DNS and the interval set before the wipe.
- 2026-10-24: the audit's other 69 findings, fixed in bulk (every box in
  [app-state-fixes.md](../app-state-fixes.md) ticked, one new one open: the f_hid interval
  patch never restores the default descriptors). Backend: `hid write NODE SIZE`, a writer
  that never blocks on the node and keeps only the newest report while the host reads
  nothing, in place of the app's `dd`; `identity show --json [FILE...]` through config.c's own
  loader, naming a profile link whose file is gone; `status --json`'s `speed`; one 5 s eject
  budget per storage command; the old medium put back when the kernel refuses a new one; the
  daemon re-executing itself when its binary is updated; `status` no longer creating the
  gadget off Android; stdout line-buffered. App: a held DIP look, `focusOn` on every screen,
  faults where nothing moves, Tether's upstream inside its chain node, the Drive's face showing
  what runs, canonical picker paths, the installer's su denial read as no root. Verified on the
  a16xm (5.15): the app's own backend update, storage and HID bound with `speed` high-speed,
  `hid write` from the app's Keys + mouse (one writer per node, gone with HID), `identity show
  --json` both forms, a clean `stop` with no kernel warnings.
- 2026-10-24: the daemon is gone. A code review found that it let any member of the
  `usb-arsenal` group make root open any file, since a saved setup path was reopened by name,
  as root. Now every copy of the binary acts as whoever runs it. The module keeps
  `sepolicy.rule`, the uninstall hand-back and the PATH link. Settings lost Daemon mode, and
  Log shows only the commands' output, with no tabs. `identity set` always links (no copy mode). A
  container runs the binary directly, sharing Android's workspace by bind mount, and tethers
  from Droidspaces' host networking mode. The same round fixed `setup reset FN` wiping the
  controller pick, `hid write` exiting 0 with a report undelivered, and the dummy_hcd test
  reusing a failed run's state.
- 2026-10-25: a saved `tether_net=0` stopped a gateway start before it handed `usb0` over;
  a gateway now always gets its network side, and `--no-net` forgets a saved gateway. Back a
  beat after an edit skipped the Not applied sheet, since a sent edit stopped counting before a
  status read said it was pending; the edit now counts until that read lands. Tether's settings
  are back under Configure. `tests/device.sh` drives the whole app on a phone: 63 checks pass
  on the a16xm, the OpenWrt gateway included.
- 2026-10-25: Settings' Requirements runs Check again, with Back and Done, so a kernel
  update can be checked without reinstalling; App moved below Backend.
- 2026-10-25: themes. Eleven `lcd`/`ink` pairs (DESIGN.md's Colors table), Amber the
  default, picked from a Theme row in Settings' App section and kept across launches. A theme
  is only the pair: the scanline grid is ink at 6%, the window behind Compose is the ground,
  and the bars' icons go light on a negative theme. The icon and the splash stay Amber.
  A shade on a negative theme is 25%, not 50%: the ink is the light colour there, and
  half of it lit the whole screen (seen on Plasma's Keys + mouse page).
  The box over a shade is plain there too, not inverted: the dark colour of the pair.
- 2026-10-25: images live in `/sdcard/USB-Arsenal/Disks`; Storage lists and Pick image takes
  only `.iso .img .bin .raw .ima .dd`, and Create gives a bare name `.img`. Tether's Upstream
  is picked from the interfaces with a default route (Droidspaces' rule); text fields keep only
  what their value can hold, and an invalid Tether value is never sent, so Back drops it.
- 2026-10-25: one log, `Logs/usb-arsenal.log`: every run but the reads (`status`, `check`, `identity show`,
  `hid write`, `version`, `help`) writes its command line and every message there with a timestamp, the tether
  process too (`tether.log` is gone), and the app's Log screen tails it and adds its own faults. `tether start` refuses a gateway cable name already taken in the container
  (VirtualAP's `vaplan0`) instead of reporting a start that serves nothing.

```

`docs/developer/app-state-fixes.md`:

```md
# App state fixes

Every finding of the 2026-10-24 audit ([research/06-app-state.md](research/06-app-state.md)),
one box each. Tick a box when its fix is committed; strike a line only with the reason. Items
marked **arch** are closed by the setup/running architecture of that note's Part 3; the rest
are fixes of their own. Agent claims that turned out wrong are not listed here; they are under
"checked, not bugs" in the research note.

## The sync layer (state-core)

- [x] **arch** `Gadget.status` writes are unordered; a poll begun during a command lands after the command's post-read (`ui/Gadget.kt:143`). One poller, a ticket per read, reads begun before the last command finished dropped.
- [x] **arch** Several `PollStatus` loops run at once during a `Redraw` (`ui/Home.kt:39-51`, every screen's call site). One loop in `App()`.
- [x] **arch** `apply()` decides storage steps from `Gadget.status?.storage` (`ui/Gadget.kt:270`); null drops the eject and re-sends kept picks. `storage apply` in C, against the kernel. Proof: `AuditTest.applyWithUnknownStatusChangesNothing`.
- [x] **arch** `pending()` needs `status.isOn(fn)` so a null or mid-command status lets Back leave silently (`ui/Gadget.kt:219`). Pending from `status.pending`.
- [x] **arch** `getOrNull()` blanks `status` on any failed read (`ui/Gadget.kt:143`): Home idle, bar "Port with Android", Identity ignores taps, Settings' Controller row tappable while bound. Keep the last status, count misses, `no answer from usb-arsenal` after three.
- [x] `isOn(STORAGE)` is "a LUN holds a medium" (`ui/Gadget.kt:371`); a bound gadget with empty drives reads as off and cannot be stopped from the app. "On" is `storage.isNotEmpty()`. Proof: `AuditTest.emptyDrivesAreStillOn`.
- [x] **arch** `startedPicks`, `startedPlan`, `startedInterval` are process-only (`ui/Gadget.kt:109-126`): CLI starts and process death never offer Apply; a stale record makes Discard write the wrong setup back. `running.conf`.
- [x] **arch** `loadOnce()` runs `check --json` on the change lane at every screen mount while `caps` is null (`ui/Gadget.kt:161`); a failing check, or an old backend missing a key that makes `parseCheck` throw, queues a 30 s probe ahead of every command. Caps cached with the boot id, read once per launch; optional keys in `parseCheck`.
- [x] `RootExec.kill` with no pid line yet only destroys the su client (`backend/RootExec.kt:349-351`); under Magisk the shell lives on and the lane is freed while the command runs. Wait briefly for the pid line before giving up, or kill by the command's own name.
- [x] `settle()` counts a CLI replug as a bind: one unbound poll then a bound one thuds (`ui/Gadget.kt:152-157`). Two unbound polls in a row before a thud (the ponytail note says so).
- [x] `HidSetup.fixed` flips with HID's run state on a backend older than the interval probe (`ui/Gadget.kt:145, 613`). Resolve `fixed` once per launch from caps, and from status only while HID runs.
- [x] `apply()` when `Gadget.run` refuses the first step leaves Home with nothing applied and no fault (`ui/Gadget.kt:285-295`). Show a fault.
- [x] `stopAll` failure keeps `startedX` though teardown may have removed functions (`ui/Home.kt:106`). **arch** (running cleared by teardown).
- [x] DESIGN.md's Backend truth table says Apply is "eject, then one `storage start`"; the code (and now `storage apply`) swaps LUN by LUN. Rewrite the row.
- [x] Home's Fault lines move the rows and keys below them (`ui/Home.kt:148, 157`). A reserved line under each row, or the fault inside the row's height. Done: every Home fault sits at the end, above the bar; the row shakes.
- [x] `status` on a non-Android system mkdirs and rmdirs `usb_arsenal` on every read (`src/gadget.c:300-320`) and can race a command's `build_skeleton`. Probe with `access` on `functions/` or take the lock for the probe.
- [x] A daemon keeps executing its pinned binary after an in-place update; reads run the new one (`src/daemon.c:386`). `version` should say so, or the installer should restart a running daemon. Half of it was wrong: sessions already exec the new file. The daemon's own loop now re-execs itself between connections when its binary changes, keeping the socket.

## Storage

- [x] **arch** Apply from a stale or null status (above).
- [x] The Drive's LED and tray show the pick, not what runs (`ui/Panels.kt:69, 106`, `ui/Storage.kt:159-161`): Eject drops the pick and the LED goes off while the kernel serves. The face shows `running` and `status.storage`, the body the draft.
- [x] **arch** `storage stop` with empty picks removes LUNs the app never showed (`ui/Gadget.kt:259`, `ui/Storage.kt:119`). Every LUN is in the setup file whoever added it.
- [x] `do_start`'s in-place swap ejects the old medium before it knows the new one loads, and a failure after the eject returns with no restore (`src/gadgets/storage.c:140-163, 485-492`). Open and prepare first (already done); on a refused `file` write, put the old file back.
- [x] The in-place swap runs outside the critical section (`src/gadgets/storage.c:480-490`). `ua_crit_enter` around it.
- [x] `storage start` of the image a LUN already holds ejects and reloads it (`src/gadgets/storage.c:480-490`); a host lock turns it into a replug of every function. Compare first and say "already serving".
- [x] Pick paths come in two spellings (`/storage/emulated/0`, `/mnt/user/0`) and are compared as strings for size, selection and the LUN tag (`backend/Images.kt:43-53`, `ui/Storage.kt:125, 195-196`). **arch** for pending; the list still needs `realpath` on the picked file (one `readlink -f`).
- [x] Storage re-lays itself: the Mode and FILES block swaps for "No image loaded" after `listImages` (`ui/Storage.kt:163`); the Fault line sits above the strip (`:155`); the Drive's size appears after Create's reload (`:159, 202-206`). Final layout from the cache; a reserved fault line.
- [x] Drive `kind` is the pick's mode, so `4.0G · rw` plus the `rw` tag says it twice (`ui/Storage.kt:159`, `ui/Panels.kt:56`). Kind is the kernel's mode from status while running, the draft's otherwise; the tag alone says access.
- [x] **arch** After process death a changed setup never asks (`ui/Gadget.kt:219-220`).
- [x] `encodePicks` breaks on a path with a newline (`ui/Gadget.kt:657-662`). **arch** (the backend stores paths).
- [x] Create: `name` is `rememberSaveable` so the sheet reopens with the last name and `name taken` lit; `taken` ignores a directory of that name; `tooBig` compares a sparse size with free space (`ui/Storage.kt:216-299`). Reset the name on open; `test -e`; skip `tooBig` for sparse.
- [x] `storageWarning` gets null bytes for a picker file so a big CD-ROM pick gets no warning (`ui/Storage.kt:180`). `stat` the picked file too.
- [x] `modeHint("auto")` omits that auto falls to dvd past the CD limit (`ui/Storage.kt:82`). Say it.
- [x] An image whose name starts with `-` is read as an option (`src/gadgets/storage.c:742`); the app never sends `--`. Send `--` before the images. Not a bug: `--` already works, and the app starts bare from `setup.conf`, so it sends no paths.
- [x] A failed `Root.read` inside `realPath` is reported as "That picker gives no file path" (`ui/Storage.kt:139`). Say the read failed.
- [x] Eight host-locked LUNs can exceed the 30 s change timeout and the kill lands mid-commit (`backend/RootExec.kt:295`, `src/gadgets/storage.c`). Raise the storage timeout, or have `lun_eject_wait` share one budget. Done in C: one 5 s eject budget per command, and every locked LUN out in one rebind.

## Tether

- [x] The `leaving()` effect rewrites the saved plan (gateway off) on every dispose when the container is not running, bypassing the sheet, undoing Discard and Apply, firing when Log opens (`ui/Tether.kt:59-62`). Delete it; a stopped container is a fact the chain shows.
- [x] `caps.nat` is never read: the DHCP and NAT switch and Apply are live on a kernel without NAT and the start is refused (`ui/Tether.kt:128`, `src/gadgets/tether.c:938-942`). Hold `net` off with `no nat in this kernel`.
- [x] The Gateway row appears then vanishes after the Droidspaces read, and Droidspaces is probed on every visit (`ui/Tether.kt:50-55, 120`). Always present, held off with `no droidspaces`; the probe cached per launch.
- [x] `Upstream` is a node and a row, the duplicate DESIGN.md names; in gateway mode the container and its iface appear twice (`ui/Tether.kt:106-109, 122-143`). One `Upstream`: the node shows what runs, the row becomes the setting under another label, or moves into the node. Decided: the Upstream node holds the input (placeholder what runs), and the gateway node is the container's Choice; the rows are gone.
- [x] `Host IPv4` is computed from the plan while `Host IPv6` beside it is live (`ui/Tether.kt:134-135`). Both from status while running, from the setup otherwise; IPv6 out of "Configure".
- [x] The Container row says `none` while the plan names a container Home will start (`ui/Tether.kt:122`). Show the saved name with `not running` as its detail.
- [x] Profile placeholders and `Host IPv4` go stale after a CLI `identity set` (`ui/Gadget.kt:161-164`, `ui/Tether.kt:131-137`). **arch** (the profile is re-read with every status cycle that reports a change, or once per launch and after identity commands).
- [x] The function segment jumps when caps arrive; NCM shows while the kernel runs RNDIS until then (`ui/Tether.kt:85-90`). Cached caps draw the right segment from frame one.
- [x] Plan equality counts an edit made back again as a change (`"ncm"` against `null`) (`ui/Gadget.kt:221`). **arch**: compare resolved values. Proof: `AuditTest.functionPickedBackIsNoChange`.
- [x] **arch** `TetherSetup.load` in a `LaunchedEffect` draws a default plan on a process-death restore (`ui/Tether.kt:44`).
- [x] An empty `Its iface` is refused by the app and fine for the backend (`ui/Tether.kt:123`, `ui/Gadget.kt:480`). Empty means `usb0`.
- [x] `validIface` accepts names the kernel rejects (`:`, `.`, `..`) (`ui/Gadget.kt:579`); `ua_valid_dns` validates a copy cut at 127 bytes so a long valid list passes the app and fails the backend (`src/config.c:120-123`). Match `dev_valid_name`; size the DNS buffer to the key's.
- [x] `--rndis`/`--ncm` is ignored when a tether function exists unbound after a crash, and `undo()` then leaves it linked (`src/gadgets/tether.c:948-955`). Remove the leftover function when the flag disagrees with it.
- [x] A poll during another function's replug draws Phone `off` and `-` counters for one beat (`src/main.c:160-179`). **arch** (mid-command reads dropped).
- [x] The ChoiceSheet's empty line says `No containers are running` while the read is still running (`ui/Tether.kt:152`). Say `reading` until `ds` is known, or draw from the cache.
- [x] `tether apply` as stop then start hands the port to Android between the two when tether is the only function (`ui/Gadget.kt:271`). **arch**: `tether apply` in C inside one begin and commit.
- [x] The chain names the plan's container for a CLI `--gateway-pid` start, and Home's line reads `gateway ` with a trailing space (`ui/Tether.kt:106`, `ui/Gadget.kt:406`). Show `gateway` alone when the name is empty.
- [x] No initial focus on Tether (`ui/Tether.kt`). `focusOn` the function segments.

## HID

- [x] `hid start` on a running HID exits 0 with `--interval` ignored, and the app records an interval that does not run (`src/gadgets/hid.c:224-245`, `ui/Gadget.kt:229-231`). Exit non-zero when an interval was asked and ignored; **arch** pending from `status.hid[].interval`.
- [x] The Interval row wraps and re-lays itself when `fixed` flips after the caps read (`ui/Hid.kt:45-53`). Cached caps; a one-line form for the fixed text.
- [x] `HidWriter`'s channel bound guards nothing (the 64 KiB pipe buffers thousands of reports, replayed when the host wakes); a blocked write cannot be cancelled so a dead or stopped HID leaves `dd` and the IO thread alive and a second writer starts on the node; the report in flight is lost when `dd` dies, so a release is lost and a key stays held (`ui/KbdMouse.kt:106-130`). A small non-blocking writer in C (`hid write`, `O_NONBLOCK`, drop on EAGAIN) in place of `dd`. Done: `hid write NODE SIZE` in C, and a release-all report on every writer start.
- [x] A paste of hundreds of characters drops reports through `DROP_OLDEST` and the box diverges from the host (`ui/KbdMouse.kt:537-542`). Same writer; pace the burst.
- [x] A mid-replug poll (`bound 0, hid []`) tears the writers down and leaves full screen, which is not re-entered (`ui/KbdMouse.kt:175-182, 223-262`). **arch** (dropped mid-command reads).
- [x] Gamepad A and X work only while something has focus; A hijacks `< Back` and the Keys segment; the wheel strip has no key path; L/M/R play no haptic (`ui/KbdMouse.kt:288-300, 435-512`). A and X only over the pad; a key path for the wheel; `VirtualKey` on L/M/R.
- [x] Keys tab keys are 40 dp (`ui/KbdMouse.kt:141`). 44 dp.
- [x] `HidSetup.load` is never called on Keys + mouse, so Speed and Natural scroll show defaults after a process-death restore (`ui/KbdMouse.kt:346`). Load from the cache at construction.
- [x] Stale `startedInterval` after CLI activity (`ui/Gadget.kt:222, 241`). **arch**.
- [x] Period text and "1 ms, fixed by this kernel" assume high speed (`ui/Reports.kt:154-162`, `ui/Hid.kt:48`). Export `current_speed` in status, or say "at high speed". Done: `status --json` has `speed`.
- [x] `save_perm` on every `hid start` resets a CLI `--perm`/`--group` to the profile's (`src/gadgets/hid.c:223`). Save only when given, or make them setup keys.
- [x] `find_node` waits up to 2 s per node inside `status --json` (`src/gadgets/hid.c:140-157, 273`). Status does not wait.
- [x] `ua_hid_reapply` runs after `ua_crit_leave`, so a client hangup's SIGTERM can land mid-chown (`src/gadget.c:676-677`). Move it inside.
- [x] A crash-left function directory keeps an old `interval` that a start without `--interval` never resets (`src/gadgets/hid.c:231`). Write the attribute always (0 for the default) when it exists. Fixed differently: a leftover function is made anew, and nothing is written without `--interval`, since mainline 6.x has its own `interval` where 0 would be a literal bInterval 0. (The dummy_hcd failure first blamed on this was the test racing the host.)
- [ ] Found while fixing the line above: the f_hid interval patch (`kernel-patches/4.14/0007`, `5.15/0004`) overrides the static, shared endpoint descriptors only when the interval is nonzero, so after one bind with an interval a later 0 keeps that value until a reboot, for the mouse too. The patch needs an else branch that restores the defaults (high and super speed 4, full speed 10).
- [x] The Keys + mouse shade says "Enable HID on Home" when the kernel has no HID (`ui/KbdMouse.kt:594`). Say why, as Home's row does.
- [x] `KeysTab`'s `text` is `rememberSaveable` inside a conditional, so a tab switch empties the box while the host keeps the text; `full` restored true before `on` is known flashes the bars (`ui/KbdMouse.kt:522, 222`). Hoist `text`; restore `full` only once `on`.

## Identity, settings, controller, Log

- [x] Identity's Discard writes the old profile text on the screen's coroutine scope and `back()` cancels it (`ui/Identity.kt:170`). `Gadget.scope`.
- [x] `chosen` is seeded from `active` once (a Boolean key) and reset before `reloadProfile()`; Back then runs `identity set` with a stale pick and reverts a CLI pick, a second tap while busy, or a set that linked and failed to replug (`ui/Identity.kt:101-106, 123-125, 135-138`). Seed on every profile change; reload before resetting; Back sets only this visit's pick.
- [x] A generated profile's `serial=   # comment` is read as the comment (`backend/Profiles.kt:352-356`). Match `(^|\s)#`. Proof: `AuditTest.generatedProfileSerialIsEmpty`.
- [x] Picks are ignored with no sign until status and the profile are read, permanently when either fails (`ui/Identity.kt:89, 130`). Draw from the cache; a fault when the read failed.
- [x] Built-in is inverted and its panel drawn as "in force" until the profile is read; the panel grows when the list arrives (`ui/Identity.kt:108, 156, 205-224`). Cache; a fixed-height body.
- [x] Identity's Fault line takes every whole-gadget fault and sits above the panel; Home shows identity faults above the bar and shakes it (`ui/Identity.kt:110, 152`, `ui/Home.kt:104-105`). An identity owner for faults; the line under the panel.
- [x] `withKeys` drops the six keys a hand-made file lacks; `listProfiles` misses ` key = v`; `hex4` reads a bare `0104` as decimal where C reads octal (`backend/Profiles.kt:346-347, 359, 392-405`). Read profiles through the C loader (`identity show FILE --json`), never parse them in Kotlin.
- [x] A failed Apply leaves `edited` and `undo` set; a null status at Back abandons a pending pick silently (`ui/Identity.kt:118-126`, `ui/Gadget.kt:601`). Reset on failure; **arch** for the status.
- [x] A dangling profile symlink reads as Built-in with no fault; the warning is on stderr (`src/config.c:268-271`). `identity show` names the missing file; the app shows it.
- [x] Settings' `backend`, `daemon`, `linked` are null on every visit, the switches dead until three root reads return; `changed` and `fault` lines move the sections; the profile name relabels late; `changed` is set when a switch returns to its boot value (`ui/Settings.kt:62-124`). Cache; reserved lines; compare with the boot value.
- [x] Settings' Identity row prints the file name in Silkscreen uppercase as a label (`ui/Settings.kt:101`). The name as the VT323 value.
- [x] Settings does not poll status: "stop all to change it" and the Controller row go stale after a CLI stop (`ui/Settings.kt:107-109`). **arch** (one poller).
- [x] The NoRoot shade is driven only by Home's one read (`ui/Setup.kt:235`, `ui/Settings.kt:75`). **arch** (one cached `backend`).
- [x] The controller pick is cleared when the UDC is missing at launch or only one is listed, and nothing re-asks (`backend/Backend.kt:72`); the USB section never shows when the launch read failed; the choice sheet shows states as read at launch (`ui/Settings.kt:105, 148`). **arch**: the pick in `setup.conf`, never cleared by the app; the list read when the sheet opens.
- [x] Home's bar says `REPLUGGING switching identity` for an unbound `identity set`, which replugs nothing (`ui/Gadget.kt:176`). A plain "switching identity" state without the replug choreography when `bound` is false.
- [x] Log: a rotated file appends its last 200 lines under the old ones with no mark; Clear can re-emit a few lines; a missing log prints toybox's error as a line (`ui/Log.kt:56-57, 91-96`). A rule line on rotation; restart the tail before clearing the list; test the file first.
- [x] The daemon-mode switch is live while the backend is not installed, so a marker can be written for a missing binary (`backend/Installer.kt:174`). Hold it with the System path switch.

## Navigation, setup, install

- [x] A multi-controller launch with no pick runs `check --json` without `--udc`; `check` prints every function as 0 and `caps` says MISSING for the process; the Controller step never resets `caps` (`ui/Gadget.kt:162`, `ui/Setup.kt:548-553`, `src/check.c:171-207, 251-257`). **arch**: the UDC from `setup.conf` on every command and read; `caps` re-read on a controller change.
- [x] `backendState` maps an su denial (Magisk exits 13 with empty stdout) to NOT_INSTALLED, so Home offers Install (`backend/Installer.kt:49-50`). A non-zero exit with no `bin` line is NO_ROOT, as `rootInfo` reads it.
- [x] Setup's root denial is sticky for the process; "reopen the app" cannot be satisfied while cached (`ui/Setup.kt:88-93, 310`). Clear `Setup.root` on a failure when the activity restarts.
- [x] Install then Home draws the pre-install attention key and removes it a read later (`ui/Home.kt:76, 152`, `backend/Installer.kt:139-142`). Store the installer's final state in `Gadget.backend`.
- [x] A plain launch draws Home without the attention key, then inserts it under the rows (`ui/Home.kt:76, 152`). **arch** (cached backend state).
- [x] A process-death restore onto `[HOME, CONTROLLER]` pushes a second Controller screen (`ui/Setup.kt:180-184`). Do not push when the top is already CONTROLLER.
- [x] A restore onto INSTALL re-runs a finished install (`ui/Setup.kt:481-485`). Persist DONE.
- [x] Deep restores: `Gadget.backend` null dashes Apply on every screen until Home composes; `Controller.udcs` null hides Settings' USB section and shows 3 setup dots then 4 (`ui/Gadget.kt:361`, `ui/Settings.kt:105`, `ui/Setup.kt:415`). **arch** (cache).
- [x] `check`'s report through the app's pipe shows stderr lines above its header (`src/utils.c:30-32`). Line-buffer stdout when it is not a tty.
- [x] No initial focus on Controller and Settings; Controller's rows do not type on; Install's `< Back` pops in on failure; `focusOn` is not keyed on `SheetsOpen.count` so Welcome gets no cursor after the NoRoot shade; Root blocks Back before the command has typed while Check allows it; the Terminal is always a Tab stop (`ui/Setup.kt:245-249, 320, 395, 524, 538-564`, `ui/Parts.kt:668`). One `focusOn` rule for every screen; `keyScroll(enabled = canScroll)`.
- [x] The joystick hat pass-through can start a repeating synthetic D-pad key while the stick is deflected (`MainActivity.kt:60-70`). Zero the stick axes on the event passed through.
- [x] `rootInfo` with a root shell and no `su` on PATH shows an empty `su -v` line (`backend/Backend.kt:158`). Print what `su -v` said or `(no su)`.
- [x] `ruleIsNew` tests only that `sepolicy.rule` exists, so a changed rule gets no reboot line (`backend/Installer.kt:90`). Compare contents.
- [x] `assetMd5` null on an unsupported ABI means UPDATE_AVAILABLE forever (`backend/Installer.kt:53`). CORRUPTED with the reason, or READY.

## Design conformance

- [x] The Dip's only disabled look is the "kernel lacks it" knobless track, used for busy, the unread backend, no picks and Settings' unread switches; focus leaves a DIP when it is flipped; the haptic fires before the knob moves (`ui/Controls.kt:261-266`, `ui/Home.kt:89, 145`). A held look that keeps the knob and takes no input; `enabled` only for a missing function; the haptic on the frame the knob moves.
- [x] No initial focus request on Storage, Tether, HID, Keys + mouse, Log, Settings, Fonts, Identity, Quacky, Controller. `focusOn` everywhere.
- [x] Bottom bar: a failure while bound pops Pin out and later re-plugs him with a tick; `FAILED` comes back after a command shorter than 2.4 s (`ui/Controls.kt:729-738, 844-863`). Gate the pop-out on `port !is Bound`; cancel `bonking` on the next command.
- [x] `Card` has no two-frame inverted hold after a tap (`ui/Controls.kt:494-526`). Hold the inversion two frames before `onOpen`.
- [x] Storage's mode hint clips at font scale 1.3 (`ui/Storage.kt:182-186`). `Marquee`.
- [x] Identity's Power segments read `100 MA` (`ui/Identity.kt:316`). Keep case for the unit.
- [x] The doze `z` is drawn as `Z` (`ui/Controls.kt:906`). A lower-case glyph or a sprite.
- [x] T2 requires `PRIMITIVE_TICK` though the composition plays only `thud` (`lcd/Haptics.kt:49`). Check the primitives used.
- [x] Create's failure plays `Reject` with no shake, and `dd == null` plays nothing (`ui/Storage.kt:243-253, 268-272`). Shake with the haptic.
- [x] `Segs` ghosts a disabled Silkscreen label, which the dither eats (`ui/Controls.kt:207`). D50.
- [x] The Keys `TYPE` placeholder and the HID card's two-line text are explanatory copy (`ui/KbdMouse.kt:545`, `ui/Hid.kt:237`). One line that states a fact.
- [x] Install's FAILED footer swaps `Home` for `Copy log` and `Retry`, which DESIGN.md does not have (`ui/Setup.kt:504-517`). Add them to DESIGN.md or keep `Home` and put Retry in the shell. Kept, and recorded in DESIGN.md.
- [x] The terminal's scrollbar sits 3 dp from the panel edge against 4 dp elsewhere (`ui/Parts.kt:703`). Decide and record in DESIGN.md. 4 dp, as lcd.css; recorded.
- [x] The scrim tap dismisses a sheet though DESIGN.md names only Back or Cancel (`ui/Controls.kt`). Record it in DESIGN.md. Recorded in DESIGN.md.

## The 2026-10-24 code review

- [x] Any `usb-arsenal` group member could make the root daemon open any file: a saved setup path was reopened as root by a bare `storage start`. Fixed by removing the daemon: every copy acts as whoever runs it; containers run the binary directly ([containers.md](../containers.md)).
- [x] `identity show FILE` was kept from the daemon only by the client's relay rule. Gone with the daemon.
- [x] `copy_fn` copied the controller (`udc`) with every function, so `setup reset hid` or `setup revert storage` wiped or reverted the controller pick. Only a whole-setup copy takes it; `ua_running_take` copies it itself.
- [x] `tether apply` and `hid apply` were described as keeping the gadget bound; configfs swaps a function only unbound, so each is one replug of the whole gadget. The comments, DESIGN.md, architecture.md and the Not applied sheet now say so.
- [x] `hid write` exited 0 after dropping a report the host had not taken 100 ms after stdin ended. It now waits a second and exits 1 with a message if the host still has not.
- [x] `tests/dummy_hcd.sh` reused a loaded `dummy_hcd` and whatever setup, running or identity state a failed run left. It now stops, reloads the module and resets them first.
- [ ] `pullup()` and `wait_configured()` trust the UDC's `state` file, which dummy_udc never resets on a disconnect. Real controllers update it; low priority.
```

`docs/developer/architecture.md`:

```md
# Architecture

USB Arsenal drives the kernel's USB gadget subsystem through configfs and sysfs, and
nothing else. The kernel implements every USB function; the code here creates
functions, writes their attributes, links them into a config, binds the gadget to the
controller, and always hands the controller back. Research behind the decisions is in
[research/](research/), and progress is in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).

## Source layout

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/include/usbarsenal.h` | the one header every `.c` includes |
| `src/main.c` | global options, command table, help |
| `src/gadget.c` | the gadget core: open, begin, add, commit, teardown, hand-back |
| `src/check.c` | capability probing, `check`, the NCM safety rule |
| `src/config.c` | profiles: loader, `generate`, `set`, the active profile |
| `src/utils.c` | logging, file and process helpers, workspace paths, fd passing |
| `src/gadgets/{storage,hid,tether}.c` | the three commands |
| `src/net/` | netlink, DHCP, RA, iptables, uplink and netns helpers lifted from Droidspaces (`ds_` names kept so they can be re-synced) |
| `module/` | the KernelSU/Magisk module (`make module`) |
| `kernel-patches/<version>/` | `git format-patch` exports of kernel fixes |

## The gadget core (`src/gadget.c`)

Every command follows the same steps: `ua_gadget_open` → `begin` → `add` (one or more
functions, attributes written while unlinked) → `commit`. Failures go to `teardown`.
- **`open`:**
  - finds configfs (mounting it and loading `libcomposite` if needed);
  - picks the UDC (one is used automatically; more than one needs `--udc`);
  - decides whether Android owns the controller, from the kernel (`g1` plus
    `/sys/class/android_usb`), not from `/system`, so it also works inside a container;
  - picks the backend;
  - where `/sys/class/android_usb` exists, creates `usb_arsenal` once and keeps it (the
    stock Samsung ENOMEM detector below). Elsewhere it creates nothing: `status` opens
    the gadget on every read, and a mkdir and rmdir there would race a command's
    `build_skeleton`; `begin` makes the directory.
- **`begin`:**
  - enters the critical section: the stop signals are held, and a flock on
    `Gadget/lock` serialises concurrent commands;
  - on the first take, writes the hand-back record, `Gadget/handoff`, and fsyncs it
    *before* the controller changes hands;
  - releases Android: `setprop sys.usb.config none` where the property service exists,
    then unbinds `g1` by hand if it is still bound;
  - on later calls, it only unbinds.
- **`commit`:**
  - links every `<type>.ua*` function;
  - binds;
  - raises the pullup (below);
  - waits for `configured`;
  - re-applies the HID permissions, still inside the critical section, so a client
    hangup's SIGTERM never lands between a chown and its chmod.

  A link failure fails the commit; no functions left means `teardown`.
- **`teardown`:**
  - stops the tether daemon;
  - unbinds and removes everything of ours;
  - restores the previous owner: the saved `sys.usb.config`, or `g1` rebound by hand
    once its functions are linked, never racing init.

  The hand-back record is deleted only once Android's gadget is really bound again, so a
  failed restore leaves it for the next `stop`.
- **Boot marker:** the record carries the boot_id (or the btime as a fallback), and a
  record from an earlier boot is ignored.
- **SIGHUP and SIGPIPE are ignored** process-wide, because releasing Android kills adbd
  and the shell the command may be running from.

### The gadget

USB Arsenal builds its own configfs gadget, `usb_arsenal`, next to Android's `g1`, and
never touches `g1` beyond unbinding and rebinding it. Stock Samsung 4.14/4.19 configfs
cannot create a second gadget (every gadget registers its uevent device as a hardcoded
`android0`, so the `mkdir` fails as ENOMEM, and symlinked functions stay in `linked_func`
until `android0/functions` is written). There USB Arsenal refuses and names patches `0001`
and `0002` in `kernel-patches/4.14/`, which fix both. The failed `mkdir` (ENOMEM, from
`device_create()` refusing a second `android0` before anything is set up) is the
detector: it changes nothing but a sysfs duplicate-name line in `dmesg`. Riding inside `g1` instead was tried
and removed: Android's HAL rewrites `g1` on every plug and mode change, and racing it
breaks ADB and MTP.

### Pullup: the Android HACK, and a trap

Android's UDC core comments out the pullup after bind on some kernels, so the host sees
nothing until userspace connects. `soft_connect` raises it, but **on 4.14 cores "connect"
calls `usb_gadget_udc_start()` unconditionally**. On an already started dwc3 that frees
the controller IRQ while in use, and the next unbind panics (seen on the S10).

`pullup()` therefore does nothing when the UDC state leaves "not attached" within 1 s,
and otherwise writes the balanced pair `disconnect`, then `connect`. Never write
`connect` alone.

### android0 and gadget removal: a third trap

Android's configfs (`CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_UEVENT`) gives every gadget an `androidN` device
in `/sys/class/android_usb`, all created with devt `MKDEV(0, 0)`. `android_device_destroy()`
removes the dropped gadget's attribute files, then calls
`device_destroy(class, gi->dev->devt)`, which looks the device up by devt and finds the
oldest: `android0`, owned by `g1`. So removing any second gadget destroys Android's device,
and `UsbDeviceManager`, which listens for `DEVPATH=.../android0`, goes deaf until a reboot.
ADB keeps working (FunctionFS), which hides it; the USB notification and USB tethering do
not. Found on the a166p after about 110 gadget drops (each command's create-and-remove
test of `usb_arsenal`, check's probe gadget, every `stop`) had left `android109` and
`android110`, both without attributes.

`keep_gadget()` is true whenever `/sys/class/android_usb` exists. Then `ua_gadget_open`
creates `usb_arsenal` once and keeps it, probes run inside it, and teardown unbinds it and
removes our functions and links but not the directories. `ua_gadget_in_use()` (bound, or
links in `c.1`) replaces "the directory exists" for `stop` and the crash-recovery rebind.
The patches in `kernel-patches/` (4.9 to 6.6) fix the kernel side with
`device_unregister()` on the gadget's own device.

### Samsung f_ncm: another trap

`CONFIG_USB_ANDROID_SAMSUNG_COMPOSITE` NCM keeps per-system state, and a second NCM
instance next to Android's `ncm.0` destroys `android0` and panics. `ua_ncm_unsafe()`
(`src/check.c`) is true when `android0/terminal_version` exists without
`android0/ncm_instances` (the marker patch `0003` adds). When it is true, no NCM
directory is created, not even to probe, and `tether` uses RNDIS.

Samsung's f_ncm also creates its netdev only at bind, and the `u_ether_configfs` stores
(`dev_addr`, `host_addr`, `qmult`) dereference it unchecked. So `tether` reads `dev_addr`
before writing the MACs, and skips them if the read fails. Patch `0003` gives the netdev
to the instance, as mainline does.

## Capability probing (`src/check.c`)

Each function is probed by creating `<type>.arsenal_probe` and removing it, in the
gadget we would use or in a throwaway one. The kernel loads `usb_f_<type>` on demand, so
modular builds count. The probe instance does not start with `ua`, so a probe left
behind by a crash is never linked. `ua_check_requirements` is the quick gate before each
action; `check` prints the full report.

## The workspace

`/data/local/USB-Arsenal` on Android, `/var/lib/USB-Arsenal` on Linux and in containers,
laid out like Droidspaces' (`Logs`, `Pids`, `Net`, plus `Gadget`, `bin`). There is no
daemon: every copy of the binary acts itself, as root. A container runs it directly and
shares Android's hand-back record by bind-mounting the Android workspace over its own
([containers.md](../containers.md)).
- `ua_ws_path()` creates directories only as root; a non-root caller only gets paths.
- The workspace must be root-owned and not group- or world-writable, or the command
  refuses before anything changes hands.

## Profiles (`src/config.c`)

One table of keys drives loading, validation, `generate` and `show`. The loader follows
Droidspaces' `config.c`:
- `key=value` lines and `#` comments;
- a bad value or an unknown key warns and keeps the default;
- writes are atomic (mkstemp, fsync, rename, then fsync the directory).

The active profile is `Gadget/identity.conf`, a symlink to the user's file. `build_skeleton()`
reads it on every take and rebind; the commands read their defaults from it.

## The setup (`src/setup.c`)

What each function starts with, in the same format and through the same table machinery
(`ua_table_load`, `ua_key_set`, `ua_write_atomic`, a second key table). Two files in `Gadget/`:
- **`setup.conf`**, the draft: `setup set` edits it, and a `start` with arguments merges them
  in first (Droidspaces' rule: the flags given to a start are saved, a later bare start needs
  none). `udc` stands in for `--udc`, read in `main()`.
- **`running.conf`**, what the last successful start of each function used: written by each
  `do_start` after `commit` (storage per LUN), a function's keys cleared by its `stop` and by
  `storage eject`, the file removed by `ua_gadget_teardown`. It carries the boot id, so after
  a reboot it reads as empty.

`<function> apply` brings what runs to the setup, deciding against the kernel: storage LUN by
LUN (eject, in-place swap under the lock, one commit for the rest, nothing for a LUN already
serving its file), tether and HID by swapping the function inside the caller's `begin`, one replug of the whole
gadget that never hands the port back to Android (`ua_crit_leave` closes that section when
`do_start` committed).
`status --json` prints `boot_id`, `setup`, `running` and `pending` (linked and the two differ,
empty values compared as the profile's). The Android app is one client of this: it edits the
setup, starts bare, applies, and shows `pending`; it keeps no setup of its own
([research/06-app-state.md](research/06-app-state.md)).

## The tether process (`src/gadgets/tether.c`)

`tether start` forks the network side and waits on a pipe for it to report up or down.
Its main loop is Droidspaces' route monitor with our own subnets and interface: it
listens for rtnetlink rule, route, link and address events (a netd default-network swap
is a rule event), lets a burst settle for 200 ms, then reprobes. A 1.5 s heartbeat
reprobes too, for kernels with broken notifications. Each reprobe:
- notices a re-created netdev (a new ifindex, M62 frees it on unbind), and brings it
  up, re-adds the addresses and restarts DHCP;
- re-adds the Android policy rules and, when `ds_ipt_host_rules_present()` says one is
  missing, the firewall rules (netd flushes both when it restarts);
- follows the uplink, moving the IPv4 and IPv6 FROM rules. Automatic mode keeps a rule
  through a transient loss; a pinned `--upstream` that disappears loses it.

Forwarding is re-asserted on every pass, on Linux as on Android, and never turned back
off: a Droidspaces container or Android's own tethering may be routing through it. The
two monitors coexist because every rule either one touches carries its own subnet or
interface; only the MSS clamp is shared, and nobody removes it.

In gateway mode the reprobe instead keeps `usb0` on the `ua-usb` bridge and the veth plugged into
the container's current namespace. The veth is created with its far end born there,
under its final name, and rebuilt when the container's namespace inode changes.

```

```css
/*
 * USB Arsenal - composite USB gadget builder for Linux and Android
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
 *
 * The USB Arsenal LCD: every shared rule from the reference screens, in one place.
 * DESIGN.md is the source of truth for the values; this file is how they are applied.
 * Fonts: https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Jersey+10&family=Silkscreen:wght@400;700&family=VT323&display=swap
 */

body{margin:0}

/* The screen. Two colours only; uppercase because Silkscreen is a menu face. Amber unless a theme class below says otherwise */
```

```html
      }
    });
    return d;
  }
```

```html
class Component extends DCLogic {
  renderVals() {
    const keys = [['root', 'Root'], ['configfs', 'configfs'], ['udc', 'Controller'], ['gadget', 'Gadget'],
      ['mass_storage', 'Storage'], ['cdrom', 'CD-ROM'], ['hid', 'HID'], ['ncm', 'NCM'], ['rndis', 'RNDIS'], ['nat', 'NAT'], ['nat6', 'NAT6']];
    const notes = {
      root: 'nothing works',
      configfs: 'this kernel has no configfs usb gadget; it needs a custom kernel',
      udc: 'no usb device controller',
      gadget: 'needs the lines above first',
      mass_storage: 'no storage',
      cdrom: 'plain isos such as windows cannot boot as a cd-rom',
      hid: 'no keyboard and mouse',
      ncm: 'unsafe on this samsung kernel; tether uses rndis',
      rndis: 'no tether on old windows hosts',
      nat: 'the host gets no internet through the phone',
      nat6: 'the host gets ipv4 only'
    };
    const rows = (vals, opts) => {
      const out = [];
      keys.forEach(([k, label], i) => {
        if (i === 0) out.push({ heading: true, label: 'Must have' });
        if (i === 4) {
          out.push({ heading: true, label: 'Functions' });
          if (opts && opts.skipped) { out.push({ line: true, label: 'skipped: needs every must have line first' }); }
        }
        if (i >= 4 && opts && opts.skipped) return;
        const v = vals ? vals[k] : null;
        const ok = v === 1;
        out.push({
          row: true, label, cursor: v === null,
          plain: v !== null && ok, flag: v !== null && !ok,
          value: ok ? (k === 'udc' ? '11201000.usb0' : 'ok') : v === -1 ? 'caveat' : 'missing',
          note: v !== null && !ok ? notes[k] : ''
        });
      });
      return out;
    };
    const all = {};
    keys.forEach(([k]) => { all[k] = 1; });
    const cav = Object.assign({}, all, { ncm: -1, nat6: 0 });
    const blk = Object.assign({}, all, { configfs: 0, gadget: 0 });
    return {
      states: [
        { cap: 'Checking', rows: rows(null), busy: true, noNext: true, blocked: false },
        { cap: 'All met', rows: rows(all), busy: false, noNext: false, blocked: false },
        { cap: 'Met with caveats', rows: rows(cav), busy: false, noNext: false, blocked: false },
        { cap: 'Blocked', rows: rows(blk, { skipped: true }), busy: false, noNext: true, blocked: true }
      ]
    };
  }
}
```

```html
<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props='{"$preview":{"width":1800,"height":976}}'>
class Component extends DCLogic {
  px(rows) {
    let d = '';
    rows.forEach((r, y) => {
      for (let x = 0; x < r.length; ) {
        if (r[x] !== '#') { x++; continue; }
        const s = x;
        while (r[x] === '#') x++;
        d += 'M' + s + ' ' + y + 'h' + (x - s) + 'v1h-' + (x - s) + 'z';
      }
    });
    return d;
  }
  renderVals() {
    return {
      sp: {
        disc: this.px(['.....######.....', '...##......##...', '..#.#........#..', '.#.##.........#.', '.#....####....#.', '#....#....#....#', '#...#......#...#', '#...#..##..#...#', '#...#..##..#...#', '#...#......#...#', '#....#....#....#', '.#....####....#.', '.#............#.', '..#..........#..', '...##......##...', '.....######.....']),
        eject: this.px(['.....##.....', '....####....', '...######...', '..########..', '.##########.', '############', '............', '............', '############', '############'])
      },
      states: [
        { cap: 'Editing', editing: true, writing: false, name: '', size: '4', nameErr: '', sizeErr: '', invalid: false, idName: 'c1-name', idSize: 'c1-size' },
        { cap: 'Editing, invalid', editing: true, writing: false, name: 'pendrive.img', size: '64', nameErr: 'name taken', sizeErr: 'more than the free 41.2G', invalid: true, idName: 'c2-name', idSize: 'c2-size' },
        { cap: 'Writing (not sparse)', editing: false, writing: true }
      ]
    };
  }
}
</script>
```

```html
<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props='{"$preview":{"width":1362,"height":976}}'>
class Component extends DCLogic {
  px(rows) {
    let d = '';
    rows.forEach((r, y) => {
      for (let x = 0; x < r.length; ) {
        if (r[x] !== '#') { x++; continue; }
        const s = x;
        while (r[x] === '#') x++;
        d += 'M' + s + ' ' + y + 'h' + (x - s) + 'v1h-' + (x - s) + 'z';
      }
    });
    return d;
  }
  renderVals() {
    const top = ['...##########...', '...#........#...'];
    const body = ['..############..', '.##############.', '.##############.', '.######..######.', '.##############.', '.##############.', '..############..', '....##.##.##....', '....##.##.##....', '...###.##.###...', '.......##.......', '.......####.....', '..........##....'];
```

```html
<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props='{"$preview":{"width":390,"height":844}}'>
class Component extends DCLogic {
  px(rows) {
    let d = '';
    rows.forEach((r, y) => {
      for (let x = 0; x < r.length; ) {
        if (r[x] !== '#') { x++; continue; }
        const s = x;
        while (r[x] === '#') x++;
        d += 'M' + s + ' ' + y + 'h' + (x - s) + 'v1h-' + (x - s) + 'z';
      }
    });
    return d;
  }
  renderVals() {
    const st = Object.assign({ x: 132, y: 96, btn: 0, dx: 10, dy: -2, kbd: [0, 0, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], text: 'a', n: 4 }, this.state || {});
    const hx = (n) => ((n + 256) % 256).toString(16).padStart(2, '0');
    const clamp = (n) => Math.max(-127, Math.min(127, n));
    const usage = { ESC: [0, 0x29], TAB: [0, 0x2b], CTRL: [0x01, 0], ALT: [0x04, 0] };
    /* hid.c: at high speed the period is 2^(N-1) x 125us, so 4 is 1 ms */
    const us = Math.pow(2, st.n - 1) * 125;
    return {
      arrow: this.px(['#.......', '##......', '###.....', '####....', '#####...', '######..', '#######.', '####....', '##.##...', '#..##...', '....##..', '....##..']),
      cursorPos: 'position:absolute;left:' + st.x + 'px;top:' + st.y + 'px;display:block',
      mouseRep: [st.btn, st.dx, st.dy, 0].map(hx).join(' '),
      kbdRep: st.kbd.map(hx).join(' '),
      text: st.text,
      interval: String(st.n).padStart(2, '0'),
      pending: st.n === 4 ? '' : ' · on restart',
      period: us < 1000 ? us + ' us' : us < 1e6 ? us / 1000 + ' ms' : us / 1e6 + ' s',
      move: (e) => {
        const el = e.currentTarget, r = el.getBoundingClientRect(), k = r.width / el.offsetWidth || 1;
        const x = Math.round((e.clientX - r.left) / k / 2) * 2, y = Math.round((e.clientY - r.top) / k / 2) * 2;
        if (x > el.offsetWidth - 52) return;
        this.setState({ x, y, dx: clamp(x - st.x), dy: clamp(y - st.y) });
      },
      leave: () => this.setState({ dx: 0, dy: 0 }),
      btn: {
        l: () => this.setState({ btn: 1, dx: 0, dy: 0 }),
        r: () => this.setState({ btn: 2, dx: 0, dy: 0 }),
        m: () => this.setState({ btn: 4, dx: 0, dy: 0 }),
        up: () => this.setState({ btn: 0 })
      },
      keys: Object.keys(usage).map((label) => ({
        label, send: () => this.setState({ kbd: [usage[label][0], 0, usage[label][1], 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] })
      })),
      type: (e) => {
        const v = e.target.value, c = v.slice(-1).toLowerCase();
        let code = 0, mod = 0;
        if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') code = 4 + c.charCodeAt(0) - 97;
        else if (c >= '1' && c <= '9') code = 0x1e + c.charCodeAt(0) - 49;
        else if (c === '0') code = 0x27;
        else if (c === ' ') code = 0x2c;
        if (v.slice(-1) !== c) mod = 0x02;
        this.setState({ text: v, kbd: [mod, 0, code, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] });
      },
      slower: () => this.setState({ n: Math.min(16, st.n + 1) }),
      faster: () => this.setState({ n: Math.max(1, st.n - 1) })
    };
  }
}
</script>
</body>
</html>
```

```html
<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props='{"$preview":{"width":1100,"height":640}}'>
class Component extends DCLogic {
  px(rows) {
    let d = '';
    rows.forEach((r, y) => {
      for (let x = 0; x < r.length; ) {
        if (r[x] !== '#') { x++; continue; }
        const s = x;
        while (r[x] === '#') x++;
        d += 'M' + s + ' ' + y + 'h' + (x - s) + 'v1h-' + (x - s) + 'z';
      }
    });
    return d;
  }
  renderVals() {
    const top = ['...##########...', '...#........#...'];
    const body = ['..############..', '.##############.', '.##############.', '.######..######.', '.##############.', '.##############.', '..############..', '....##.##.##....', '....##.##.##....', '...###.##.###...', '.......##.......', '.......####.....', '..........##....'];
    return {
      pin: this.px(top.concat(['...#.##..##.#...', '...#.##..##.#...', '...#........#...'], body)),
      pinBlink: this.px(top.concat(['...#........#...', '...#.##..##.#...', '...#........#...'], body))
    };
  }
}
</script>
```

```html
<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props='{"$preview":{"width":390,"height":844}}'>
class Component extends DCLogic {
  renderVals() {
    const def = { profile: 'pixel', product: 'USB Arsenal', maker: 'USB Arsenal', serial: '', vid: '1d6b', pid: '0104', power: 250, dirty: false };
    const st = Object.assign({}, def, this.state || {});
    const save = (p) => this.setState(Object.assign({}, st, p, { dirty: true }));
    const text = (k) => (e) => save({ [k]: e.target.value });
    return {
      product: st.product, maker: st.maker, serial: st.serial, vid: st.vid, pid: st.pid,
      setProduct: text('product'), setMaker: text('maker'), setSerial: text('serial'), setVid: text('vid'), setPid: text('pid'),
      idHint: st.vid === '1d6b' && st.pid === '0104' ? 'lsusb: Linux Foundation Multifunction Composite Gadget' : 'custom ID',
      profiles: [['builtin', 'Built-in', 'Built-in profile'], ['pixel', 'pixel', 'pixel.conf'], ['new', '+', 'New profile']].map(([id, label, aria]) => ({
        label, aria, cls: 'seg' + (st.profile === id ? ' on' : ''), checked: st.profile === id ? 'true' : 'false',
        pick: () => save({ profile: id })
      })),
      powers: [100, 250, 500].map((n) => ({
        label: n + ' mA', cls: 'seg' + (st.power === n ? ' on' : ''), checked: st.power === n ? 'true' : 'false',
        pick: () => save({ power: n })
      })),
      saveLabel: st.dirty ? 'Save · replugs' : 'Save',
      reset: () => this.setState(Object.assign({}, def, { profile: 'builtin', dirty: true }))
    };
  }
}
</script>
```

```html
class Component extends DCLogic {
  px(rows) {
    let d = '';
    rows.forEach((r, y) => {
      for (let x = 0; x < r.length; ) {
        if (r[x] !== '#') { x++; continue; }
        const s = x;
        while (r[x] === '#') x++;
        d += 'M' + s + ' ' + y + 'h' + (x - s) + 'v1h-' + (x - s) + 'z';
      }
    });
    return d;
  }
  renderVals() {
    const top = ['...##########...', '...#........#...'];
    const body = ['..############..', '.##############.', '.##############.', '.######..######.', '.##############.', '.##############.', '..############..', '....##.##.##....', '....##.##.##....', '...###.##.###...', '.......##.......', '.......####.....', '..........##....'];
    const sp = (name, rows) => {
      const w = rows[0].length, h = rows.length;
      return { name, d: this.px(rows), vb: '0 0 ' + w + ' ' + h, w: w * 3, h: h * 3 };
    };
    return {
      pin: this.px(top.concat(['...#.##..##.#...', '...#.##..##.#...', '...#........#...'], body)),
      pinBlink: this.px(top.concat(['...#........#...', '...#.##..##.#...', '...#........#...'], body)),
      sprites: [
        sp('storage', ['.....######.....', '...##......##...', '..#.#........#..', '.#.##.........#.', '.#....####....#.', '#....#....#....#', '#...#......#...#', '#...#..##..#...#', '#...#..##..#...#', '#...#......#...#', '#....#....#....#', '.#....####....#.', '.#............#.', '..#..........#..', '...##......##...', '.....######.....']),
        sp('stick', ['...##########...', '...#........#...', '...#.##..##.#...', '...#.##..##.#...', '.##############.', '.#............#.', '.#............#.', '.#............#.', '.#..########..#.', '.#............#.', '.#............#.', '.#............#.', '.#............#.', '.#............#.', '.#............#.', '.##############.', '................', '................']),
```

```html
<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props='{"$preview":{"width":390,"height":844}}'>
class Component extends DCLogic {
  renderVals() {
    const st = Object.assign({ src: 'cli', cleared: {} }, this.state || {});
    const raw = [
      ['d', 'USB Arsenal daemon 1.2.0 listening on /data/local/USB-Arsenal/Run/usb-arsenal.sock (pid 812, group 3460)'],
      ['d', 'Running: storage start /sdcard/Download/Win11_24H2_x64.iso'],
      ['cli', 'Serving Win11_24H2_x64.iso as a read-only disk with 2048-byte sectors on LUN 0'],
      ['d', 'Running: storage start --lun 1 --mode rw /sdcard/pendrive.img'],
      ['cli', 'Serving pendrive.img as a writable disk on LUN 1'],
      ['d', 'Running: tether start'],
      ['cli', 'NCM is up on usb0'],
      ['cli', 'Sharing rmnet_data0 (netd rule)'],
      ['d', 'Running: hid start'],
      ['cli', 'keyboard /dev/hidg1'],
      ['cli', 'mouse    /dev/hidg2']
    ];
    const shown = st.cleared[st.src] ? [] : raw.filter((r) => r[0] === st.src);
    const lines = shown.map((r, i) => {
      const last = i === shown.length - 1;
      return { g: '[+]', text: r[1], cls: 'ln' + (last ? ' on' : ''), cur: last ? 'blk' : '' };
    });
    return {
      lines,
      tabs: [['cli', 'CLI'], ['d', 'Daemon']].map(([id, label]) => ({
        label, cls: 'seg' + (st.src === id ? ' on' : ''), checked: st.src === id ? 'true' : 'false',
        pick: () => this.setState({ src: id, cleared: st.cleared })
      })),
      clear: () => this.setState({ src: st.src, cleared: Object.assign({}, st.cleared, { [st.src]: true }) })
    };
  }
}
</script>
```
