<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props='{"$preview":{"width":390,"height":844}}'>
class Component extends DCLogic {
  px(rows) {
    let d = '';
    rows.forEach((r, y) => {
      for (let x = 0; x < r.length; ) {
        if (r[x] !== '#') { x++; continue; }
        const s = x;
        while (r[x] === '#') x++;
        d += 'M' + s + ' ' + y + 'h' + (x - s) + 'v1h-' + (x - s) + 'z';
      }
    });
    return d;
  }
  art() {
    if (this._art) return this._art;
    const top = ['...##########...', '...#........#...'];
    const body = ['..############..', '.##############.', '.##############.', '.######..######.', '.##############.', '.##############.', '..############..', '....##.##.##....', '....##.##.##....', '...###.##.###...', '.......##.......', '.......####.....', '..........##....'];
    this._art = {
      pin: this.px(top.concat(['...#.##..##.#...', '...#.##..##.#...', '...#........#...'], body)),
      pinBlink: this.px(top.concat(['...#........#...', '...#.##..##.#...', '...#........#...'], body)),
      disc: this.px(['.....######.....', '...##......##...', '..#.#........#..', '.#.##.........#.', '.#....####....#.', '#....#....#....#', '#...#......#...#', '#...#..##..#...#', '#...#..##..#...#', '#...#......#...#', '#....#....#....#', '.#....####....#.', '.#............#.', '..#..........#..', '...##......##...', '.....######.....']),
      jack: this.px(['................', '################', '#..............#', '#..##..##..##..#', '#..##..##..##..#', '#..............#', '#..............#', '#..............#', '#..............#', '###..........###', '..#..........#..', '..#..........#..', '..###......###..', '....#......#....', '....########....']),
      keyb: this.px(['...............', '...............', '...............', '###############', '#.............#', '#.#.#.#.#.#.#.#', '#.............#', '#..#.#.#.#.#..#', '#.............#', '#.#..#####..#.#', '#.............#', '###############'])
    };
    return this._art;
  }
  componentWillUnmount() { clearTimeout(this._t); }
  renderVals() {
    const a = this.art();
    const st = Object.assign({ on: { storage: true, tether: true, hid: true }, busy: '', cur: 'storage' }, this.state || {});
    const save = (p) => this.setState(Object.assign({ on: st.on, busy: st.busy, cur: st.cur }, p));
    const defs = [
      { id: 'storage', label: 'Storage', icon: a.disc, href: 'Storage.dc.html', live: ['LUN0 Win11_24H2_x64.iso · dvd', 'LUN1 pendrive.img · rw'], off: 'pick an image to start' },
      { id: 'tether', label: 'Tether', icon: a.jack, href: 'Tether.dc.html', live: ['ncm 192.168.42.129 → .130', 'via rmnet_data0'], off: 'ncm · 192.168.42.129/24' },
      { id: 'hid', label: 'HID', icon: a.keyb, href: 'Hid.dc.html', live: ['keyboard /dev/hidg1', 'mouse /dev/hidg2'], off: 'keyboard and 5-button mouse' }
    ];
    const anyOn = defs.some((d) => st.on[d.id]);
    const fns = defs.map((d) => {
      const on = !!st.on[d.id];
      let l1 = on ? d.live[0] : 'off', l2 = on ? d.live[1] : d.off;
      if (st.busy === d.id) { l1 = on ? 'starting' : 'stopping'; l2 = (on ? d.label + ' start' : d.label + ' stop').toLowerCase(); }
      return Object.assign({}, d, {
        l1, l2,
        rowClass: 'row' + (st.cur === d.id ? ' on' : ''),
        dipClass: 'dip' + (on ? '' : ' off'),
        pressed: on ? 'true' : 'false',
        aria: d.label + (on ? ' on' : ' off'),
        hover: () => { if (st.cur !== d.id) save({ cur: d.id }); },
        toggle: () => {
          save({ on: Object.assign({}, st.on, { [d.id]: !on }), busy: d.id });
          clearTimeout(this._t);
          this._t = setTimeout(() => this.setState({ busy: '' }), 1200);
        }
      });
    });
    const up = defs.filter((d) => st.on[d.id]).length;
    return {
      sp: a, fns,
      busy: !!st.busy,
      busyLine: 'usb-arsenal ' + st.busy + (st.on[st.busy] ? ' start' : ' stop'),
      upBig: up ? up + ' up' : 'idle',
      isBound: !st.busy && anyOn,
      isAndroid: !st.busy && !anyOn,
      stopAll: () => save({ on: { storage: false, tether: false, hid: false }, busy: '' })
    };
  }
}
</script>

<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props='{"$preview":{"width":924,"height":976}}'>
class Component extends DCLogic {
  renderVals() {
    const st = Object.assign({ motion: true, haptics: true }, this.state || {});
    return {
      motionClass: 'dip' + (st.motion ? '' : ' off'),
      motionPressed: st.motion ? 'true' : 'false',
      hapticsClass: 'dip' + (st.haptics ? '' : ' off'),
      hapticsPressed: st.haptics ? 'true' : 'false',
      toggleMotion: () => this.setState({ motion: !st.motion, haptics: st.haptics }),
      toggleHaptics: () => this.setState({ motion: st.motion, haptics: !st.haptics })
    };
  }
}
</script>

<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props='{"$preview":{"width":390,"height":844}}'>
class Component extends DCLogic {
  px(rows) {
    let d = '';
    rows.forEach((r, y) => {
      for (let x = 0; x < r.length; ) {
        if (r[x] !== '#') { x++; continue; }
        const s = x;
        while (r[x] === '#') x++;
        d += 'M' + s + ' ' + y + 'h' + (x - s) + 'v1h-' + (x - s) + 'z';
      }
    });
    return d;
  }
  renderVals() {
    const st = Object.assign({ mode: 'auto', img: 0, open: false }, this.state || {});
    const save = (p) => this.setState(Object.assign({ mode: st.mode, img: st.img, open: st.open }, p));
    const list = [
      { name: 'Win11_24H2_x64.iso', size: '5.8G', gb: 5.8, auto: 'dvd' },
      { name: 'archlinux-2026.10.01-x86_64.iso', size: '1.2G', gb: 1.2, auto: 'disk' },
      { name: 'drivers-2025.iso', size: '412M', gb: 0.4, auto: 'cdrom' },
      { name: 'pendrive.img', size: '4.0G', gb: 4, auto: 'dvd', lun: 'lun1' }
    ];
    const img = list[st.img];
    const kind = st.mode === 'auto' ? img.auto : st.mode === 'rw' ? 'disk' : st.mode;
    let warn = '';
    if (st.mode === 'cdrom' && img.gb > 2.36) warn = 'cd-rom stops at 2.36G. the host reads a truncated disc';
    else if (st.mode === 'rw') warn = 'host can write to this file';
    return {
      disc: this.px(['.....######.....', '...##......##...', '..#.#........#..', '.#.##.........#.', '.#....####....#.', '#....#....#....#', '#...#......#...#', '#...#..##..#...#', '#...#..##..#...#', '#...#......#...#', '#....#....#....#', '.#....####....#.', '.#............#.', '..#..........#..', '...##......##...', '.....######.....']),
      ejectIcon: this.px(['.....##.....', '....####....', '...######...', '..########..', '.##########.', '############', '............', '............', '############', '############']),
      img, kind, warn,
      access: st.mode === 'rw' ? 'rw' : 'ro',
      open: st.open,
      trayClass: 'tray' + (st.open ? ' open' : ''),
      trayHidden: st.open ? 'false' : 'true',
      eject: () => save({ open: true }),
      modes: ['auto', 'cdrom', 'dvd', 'disk', 'rw'].map((m) => ({
        label: m === 'cdrom' ? 'cd' : m, cls: 'seg' + (st.mode === m ? ' on' : ''), checked: st.mode === m ? 'true' : 'false', pick: () => save({ mode: m })
      })),
      imgs: list.map((x, n) => ({
        name: x.name, size: x.size, lun: x.lun || '', busy: !!x.lun,
        cls: 'row' + (n === st.img && !st.open ? ' on' : ''), checked: n === st.img ? 'true' : 'false',
        pick: () => save({ img: n, open: false })
      }))
    };
  }
}
</script>

<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props='{"$preview":{"width":1280,"height":800}}'>
class Component extends DCLogic {
  px(rows) {
    let d = '';
    rows.forEach((r, y) => {
      for (let x = 0; x < r.length; ) {
        if (r[x] !== '#') { x++; continue; }
        const s = x;
        while (r[x] === '#') x++;
        d += 'M' + s + ' ' + y + 'h' + (x - s) + 'v1h-' + (x - s) + 'z';
      }
    });
    return d;
  }
  art() {
    if (this._art) return this._art;
    this._art = {
      pin: this.px(['...##########...', '...#........#...', '...#.##..##.#...', '...#.##..##.#...', '...#........#...', '..############..', '.##############.', '.##############.', '.######..######.', '.##############.', '.##############.', '..############..', '....##.##.##....', '....##.##.##....', '...###.##.###...', '.......##.......', '.......####.....', '..........##....']),
      pinBlink: this.px(['...##########...', '...#........#...', '...#........#...', '...#.##..##.#...', '...#........#...', '..############..', '.##############.', '.##############.', '.######..######.', '.##############.', '.##############.', '..############..', '....##.##.##....', '....##.##.##....', '...###.##.###...', '.......##.......', '.......####.....', '..........##....']),
      disc: this.px(['.....######.....', '...##......##...', '..#.#........#..', '.#.##.........#.', '.#....####....#.', '#....#....#....#', '#...#......#...#', '#...#..##..#...#', '#...#..##..#...#', '#...#......#...#', '#....#....#....#', '.#....####....#.', '.#............#.', '..#..........#..', '...##......##...', '.....######.....']),
      jack: this.px(['................', '################', '#..............#', '#..##..##..##..#', '#..##..##..##..#', '#..............#', '#..............#', '#..............#', '#..............#', '###..........###', '..#..........#..', '..#..........#..', '..###......###..', '....#......#....', '....########....']),
      keyb: this.px(['...............', '...............', '...............', '###############', '#.............#', '#.#.#.#.#.#.#.#', '#.............#', '#..#.#.#.#.#..#', '#.............#', '#.#..#####..#.#', '#.............#', '###############'])
    };
    return this._art;
  }
  renderVals() {
    const a = this.art();
    const st = Object.assign({ sel: 'storage', mode: 'auto', img: 0 }, this.state || {});
    const save = (p) => this.setState(Object.assign({ sel: st.sel, mode: st.mode, img: st.img }, p));
    const fns = [
      { id: 'storage', label: 'Storage', icon: a.disc, l1: 'LUN0 Win11_24H2_x64.iso · dvd', l2: 'LUN1 pendrive.img · rw' },
      { id: 'tether', label: 'Tether', icon: a.jack, l1: 'ncm 192.168.42.129 → .130', l2: 'via rmnet_data0' },
      { id: 'hid', label: 'HID', icon: a.keyb, l1: 'keyboard /dev/hidg1', l2: 'mouse /dev/hidg2' }
    ].map((f) => Object.assign(f, {
      cls: 'row' + (st.sel === f.id ? ' on' : ''),
      current: st.sel === f.id ? 'page' : 'false',
      pick: () => save({ sel: f.id })
    }));
    const list = [
      { name: 'Win11_24H2_x64.iso', size: '5.8G', gb: 5.8, auto: 'dvd' },
      { name: 'archlinux-2026.10.01-x86_64.iso', size: '1.2G', gb: 1.2, auto: 'disk' },
      { name: 'drivers-2025.iso', size: '412M', gb: 0.4, auto: 'cdrom' },
      { name: 'pendrive.img', size: '4.0G', gb: 4, auto: 'dvd', lun: 'lun1' }
    ];
    const img = list[st.img];
    let warn = '';
    if (st.mode === 'cdrom' && img.gb > 2.36) warn = 'cd-rom stops at 2.36G. the host reads a truncated disc';
    else if (st.mode === 'rw') warn = 'host can write to this file';
    return {
      sp: a, fns, warn,
      isStorage: st.sel === 'storage', isTether: st.sel === 'tether', isHid: st.sel === 'hid',
      modes: ['auto', 'cdrom', 'dvd', 'disk', 'rw'].map((m) => ({ label: m === 'cdrom' ? 'cd' : m, cls: 'seg' + (st.mode === m ? ' on' : ''), checked: st.mode === m ? 'true' : 'false', pick: () => save({ mode: m }) })),
      imgs: list.map((x, n) => ({
        name: x.name, size: x.size, lun: x.lun || '',
        cls: 'row img' + (n === st.img ? ' on' : ''), checked: n === st.img ? 'true' : 'false', pick: () => save({ img: n })
      }))
    };
  }
}
</script>
</body>

class Component extends DCLogic {
  renderVals() {
    const st = Object.assign({ fn: 'ncm', gw: false }, this.state || {});
    const save = (p) => this.setState(Object.assign({ fn: st.fn, gw: st.gw }, p));
    return {
      fnName: st.fn,
      fns: [['ncm', 'NCM'], ['rndis', 'RNDIS']].map(([id, label]) => ({
        label, cls: 'seg' + (st.fn === id ? ' on' : ''), checked: st.fn === id ? 'true' : 'false', pick: () => save({ fn: id })
      })),
      nat: !st.gw, gw: st.gw,
      phone: st.gw ? 'ua-usb' : 'usb0',
      midLine: st.gw ? 'virtual cable' : 'masquerade',
      upTitle: st.gw ? 'OpenWrt' : 'Upstream',
      up: st.gw ? 'usb0' : 'rmnet_data0',
      v4: st.gw ? 'by OpenWrt' : '192.168.42.130',
      v6: st.gw ? 'by OpenWrt' : 'fd75:7361::/64',
      gwClass: 'dip' + (st.gw ? '' : ' off'),
      gwPressed: st.gw ? 'true' : 'false',
      gwToggle: () => save({ gw: !st.gw })
    };
  }
}

<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props='{"$preview":{"width":390,"height":844}}'>
class Component extends DCLogic {
  px(rows) {
    let d = '';
    rows.forEach((r, y) => {
      for (let x = 0; x < r.length; ) {
        if (r[x] !== '#') { x++; continue; }
        const s = x;
        while (r[x] === '#') x++;
        d += 'M' + s + ' ' + y + 'h' + (x - s) + 'v1h-' + (x - s) + 'z';
      }
    });
    return d;
  }
  renderVals() {
    const top = ['...##########...', '...#........#...'];
    const body = ['..############..', '.##############.', '.##############.', '.######..######.', '.##############.', '.##############.', '..############..', '....##.##.##....', '....##.##.##....', '...###.##.###...', '.......##.......', '.......####.....', '..........##....'];
    return {
      pin: this.px(top.concat(['...#.##..##.#...', '...#.##..##.#...', '...#........#...'], body)),
      pinBlink: this.px(top.concat(['...#........#...', '...#.##..##.#...', '...#........#...'], body)),
      disc: this.px(['.....######.....', '...##......##...', '..#.#........#..', '.#.##.........#.', '.#....####....#.', '#....#....#....#', '#...#......#...#', '#...#..##..#...#', '#...#..##..#...#', '#...#......#...#', '#....#....#....#', '.#....####....#.', '.#............#.', '..#..........#..', '...##......##...', '.....######.....']),
      jack: this.px(['................', '################', '#..............#', '#..##..##..##..#', '#..##..##..##..#', '#..............#', '#..............#', '#..............#', '#..............#', '###..........###', '..#..........#..', '..#..........#..', '..###......###..', '....#......#....', '....########....']),

# 01. Kernel survey: the gadget subsystem from 3.18 to GKI 6.6

Read-only survey of the trees below (2026-10-18). Paths are relative to each tree, and
line numbers are from that date's checkouts.

The trees, all public:

| Name below | Device | Repository |
|---|---|---|
| t385 | Galaxy Tab A 8.0 2017 (3.18) | [Kernels-by-ravindu644/samsung_kernel_t385](https://github.com/Kernels-by-ravindu644/samsung_kernel_t385) |
| t295 | Galaxy Tab A 8.0 2019 (4.9) | [Kernels-by-ravindu644/samsung_kernel_t295](https://github.com/Kernels-by-ravindu644/samsung_kernel_t295) |
| a015f, a015g | Galaxy A01 (4.9) | [samsung_kernel_a015f](https://github.com/Kernels-by-ravindu644/samsung_kernel_a015f), [kernel_samsung_a01](https://github.com/ravindu644/kernel_samsung_a01) |
| exynos9820_lineageos | Galaxy S10 family, LineageOS (4.14) | [Kernels-by-ravindu644/samsung_kernel_exynos9820_lineageos](https://github.com/Kernels-by-ravindu644/samsung_kernel_exynos9820_lineageos) |
| M62-backport | Galaxy S10 family, custom (4.14) | [ravindu644/M62-backport](https://github.com/ravindu644/M62-backport) |
| exynos990 | Galaxy S20 family (4.19) | [ravindu644/samsung_kernel_exynos990](https://github.com/ravindu644/samsung_kernel_exynos990) |
| a165f | Galaxy A16 4G (5.10) | [Kernels-by-ravindu644/samsung_kernel_a165f](https://github.com/Kernels-by-ravindu644/samsung_kernel_a165f) |
| a166p | Galaxy A16 5G (5.15) | [Kernels-by-ravindu644/samsung_kernel_a166p](https://github.com/Kernels-by-ravindu644/samsung_kernel_a166p) |
| sm8550 | Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 Samsung tablets (5.15) | [samsung-sm8550-tab/android_kernel_samsung_sm8550](https://github.com/samsung-sm8550-tab/android_kernel_samsung_sm8550) |
| Pixel 10 | Pixel 10 GKI (6.6) | [Kernels-by-ravindu644/google_kernel_GKI-6.6.118-android15.8](https://github.com/Kernels-by-ravindu644/google_kernel_GKI-6.6.118-android15.8) |

**Short answer.** Every kernel from 4.9 up can build a configfs gadget, but three
variants exist, and the 3.18 floor ships without configfs gadget support at all.

## Summary

| Tree | Version | configfs.c | uevent device | linked_func staging | Second gadget | Pullup HACK |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| t385 | 3.18.120 | Samsung UEVENT, minimal (`state` only) | hardcoded `android0` (configfs.c:1732) | no | no | yes (udc-core.c:411-418) |
| t295, a015f, a015g | 4.9.227 | AOSP UEVENT (Qualcomm) | `android%d` (t295 configfs.c:1948) | no | yes | no (core.c:1370) |
| exynos9820_lineageos | 4.14.356 | Samsung UEVENT + GSI | hardcoded `android0` (configfs.c:2309) | yes (2094, 2168) | no | no in effect, see note |
| M62-backport | 4.14.356 | Samsung + the two fixes | `android0`, then `android1..` (configfs.c:2222) | yes, rescued at bind | yes | yes (core.c:1340-1346) |
| exynos990 | 4.19.325 | Samsung UEVENT + GSI | hardcoded `android0` (configfs.c:2268) | yes (2056, 2130) | no | yes (core.c:1403-1409) |
| a165f | 5.10.226 | AOSP UEVENT | `android%d` (configfs.c:1791) | no | yes | no |
| a166p | 5.15.178 | AOSP UEVENT | `android%d` (1785) | no | yes | no |
| sm8550 | 5.15.202 | AOSP UEVENT | `android%d` (1789) | no | yes | no |
| Pixel 10 | 6.6.118 | mainline + `android_configfs_uevent.c` | IDA-allocated `android%d` (:172-179) | no | yes | no (connect from a workqueue) |

Note on exynos9820: the connect call is wrapped in `#ifndef CONFIG_USB_OLD_CONFIG`
(core.c:1355), but Kconfig defines `USB_OLD_CONFIGFS` (Kconfig:137). The typo means the
pullup does go up on bind there.

## What it means for USB Arsenal

- **3.18 (t385).** `USB_CONFIGFS` and `USB_G_ANDROID` share one Kconfig `choice`
  (gadget/Kconfig:206-514). Both shipped defconfigs pick `G_ANDROID`. There is no
  configfs `f_hid` (f_hid.c is legacy-only, not in function/Makefile). Needs a custom
  kernel; `check` says so.
- **Stock Samsung 4.14 / 4.19.** `mkdir` of a second gadget collides on `android0` and
  fails as ENOMEM. A link puts the function on `gi->linked_func`, not `cfg->func_list`
  (exynos9820 configfs.c:729), so a hand-built gadget fails bind with "needs at least
  one function". Only `android0/functions` moves it across, so USB Arsenal needs patches
  `0001` and `0002` here and refuses without them. There is one exception: a config string other than `"Conf 1"` set before
  linking turns on "symlink change mode" (exynos9820 :466, exynos990 :434). We set
  `"USB Arsenal"`, which is harmless everywhere else.
- **M62-backport.** Commit `aa8867995` (`kernel-patches/4.14/0001`) gives every gadget its own uevent
  device. Commit `3090dac36` (`0002`) splices `linked_func` at bind (configfs.c:1599-1610)
  and searches it on unlink (:765-779). The own-gadget backend works there.
- **M62 `enable_store(0)`** calls `unregister_gadget` + `clear_current_usb_link`
  (configfs.c:~2125). If Android's HAL writes `android0` while we hold the controller, it
  can unbind us.

## UDC core

- `soft_connect` (write-only, `connect`/`disconnect`, EOPNOTSUPP with no driver bound)
  and `state` (read-only) exist on every version, 3.18 included (udc-core.c:522-555).
  USB Arsenal always writes `connect` after bind: required on HACK kernels, a no-op
  elsewhere.
- The `function` attribute exists only on 4.14+.

## f_mass_storage

| Version | LUN attributes |
|---|---|
| 3.18 | file, ro, removable, cdrom, nofua (f_mass_storage.c:3991) |
| 4.9 to 6.1 era | + inquiry_string |
| 6.6 | + forced_eject (f_mass_storage.c:3266) |

Function level: `stall`. FSG_MAX_LUNS is 8 on 3.18, 16 later. CD-ROM details are in
[03-mass-storage-cdrom.md](03-mass-storage-cdrom.md).

## f_hid

- 3.18: no configfs HID.
- 4.9 / 4.14: subclass, protocol, report_length, report_desc, dev.
- 4.19+, 5.10, 5.15, 6.6: + no_out_endpoint.
- Node `/dev/hidg<minor>`. HIDG_MINORS = 4, so at most four HID functions.
- Attributes return EBUSY once the function is in a config (`opts->refcnt`), so they
  are written before linking.

## NCM / RNDIS

- NCM attributes everywhere: dev_addr, host_addr, qmult, ifname; 5.10 adds
  max_segment_size; NCM os_desc only on 4.19+.
- RNDIS: 3.18 has dev_addr, host_addr, qmult, ifname and os_desc `interface.rndis`;
  4.9 (Qualcomm) adds `wceis`; 4.14+ adds class/subclass/protocol.

| Defconfig | NCM | RNDIS | MASS_STORAGE | F_HID | UVC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4.9 Samsung | y | y | y | y | n |
| exynos9820, M62, exynos990 stock | y | y | n | n | n |
| M62 `custom.config` | y | y | y | y | n |
| 5.10 GKI (a165f) | y | y | y | y | y |
| 5.15 / 6.6 GKI | y | **n** | y | y | y |

So: NCM is the only network function present everywhere, which is why `tether`
prefers it, and why stock exynos kernels can tether but not boot an ISO.

## Other cross-version traps

- **Unbind.** Every version takes `""` or `"none"`, but Samsung 4.14/4.19 reject a
  zero-length write or one containing a NUL (`if(!len || strlen(name)!=len)`,
  exynos9820 configfs.c:422). We always write `none\n`. Those kernels also `mdelay(50)`
  on every UDC write.
- Writing UDC while it is already bound returns EBUSY everywhere.
- `max_speed` exists only on 5.10+; `webusb/` only on 6.6. We use neither.
- Function directory names must be `type.instance`, under 40 characters, everywhere.
- Samsung GSI code special-cases a function named `adb` when relinking. We never
  relink Android's functions.

## os_desc

Present on 3.18 already: `use`, `b_vendor_code`, `qw_sign` (configfs.c:815-924), the
config link (:934), and `interface.*` compatible_id / sub_compatible_id (:1229-1314).

## Two kernel traps that panicked the S10 (M62, 4.14)

Found on hardware on 2026-10-18. Both are in kernel code that USB Arsenal drives
through plain configfs and sysfs writes.

### `soft_connect` "connect" double-starts the controller (4.14 and older cores)

```c
/* M62 drivers/usb/gadget/udc/core.c:1454 usb_udc_softconn_store */
if (sysfs_streq(buf, "connect")) {
        usb_gadget_udc_start(udc);      /* unconditional */
        usb_gadget_connect(udc->gadget);
```

The 5.15 core tracks `udc->started` (a166p `core.c:1123`); 4.14 does not.
`dwc3_gadget_start()` requests its IRQ before checking for a bound driver (M62
`dwc3/gadget.c:2476-2491`). On an already started controller it frees the IRQ while
it is still in use, which logs "Trying to free already-free IRQ" and corrupts the
controller. The next unbind panics.

The fix is in `pullup()` (`src/gadget.c`):
- if the UDC `state` leaves "not attached" within 1 s, the host is already
  enumerating, so nothing is written;
- otherwise it writes the balanced pair `disconnect` (`udc_stop`) then `connect`
  (`udc_start`).

On M62 our configuration string also enables Samsung's symlink change mode, so
`UDC_store` raises the pullup itself and `soft_connect` is never needed.

### Samsung `f_ncm` destroys `android0` on a second NCM instance

```c
/* f_ncm.c create_terminal_attribute(), CONFIG_USB_ANDROID_SAMSUNG_COMPOSITE */
android_dev = create_function_device("terminal_version");  /* == android0 */
err = device_create_file(android_dev, &dev_attr_terminal_version);
if (err) {
        device_destroy(android_dev->class, android_dev->devt); /* android0! */
```

- `ncm_alloc_inst()` runs this on every NCM `mkdir`.
- Android's `g1` already has `ncm.0`, so a second instance fails with a duplicate
  `terminal_version`, and the error path destroys `android0`.
- The next NCM instance hits `kernel BUG at fs/sysfs/file.c:333`. The same freed device
  under Android's gadget is a panic waiting to happen.
- The code is in M62, exynos9820, exynos990, a015f/g and t295.

USB Arsenal's guard: when `android0/terminal_version` exists, no NCM directory is ever
created, not even for the capability probe. `check` flags NCM as unsafe and `tether`
uses RNDIS. Samsung's `rndis_alloc_inst` allocates everything per instance and is fine.

The real fix is a kernel one: drop the `device_destroy()` in that error path, since the
device belongs to Android's gadget, not to this NCM instance.


```

`docs/developer/research/02-android-usb-handoff.md`:

```md
# 02. Taking the controller from Android, and giving it back

The one thing USB Arsenal must never break: after any command, crash or kill, the
phone's own USB (ADB, MTP) has to come back. This doc is why the core does what it does.
Code: `src/gadget.c`.

## How Android drives its gadget

From AOSP `system/core/rootdir/init.usb.configfs.rc`:

- `on property:sys.usb.config=none && property:sys.usb.configfs=1` writes `none` to
  `g1/UDC`, stops adbd, sets `sys.usb.ffs.ready 0`, removes links `f1`..`f3`, sets
  `sys.usb.state`.
- Each mode (`adb`, `mtp`, `mtp,adb`, `rndis`, ...) links its functions into
  `g1/configs/b.1/fN` and writes `${sys.usb.controller}` to `g1/UDC`. The `*,adb` modes
  wait for `sys.usb.ffs.ready=1`, which is set once adbd is up.
- The framework (`UsbDeviceManager`) drives `sys.usb.config` directly on legacy devices,
  or calls the gadget HAL's `setCurrentFunctions` when one exists.
- The Pixel HAL (`hardware/google/pixel/usb`) hardcodes `/config/usb_gadget/g1/`, and its
  `MonitorFfs` writes the controller to `g1/UDC` whenever the adb endpoints appear. In
  other words, it rebinds on its own when adbd comes back.

Samsung's stock configfs adds `/sys/class/android_usb/android0/{functions,enable,state}`
on top. Its HAL writes `functions`, then `UDC`, then `enable`.

## What we do (own-gadget backend)

1. **Save first.** `sys.usb.config` (falling back to `persist.sys.usb.config`, then
   `mtp`), the UDC and the boot_id go into the handoff file. It is fsynced before
   anything changes hands.
2. **Release.** `setprop sys.usb.config none`, then wait for `sys.usb.state=none`
   (`UA_HANDOFF_TIMEOUT_MS`, 5 s). If `g1/UDC` is still bound after that, because a HAL
   ignored the property, write `none\n` to it ourselves.
3. **Bind ours.** Write the UDC, write `connect` to `soft_connect`, then wait for
   `state=configured` (`UA_ENUM_TIMEOUT_MS`, 3 s; a timeout only warns, since the cable
   may simply be unplugged).
4. **Give it back.** Unbind, remove everything, `setprop sys.usb.config <saved>`, wait for
   `sys.usb.state`. If `g1/UDC` is still empty, bind it by hand and `soft_connect`.

While we hold the controller, any attempt by `g1` to bind gets EBUSY from the UDC core.
Stopping adbd through the property also stops `MonitorFfs` from trying.

## Crash safety

- The handoff runs with SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGQUIT blocked (`ua_crit_enter`),
  so Ctrl-C cannot land between "Android released" and "ours bound".
- SIGHUP and SIGPIPE are ignored process-wide. Releasing Android stops adbd, which
  kills the `adb shell` the command may be running from. The handoff must finish anyway.
- `kill -9` still gets through. `usb-arsenal stop` reads the handoff file and finishes
  the job. It is idempotent and is a no-op when nothing is held.
- The workspace (`/data/local/USB-Arsenal`, `/var/lib/USB-Arsenal`) survives a reboot but the gadget does not. The handoff file carries
  the boot_id and is ignored (and deleted) on a different boot.

## Inside a container on Android

A Droidspaces (or chroot) rootfs has no `/system`, so `is_android()` is false, but the
kernel is Android's and `g1` still owns the controller. The core therefore asks the
kernel: `g1` plus `/sys/class/android_usb` means Android's gadget. Without the property
service there is nobody to ask, so the handoff unbinds `g1` by hand, records it as
`g1_udc` in the handoff file, and writes it back on teardown (plus `soft_connect`).
Verified on the a166p from its Ubuntu container.

## Off Android

There is no owner to negotiate with. If another configfs gadget holds the controller we
name it and refuse; we never unbind someone else's gadget. A legacy `g_*` module shows up
as EBUSY at bind, and the error says so.

## Open questions (verify on hardware)

- Samsung 5.x with its own USB HAL: does `setprop sys.usb.config` still drive it, or does
  the hand-unbind fallback carry the day?
- Pixel: does `MonitorFfs` try to rebind `g1` while we hold the controller (harmless
  EBUSY), and does it restore cleanly afterwards?

```

`docs/developer/research/03-mass-storage-cdrom.md`:

```md
# 03. Mass storage: booting an ISO, and the CD-ROM limits

Code: `src/gadgets/storage.c`. Kernel: `f_mass_storage.c`, `storage_common.c`.

## The mechanism

A LUN has `file`, `ro`, `removable`, `cdrom`, `nofua` (plus `inquiry_string` from 4.9 and
`forced_eject` from 6.6). Booting is entirely the host firmware's job. We only choose
how the image is presented:

- **CD-ROM** (`cdrom=1`): the gadget is a SCSI MMC drive with 2048-byte sectors.
  BIOS/UEFI boots a plain ISO9660/UDF image through El Torito. This is the only way a
  non-hybrid ISO can boot.
- **Disk** (`cdrom=0`): a 512-byte-sector disk. Isohybrid ISOs (most Linux ISOs) and
  pen-drive images boot this way.

## Choosing the mode (auto)

An MBR signature (`0x55AA` at offset 510) or a GPT header (`EFI PART` at offset 512) means
the image was built to boot as a disk. Isohybrid ISOs carry an MBR for exactly that
reason, and so do FAT superfloppies. A plain ISO9660 image starts with 32 KB of zeros, so
it gets CD-ROM mode.

DriveDroid did not detect anything: the user picked writable USB, read-only USB or
CD-ROM per image, and CD-ROM needed a patched kernel. Our auto mode makes that choice
from the image, and `--mode` overrides it.

## Limits that bite (every kernel surveyed)

- **Maximum size.** `fsg_lun_open` clamps a CD-ROM to `256*60*75 - 1` frames of 2048
  bytes, about 2.36 GB, and only logs it ("file too big"). See "Getting past 2.36 GB"
  below. We warn above the limit.
- **Minimum size.** 300 frames (600 KB). We refuse below that.
- **Read-only.** `cdrom=1` forces read-only.
- **READ TOC.** 4.9 to 4.19 answer format 0 only, with start_track at most 1
  (exynos990 f_mass_storage.c:1200). 5.10+ answer formats 0, 1 and 2 (a165f :1201).
  t385 has Samsung's raw format-2 TOC (`_SUPPORT_MAC_`). Some picky UEFI or Mac
  firmware may need 5.10+.
- **Single data track,** no audio.

## Getting past 2.36 GB

**Where the limit comes from.** `store_cdrom_address()` writes READ TOC and READ HEADER
addresses in MSF form when the host asks for it, and the minutes go in one byte. 256
minutes of 75 frames a second is the last lead-out it can describe, so `fsg_lun_open`
truncates the whole medium to fit. Data reads use READ(10) with a 32-bit LBA and never
needed the clamp. The clamp is in every tree we have, from 3.18 to the 6.6 GKI
(the Pixel 10 6.6 GKI tree, `drivers/usb/gadget/function/storage_common.c:247`), and in mainline.

**Upstream said no.** Dave Young sent a patch deleting the clamp in March 2015
(lkml 1503.0/06234). Alan Stern NAKed it: the gadget emulates a CD drive, not an image,
and a real drive with a 5 GB disc is a DVD drive with a different command set. He asked
for DVD emulation instead. Nobody upstreamed one.

**Downstream did it two ways.**
- Delete the clamp only (tjmnmk/gadget_cdrom `00-remove_iso_limit.patch`, an OpenBMC
  series from 2021). Reads work because they are LBA based; only an MSF TOC request
  gets a wrapped lead-out. The author calls it "not a good way".
- Real DVD-ROM emulation: PiKVM's `1102-pikvm-msd-dvd-support.patch` (Maxim Devaev,
  November 2025, in pikvm/packages `linux-rpi-pikvm`, KVMD 4.49+). Above the MSF limit
  the LUN sets `cd_as_dvd` and answers GET CONFIGURATION with the DVD-ROM profile, READ
  DISC INFORMATION, READ TRACK INFORMATION, READ DISC STRUCTURE (physical format), the
  0x2A capabilities mode page, and a fixed lead-out in the TOC. Images below the limit
  stay CD-ROMs. About 390 lines in `f_mass_storage.c` and `storage_common.[ch]`, GPL-2,
  no userspace interface change. Backported to 4.14 as `kernel-patches/4.14/0006`.

  First attempt on the S10: the clamp was gone (Fedora read all 4.9 GB of `sr0`, and its
  last sectors), WinPE booted, but Windows never mounted the disc. 4.14's READ TOC only
  answers format 0, and Windows asks for format 1 (multi-session info) to find the last
  session before mounting UDF. Upstream added formats 2 and 1 in 2022 (`89ada0fe669a`
  for Mac OS-X, then `3b91edd624ab` "Make CD-ROM emulation works with Windows OS"); 5.10+
  carry them, PiKVM's patch assumes them. They are now `4.14/0004` and `0005`, and
  PiKVM's patch applies as is on top as `0006`.

**Without a kernel patch: a 2048-byte disk (verified).** EDK2's `PartitionDxe/ElTorito.c`
parses El Torito on any block device whose block size divides 2048 ("If the ISO image has
been copied onto a different storage media"), and disk mode has no size clamp. Two steps,
both tested on the S10 (stock f_mass_storage) with a 4.9 GB Sergei Strelec WinPE 11 ISO
and an MSI laptop (UEFI):

1. The ISO file in plain disk mode (512-byte sectors): the firmware listed it, the Windows
   boot manager loaded `boot.wim` and WinPE reached the desktop. But WinPE never mounted
   the UDF volume, so everything outside `boot.wim` was missing. UDF counts its anchor
   at block 256 in units of the sector size, so on a 512-byte disk it looks at 128 KiB
   instead of 512 KiB. Linux retries with 2048 and mounts it; Windows does not.
2. The ISO behind a loop device with 2048-byte blocks (`LOOP_SET_BLOCK_SIZE`, 4.14+),
   that loop device in disk mode: `fsg_lun_open` takes the `S_ISBLK` path and reports
   2048-byte sectors (Fedora: `LOG-SEC 2048`, UDF found on the first scan). WinPE booted
   and mounted `USB_STRELEC` (4.56 GB, UDF) with all its programs.

SELinux: the kernel's storage thread must read the loop node. On the S10, `u:r:kernel:s0`
has no `read` on `loop_device` (only on Samsung's `vendor_block_device` and two others),
so the host saw "Unrecovered read error" on sector 0 until
`allow kernel loop_device blk_file { open read getattr ioctl }` was loaded
(`ksud sepolicy patch`; a module ships it as `sepolicy.rule`).

`storage --mode dvd` does this (`loop_attach()` in `src/gadgets/storage.c`), with
`LO_FLAGS_AUTOCLEAR` so the loop detaches when f_mass_storage closes it, and checks the
SELinux rule through selinuxfs `access` before serving.

Why Droidspaces' trick does not cover this: before loop-mounting a rootfs image it
relabels the **image file** to `vold_data_file` (`src/mount.c`), which satisfies the
kernel's read of the backing file, the same check `selinux_fix()` answers with
`media_rw_data_file`. Our denial is the kernel reading the **loop device node** (class
`blk_file`), which Droidspaces never meets because its `mount()` opens the node from its
own permissive domain. No stock label is readable that way on both test phones: as
`blk_file`, `loop_device` and `vold_device` are readable on the a166p but not on the S10,
and `vold_data_file`, `media_rw_data_file`, `app_data_file`, `system_data_file`,
`block_device` and `dm_device` on neither. So the node keeps its label and the module
ships the rule. Both SELinux steps are skipped when selinuxfs is not mounted, since
labels stay on disk after SELinux is turned off.

Also: toybox `losetup` has no block-size option and refuses paths over 64 bytes, and with
`loop.max_part=7` a loop's minor is `n * 8`, so a fallback `mknod` must read the
minor from sysfs.

The old fallback still works everywhere: an NTFS disk image (Rufus, woeusb) plus
UEFI:NTFS. A FAT32 copy fails because `install.wim` is over 4 GB.

## Write order

`cdrom` and `ro` return EBUSY while a file is open (`_fsg_store_ro`,
storage_common.c:379-383), so the order is: `removable=1`, `cdrom`, `ro`, then `file`
last. To change a live LUN, eject first.

## SELinux: the kernel reads the image, not us

f_mass_storage reads the backing file from a kernel thread, so SELinux checks
`u:r:kernel:s0` against the file's label. On the a166p (enforcing), the policy allows
`media_rw_data_file`, `vold_data_file`, `fuse`, `app_data_file` and `system_data_file`
(read and write, checked through selinuxfs `access`). It denies `tmpfs` and
`unlabeled`, which covers a container's `/tmp` and its ext4 loop rootfs. The denial is
dontaudit'ed, so the only symptom is the host logging "Unrecovered read error" on sector
0 of a disk of the right size. DriveDroid never hit this because its images lived on
`/sdcard`.

`storage start` does not trust a label list: wherever SELinux is running (selinuxfs
mounted), it asks `/sys/fs/selinux/access` whether the kernel's own context, read from
kthreadd's `/proc/2/attr/current`, may read (and for `rw`, write) the image's label.
- On Android a denied image is relabelled to `u:object_r:media_rw_data_file:s0`
  (setxattr, logged); if that fails it warns and suggests `/sdcard` or `/data`. Verified
  on the a166p: `shell_data_file` and `unlabeled` images were relabelled, a
  `media_rw_data_file` one was left alone.
- Other distros have no label every policy grants, so a denial is a warning naming the
  label (relabel with `chcon`, or move the file). Fedora's targeted policy lets
  `kernel_t` read `user_home_t`, `tmp_t`, `user_tmp_t` and `var_lib_t` files and
  `fixed_disk_device_t` / `removable_device_t` block devices, so nothing is touched there.
- A block device passed as IMAGE gets the same query as class `blk_file` and is
  refused when denied, since no stock label is readable everywhere. On the a166p
  `/dev/block/dm-56` (`dm_device`, the f2fs `/data`) was refused that way; with SELinux
  permissive it was served and the host's f2fs found the live filesystem mid-checkpoint
  (orphan and quota errors) and would not mount it.
- A denial only counts when enforced: SELinux permissive (`enforce` 0) or a permissive
  domain (flag 1 in the `access` reply) passes, since the policy answers the same either
  way.
- In a PID namespace `/proc/2` is not kthreadd; on Android the query falls back to
  `u:r:kernel:s0`, elsewhere it is skipped. Verified on the a166p: before the
relabel the host saw an unreadable disk; afterwards it read the FAT16 label.

## Ejecting and hot-swapping

- `file` takes `"\n"` to eject. A zero-length write never reaches the store function.
- If the host has locked the medium (PREVENT ALLOW MEDIUM REMOVAL), writing `file`
  returns EBUSY (storage_common.c:441). `forced_eject` (6.6) clears the lock first, so we
  use it when it exists.
- `storage start` on a live LUN, in the same mode, ejects and loads the new image without
  touching the UDC. The host sees a medium change, like swapping a disc.
- Two cases take a rebind instead (a short re-enumeration; the other functions come back
  with it):
  - **Disk to CD-ROM or back.** This is a different SCSI device type, which a host only
    reads at enumeration.
  - **A host lock.** Linux locks a CD-ROM or removable disk it has open, so before 6.6
    (no `forced_eject`) the eject returns EBUSY. Every reset or disconnect clears
    `prevent_medium_removal` (a166p `f_mass_storage.c:2421`), so after the unbind the
    eject is retried for up to 3 s.

  Verified on the a166p against a Fedora host: a disk-to-CD-ROM switch and a
  CD-ROM-to-CD-ROM swap both went through the rebind, with the CD-ROM and HID intact.

```

`docs/developer/research/04-tethering.md`:

```md
# 04. Tethering

Code: `src/gadgets/tether.c`, with `src/net/` lifted from Droidspaces.

## Which function

- **NCM** is the default. It is built into every defconfig surveyed (including stock
  exynos and GKI 5.15/6.6), and Windows 11, macOS and Linux all have a class driver for
  it.
- **RNDIS** is the fallback, used when NCM is missing or `--rndis` is passed. It is
  gone from GKI after 5.10. Windows only loads its driver unprompted when the device
  carries Microsoft OS descriptors with compatible ID `RNDIS` / `5162001`, so
  `rndis_os_desc()` writes `os_desc/use`, `b_vendor_code=0xcd`, `qw_sign=MSFT100`, and
  links the config into `os_desc/`.
- The device class is Misc/IAD (0xEF/0x02/0x01) for every composite, which is what
  Windows wants for an NCM or RNDIS function inside one.
- MACs are fixed per device (FNV hash of `ro.serialno` or `/etc/machine-id`, locally
  administered). With random MACs Windows adds "Ethernet 7, 8, 9..." on every start.

## The network side (daemon)

After bind:
1. Read the function's `ifname` (old kernels report `(unnamed net_device)` until bound).
2. Bring the link up and add 192.168.42.129/24 (`--address`). The host is offered the
   next address by `ds_dhcp_server_start`, a single-lease DHCP server on an AF_PACKET
   socket bound to the interface.
3. Save `ip_forward`, then set it to 1.
4. NAT: `ds_ipt_ensure_masquerade(subnet)`, plus FORWARD and INPUT ACCEPT on the
   interface and an MSS clamp. These go through the raw ip_tables socket first and fall
   back to the iptables binary. Droidspaces' safety contract still holds: never flush,
   never change a policy, only insert rules scoped to our interface and subnet.
5. Uplink (`ua_find_uplink`): `--upstream` if given, else Android's netd
   default-network rule, else the main table's default route, else a name scan
   (`wlan*`, `eth*`, `v4-*`, `rmnet*`, ...).
6. Android only: `to <subnet> lookup main` (priority 6090) so replies find our connected
   route, and `from <subnet> lookup <uplink table>` (6100) so the host's traffic leaves
   through the uplink. Both are below Android's VPN rules (10000+). Plain Linux needs
   neither, because the main table already routes everything.

The daemon runs Droidspaces' route monitor (rtnetlink events plus a 1.5 s heartbeat): it
re-asserts forwarding, puts back rules netd flushed, and moves the FROM rule when the
default network moves between Wi-Fi and mobile data.

On SIGTERM: stop DHCP, remove the MASQUERADE and ACCEPT rules and the policy rules.
Forwarding stays on, on Android and Linux alike: a Droidspaces container or Android's
own tethering may need it by then. The MSS clamp stays: it is not scoped to us, and
Droidspaces inserts the identical rule.

## Lessons from the NetHunter `usbtethering` script

The script (`ravindu644/Nethunter_APK_KernelSU@a488e77`, `NetHunter/assets/scripts/bin/usbtethering`)
does not build a gadget. It expects `rndis0` to exist. Its sequence (flush, add an
address, link up, add a route, `ip rule ... iif usb lookup <upstream>`, FORWARD and
MASQUERADE, `ip_forward=1`, ISC dhcpd inside a chroot) is the right shape. Three things
were not copied:
- The route goes into whatever table the *first* `ip rule` line names. On many Android
  versions that line is `local`. We find the uplink table from netd's rule instead.
- Teardown writes `ip_forward=0`, which also breaks Android's own tethering.
- It needs dhcpd from a Kali chroot. Ours is built in.

## Known limits

- The kernel creates `usb0` in the initial network namespace. A container with its own
  (Droidspaces NAT or gateway mode) cannot see it, so `tether start` refuses with that
  reason and removes the function it added. `--no-net` still works there, and the
  network side has to run in the host namespace.
- A composition change while tethering (for example `storage start` adding the drive)
  rebinds the gadget. If the kernel re-registers the netdev, the address and the DHCP
  socket go stale; `tether stop` + `tether start` fixes it. This is on the roadmap.
- IPv6: NAT66 after Droidspaces (ULA `fd75:7361::/64`, RAs from `ra.c`, ip6tables
  MASQUERADE when `ds_ipt6_available()`); IPv4 only on kernels without the nat table.

```

`docs/developer/research/05-netns.md`:

```md
# 05. Getting the tether interface into the tool's network namespace

Research of 2026-10-18, on the kernel trees listed in
[01-kernel-survey.md](01-kernel-survey.md) (the a166p tree keeps its kernel under
`kernel-5.15/`). The problem: run from a container with its own network namespace
(Droidspaces NAT or gateway mode), `tether start` cannot see `usb0`.

## Facts

- **usb0 is always born in init_net.** `gether_setup_name_default()` calls
  `alloc_etherdev` with no `dev_net_set` (a166p `u_ether.c:825-866`, also t385 :1838,
  M62 :1106, p10 :819). Which netns the writer of the configfs files is in plays no part.
- **Registered once per function instance,** at the first bind
  (`if (!ncm_opts->bound)`, a166p `f_ncm.c:1460-1467`; rndis :704-709). It survives UDC
  unbind/rebind and is unregistered only when the function directory is removed
  (`gether_cleanup`, `f_ncm.c:1622-1633`).
  - **Exception: M62 4.14 with `CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_UEVENT`.** `ncm_unbind` frees it
    (`f_ncm.c:1833-1853`) and rndis reallocates it (`f_rndis.c:1040-1060`), so every
    rebind makes a fresh usb0 in init_net.
- **Nothing blocks a move.** There is no `NETIF_F_NETNS_LOCAL` and no `rtnl_link_ops` in
  u_ether on any version, so `ip link set usb0 netns X` works.
- **The move must be asked from usb0's current netns.** `rtnl_setlink` looks the device
  up in `sock_net(skb->sk)` (5.15 `rtnetlink.c:3107`), then checks CAP_NET_ADMIN over
  the target (`rtnl_link_get_net_capable`, :2349). It is the same on 3.18 (:1510-1521).
  `IFLA_TARGET_NETNSID` does not change where the device is looked up.
- **Container exit is safe.** `default_device_exit` moves a device without
  `rtnl_link_ops` back to init_net (a166p `dev.c:11558-11590`) instead of deleting it.
  Removing the function while usb0 is in another netns is also fine.

## Getting a handle on init_net from inside the container

| Way | Works |
|---|---|
| `/proc/<host pid>/ns/net` | No: host pids are invisible from a separate pid ns |
| `/proc/1/ns/net` when the pid ns is shared (chroot, Droidspaces host-net mode) | Yes |
| `IFLA_NET_NS_PID`, `pidfd_open` | No: pids resolve in the caller's pid ns |
| `RTM_GETNSID`, nsfs ioctls | No: ids or user namespaces, never a net ns fd |
| An fd passed over a filesystem-path unix socket | Yes |
| Droidspaces socketd | No: abstract socket (per netns), no netns opcodes |
| A host netns file bind-mounted into the container | Yes, but it gives container root all of host networking |

## Approaches, ranked

1. **Droidspaces moves it (host side).** The monitor already runs in init_net, already
   opens the container netns fd, and already re-checks every heartbeat
   (`ds_net_macvlan_wire`). A config option such as `usb_net_passthrough=usb0,ncm0,rndis0`
   would make the heartbeat move any matching link in with one RTM_NEWLINK carrying
   `IFLA_NET_NS_FD`. The heartbeat also catches M62's re-registration and a container
   restart. Least privilege; nothing new is exposed to the container.
2. **USB Arsenal moves it, given a host netns handle.** Open `/proc/self/ns/net` as
   `self`, `setns()` into the host netns, open a netlink socket, send RTM_NEWLINK
   (`ifi_index` = usb0, `IFLA_NET_NS_FD` = `self`), then `setns(self)` back. This is the
   pattern of `ds_netns_link_up` in Droidspaces `network.c:206-248`, and `ds_nl_rename`
   in our `netlink.c` is the request template. The handle comes from `/proc/1/ns/net` in
   a chroot, or from an opt-in bind mount (e.g. `/run/host-netns`) in a container. It
   must be redone after every rebind on M62-style kernels.
3. Do all of the networking from init_net (setns for the whole daemon). Not
   recommended: NAT would land in Android's tables, next to netd, and state would leak
   out of the container.

## What each setup needs

- **Plain host (Android or Linux):** nothing. usb0 is already in the tool's netns.
- **Chroot sharing the pid ns:** approach 2 with `/proc/1/ns/net`, entirely inside USB
  Arsenal.
- **Droidspaces with its own pid and net ns:** approach 1 in Droidspaces. USB Arsenal
  waits a few seconds for the link to appear, then fails with "enable Droidspaces USB
  passthrough".
- **docker / lxc on a board:** the host moves it
  (`ip link set usb0 netns $(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Pid}}' c)`, or LXC
  `lxc.net.N.type=phys`, `lxc.net.N.link=usb0`). USB Arsenal prints that command.

Moving usb0 into the container means the container's own uplink (for Droidspaces
gateway mode, the OpenWrt container) is what the host gets NATed through.

```

`docs/developer/research/06-app-state.md`:

```md
# 06. The app's state: map, audit, and the unified architecture

Written 2026-10-24 at commit `6ac7fba`, against the Kotlin under
`Android/app/src/main/java/com/usbarsenal/app/` and the C in `src/`. The reasons: the user saw
Home say "storage off" under a bottom bar that said "bound" while the PC had a drive on LUN0;
Settings and other screens draw their controls only once root has answered; and every setup
(the picks, the tether plan, the HID interval, the controller) lives only in the app's
`SharedPreferences`, so clearing the app's data loses it all.

Part 1 is the map. Part 2 is the audit (what the parallel scan found, verified, and what it
cleared). Part 3 is the architecture that fixes it.

## Part 1: the map

### 1.1 Navigation

- **The back stack** is `stack: List<Step>` in `App()` (`ui/Setup.kt`), `rememberSaveable`,
  seeded with `HOME` when prefs `setup/done` is true, else `WELCOME`. `push` and `pop` go
  through `show()`, which refuses a second change while one is in flight (`showing`), clears
  focus, waits two frames (so the pressed key is seen lifting), then sets `back` and `stack`.
  `Redraw` (`ui/Parts.kt`) paints the new screen in four bands and keeps the old one composed
  underneath until the last band; it only swallows touches on it.
- **Steps:** `WELCOME, ROOT, CONTROLLER, CHECK, INSTALL, HOME, LOG, SETTINGS, FONTS, STORAGE,
  TETHER, HID, KEYS, QUACKY, IDENTITY`. Setup is `stack.first() != HOME`. `home()` writes
  `setup/done` and resets the stack to `[HOME]`.
- **Focus return:** each opener carries `Modifier.opener(id)`; `ReturnFocus.focused` is the id
  holding focus now, `openers[i]` (also `rememberSaveable`) is the id that held focus on
  `stack[i]` when `stack[i+1]` was pushed, and a pop sets `ReturnFocus.returning` so that
  opener asks for focus once. `Sheet` does the same for the key that opened it.
- **What survives what:**

| Lifetime | State |
|---|---|
| Rotation (Activity recreated, process alive) | everything: `rememberSaveable` and every process object |
| Process death (stack restored, objects gone) | `stack`, `openers`, each screen's `rememberSaveable` (`lun`, `nextMode`, `creating`, `tab`, `full`, sheet `asking`, `picked` on Controller). Lost: `Setup.*` (root, check, report, install log and phase), `Gadget.*` (status, caps, profile, busy, fault, cli, `startedX`, `binds`), `Controller.udcs`, `DaemonLog`, `Picks`/`TetherSetup`/`HidSetup` until some screen calls `load` |
| A data wipe or reinstall | the prefs below; nothing on the backend side records a setup |

- **Who loads the prefs objects:** `Picks.load`, `TetherSetup.load`, `HidSetup.load` run in
  `HomeScreen`'s `LaunchedEffect(Unit)`; `StorageScreen` also calls `Picks.load`, `TetherScreen`
  `TetherSetup.load`, `HidScreen` `HidSetup.load`. Each is guarded by a `loaded` flag. The first
  frame of any of these screens composes before the effect runs. `Controller.load` runs in
  `MainActivity.onCreate`, so the pick is there before the first command.
- **Launch effects in `App()`:** on a `HOME` stack, `Controller.refresh()` (one root read) and,
  with several controllers and no pick, a push of `CONTROLLER`; the bind thud watches
  `Gadget.binds`.

### 1.2 State holders

| Holder | Lives | Written by | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Gadget.status: GadgetStatus?` | process | `Gadget.refresh()` only: every `PollStatus` loop (2 s, while STARTED) and `Gadget.run` after each command; set to `null` on any failed read | Home rows and bar, `pending`, `apply`, `isOn`, Storage `live`/`served`/`shownLive`, Tether chain and counters, Hid nodes, KbdMouse writers (through its own `hid` copy), Identity `known`/`bound`, Settings' controller note |
| `Gadget.caps: Capabilities?` | process | `CheckScreen` on success; `Gadget.loadOnce()` (`check --json` on the change lane) when null; Settings sets it to null after a controller pick | `rowLines` (unavailable rows), `has`, `tetherFunction`, Tether segment `enabled`, `HidSetup.fixed` |
| `Gadget.profile: Map` | process | `loadOnce()` when empty; `reloadProfile()` after identity commands; Settings on every visit | `tetherFunction`, Tether placeholders, Settings' Identity row, Identity `active`/`chosen` seed |
| `Gadget.busy: Busy?` | process | `Gadget.run` (set before the command, cleared after its post-read) | Home's bar and rows, `canApply`, every DIP's `enabled`, Identity `canApply` |
| `Gadget.fault: Fault?` | process | `Gadget.run` on failure, `Storage`'s picker refusal; cleared on the next `run` and when Log opens | the Fault line under the row or on the screen that owns `fn` |
| `Gadget.binds`, `fails`, `wasBound`, `finished` | process | `run`, `refresh`, `settle` | the thud in `App`, Pin in the bottom bar |
| `Gadget.backend: Backend?` | process | Home's `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` once per Home composition | `holds()` (DIPs, Apply), the attention key, the NoRoot shade; Settings reads its own copy |
| `Gadget.startedPicks / startedPlan / startedInterval`, `applying` | process | `flip` on a successful start (the setup taken when the start was sent), `apply` at its end, `forgetStart` on stop, stop all, a failed apply | `pending`, `apply` (`before`), `discard`, Storage's `shownLive` |
| `Gadget.cli` | process | `run` | Log's CLI tab |
| `Picks.all` | prefs `storage/picks` (tab-separated `lun mode path` lines) | Storage's file rows, Create, eject, mode segments; `discard` | Home's switch (`startable`), `setupArgs`, `pending`, Storage's strip and Drive |
| `TetherSetup.plan` | prefs `tether` (8 keys) | Tether's rows and sheets; the gateway auto-off on leave and on "Droidspaces not installed"; `discard` | `setupArgs`, `pending`, Tether's rows and chain fallbacks |
| `HidSetup.interval`, `speed`, `natural`; `keyboardFixed` (process) | prefs `hid`; `keyboardFixed` from every status read | Hid's steppers, KbdMouse's Speed and Natural scroll | `setupArgs`, `pending`, `fixed`, the report scaling |
| `IdentitySetup.chosen`, `edited`, `undo` | process, seeded from `Gadget.profile` | Identity picks, edits, apply, discard | Identity's panel, rows, sheet |
| `Controller.picked`, `udcs` | prefs `usb/udc`; `udcs` process | `Controller.refresh` (clears a pick no longer listed or when one controller), Controller step, Settings' choice | `udcFlag` on every command and read, Settings' USB section, setup's step count |
| `Setup.root`, `check`, `report`, `staged`, `log`, `phase`, `retries` | process | Root, Check, Install screens | the same screens on a revisit |
| `Switches.motion`, `haptics` | prefs `switches` | Settings | the theme, every loop, `Haptics.allowed()` |
| `DaemonLog.lines`, `offset` | process | Log's Daemon tab | Log |
| `SheetsOpen.count`, `ReturnFocus`, `Stick.sink` | process | `Sheet`, `opener`, KbdMouse | `Screen`, `opener`, `MainActivity` |
| Per-screen `remember`: Storage `dir`, `files`, `free`, `reload`; Tether `ds`, `choosing`; Settings `backend`, `daemon`, `linked`, `changed`, `fault`, `choosingUdc`; Identity `dir`, `profiles`, `sheet`; KbdMouse `hid`, `buttons`, `mods`, `stick` | screen | their screen | their screen |

### 1.3 Root calls

`Root` is one `RootExec`, `su --mount-master -c`. Three lanes: `read` (own shell, 15 s
default, never waits), `change` (one `Mutex`, 30 s default), `stream` (a shell kept open
until closed). Every call starts its own `sh`, prints its pid first, and a timeout or cancel
kills the whole tree. Reads of the backend carry `UA_NO_PROXY=1` so they never go through a
daemon and never show up in its log.

| Call | Lane, timeout | Caller | In flight | Failed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `status --json` | read, 15 s | `PollStatus` every 2 s on Home, Storage, Tether, Hid, Identity, Keys + mouse; `Gadget.run` after each command | nothing shown | `status = null`: Home idle, bar "Port with Android", rows off, Storage `live` empty, Identity `known` false |
| `check --json` | change, 30 s | `loadOnce()` on every `PollStatus` mount while `caps == null` | rows show as available (`caps == null` counts as yes) | `caps` stays null, retried at the next screen |
| `check` then `check --json` (staged binary) | read, 30 s | Check screen | the shell types; `Recheck`/`Next` dead until the report has typed | the report shows what printed and why it stopped |
| `identity show` | read, 15 s | `loadOnce()` while `profile` empty; `reloadProfile()`; Settings on each visit | Settings' Identity row says `Built-in` | `profile` stays as it was (`reloadProfile`), or empty (`loadOnce`) |
| `id -u; su -v` | read, 15 s | Root screen | the shell waits on `su` | the denial prints, NoRoot shade |
| `/sys/class/udc/*` list | read, 15 s | `Controller.refresh` from `App`, Root, Controller | setup's steps show 3 | nothing changes, nothing asked |
| `test -x …; module.prop; version; md5sum` | read, 15 s | `backendState` from Home once, Settings each visit, after install | Home: no attention key, DIPs held (`holds()` true while null); Settings: Reinstall dead | `NO_ROOT` on 127 or a timeout with no `bin` |
| `cat .daemon_mode`, `test -L link` | read | Settings each visit | both DIPs disabled | both DIPs stay disabled |
| `echo N > .daemon_mode`, `ln -sfn`/`rm -rf system` | change | Settings | nothing | Fault under the switches, shake |
| `d show --json` (Droidspaces) | read | Tether each visit | Gateway row shown (`ds == null` counts as installed), Container row says the saved name | `running = null`: Container says the saved name, the sheet says it cannot read |
| `mkdir -p; readlink -f`, `stat` per file, `stat -f` | read | Storage on open and after Create; Identity on open and after a save | `files == null`: no "No image loaded", no file rows | empty list |
| `stat -c '%d %i'` | read | `realPath` after the picker | nothing | the pick is refused with a Fault |
| `truncate -s`, `rm -f`, `printf > tmp && mv` | change | Create (sparse), Create cleanup, profile writes | Create key disabled while the job runs | Fault inside the sheet |
| `dd if=/dev/zero` | stream | Create (full) | Cells progress from `stat -c %s` every 500 ms | the short file is removed |
| `dd of=/dev/hidgN bs=8|4` | stream | KbdMouse, one per node, restarted after 1 s when it dies | nothing | reports dropped |
| `tail -n 200|-c +N -f` | stream | Log's Daemon tab | lines append | one `[-] Cannot follow` line |
| `: > log; rm -f .old`, `stat -c %s` | read | Log Clear and tab leave | | |
| `cat profile`, `identity generate tmp --force && cat` | read / change | Identity edit and create | Save key disabled while writing | Fault in the sheet |
| `usb-arsenal <args>` (every command below) | change, 30 s | `Gadget.run` only | `busy`: the bar inverted with the words from `says()`, the row says `starting`/`stopping` and the typed line, every DIP and Apply held | `fault` under the row or the bar, `fails++`, stderr's last line or `[-] Timed out (30s)` |

### 1.4 Command round trips

Every change goes `UI event → Gadget.run(fn, args) → Root.change("<UA> --udc X args") → the
binary (relayed to a daemon when one listens, else direct) → refresh() → status`. The
screens read the field named in the last column.

| UI event | Command | C entry | `status --json` field | Reader |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Home Storage DIP on | `storage start [--lun N --mode M PATH]…` from `Picks.all` | `storage.c` `do_start`: prepare every image, one begin/commit; or an in-place `lun_load` swap when one image goes on a live LUN of the same type | `storage[]` (`lun`, `file` as the kernel shows it, `mode` resolved, `access`) | Home row lines, Storage `live`, `served`, `shownLive` |
| Home Storage DIP off | `storage stop` | `do_stop`: remove the function, commit (teardown when nothing is left) | `storage: []`, `bound` | the same |
| Storage Back, Apply | `storage eject --lun N` per dropped loaded LUN, then one `storage start` per changed live LUN, then one for new LUNs (`storageApply`), or `storage stop` with no picks | `do_eject` (in place; before 6.6 a host lock makes it rebind), `do_start` | `storage[]` | Storage, Home |
| Home Tether DIP on | `tether start --ncm|--rndis [--gateway C [--gateway-iface I]] | [--no-net] | [--address A] [--dns D] [--upstream U]` | `tether.c` `do_start`: function (NCM unless unsafe or missing), MACs, commit, fork the network side, wait for its verdict | `tether` (`function`, `iface`, `running`, `address`, `ipv6`, `upstream`, `gateway*`, `tx/rx_bytes`) | Home row, Tether chain, counters |
| Tether DIP off, Apply | `tether stop`; Apply is `stop` then `start` | `do_stop` | `tether: null` | the same |
| Home HID DIP on | `hid start [--interval N]` (omitted at 4 or when fixed) | `hid.c` `do_start`: both functions, descriptors, `interval` when the attribute exists, commit, `apply_perm` | `hid[]` (`function`, `node`, `interval`) | Home row, Hid card line, KbdMouse writers, `keyboardFixed` |
| HID DIP off, Apply | `hid stop`; Apply is `stop` then `start` | `do_stop` | `hid: []` | the same |
| Stop all | `stop` | `main.c` `cmd_stop`: kill the tether daemon, `ua_gadget_teardown`, hand back | `bound: 0`, everything empty | the bar, every row |
| Identity pick or Apply | `identity set PATH` / `identity unset` | `config.c` `do_set` (symlink or copy, replug if live) / `do_unset` | none: `identity show` is re-read | Identity, Settings |
| Identity Create | `identity generate tmp --force` then the app's own write | `config.c` generate | none | Identity's list |

What `status --json` cannot say: what was asked for (the picked path and `auto`, the plan,
the interval when the kernel has no control), who started it, and whether it is what the
screen is set up to start. Those live only in the process-only `startedX` and the prefs.

### 1.5 The C side of a status read

`cmd_status` (`src/main.c`) opens the gadget (`ua_gadget_open`: configfs, the UDC from the
handoff record when one is held, else `--udc` or the only one), reads the UDC state, and
`live = ua_gadget_live()` = the handoff record exists for this boot and `usb_arsenal/UDC` is
non-empty. With `live` it prints each function's part; without it the arrays are empty and
`tether` is `null`. `ua_status_storage` prints one object per existing `lun.N` with `file`,
`cdrom` and `ro` as the kernel holds them (a dvd LUN names its loop's `backing_file`), so an
ejected LUN is `{"file": ""}`. `ua_status_hid` lists each linked function with its node found
by major:minor (up to 2 s) and the `interval` attribute (`-1` without one). `ua_status_tether`
reads `Net/tether.info`, written by the network side, and the netdev counters.

Windows a reader can land in, all inside one command on the change lane:
- `begin` unbinds the UDC first, so until `commit` rebinds, `bound` is 0 and every array is
  empty. A replug (identity set, a LUN of a new type, an eject the host blocks before 6.6, HID
  or tether start on a live gadget) spends a few seconds here.
- `lun_load` ejects before it loads, so a swap in place has a moment of `bound: 1` with that
  LUN's `file` empty.
- `do_start`'s failure path on an existing function ejects every LUN it reached and commits,
  which leaves `bound: 1` with empty drives for good.

## Part 2: the audit

Seven agents read the code in parallel (sync layer, navigation, storage, tether, HID,
identity and settings, design). Every finding below was checked against the code by hand;
four are proved by `Android/app/src/test/java/com/usbarsenal/app/ui/AuditTest.kt`, which
fails on the audited code and passes once the fix is in. One agent claim was wrong and is
listed under "checked, not bugs".

### 2.1 The storage report

With a fresh status, the taps in the report (two LUNs up, one pick dropped in Storage, Back,
Apply) issue one command, `storage eject --lun 1`, and no snapshot of that command reads as
"bound with no images": `do_eject` leaves LUN0 alone, and during its rebind path the UDC is
unbound, so `bound` is 0. The screen the user saw therefore came from one of three paths,
all real:

1. **A late poll kept a mid-apply snapshot.** When `live` showed LUN0 empty (the host had
   ejected it, or its pick differed from `startedPicks` by path or mode), `storageApply`
   issues two steps, `eject --lun 1` then `start --lun 0`. Between them the kernel is bound
   with every LUN empty for hundreds of milliseconds. A poll that started in that window and
   returned after the second step's own post-read overwrites it, because `Gadget.refresh()`
   writes `status` with no ordering (`ui/Gadget.kt:143`). Home then shows `idle`, the storage
   row off, the bar `BOUND`, until the next poll. The PC keeps LUN0. This matches the report
   word for word and explains why it did not reproduce.
2. **Apply decided from a null status.** A failed read sets `status = null`; Apply then sees
   `live = []`, drops the eject and re-sends the kept pick as a `start`, which the kernel
   takes as an in-place reload of LUN0 (or a full replug when the host holds a lock). LUN1 keeps
   serving while the app has forgotten it. Proved by `applyWithUnknownStatusChangesNothing`.
3. **A bound gadget with empty drives reads as off.** `isOn(STORAGE)` is "a LUN holds a
   medium", so a linked, bound `mass_storage.ua` with every LUN ejected (a CLI eject, a host
   eject, `do_start`'s failure path) shows the row off and the bar bound, and `pending()` is
   false so Apply can never reach `storage stop`. Proved by `emptyDrivesAreStillOn`.

The architecture in Part 3 closes all three: status reads are ordered and a read that began
during a command is dropped; Apply is a backend command that reads the kernel itself; and
"on" means "the function is linked", as the backend already defines it.
