```patch
+static int do_get_configuration(struct fsg_common *common,
+			struct fsg_buffhd *bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+	u8		*buf0 = buf;
+	int		len;
+	int		profile;
+	int		rt; /* Request type */
+	int		starting; /* Feature code */
+
+	/*
+	 * The standard prescribes to return disabled profiles
+	 * MMC_PROFILE_NONE when we have no medium, but it seems
+	 * it is enough to make unknown_cmnd in do_scsi_command().
+	 */
+	if (curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/* Big images will be handled as DVD */
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM;
+	} else {
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM;
+	}
+
+	/*
+	 * RT == 0x00 - Return all features since starting;
+	 * RT == 0x01 - Same but filtered by Current bit (all in our case);
+	 * RT == 0x02 - Return only header and zero or one supported feature;
+	 * RT == 0x03 - Reserved, but we'll handle it as 0x00 for paranoia;
+	 * ... So we have only one special case for 0x02.
+	 */
+	rt = common->cmnd[1] & 0x03;
+	starting = get_unaligned_be16(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 256); /* This should be enough for our all features */
+	/* Allocation Length in buf[0,1,2,3] will be calculated later */
+	put_unaligned_be16(profile, &buf[6]);
+	buf += 8;
+
+#define NEED_REPORT(feature) \
+		(rt == 0x02 ? (starting == feature) : (starting <= feature))
+
+	/* Profile List feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0)) {
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0 for the feature */
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length for two profiles */
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM, &buf[4]);
+		buf[6] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM);
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM, &buf[8]);
+		buf[10] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM);
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Core feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0001)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0001, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(1, &buf[4]); /* Phy = SCSI Family */
+		buf[8] = 0x01;		/* Device Busy Class Events = 1 */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Morphing feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0002)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0002, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Removable Medium feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0003)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0003, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x20 | 0x19;	/* Tray mechanism, Load|Eject|Lock */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Random Readable feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0010)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0010, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(2048, &buf[4]); /* Logical Block Size */
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0, no Blocking size presented */
+		buf[10] = 0x01;		/* RW Error Recovery Mode Page */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* MultiRead feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001D)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001D, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* CD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001E)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001E, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x03;		/* C2|CD-Text */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* DVD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001F)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001F, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x01;		/* MULTI110 */
+		buf[6] = 0x01;		/* Dual-R */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Power Management feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0100)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0100, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* Timeout feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0105)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0105,&buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Real Time Streaming feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0107)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0107, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x10 | 0x03;	/* Version = 4, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x0F;		/* SCS|MP2A|WSPD|SW */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+#undef NEED_REPORT
+
+	len = buf - buf0;
+	/* Put len minus the size of data length field (be32) */
+	put_unaligned_be32(len - 4, &buf0[0]);
+	return len;
+}
+
+static int do_read_disc_information(struct fsg_common *common,
+			struct fsg_buffhd *bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/*
+	 * (common->cmnd[1] & 0x07) contains Data Type, but it is safe
+	 * to ignore it and always return Data Type = 0 in buf[2]
+	 * for the Standard Disc Information.
+	 */
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 34);
+	put_unaligned_be16(32, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 0x0E;	/* Last session complete, disc finalized */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* First track on disc */
+	buf[4] = 1;	/* Number of sessions */
+	buf[5] = 1;	/* First track of last session */
+	buf[6] = 1;	/* Last track of last session */
+	buf[7] = 0x20;	/* Unrestricted use */
+	buf[8] = 0;	/* For CD should be 0, for DVD is inapplicable */
+
+	if (!curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/*
+		 * For CD if the disc is complete, both should be 0xFF.
+		 * For DVD it's inapplicable and shall be set to 0.
+		 * buf[16,17,18,19] - Last Session Lead-in Start Time.
+		 * buf[20,21,22,23] - Last Possible Start Time
+		 *                    for Start of Lead-out.
+		 */
+		memset(&buf[16], 0, 8);
+	}
+	return 34;
+}
+
+static int do_read_track_information(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+	u32		track;
+
+	track = get_unaligned_be32(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	/* We only support T_CDB */
+	if ((common->cmnd[1] & 0x03) != 1 || track != 1) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 36);
+	put_unaligned_be16(34, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 1;	/* Track 1 */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* Session 1 */
+	buf[5] = 0x06;	/* Data track | Digital copy permitted */
+	buf[6] = 0x01;	/* Data mode 1 */
+	put_unaligned_be32(curlun->num_sectors, &buf[24]);
+	return 36;
+}
+
+/* put_unaligned_be24() only arrived in 5.x */
+static void put_be24(u32 val, u8 *p)
+{
+	p[0] = val >> 16;
+	p[1] = val >> 8;
+	p[2] = val;
+}
+
+static int do_read_disc_structure(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/* We only support physical format info */
+	if (common->cmnd[7] != 0x00) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 2052);
+	put_unaligned_be16(2050, &buf[0]);
+	buf += 4;		/* Skip size and 2 reserved bytes */
+	buf[0] = 0 | 0x01;	/* DVD-ROM, DVD-R Part Version 1 */
+	buf[1] = 0 | 0x0F;	/* 120mm disc, No transfer rate limit */
+	buf[2] = 0 | 0 | 0x01;	/* 1 Layer, Single Layer, Read-Only */
+	/* buf[3] = 0 - Linear Density = 0.267, Track Density = 0.74 */
+
+	/* Starting sector of main data is always 0x30000 for DVD-ROM */
+	put_be24(0x030000, &buf[5]);
+
+	/*
+	 * We can't address more than (2 ^^ 24) - 0x30000 sectors
+	 * i.e. 32384MB per layer, and it seems we will never reach
+	 * this limit. But maybe we should make a check to be sure.
+	 */
+	put_be24(0x030000 + curlun->num_sectors, &buf[9]);
+
+	/* It is okay to keep 0 in End physical sector number of Layer 0 */
+	return 2052;
+}
```

`kernel-patches/4.9/0001-usb-gadget-configfs-unregister-the-gadget-s-own-andr.patch`:

```patch
From 95f5c5c025cf2c19aa862e6680ea04e3277ae179 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 19:26:56 +0530
Subject: [PATCH 1/5] usb: gadget: configfs: unregister the gadget's own
 android device

Every gadget gets an androidN device in the android_usb class, all
created with devt MKDEV(0, 0). android_device_destroy() and the create
error path then call device_destroy(class, devt), which looks the
device up by devt and finds the oldest one: android0, which belongs to
Android's own gadget g1. Dropping any second gadget therefore destroys
Android's device while the dropped gadget's own stays behind without its
attributes, and UsbDeviceManager, which listens for android0's uevents,
hears nothing more until a reboot: no USB notification, USB tethering
greyed out.

Unregister gi->dev itself, and forget android_device when it is the
one going away.

Signed-off-by: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
---

 			return err;

 	attrs = android_usb_attributes;

+	/*
+	 * Not device_destroy(): every gadget's device has devt 0, so a lookup
+	 * by devt finds the oldest one, android0, whichever gadget is dropped.
```

`kernel-patches/4.9/0002-usb-gadget-f_ncm-fix-Samsung-s-changes-for-a-second-.patch`:

```patch
From f53582bc55ef773bf6d139265148a9a72bbe4215 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 19:30:27 +0530
Subject: [PATCH 2/5] usb: gadget: f_ncm: fix Samsung's changes for a second
 instance

Samsung's f_ncm (CONFIG_USB_ANDROID_SAMSUNG_COMPOSITE and
CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_UEVENT) only survives the one NCM instance its HAL
creates. A second one next to Android's ncm.0, in a separate configfs
gadget as USB Arsenal builds, breaks in two ways in this file:

- Samsung's extras exist once per system but were created and destroyed
  per instance. create_terminal_attribute() device_destroy()ed the shared
  android0 when it could not add terminal_version; ncm_function_init()
  overwrote _ncm_dev and re-registered the usb_ncm misc device; a second
  _ncm_setup_desc leaked the first, its duplicate f_ncm device failed to
  register and ncm_free_inst() then destroyed through the error pointer;
  and the first instance to go freed all of it under the other. Count
  the instances under a mutex: create on the first, never destroy
  android0, tear down after the last, and unregister the f_ncm device
  itself, since a lookup by devt (MKDEV(0, 0) for the first function
  device) can find android0. The count is exposed read-only as
  android0/ncm_instances, which tells userspace the kernel is fixed.

- The netdev was created in ncm_bind() and freed in ncm_unbind(), so
  until the first bind opts->net was NULL for the u_ether_configfs
  stores, and every rebind made a new interface. Give the netdev to the
  instance as mainline does: allocate it in ncm_alloc_inst(), register
  it once at the first bind, keep it across unbind, release it in
  ncm_free_inst().

Port of kernel-patches/4.14/0003 to Samsung's 4.9 (Qualcomm) f_ncm. Its
third fix, the rx skb, is not needed: ncm_unwrap_ntb() here already
copies every datagram into a new skb.

Signed-off-by: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
```

`kernel-patches/4.9/0005-usb-gadget-f_mass_storage-emulate-a-DVD-ROM-for-big-.patch`:

```patch
From 609f66e68df46c56f5f403806588658fea20a763 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Maxim Devaev <mdevaev@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 19:32:04 +0530
Subject: [PATCH 5/5] usb: gadget: f_mass_storage: emulate a DVD-ROM for big
 CD-ROM images

fsg_lun_open() truncates a CD-ROM image to 256*60*75 - 1 frames (about
2.36 GB) because the lead-out has to fit in a one-byte MSF minute. A
modern Windows ISO is 5 to 7 GB, so it is silently cut short and setup
fails part-way through.

Drop the clamp. An image too big for MSF addressing is presented as a
DVD-ROM instead: GET CONFIGURATION reports the DVD-ROM profile, READ
DISC INFORMATION, READ TRACK INFORMATION and READ DISC STRUCTURE are
answered, MODE SENSE gains the C/DVD capabilities page, and the TOC
carries a fabricated lead-out as real DVD drives do. Smaller images
stay CD-ROMs.

PiKVM's 1102-pikvm-msd-dvd-support.patch, applied as is on top of the
upstream READ TOC fixes (89ada0fe669a, 3b91edd624ab), with a local
put_be24() since put_unaligned_be24() only arrived in 5.x.

Link: https://github.com/pikvm/packages/blob/master/packages/linux-rpi-pikvm/1102-pikvm-msd-dvd-support.patch
[Backported to Samsung's 4.9 f_mass_storage: Samsung's own short mode page
 0x2A stays the answer for a disk LUN, while a CD-ROM LUN gets PiKVM's full
 page, so a CD-ROM never reports the page twice.]

Signed-off-by: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
---

+static int do_get_configuration(struct fsg_common *common,
+			struct fsg_buffhd *bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+	u8		*buf0 = buf;
+	int		len;
+	int		profile;
+	int		rt; /* Request type */
+	int		starting; /* Feature code */
+
+	/*
+	 * The standard prescribes to return disabled profiles
+	 * MMC_PROFILE_NONE when we have no medium, but it seems
+	 * it is enough to make unknown_cmnd in do_scsi_command().
+	 */
+	if (curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/* Big images will be handled as DVD */
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM;
+	} else {
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM;
+	}
+
+	/*
+	 * RT == 0x00 - Return all features since starting;
+	 * RT == 0x01 - Same but filtered by Current bit (all in our case);
+	 * RT == 0x02 - Return only header and zero or one supported feature;
+	 * RT == 0x03 - Reserved, but we'll handle it as 0x00 for paranoia;
+	 * ... So we have only one special case for 0x02.
+	 */
+	rt = common->cmnd[1] & 0x03;
+	starting = get_unaligned_be16(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 256); /* This should be enough for our all features */
+	/* Allocation Length in buf[0,1,2,3] will be calculated later */
+	put_unaligned_be16(profile, &buf[6]);
+	buf += 8;
+
+#define NEED_REPORT(feature) \
+		(rt == 0x02 ? (starting == feature) : (starting <= feature))
+
+	/* Profile List feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0)) {
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0 for the feature */
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length for two profiles */
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM, &buf[4]);
+		buf[6] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM);
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM, &buf[8]);
+		buf[10] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM);
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Core feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0001)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0001, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(1, &buf[4]); /* Phy = SCSI Family */
+		buf[8] = 0x01;		/* Device Busy Class Events = 1 */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Morphing feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0002)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0002, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Removable Medium feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0003)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0003, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x20 | 0x19;	/* Tray mechanism, Load|Eject|Lock */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Random Readable feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0010)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0010, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(2048, &buf[4]); /* Logical Block Size */
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0, no Blocking size presented */
+		buf[10] = 0x01;		/* RW Error Recovery Mode Page */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* MultiRead feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001D)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001D, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* CD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001E)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001E, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x03;		/* C2|CD-Text */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* DVD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001F)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001F, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x01;		/* MULTI110 */
+		buf[6] = 0x01;		/* Dual-R */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Power Management feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0100)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0100, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* Timeout feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0105)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0105,&buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Real Time Streaming feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0107)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0107, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x10 | 0x03;	/* Version = 4, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x0F;		/* SCS|MP2A|WSPD|SW */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+#undef NEED_REPORT
+
+	len = buf - buf0;
+	/* Put len minus the size of data length field (be32) */
+	put_unaligned_be32(len - 4, &buf0[0]);
+	return len;
+}
+
+static int do_read_disc_information(struct fsg_common *common,
+			struct fsg_buffhd *bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/*
+	 * (common->cmnd[1] & 0x07) contains Data Type, but it is safe
+	 * to ignore it and always return Data Type = 0 in buf[2]
+	 * for the Standard Disc Information.
+	 */
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 34);
+	put_unaligned_be16(32, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 0x0E;	/* Last session complete, disc finalized */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* First track on disc */
+	buf[4] = 1;	/* Number of sessions */
+	buf[5] = 1;	/* First track of last session */
+	buf[6] = 1;	/* Last track of last session */
+	buf[7] = 0x20;	/* Unrestricted use */
+	buf[8] = 0;	/* For CD should be 0, for DVD is inapplicable */
+
+	if (!curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/*
+		 * For CD if the disc is complete, both should be 0xFF.
+		 * For DVD it's inapplicable and shall be set to 0.
+		 * buf[16,17,18,19] - Last Session Lead-in Start Time.
+		 * buf[20,21,22,23] - Last Possible Start Time
+		 *                    for Start of Lead-out.
+		 */
+		memset(&buf[16], 0, 8);
+	}
+	return 34;
+}
+
+static int do_read_track_information(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+	u32		track;
+
+	track = get_unaligned_be32(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	/* We only support T_CDB */
+	if ((common->cmnd[1] & 0x03) != 1 || track != 1) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 36);
+	put_unaligned_be16(34, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 1;	/* Track 1 */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* Session 1 */
+	buf[5] = 0x06;	/* Data track | Digital copy permitted */
+	buf[6] = 0x01;	/* Data mode 1 */
+	put_unaligned_be32(curlun->num_sectors, &buf[24]);
+	return 36;
+}
+
+/* put_unaligned_be24() only arrived in 5.x */
+static void put_be24(u32 val, u8 *p)
+{
+	p[0] = val >> 16;
+	p[1] = val >> 8;
+	p[2] = val;
+}
+
+static int do_read_disc_structure(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/* We only support physical format info */
+	if (common->cmnd[7] != 0x00) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 2052);
+	put_unaligned_be16(2050, &buf[0]);
+	buf += 4;		/* Skip size and 2 reserved bytes */
+	buf[0] = 0 | 0x01;	/* DVD-ROM, DVD-R Part Version 1 */
+	buf[1] = 0 | 0x0F;	/* 120mm disc, No transfer rate limit */
+	buf[2] = 0 | 0 | 0x01;	/* 1 Layer, Single Layer, Read-Only */
+	/* buf[3] = 0 - Linear Density = 0.267, Track Density = 0.74 */
+
+	/* Starting sector of main data is always 0x30000 for DVD-ROM */
+	put_be24(0x030000, &buf[5]);
+
+	/*
+	 * We can't address more than (2 ^^ 24) - 0x30000 sectors
+	 * i.e. 32384MB per layer, and it seems we will never reach
+	 * this limit. But maybe we should make a check to be sure.
+	 */
+	put_be24(0x030000 + curlun->num_sectors, &buf[9]);
+
+	/* It is okay to keep 0 in End physical sector number of Layer 0 */
+	return 2052;
+}
```

`kernel-patches/4.9/t295/0001-usb-gadget-configfs-unregister-the-gadget-s-own-andr.patch`:

```patch
From 9831fb87beac8498efebe332458ba7e04c1b775f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 19:26:56 +0530
Subject: [PATCH 1/5] usb: gadget: configfs: unregister the gadget's own
 android device

Every gadget gets an androidN device in the android_usb class, all
created with devt MKDEV(0, 0). android_device_destroy() and the create
error path then call device_destroy(class, devt), which looks the
device up by devt and finds the oldest one: android0, which belongs to
Android's own gadget g1. Dropping any second gadget therefore destroys
Android's device while the dropped gadget's own stays behind without its
attributes, and UsbDeviceManager, which listens for android0's uevents,
hears nothing more until a reboot: no USB notification, USB tethering
greyed out.

Unregister gi->dev itself, and forget android_device when it is the
one going away.

Signed-off-by: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
---

 1 file changed, 10 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

 		err = device_create_file(gi->dev, attr);

+			if (android_device == gi->dev)
```

`kernel-patches/4.9/t295/0002-usb-gadget-f_ncm-fix-Samsung-s-changes-for-a-second-.patch`:

```patch
From b39eeef220daefed074fcaa2e41ff7b8629226c4 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 19:30:27 +0530
Subject: [PATCH 2/5] usb: gadget: f_ncm: fix Samsung's changes for a second
 instance

Samsung's f_ncm (CONFIG_USB_ANDROID_SAMSUNG_COMPOSITE and
CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_UEVENT) only survives the one NCM instance its HAL
creates. A second one next to Android's ncm.0, in a separate configfs
gadget as USB Arsenal builds, breaks in two ways in this file:

- Samsung's extras exist once per system but were created and destroyed
  per instance. create_terminal_attribute() device_destroy()ed the shared
  android0 when it could not add terminal_version; ncm_function_init()
  overwrote _ncm_dev and re-registered the usb_ncm misc device; a second
  _ncm_setup_desc leaked the first, its duplicate f_ncm device failed to
  register and ncm_free_inst() then destroyed through the error pointer;
  and the first instance to go freed all of it under the other. Count
  the instances under a mutex: create on the first, never destroy
  android0, tear down after the last, and unregister the f_ncm device
  itself, since a lookup by devt (MKDEV(0, 0) for the first function
  device) can find android0. The count is exposed read-only as
  android0/ncm_instances, which tells userspace the kernel is fixed.

- The netdev was created in ncm_bind() and freed in ncm_unbind(), so
  until the first bind opts->net was NULL for the u_ether_configfs
  stores, and every rebind made a new interface. Give the netdev to the
  instance as mainline does: allocate it in ncm_alloc_inst(), register
  it once at the first bind, keep it across unbind, release it in
  ncm_free_inst().

Port of kernel-patches/4.14/0003 to Samsung's 4.9 (Qualcomm) f_ncm. Its
third fix, the rx skb, is not needed: ncm_unwrap_ntb() here already
copies every datagram into a new skb.

Signed-off-by: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
```

`kernel-patches/4.9/t295/0003-usb-gadget-f_mass_storage-Make-CD-ROM-emulation-work.patch`:

```patch
From 26f8d119ba4770e696db3c8e2ce7574af3c9e1ba Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Roger Quadros <roger.quadros@nokia.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Jan 2022 08:01:50 -0800
Subject: [PATCH 3/5] usb: gadget: f_mass_storage: Make CD-ROM emulation work
 with Mac OS-X

Mac OS-X expects CD-ROM TOC in raw format (i.e. format:2). It also
sends the READ_TOC CDB in old style SFF8020i format. i.e. 2 format bits
are encoded in MSBs of CDB byte 9.

This patch will enable CD-ROM emulation to work with Mac OS-X. Tested on
Mac OS X v10.6.3.

+	 * i.e. format is in 2 MSBs of byte 9
+	 * Mac OS-X host sends us this.
+	 */

+	switch (format) {

+		buf[3] = 1;		/* Last complete session */

+			buf[0] = 1;	/* Session number */
+			buf[1] = 0x16;	/* Data track, copying allowed */
+			/* 2 - Track number 0 ->  TOC */
+			buf[3] = 0xA0 + i; /* A0, A1, A2 point */
+			/* 4, 5, 6 - Min, sec, frame is zero */
+			buf[8] = 1;	/* Pmin: last track number */
+			buf += 11;	/* go to next track descriptor */
```

`kernel-patches/4.9/t295/0005-usb-gadget-f_mass_storage-emulate-a-DVD-ROM-for-big-.patch`:

```patch
From 7afda235a16639dce6fff6c74fb9c8767e6f87f3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Maxim Devaev <mdevaev@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 03:05:59 +0530
Subject: [PATCH 5/5] usb: gadget: f_mass_storage: emulate a DVD-ROM for big
 CD-ROM images

fsg_lun_open() truncates a CD-ROM image to 256*60*75 - 1 frames (about
2.36 GB) because the lead-out has to fit in a one-byte MSF minute. A
modern Windows ISO is 5 to 7 GB, so it is silently cut short and setup
fails part-way through.

Drop the clamp. An image too big for MSF addressing is presented as a
DVD-ROM instead: GET CONFIGURATION reports the DVD-ROM profile, READ
DISC INFORMATION, READ TRACK INFORMATION and READ DISC STRUCTURE are
answered, MODE SENSE gains the C/DVD capabilities page, and the TOC
carries a fabricated lead-out as real DVD drives do. Smaller images
stay CD-ROMs.

PiKVM's 1102-pikvm-msd-dvd-support.patch, applied as is on top of the
upstream READ TOC fixes (89ada0fe669a, 3b91edd624ab), with a local
put_be24() since put_unaligned_be24() only arrived in 5.x.

Link: https://github.com/pikvm/packages/blob/master/packages/linux-rpi-pikvm/1102-pikvm-msd-dvd-support.patch
Signed-off-by: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>

+static int do_get_configuration(struct fsg_common *common,
+			struct fsg_buffhd *bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+	u8		*buf0 = buf;
+	int		len;
+	int		profile;
+	int		rt; /* Request type */
+	int		starting; /* Feature code */
+
+	/*
+	 * The standard prescribes to return disabled profiles
+	 * MMC_PROFILE_NONE when we have no medium, but it seems
+	 * it is enough to make unknown_cmnd in do_scsi_command().
+	 */
+	if (curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/* Big images will be handled as DVD */
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM;
+	} else {
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM;
+	}
+
+	/*
+	 * RT == 0x00 - Return all features since starting;
+	 * RT == 0x01 - Same but filtered by Current bit (all in our case);
+	 * RT == 0x02 - Return only header and zero or one supported feature;
+	 * RT == 0x03 - Reserved, but we'll handle it as 0x00 for paranoia;
+	 * ... So we have only one special case for 0x02.
+	 */
+	rt = common->cmnd[1] & 0x03;
+	starting = get_unaligned_be16(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 256); /* This should be enough for our all features */
+	/* Allocation Length in buf[0,1,2,3] will be calculated later */
+	put_unaligned_be16(profile, &buf[6]);
+	buf += 8;
+
+#define NEED_REPORT(feature) \
+		(rt == 0x02 ? (starting == feature) : (starting <= feature))
+
+	/* Profile List feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0)) {
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0 for the feature */
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length for two profiles */
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM, &buf[4]);
+		buf[6] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM);
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM, &buf[8]);
+		buf[10] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM);
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Core feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0001)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0001, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(1, &buf[4]); /* Phy = SCSI Family */
+		buf[8] = 0x01;		/* Device Busy Class Events = 1 */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Morphing feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0002)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0002, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Removable Medium feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0003)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0003, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x20 | 0x19;	/* Tray mechanism, Load|Eject|Lock */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Random Readable feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0010)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0010, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(2048, &buf[4]); /* Logical Block Size */
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0, no Blocking size presented */
+		buf[10] = 0x01;		/* RW Error Recovery Mode Page */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* MultiRead feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001D)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001D, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* CD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001E)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001E, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x03;		/* C2|CD-Text */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* DVD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001F)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001F, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x01;		/* MULTI110 */
+		buf[6] = 0x01;		/* Dual-R */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Power Management feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0100)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0100, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* Timeout feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0105)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0105,&buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Real Time Streaming feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0107)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0107, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x10 | 0x03;	/* Version = 4, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x0F;		/* SCS|MP2A|WSPD|SW */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+#undef NEED_REPORT
+
+	len = buf - buf0;
+	/* Put len minus the size of data length field (be32) */
+	put_unaligned_be32(len - 4, &buf0[0]);
+	return len;
+}
+
+static int do_read_disc_information(struct fsg_common *common,
+			struct fsg_buffhd *bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/*
+	 * (common->cmnd[1] & 0x07) contains Data Type, but it is safe
+	 * to ignore it and always return Data Type = 0 in buf[2]
+	 * for the Standard Disc Information.
+	 */
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 34);
+	put_unaligned_be16(32, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 0x0E;	/* Last session complete, disc finalized */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* First track on disc */
+	buf[4] = 1;	/* Number of sessions */
+	buf[5] = 1;	/* First track of last session */
+	buf[6] = 1;	/* Last track of last session */
+	buf[7] = 0x20;	/* Unrestricted use */
+	buf[8] = 0;	/* For CD should be 0, for DVD is inapplicable */
+
+	if (!curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/*
+		 * For CD if the disc is complete, both should be 0xFF.
+		 * For DVD it's inapplicable and shall be set to 0.
+		 * buf[16,17,18,19] - Last Session Lead-in Start Time.
+		 * buf[20,21,22,23] - Last Possible Start Time
+		 *                    for Start of Lead-out.
+		 */
+		memset(&buf[16], 0, 8);
+	}
+	return 34;
+}
+
+static int do_read_track_information(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+	u32		track;
+
+	track = get_unaligned_be32(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	/* We only support T_CDB */
+	if ((common->cmnd[1] & 0x03) != 1 || track != 1) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 36);
+	put_unaligned_be16(34, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 1;	/* Track 1 */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* Session 1 */
+	buf[5] = 0x06;	/* Data track | Digital copy permitted */
+	buf[6] = 0x01;	/* Data mode 1 */
+	put_unaligned_be32(curlun->num_sectors, &buf[24]);
+	return 36;
+}
+
+/* put_unaligned_be24() only arrived in 5.x */
+static void put_be24(u32 val, u8 *p)
+{
+	p[0] = val >> 16;
+	p[1] = val >> 8;
+	p[2] = val;
+}
+
+static int do_read_disc_structure(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/* We only support physical format info */
+	if (common->cmnd[7] != 0x00) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 2052);
+	put_unaligned_be16(2050, &buf[0]);
+	buf += 4;		/* Skip size and 2 reserved bytes */
+	buf[0] = 0 | 0x01;	/* DVD-ROM, DVD-R Part Version 1 */
+	buf[1] = 0 | 0x0F;	/* 120mm disc, No transfer rate limit */
+	buf[2] = 0 | 0 | 0x01;	/* 1 Layer, Single Layer, Read-Only */
+	/* buf[3] = 0 - Linear Density = 0.267, Track Density = 0.74 */
+
+	/* Starting sector of main data is always 0x30000 for DVD-ROM */
+	put_be24(0x030000, &buf[5]);
+
+	/*
+	 * We can't address more than (2 ^^ 24) - 0x30000 sectors
+	 * i.e. 32384MB per layer, and it seems we will never reach
+	 * this limit. But maybe we should make a check to be sure.
+	 */
+	put_be24(0x030000 + curlun->num_sectors, &buf[9]);
+
+	/* It is okay to keep 0 in End physical sector number of Layer 0 */
+	return 2052;
+}
```

```patch
 android device

Every gadget gets an androidN device in the android_usb class, all
created with devt MKDEV(0, 0). android_device_destroy() and the create
error path then call device_destroy(class, devt), which looks the
device up by devt and finds the oldest one: android0, which belongs to
Android's own gadget g1. Dropping any second gadget therefore destroys
Android's device while the dropped gadget's own stays behind without its
attributes, and UsbDeviceManager, which listens for android0's uevents,
hears nothing more until a reboot: no USB notification, USB tethering
greyed out.

Unregister gi->dev itself, and forget android_device when it is the
one going away.

Signed-off-by: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
```

```patch
+static int do_get_configuration(struct fsg_common *common,
+			struct fsg_buffhd *bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+	u8		*buf0 = buf;
+	int		len;
+	int		profile;
+	int		rt; /* Request type */
+	int		starting; /* Feature code */
+
+	/*
+	 * The standard prescribes to return disabled profiles
+	 * MMC_PROFILE_NONE when we have no medium, but it seems
+	 * it is enough to make unknown_cmnd in do_scsi_command().
+	 */
+	if (curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/* Big images will be handled as DVD */
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM;
+	} else {
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM;
+	}
+
+	/*
+	 * RT == 0x00 - Return all features since starting;
+	 * RT == 0x01 - Same but filtered by Current bit (all in our case);
+	 * RT == 0x02 - Return only header and zero or one supported feature;
+	 * RT == 0x03 - Reserved, but we'll handle it as 0x00 for paranoia;
+	 * ... So we have only one special case for 0x02.
+	 */
+	rt = common->cmnd[1] & 0x03;
+	starting = get_unaligned_be16(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 256); /* This should be enough for our all features */
+	/* Allocation Length in buf[0,1,2,3] will be calculated later */
+	put_unaligned_be16(profile, &buf[6]);
+	buf += 8;
+
+#define NEED_REPORT(feature) \
+		(rt == 0x02 ? (starting == feature) : (starting <= feature))
+
+	/* Profile List feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0)) {
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0 for the feature */
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length for two profiles */
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM, &buf[4]);
+		buf[6] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM);
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM, &buf[8]);
+		buf[10] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM);
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Core feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0001)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0001, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(1, &buf[4]); /* Phy = SCSI Family */
+		buf[8] = 0x01;		/* Device Busy Class Events = 1 */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Morphing feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0002)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0002, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Removable Medium feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0003)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0003, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x20 | 0x19;	/* Tray mechanism, Load|Eject|Lock */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Random Readable feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0010)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0010, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(2048, &buf[4]); /* Logical Block Size */
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0, no Blocking size presented */
+		buf[10] = 0x01;		/* RW Error Recovery Mode Page */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* MultiRead feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001D)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001D, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* CD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001E)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001E, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x03;		/* C2|CD-Text */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* DVD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001F)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001F, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x01;		/* MULTI110 */
+		buf[6] = 0x01;		/* Dual-R */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Power Management feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0100)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0100, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* Timeout feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0105)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0105,&buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Real Time Streaming feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0107)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0107, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x10 | 0x03;	/* Version = 4, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x0F;		/* SCS|MP2A|WSPD|SW */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+#undef NEED_REPORT
+
+	len = buf - buf0;
+	/* Put len minus the size of data length field (be32) */
+	put_unaligned_be32(len - 4, &buf0[0]);
+	return len;
+}

+static int do_read_disc_information(struct fsg_common *common,
+			struct fsg_buffhd *bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/*
+	 * (common->cmnd[1] & 0x07) contains Data Type, but it is safe
+	 * to ignore it and always return Data Type = 0 in buf[2]
+	 * for the Standard Disc Information.
+	 */
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 34);
+	put_unaligned_be16(32, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 0x0E;	/* Last session complete, disc finalized */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* First track on disc */
+	buf[4] = 1;	/* Number of sessions */
+	buf[5] = 1;	/* First track of last session */
+	buf[6] = 1;	/* Last track of last session */
+	buf[7] = 0x20;	/* Unrestricted use */
+	buf[8] = 0;	/* For CD should be 0, for DVD is inapplicable */
+
+	if (!curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/*
+		 * For CD if the disc is complete, both should be 0xFF.
+		 * For DVD it's inapplicable and shall be set to 0.
+		 * buf[16,17,18,19] - Last Session Lead-in Start Time.
+		 * buf[20,21,22,23] - Last Possible Start Time
+		 *                    for Start of Lead-out.
+		 */
+		memset(&buf[16], 0, 8);
+	}
+	return 34;
+}
+
+static int do_read_track_information(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+	u32		track;
+
+	track = get_unaligned_be32(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	/* We only support T_CDB */
+	if ((common->cmnd[1] & 0x03) != 1 || track != 1) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 36);
+	put_unaligned_be16(34, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 1;	/* Track 1 */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* Session 1 */
+	buf[5] = 0x06;	/* Data track | Digital copy permitted */
+	buf[6] = 0x01;	/* Data mode 1 */
+	put_unaligned_be32(curlun->num_sectors, &buf[24]);
+	return 36;
+}
+
+static int do_read_disc_structure(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/* We only support physical format info */
+	if (common->cmnd[7] != 0x00) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 2052);
+	put_unaligned_be16(2050, &buf[0]);
+	buf += 4;		/* Skip size and 2 reserved bytes */
+	buf[0] = 0 | 0x01;	/* DVD-ROM, DVD-R Part Version 1 */
+	buf[1] = 0 | 0x0F;	/* 120mm disc, No transfer rate limit */
+	buf[2] = 0 | 0 | 0x01;	/* 1 Layer, Single Layer, Read-Only */
+	/* buf[3] = 0 - Linear Density = 0.267, Track Density = 0.74 */
+
+	/* Starting sector of main data is always 0x30000 for DVD-ROM */
+	put_unaligned_be24(0x030000, &buf[5]);
+
+	/*
+	 * We can't address more than (2 ^^ 24) - 0x30000 sectors
+	 * i.e. 32384MB per layer, and it seems we will never reach
+	 * this limit. But maybe we should make a check to be sure.
+	 */
+	put_unaligned_be24(0x030000 + curlun->num_sectors, &buf[9]);
+
+	/* It is okay to keep 0 in End physical sector number of Layer 0 */
+	return 2052;
+}
```

`kernel-patches/5.10/0003-usb-gadget-hid-add-a-writable-bInterval-configfs-att.patch`:

```patch
From 437e02efc57ae72ab02b1ef3ef2edde3a447e733 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:34:26 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] usb: gadget: hid: add a writable bInterval configfs attribute

f_hid hardcodes the interrupt endpoint's bInterval in its endpoint
descriptors (1 ms at high speed, the /* FIXME: Add this field in the
configfs */ the driver has carried for years), so a HID keyboard is
polled no faster than once per millisecond however fast userspace writes
reports. At about one report per poll that caps a boot keyboard near
1000 reports per second.

Add an "interval" configfs attribute, the raw bInterval, defaulting to 0
which keeps the compiled-in descriptors. A nonzero value overrides the
fs/hs/ss in and out endpoint descriptors at bind, the same place
report_length already sets wMaxPacketSize. At high and super speed the
period is 2^(interval-1) microframes, so interval 1 polls every 125 us
instead of 1 ms.

Used by USB Arsenal's hid start --interval N to let a HID keyboard
gadget type faster when the UDC and host allow it.

Works on 5.10 and above.

Signed-off-by: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
```

`kernel-patches/5.15/0001-usb-gadget-configfs-unregister-the-gadget-s-own-andr.patch`:

```patch
From 98ba5b58e08cd56cb9d0057d5db79d754565446b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 19:16:01 +0530
Subject: [PATCH 1/2] usb: gadget: configfs: unregister the gadget's own
 android device

Every gadget gets an androidN device in the android_usb class, all
created with devt MKDEV(0, 0). android_device_destroy() and the create
error path then call device_destroy(class, devt), which looks the
device up by devt and finds the oldest one: android0, which belongs to
Android's own gadget g1. Dropping any second gadget therefore destroys
Android's device while the dropped gadget's own stays behind without its
attributes, and UsbDeviceManager, which listens for android0's uevents,
hears nothing more until a reboot: no USB notification, USB tethering
greyed out.

Unregister gi->dev itself, and forget android_device when it is the
one going away.

Signed-off-by: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
---

+++ b/drivers/usb/gadget/configfs.c
@@ -1796,8 +1796,9 @@ static int android_device_create(struct gadget_info *gi)

 		if (err) {
-			device_destroy(gi->dev->class,
-				       gi->dev->devt);
+			if (android_device == gi->dev)
+				android_device = NULL;
+			device_unregister(gi->dev);
 			return err;
 		}
 	}
@@ -1813,7 +1814,13 @@ static void android_device_destroy(struct gadget_info *gi)
 	attrs = android_usb_attributes;

-	device_destroy(gi->dev->class, gi->dev->devt);

+		android_device = NULL;
+	/*
+	 * Not device_destroy(): every gadget's device has devt 0, so a lookup
+	 * by devt finds the oldest one, android0, whichever gadget is dropped.

 }
 #else
```

```patch
+static int do_get_configuration(struct fsg_common *common,
+			struct fsg_buffhd *bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+	u8		*buf0 = buf;
+	int		len;
+	int		profile;
+	int		rt; /* Request type */
+	int		starting; /* Feature code */
+
+	/*
+	 * The standard prescribes to return disabled profiles
+	 * MMC_PROFILE_NONE when we have no medium, but it seems
+	 * it is enough to make unknown_cmnd in do_scsi_command().
+	 */
+	if (curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/* Big images will be handled as DVD */
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM;
+	} else {
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM;
+	}
+
+	/*
+	 * RT == 0x00 - Return all features since starting;
+	 * RT == 0x01 - Same but filtered by Current bit (all in our case);
+	 * RT == 0x02 - Return only header and zero or one supported feature;
+	 * RT == 0x03 - Reserved, but we'll handle it as 0x00 for paranoia;
+	 * ... So we have only one special case for 0x02.
+	 */
+	rt = common->cmnd[1] & 0x03;
+	starting = get_unaligned_be16(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 256); /* This should be enough for our all features */
+	/* Allocation Length in buf[0,1,2,3] will be calculated later */
+	put_unaligned_be16(profile, &buf[6]);
+	buf += 8;
+
+#define NEED_REPORT(feature) \
+		(rt == 0x02 ? (starting == feature) : (starting <= feature))
+
+	/* Profile List feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0)) {
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0 for the feature */
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length for two profiles */
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM, &buf[4]);
+		buf[6] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM);
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM, &buf[8]);
+		buf[10] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM);
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Core feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0001)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0001, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(1, &buf[4]); /* Phy = SCSI Family */
+		buf[8] = 0x01;		/* Device Busy Class Events = 1 */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Morphing feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0002)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0002, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Removable Medium feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0003)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0003, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x20 | 0x19;	/* Tray mechanism, Load|Eject|Lock */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Random Readable feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0010)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0010, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(2048, &buf[4]); /* Logical Block Size */
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0, no Blocking size presented */
+		buf[10] = 0x01;		/* RW Error Recovery Mode Page */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* MultiRead feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001D)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001D, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* CD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001E)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001E, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x03;		/* C2|CD-Text */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* DVD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001F)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001F, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x01;		/* MULTI110 */
+		buf[6] = 0x01;		/* Dual-R */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Power Management feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0100)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0100, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* Timeout feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0105)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0105,&buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Real Time Streaming feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0107)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0107, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x10 | 0x03;	/* Version = 4, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x0F;		/* SCS|MP2A|WSPD|SW */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+#undef NEED_REPORT
+
+	len = buf - buf0;
+	/* Put len minus the size of data length field (be32) */
+	put_unaligned_be32(len - 4, &buf0[0]);
+	return len;
+}
+
+static int do_read_disc_information(struct fsg_common *common,
+			struct fsg_buffhd *bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/*
+	 * (common->cmnd[1] & 0x07) contains Data Type, but it is safe
+	 * to ignore it and always return Data Type = 0 in buf[2]
+	 * for the Standard Disc Information.
+	 */
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 34);
+	put_unaligned_be16(32, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 0x0E;	/* Last session complete, disc finalized */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* First track on disc */
+	buf[4] = 1;	/* Number of sessions */
+	buf[5] = 1;	/* First track of last session */
+	buf[6] = 1;	/* Last track of last session */
+	buf[7] = 0x20;	/* Unrestricted use */
+	buf[8] = 0;	/* For CD should be 0, for DVD is inapplicable */
+
+	if (!curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/*
+		 * For CD if the disc is complete, both should be 0xFF.
+		 * For DVD it's inapplicable and shall be set to 0.
+		 * buf[16,17,18,19] - Last Session Lead-in Start Time.
+		 * buf[20,21,22,23] - Last Possible Start Time
+		 *                    for Start of Lead-out.
+		 */
+		memset(&buf[16], 0, 8);
+	}
+	return 34;
+}
+
+static int do_read_track_information(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+	u32		track;
+
+	track = get_unaligned_be32(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	/* We only support T_CDB */
+	if ((common->cmnd[1] & 0x03) != 1 || track != 1) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 36);
+	put_unaligned_be16(34, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 1;	/* Track 1 */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* Session 1 */
+	buf[5] = 0x06;	/* Data track | Digital copy permitted */
+	buf[6] = 0x01;	/* Data mode 1 */
+	put_unaligned_be32(curlun->num_sectors, &buf[24]);
+	return 36;
+}
+
+static int do_read_disc_structure(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/* We only support physical format info */
+	if (common->cmnd[7] != 0x00) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 2052);
+	put_unaligned_be16(2050, &buf[0]);
+	buf += 4;		/* Skip size and 2 reserved bytes */
+	buf[0] = 0 | 0x01;	/* DVD-ROM, DVD-R Part Version 1 */
+	buf[1] = 0 | 0x0F;	/* 120mm disc, No transfer rate limit */
+	buf[2] = 0 | 0 | 0x01;	/* 1 Layer, Single Layer, Read-Only */
+	/* buf[3] = 0 - Linear Density = 0.267, Track Density = 0.74 */
+
+	/* Starting sector of main data is always 0x30000 for DVD-ROM */
+	put_unaligned_be24(0x030000, &buf[5]);
+
+	/*
+	 * We can't address more than (2 ^^ 24) - 0x30000 sectors
+	 * i.e. 32384MB per layer, and it seems we will never reach
+	 * this limit. But maybe we should make a check to be sure.
+	 */
+	put_unaligned_be24(0x030000 + curlun->num_sectors, &buf[9]);
+
+	/* It is okay to keep 0 in End physical sector number of Layer 0 */
+	return 2052;
+}
```

`kernel-patches/5.15/0004-usb-gadget-hid-add-a-writable-bInterval-configfs-att.patch`:

```patch
From 437e02efc57ae72ab02b1ef3ef2edde3a447e733 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:34:26 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] usb: gadget: hid: add a writable bInterval configfs attribute

f_hid hardcodes the interrupt endpoint's bInterval in its endpoint
descriptors (1 ms at high speed, the /* FIXME: Add this field in the
configfs */ the driver has carried for years), so a HID keyboard is
polled no faster than once per millisecond however fast userspace writes
reports. At about one report per poll that caps a boot keyboard near
1000 reports per second.

Add an "interval" configfs attribute, the raw bInterval, defaulting to 0
which keeps the compiled-in descriptors. A nonzero value overrides the
fs/hs/ss in and out endpoint descriptors at bind, the same place
report_length already sets wMaxPacketSize. At high and super speed the
period is 2^(interval-1) microframes, so interval 1 polls every 125 us
instead of 1 ms.

Used by USB Arsenal's hid start --interval N to let a HID keyboard
gadget type faster when the UDC and host allow it.

Signed-off-by: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
```

`kernel-patches/5.15/sm8550/0001-usb-gadget-configfs-unregister-the-gadget-s-own-andr.patch`:

```patch
From f89f09c4e33c6280810d99f98615f86627adbdd5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 19:16:01 +0530
Subject: [PATCH 1/2] usb: gadget: configfs: unregister the gadget's own
 android device

Every gadget gets an androidN device in the android_usb class, all
created with devt MKDEV(0, 0). android_device_destroy() and the create
error path then call device_destroy(class, devt), which looks the
device up by devt and finds the oldest one: android0, which belongs to
Android's own gadget g1. Dropping any second gadget therefore destroys
Android's device while the dropped gadget's own stays behind without its
attributes, and UsbDeviceManager, which listens for android0's uevents,
hears nothing more until a reboot: no USB notification, USB tethering
greyed out.

Unregister gi->dev itself, and forget android_device when it is the
one going away.

Signed-off-by: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
---

+++ b/drivers/usb/gadget/configfs.c

@@ -1817,7 +1818,13 @@ static void android_device_destroy(struct gadget_info *gi)

+	/*
+	 * Not device_destroy(): every gadget's device has devt 0, so a lookup
+	 * by devt finds the oldest one, android0, whichever gadget is dropped.

 }
```

`kernel-patches/5.15/sm8550/0002-usb-gadget-f_mass_storage-emulate-a-DVD-ROM-for-big-.patch`:

```patch
From 175401787edc0c0021d92b22784ede50c6c990c0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Maxim Devaev <mdevaev@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 19:19:02 +0530
Subject: [PATCH 2/2] usb: gadget: f_mass_storage: emulate a DVD-ROM for big
 CD-ROM images

fsg_lun_open() truncates a CD-ROM image to 256*60*75 - 1 frames (about
2.36 GB), because the lead-out has to fit a one-byte MSF minute. Drop
the clamp and present bigger images as a DVD-ROM: GET CONFIGURATION
with the DVD-ROM profile, READ DISC INFORMATION, READ TRACK
INFORMATION, READ DISC STRUCTURE, the C/DVD capabilities mode page and
a fabricated lead-out in the TOC. Smaller images stay CD-ROMs.

PiKVM's 1102-pikvm-msd-dvd-support.patch, rebased on Samsung's
f_mass_storage: Samsung already answers mode page 0x2A with a short
page, which now remains the answer for a disk LUN while a CD-ROM LUN
gets PiKVM's full page, and PiKVM's READ TOC CDB mask replaces both
_SUPPORT_MAC_ variants (it allows a superset of each).

+	/*
+	 * The standard prescribes to return disabled profiles
+	 * MMC_PROFILE_NONE when we have no medium, but it seems
+	 * it is enough to make unknown_cmnd in do_scsi_command().
+	 */
+	if (curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/* Big images will be handled as DVD */
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM;
+	} else {
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM;
+	}
+
+	/*
+	 * RT == 0x00 - Return all features since starting;
+	 * RT == 0x01 - Same but filtered by Current bit (all in our case);
+	 * RT == 0x02 - Return only header and zero or one supported feature;
+	 * RT == 0x03 - Reserved, but we'll handle it as 0x00 for paranoia;
+	 * ... So we have only one special case for 0x02.
+	 */
+	rt = common->cmnd[1] & 0x03;
+	starting = get_unaligned_be16(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 256); /* This should be enough for our all features */
+	/* Allocation Length in buf[0,1,2,3] will be calculated later */
+	put_unaligned_be16(profile, &buf[6]);
+	buf += 8;
+
+#define NEED_REPORT(feature) \
+		(rt == 0x02 ? (starting == feature) : (starting <= feature))
+
+	/* Profile List feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0)) {
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0 for the feature */
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length for two profiles */
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM, &buf[4]);
+		buf[6] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM);
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM, &buf[8]);
+		buf[10] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM);
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Core feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0001)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0001, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(1, &buf[4]); /* Phy = SCSI Family */
+		buf[8] = 0x01;		/* Device Busy Class Events = 1 */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Morphing feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0002)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0002, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Removable Medium feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0003)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0003, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x20 | 0x19;	/* Tray mechanism, Load|Eject|Lock */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Random Readable feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0010)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0010, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(2048, &buf[4]); /* Logical Block Size */
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0, no Blocking size presented */
+		buf[10] = 0x01;		/* RW Error Recovery Mode Page */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* MultiRead feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001D)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001D, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* CD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001E)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001E, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x03;		/* C2|CD-Text */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* DVD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001F)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001F, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x01;		/* MULTI110 */
+		buf[6] = 0x01;		/* Dual-R */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Power Management feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0100)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0100, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* Timeout feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0105)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0105,&buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Real Time Streaming feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0107)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0107, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x10 | 0x03;	/* Version = 4, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x0F;		/* SCS|MP2A|WSPD|SW */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+#undef NEED_REPORT
+
+	len = buf - buf0;
+	/* Put len minus the size of data length field (be32) */
+	put_unaligned_be32(len - 4, &buf0[0]);
+	return len;
+}
+
+static int do_read_disc_information(struct fsg_common *common,
+			struct fsg_buffhd *bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/*
+	 * (common->cmnd[1] & 0x07) contains Data Type, but it is safe
+	 * to ignore it and always return Data Type = 0 in buf[2]
+	 * for the Standard Disc Information.
+	 */
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 34);
+	put_unaligned_be16(32, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 0x0E;	/* Last session complete, disc finalized */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* First track on disc */
+	buf[4] = 1;	/* Number of sessions */
+	buf[5] = 1;	/* First track of last session */
+	buf[6] = 1;	/* Last track of last session */
+	buf[7] = 0x20;	/* Unrestricted use */
+	buf[8] = 0;	/* For CD should be 0, for DVD is inapplicable */
+
+	if (!curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/*
+		 * For CD if the disc is complete, both should be 0xFF.
+		 * For DVD it's inapplicable and shall be set to 0.
+		 * buf[16,17,18,19] - Last Session Lead-in Start Time.
+		 * buf[20,21,22,23] - Last Possible Start Time
+		 *                    for Start of Lead-out.
+		 */
+		memset(&buf[16], 0, 8);
+	}
+	return 34;
+}
+
+static int do_read_track_information(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+	u32		track;
+
+	track = get_unaligned_be32(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	/* We only support T_CDB */
+	if ((common->cmnd[1] & 0x03) != 1 || track != 1) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 36);
+	put_unaligned_be16(34, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 1;	/* Track 1 */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* Session 1 */
+	buf[5] = 0x06;	/* Data track | Digital copy permitted */
+	buf[6] = 0x01;	/* Data mode 1 */
+	put_unaligned_be32(curlun->num_sectors, &buf[24]);
+	return 36;
+}
+
+static int do_read_disc_structure(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/* We only support physical format info */
+	if (common->cmnd[7] != 0x00) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 2052);
+	put_unaligned_be16(2050, &buf[0]);
+	buf += 4;		/* Skip size and 2 reserved bytes */
+	buf[0] = 0 | 0x01;	/* DVD-ROM, DVD-R Part Version 1 */
+	buf[1] = 0 | 0x0F;	/* 120mm disc, No transfer rate limit */
+	buf[2] = 0 | 0 | 0x01;	/* 1 Layer, Single Layer, Read-Only */
+	/* buf[3] = 0 - Linear Density = 0.267, Track Density = 0.74 */
+
+	/* Starting sector of main data is always 0x30000 for DVD-ROM */
+	put_unaligned_be24(0x030000, &buf[5]);
+
+	/*
+	 * We can't address more than (2 ^^ 24) - 0x30000 sectors
+	 * i.e. 32384MB per layer, and it seems we will never reach
+	 * this limit. But maybe we should make a check to be sure.
+	 */
+	put_unaligned_be24(0x030000 + curlun->num_sectors, &buf[9]);
+
+	/* It is okay to keep 0 in End physical sector number of Layer 0 */
+	return 2052;
+}
+
```

```patch
+static int do_get_configuration(struct fsg_common *common,
+			struct fsg_buffhd *bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+	u8		*buf0 = buf;
+	int		len;
+	int		profile;
+	int		rt; /* Request type */
+	int		starting; /* Feature code */
+
+	/*
+	 * The standard prescribes to return disabled profiles
+	 * MMC_PROFILE_NONE when we have no medium, but it seems
+	 * it is enough to make unknown_cmnd in do_scsi_command().
+	 */
+	if (curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/* Big images will be handled as DVD */
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM;
+	} else {
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM;
+	}
+
+	/*
+	 * RT == 0x00 - Return all features since starting;
+	 * RT == 0x01 - Same but filtered by Current bit (all in our case);
+	 * RT == 0x02 - Return only header and zero or one supported feature;
+	 * RT == 0x03 - Reserved, but we'll handle it as 0x00 for paranoia;
+	 * ... So we have only one special case for 0x02.
+	 */
+	rt = common->cmnd[1] & 0x03;
+	starting = get_unaligned_be16(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 256); /* This should be enough for our all features */
+	/* Allocation Length in buf[0,1,2,3] will be calculated later */
+	put_unaligned_be16(profile, &buf[6]);
+	buf += 8;
+
+#define NEED_REPORT(feature) \
+		(rt == 0x02 ? (starting == feature) : (starting <= feature))
+
+	/* Profile List feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0)) {
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0 for the feature */
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length for two profiles */
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM, &buf[4]);
+		buf[6] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM);
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM, &buf[8]);
+		buf[10] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM);
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Core feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0001)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0001, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(1, &buf[4]); /* Phy = SCSI Family */
+		buf[8] = 0x01;		/* Device Busy Class Events = 1 */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Morphing feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0002)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0002, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Removable Medium feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0003)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0003, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x20 | 0x19;	/* Tray mechanism, Load|Eject|Lock */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Random Readable feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0010)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0010, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(2048, &buf[4]); /* Logical Block Size */
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0, no Blocking size presented */
+		buf[10] = 0x01;		/* RW Error Recovery Mode Page */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* MultiRead feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001D)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001D, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* CD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001E)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001E, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x03;		/* C2|CD-Text */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* DVD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001F)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001F, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x01;		/* MULTI110 */
+		buf[6] = 0x01;		/* Dual-R */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Power Management feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0100)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0100, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* Timeout feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0105)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0105,&buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Real Time Streaming feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0107)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0107, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x10 | 0x03;	/* Version = 4, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x0F;		/* SCS|MP2A|WSPD|SW */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+#undef NEED_REPORT
+
+	len = buf - buf0;
+	/* Put len minus the size of data length field (be32) */
+	put_unaligned_be32(len - 4, &buf0[0]);
+	return len;
+}
+
+static int do_read_disc_information(struct fsg_common *common,
+			struct fsg_buffhd *bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/*
+	 * (common->cmnd[1] & 0x07) contains Data Type, but it is safe
+	 * to ignore it and always return Data Type = 0 in buf[2]
+	 * for the Standard Disc Information.
+	 */
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 34);
+	put_unaligned_be16(32, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 0x0E;	/* Last session complete, disc finalized */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* First track on disc */
+	buf[4] = 1;	/* Number of sessions */
+	buf[5] = 1;	/* First track of last session */
+	buf[6] = 1;	/* Last track of last session */
+	buf[7] = 0x20;	/* Unrestricted use */
+	buf[8] = 0;	/* For CD should be 0, for DVD is inapplicable */
+
+	if (!curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/*
+		 * For CD if the disc is complete, both should be 0xFF.
+		 * For DVD it's inapplicable and shall be set to 0.
+		 * buf[16,17,18,19] - Last Session Lead-in Start Time.
+		 * buf[20,21,22,23] - Last Possible Start Time
+		 *                    for Start of Lead-out.
+		 */
+		memset(&buf[16], 0, 8);
+	}
+	return 34;
+}
+
+static int do_read_track_information(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+	u32		track;
+
+	track = get_unaligned_be32(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	/* We only support T_CDB */
+	if ((common->cmnd[1] & 0x03) != 1 || track != 1) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 36);
+	put_unaligned_be16(34, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 1;	/* Track 1 */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* Session 1 */
+	buf[5] = 0x06;	/* Data track | Digital copy permitted */
+	buf[6] = 0x01;	/* Data mode 1 */
+	put_unaligned_be32(curlun->num_sectors, &buf[24]);
+	return 36;
+}
+
+static int do_read_disc_structure(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/* We only support physical format info */
+	if (common->cmnd[7] != 0x00) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 2052);
+	put_unaligned_be16(2050, &buf[0]);
+	buf += 4;		/* Skip size and 2 reserved bytes */
+	buf[0] = 0 | 0x01;	/* DVD-ROM, DVD-R Part Version 1 */
+	buf[1] = 0 | 0x0F;	/* 120mm disc, No transfer rate limit */
+	buf[2] = 0 | 0 | 0x01;	/* 1 Layer, Single Layer, Read-Only */
+	/* buf[3] = 0 - Linear Density = 0.267, Track Density = 0.74 */
+
+	/* Starting sector of main data is always 0x30000 for DVD-ROM */
+	put_unaligned_be24(0x030000, &buf[5]);
+
+	/*
+	 * We can't address more than (2 ^^ 24) - 0x30000 sectors
+	 * i.e. 32384MB per layer, and it seems we will never reach
+	 * this limit. But maybe we should make a check to be sure.
+	 */
+	put_unaligned_be24(0x030000 + curlun->num_sectors, &buf[9]);
+
+	/* It is okay to keep 0 in End physical sector number of Layer 0 */
+	return 2052;
+}
+
```

`kernel-patches/6.6/0001-usb-gadget-android_configfs_uevent-unregister-the-ga.patch`:

```patch
From 4a9ef6a1bfcc69e45c0ec41ce4bc71412f40620f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 19:19:46 +0530
Subject: [PATCH 1/2] usb: gadget: android_configfs_uevent: unregister the
 gadget's own device

Every gadget gets an androidN device in the android_usb class, all
created with devt MKDEV(0, 0). android_device_destroy() then calls
device_destroy(class, devt), which looks the device up by devt and
finds the oldest one: android0, which belongs to Android's own gadget.
Dropping any second gadget destroys Android's device instead, and
UsbDeviceManager hears no USB state until a reboot. The same path also
cleared android_opts even when another gadget was being dropped.

Unregister the gadget's own device, outside opts_lock since that may
sleep, and clear android_opts only when it is the one going away.

Signed-off-by: ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
---
 drivers/usb/gadget/android_configfs_uevent.c | 11 +++++++++--
 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/drivers/usb/gadget/android_configfs_uevent.c b/drivers/usb/gadget/android_configfs_uevent.c
index c89341039..668311aae 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/gadget/android_configfs_uevent.c
+++ b/drivers/usb/gadget/android_configfs_uevent.c
@@ -222,10 +222,17 @@ void android_device_destroy(struct android_uevent_opts *opts)
 	if (opts->device_id >= 0)
 		ida_free(&android_ida, opts->device_id);
 
-	android_opts = NULL;
+	if (android_opts == opts)
+		android_opts = NULL;
 	ida_destroy(&opts->function_ida);
-	device_destroy(dev->class, dev->devt);
 	spin_unlock_irqrestore(&opts_lock, flags);
+
+	/*
+	 * Not device_destroy(): every gadget's device has devt 0, so a lookup
+	 * by devt finds the oldest one, android0, whichever gadget is dropped.
+	 * Outside the lock, since unregistering a device may sleep.
+	 */
+	device_unregister(dev);
 }
```

```patch
+		memcpy(buf+2, capabilities, buf[1]);
+		buf += buf[1] + 2;

+static int do_get_configuration(struct fsg_common *common,
+			struct fsg_buffhd *bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+	u8		*buf0 = buf;
+	int		len;
+	int		profile;
+	int		rt; /* Request type */
+	int		starting; /* Feature code */
+
+	/*
+	 * The standard prescribes to return disabled profiles
+	 * MMC_PROFILE_NONE when we have no medium, but it seems
+	 * it is enough to make unknown_cmnd in do_scsi_command().
+	 */
+	if (curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/* Big images will be handled as DVD */
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM;
+	} else {
+		profile = MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM;
+	}
+
+	/*
+	 * RT == 0x00 - Return all features since starting;
+	 * RT == 0x01 - Same but filtered by Current bit (all in our case);
+	 * RT == 0x02 - Return only header and zero or one supported feature;
+	 * RT == 0x03 - Reserved, but we'll handle it as 0x00 for paranoia;
+	 * ... So we have only one special case for 0x02.
+	 */
+	rt = common->cmnd[1] & 0x03;
+	starting = get_unaligned_be16(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 256); /* This should be enough for our all features */
+	/* Allocation Length in buf[0,1,2,3] will be calculated later */
+	put_unaligned_be16(profile, &buf[6]);
+	buf += 8;
+
+#define NEED_REPORT(feature) \
+		(rt == 0x02 ? (starting == feature) : (starting <= feature))
+
+	/* Profile List feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0)) {
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0 for the feature */
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length for two profiles */
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM, &buf[4]);
+		buf[6] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_DVD_ROM);
+		put_unaligned_be16(MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM, &buf[8]);
+		buf[10] = (profile == MMC_PROFILE_CD_ROM);
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Core feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0001)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0001, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(1, &buf[4]); /* Phy = SCSI Family */
+		buf[8] = 0x01;		/* Device Busy Class Events = 1 */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* Morphing feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0002)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0002, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Removable Medium feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0003)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0003, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x08 | 0x03;	/* Version = 2, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x20 | 0x19;	/* Tray mechanism, Load|Eject|Lock */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Random Readable feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0010)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0010, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 8;		/* Additional length */
+		put_unaligned_be32(2048, &buf[4]); /* Logical Block Size */
+		/* buf[8,9] = 0, no Blocking size presented */
+		buf[10] = 0x01;		/* RW Error Recovery Mode Page */
+		buf += 12;
+	}
+
+	/* MultiRead feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001D)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001D, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* CD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001E)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001E, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x03;		/* C2|CD-Text */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* DVD Read feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x001F)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x001F, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x01;		/* MULTI110 */
+		buf[6] = 0x01;		/* Dual-R */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Power Management feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0100)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0100, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0 | 0x03;	/* Version = 0, Persistent|Current */
+		buf += 4;
+	}
+
+	/* Timeout feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0105)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0105,&buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x04 | 0x03;	/* Version = 1, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+	/* Real Time Streaming feature */
+	if (NEED_REPORT(0x0107)) {
+		put_unaligned_be16(0x0107, &buf[0]);
+		buf[2] = 0x10 | 0x03;	/* Version = 4, Persistent|Current */
+		buf[3] = 4;		/* Additional length */
+		buf[4] = 0x0F;		/* SCS|MP2A|WSPD|SW */
+		buf += 8;
+	}
+
+#undef NEED_REPORT
+
+	len = buf - buf0;
+	/* Put len minus the size of data length field (be32) */
+	put_unaligned_be32(len - 4, &buf0[0]);
+	return len;
+}
+
+static int do_read_disc_information(struct fsg_common *common,
+			struct fsg_buffhd *bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/*
+	 * (common->cmnd[1] & 0x07) contains Data Type, but it is safe
+	 * to ignore it and always return Data Type = 0 in buf[2]
+	 * for the Standard Disc Information.
+	 */
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 34);
+	put_unaligned_be16(32, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 0x0E;	/* Last session complete, disc finalized */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* First track on disc */
+	buf[4] = 1;	/* Number of sessions */
+	buf[5] = 1;	/* First track of last session */
+	buf[6] = 1;	/* Last track of last session */
+	buf[7] = 0x20;	/* Unrestricted use */
+	buf[8] = 0;	/* For CD should be 0, for DVD is inapplicable */
+
+	if (!curlun->cd_as_dvd) {
+		/*
+		 * For CD if the disc is complete, both should be 0xFF.
+		 * For DVD it's inapplicable and shall be set to 0.
+		 * buf[16,17,18,19] - Last Session Lead-in Start Time.
+		 * buf[20,21,22,23] - Last Possible Start Time
+		 *                    for Start of Lead-out.
+		 */
+		memset(&buf[16], 0, 8);
+	}
+	return 34;
+}
+
+static int do_read_track_information(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+	u32		track;
+
+	track = get_unaligned_be32(&common->cmnd[2]);
+
+	/* We only support T_CDB */
+	if ((common->cmnd[1] & 0x03) != 1 || track != 1) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 36);
+	put_unaligned_be16(34, &buf[0]);
+	buf[2] = 1;	/* Track 1 */
+	buf[3] = 1;	/* Session 1 */
+	buf[5] = 0x06;	/* Data track | Digital copy permitted */
+	buf[6] = 0x01;	/* Data mode 1 */
+	put_unaligned_be32(curlun->num_sectors, &buf[24]);
+	return 36;
+}
+
+static int do_read_disc_structure(struct fsg_common* common,
+		struct fsg_buffhd * bh)
+{
+	struct fsg_lun	*curlun = common->curlun;
+	u8		*buf = (u8 *) bh->buf;
+
+	/* We only support physical format info */
+	if (common->cmnd[7] != 0x00) {
+		curlun->sense_data = SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB;
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	memset(buf, 0, 2052);
+	put_unaligned_be16(2050, &buf[0]);
+	buf += 4;		/* Skip size and 2 reserved bytes */
+	buf[0] = 0 | 0x01;	/* DVD-ROM, DVD-R Part Version 1 */
+	buf[1] = 0 | 0x0F;	/* 120mm disc, No transfer rate limit */
+	buf[2] = 0 | 0 | 0x01;	/* 1 Layer, Single Layer, Read-Only */
+	/* buf[3] = 0 - Linear Density = 0.267, Track Density = 0.74 */
+
+	/* Starting sector of main data is always 0x30000 for DVD-ROM */
+	put_unaligned_be24(0x030000, &buf[5]);
+
+	/*
+	 * We can't address more than (2 ^^ 24) - 0x30000 sectors
+	 * i.e. 32384MB per layer, and it seems we will never reach
+	 * this limit. But maybe we should make a check to be sure.
+	 */
+	put_unaligned_be24(0x030000 + curlun->num_sectors, &buf[9]);
+
+	/* It is okay to keep 0 in End physical sector number of Layer 0 */
+	return 2052;
+}
```
