`kernel-patches/README.md`:

```md
# Kernel requirements

`usb-arsenal check` asks the running kernel what it can do. This page says what a kernel
needs built in for each feature, and which patches in this folder a feature needs on which
kernel versions.

## Options

| Option | Needed for |
|---|---|
| `CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS` | everything: the gadget interface (a 3.18 kernel built with the legacy android gadget instead needs a rebuild) |
| a peripheral-capable UDC driver | everything |
| `CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_MASS_STORAGE` | `storage` |
| `CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_F_HID` | `hid` |
| `CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_NCM` | `tether` |
| `CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_RNDIS` | `tether --rndis` (gone from GKI after 5.10) |
| `CONFIG_IP_NF_NAT`, `CONFIG_IP_NF_TARGET_MASQUERADE` | `tether` NAT |

Modules work too: the kernel loads `usb_f_<name>` when the function directory is created.

## Patches

Each `<version>/` folder holds `git format-patch` exports for that kernel version. Apply a
folder in order:

```sh
cd /path/to/kernel
git am /path/to/USB-Arsenal/kernel-patches/<version>/*.patch
```

A variant subfolder inside a version is the same set rebased on a tree whose mass storage
code differs; take the one that applies cleanly.

| Patch | Recommended for | Kernels |
|---|---|---|
| configfs: allow creating more than one gadget | running at all: without it a second gadget fails to be created, and `check` names the patch | [4.14](4.14/0001-usb-gadget-configfs-allow-creating-more-than-one-gad.patch), [4.19](4.19/0001-usb-gadget-configfs-allow-creating-more-than-one-gad.patch) |
| configfs: support mainline gadget bring-up alongside Android | running at all: without it a hand-built gadget never binds | [4.14](4.14/0002-usb-gadget-configfs-support-mainline-gadget-bring-up.patch), [4.19](4.19/0002-usb-gadget-configfs-support-mainline-gadget-bring-up.patch) |
| configfs: unregister the gadget's own android device | keeping Android's USB alive: without it removing any gadget kills Android's own until a reboot (USB Arsenal never removes its gadget, so it avoids the bug either way) | [4.9](4.9/0001-usb-gadget-configfs-unregister-the-gadget-s-own-andr.patch), [variant](4.9/t295/0001-usb-gadget-configfs-unregister-the-gadget-s-own-andr.patch), [5.10](5.10/0001-usb-gadget-configfs-unregister-the-gadget-s-own-andr.patch), [5.15](5.15/0001-usb-gadget-configfs-unregister-the-gadget-s-own-andr.patch), [variant](5.15/sm8550/0001-usb-gadget-configfs-unregister-the-gadget-s-own-andr.patch), [6.6](6.6/0001-usb-gadget-android_configfs_uevent-unregister-the-ga.patch); part of the first patch on 4.14 and 4.19 |
| f_ncm: fix Samsung's changes for a second instance | `tether` over NCM: without it `tether` uses RNDIS on a kernel with Samsung's NCM extras | [4.9](4.9/0002-usb-gadget-f_ncm-fix-Samsung-s-changes-for-a-second-.patch), [variant](4.9/t295/0002-usb-gadget-f_ncm-fix-Samsung-s-changes-for-a-second-.patch), [4.14](4.14/0003-usb-gadget-f_ncm-fix-Samsung-s-changes-for-a-second-.patch), [4.19](4.19/0003-usb-gadget-f_ncm-fix-Samsung-s-changes-for-a-second-.patch) |
| f_mass_storage: CD-ROM emulation for Mac OS X and Windows | `storage --mode cdrom` on Windows: without it Windows never mounts the disc | two patches each: [4.9](4.9/0003-usb-gadget-f_mass_storage-Make-CD-ROM-emulation-work.patch), [4.14](4.14/0004-usb-gadget-f_mass_storage-Make-CD-ROM-emulation-work.patch), [4.19](4.19/0004-usb-gadget-f_mass_storage-Make-CD-ROM-emulation-work.patch) and the [variant](4.9/t295/0003-usb-gadget-f_mass_storage-Make-CD-ROM-emulation-work.patch) (5.10 and up have them) |
| f_mass_storage: emulate a DVD-ROM for big CD-ROM images | `storage` with an image over 2.36G: without it the host reads a truncated disc (`--mode dvd` does not need it) | [4.9](4.9/0005-usb-gadget-f_mass_storage-emulate-a-DVD-ROM-for-big-.patch), [variant](4.9/t295/0005-usb-gadget-f_mass_storage-emulate-a-DVD-ROM-for-big-.patch), [4.14](4.14/0006-usb-gadget-f_mass_storage-emulate-a-DVD-ROM-for-big-.patch), [4.19](4.19/0006-usb-gadget-f_mass_storage-emulate-a-DVD-ROM-for-big-.patch), [5.10](5.10/0002-pikvm-msd-dvd-support.patch), [5.15](5.15/0002-pikvm-msd-dvd-support.patch), [variant](5.15/sm8550/0002-usb-gadget-f_mass_storage-emulate-a-DVD-ROM-for-big-.patch), [6.6](6.6/0002-pikvm-msd-dvd-support.patch), [6.12](6.12/0001-pikvm-msd-dvd-support.patch) |
| f_hid: writable bInterval configfs attribute | `hid --interval`: without it the keyboard is polled at the kernel's default 1 ms | [4.14](4.14/0007-usb-gadget-hid-add-a-writable-bInterval-configfs-att.patch), [5.10](5.10/0003-usb-gadget-hid-add-a-writable-bInterval-configfs-att.patch), [5.15](5.15/0004-usb-gadget-hid-add-a-writable-bInterval-configfs-att.patch) |

USB Arsenal reads whether a patch is there and never probes, since probing is what panics an
unpatched kernel: `check` shows whether a gadget of our own can be created, `tether` picks
RNDIS when Samsung's NCM extras are there without the f_ncm fix, and `hid --interval` warns
when the attribute is missing.

`module/customize.sh`:

```sh
#!/system/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
# KernelSU / Magisk install script: keep the one binary this device can run.

SKIPUNZIP=0

case "$ARCH" in
  arm64) BIN=usb-arsenal-aarch64 ;;
  arm) BIN=usb-arsenal-armhf ;;
  x64) BIN=usb-arsenal-x86_64 ;;
  x86) BIN=usb-arsenal-x86 ;;
  *) abort "! Unsupported architecture: $ARCH" ;;
esac
[ -f "$MODPATH/bin/$BIN" ] || abort "! $BIN is missing from the zip"

# The binary lives in the workspace, as the app installs it: copied beside the
# target and renamed over it, so a binary that is running is never written to
UA=/data/local/USB-Arsenal/bin/usb-arsenal
mkdir -p /data/local/USB-Arsenal/bin
cp "$MODPATH/bin/$BIN" "$UA.new" && chmod 755 "$UA.new" && mv -f "$UA.new" "$UA" ||
  abort "! Cannot install $UA"
rm -rf "$MODPATH/bin"

# A flashed zip has no app to switch the PATH link on, so it makes it: after
# the reboot `usb-arsenal` works from any root shell. The app's Settings
# toggle removes it or makes it again
mkdir -p "$MODPATH/system/bin"
ln -sf "$UA" "$MODPATH/system/bin/usb-arsenal"

ui_print "- USB Arsenal for $ARCH installed"

```

`src/check.c`:

```c
/*
 * USB Arsenal - composite USB gadget builder for Linux and Android
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
 *
 * Capability probing, after Droidspaces' check.c: ask the running kernel by
 * doing the real thing (create the function, remove it again) rather than
 * reading a config dump that may not match what is loaded.
 */

#include "net/net.h"
#include "usbarsenal.h"

#define PROBE_GADGET "ua_probe"

/* Not a "ua" instance: a probe left behind by a crash must never look like
 * one of ours and get linked into a gadget.
 * 1 if the kernel can create a <type> function (and, if attr is given, that
 * function has that attribute). Probes inside the gadget we would use, or a
 * throwaway one when ours does not exist yet. */
/* Samsung's f_ncm (CONFIG_USB_ANDROID_SAMSUNG_COMPOSITE, every 4.x tree we
 * have) hangs a terminal_version attribute on the shared android0 device
 * for each NCM instance. A second instance fails to add it, and the error
 * path calls device_destroy() on android0 itself (f_ncm.c
 * create_terminal_attribute). The next NCM instance, or Android's own
 * gadget, then touches a freed device and the kernel BUGs. The attribute
 * existing means an instance is already there: never make another one,
 * not even to probe. */
int ua_ncm_unsafe(void) {
  /* A kernel carrying the fix (an instance count instead of per-instance
   * create and destroy) says so with android0/ncm_instances. Without it,
   * Samsung's extras present means the bug is present. Asked by looking,
   * never by trying: trying is what panics. */
  return access("/sys/class/android_usb/android0/terminal_version", F_OK) ==
             0 &&
         access("/sys/class/android_usb/android0/ncm_instances", F_OK) != 0;
}

int ua_probe_function(const struct ua_gadget *g, const char *type,
                      const char *attr) {
  char root[PATH_MAX], fdir[PATH_MAX], a[PATH_MAX];
  int temp = 0, ok = 0;
  if (!strcmp(type, "ncm") && ua_ncm_unsafe())
    return 0;

  if (access(g->path, F_OK) == 0) {
    safe_strncpy(root, g->path, sizeof(root));
  } else if (access("/sys/class/android_usb", F_OK) == 0) {
    return 0; /* removing a probe gadget here destroys android0 */
  } else {
    snprintf(root, sizeof(root), "%s/" PROBE_GADGET, g->cfs);
    if (mkdir(root, 0755) < 0 && errno != EEXIST)
      return 0;
    temp = 1;
  }
  if (snprintf(fdir, sizeof(fdir), "%s/functions/%s.arsenal_probe", root,
               type) >= (int)sizeof(fdir))
    goto out;
  /* The kernel loads usb_f_<type> on demand here, so a modular build counts */
  if (mkdir(fdir, 0755) == 0) {
    ok = 1;
    if (attr) {
      snprintf(a, sizeof(a), "%s/%s", fdir, attr);
      ok = access(a, F_OK) == 0;
    }
    rmdir(fdir);
  }
out:
  if (temp)
    rmdir(root);
  return ok;
}

/* The quick gate in front of every action. Fails closed, and names the check
 * report for the details. */
int ua_check_requirements(struct ua_gadget *g, int need) {
  if (geteuid() != 0) {
    ua_error("Must be run as root");
    return -1;
  }
  int missing = 0;
  if ((need & UA_NEED_STORAGE) && !ua_probe_function(g, "mass_storage", NULL)) {
    ua_error("This kernel has no mass_storage gadget function "
             "(CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_MASS_STORAGE)");
    missing++;
  }
  if ((need & UA_NEED_HID) && !ua_probe_function(g, "hid", NULL)) {
    ua_error("This kernel has no hid gadget function "
             "(CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_F_HID)");
    missing++;
  }
  if ((need & UA_NEED_NET) && !ua_probe_function(g, "ncm", NULL) &&
      !ua_probe_function(g, "rndis", NULL)) {
    ua_error("This kernel has neither the ncm nor the rndis gadget function "
             "(CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_NCM / _RNDIS)");
    missing++;
  }
  if (missing)
    ua_log("Run '" UA_NAME " check' for the full report.");
  return missing ? -1 : 0;
}

/* check --json: one flat object, one int per probe, for an app to read */
static int json_mode, json_first = 1;

/* status: 1 ok, 0 missing, -1 works with caveats */
static void line(const char *key, int status, int must, const char *name,
                 const char *desc) {
  if (json_mode) {
    ua_json_int(key, status, &json_first);
    return;
  }
  const char *color = status > 0   ? C_GREEN
                      : status < 0 ? C_YELLOW
                      : must       ? C_RED
                                   : C_YELLOW;
  const char *sym = status > 0 ? "✓" : status < 0 ? "!" : "✗";
  printf("  [%s%s" C_RESET "] %s\n", color, sym, name);
  if (status <= 0 && desc)
    printf("      " C_DIM "%s" C_RESET "\n", desc);
}

void ua_help_check(void) {
  printf("Usage: " UA_NAME " check [--json]\n\n"
         "Probe the running kernel for everything USB Arsenal needs, the way\n"
         "it will actually be used: each gadget function is created and\n"
         "removed again, no config dump is read.\n\n"
         "MUST HAVE lines block every command. A missing FUNCTIONS line only\n"
         "blocks the command that needs it.\n\n"
         "  --json    One JSON object instead: each probe as 1 (ok), 0\n"
         "            (missing) or -1 (works with caveats), plus version,\n"
         "            udc_name and requirements_met. Same exit code.\n\n"
         "Examples:\n"
         "  " UA_NAME " check\n"
         "  " UA_NAME " check --json\n"
         "  " UA_NAME " --udc fe980000.usb check\n");
}

int ua_cmd_check(int argc, char **argv) {
  if (ua_want_help(argc, argv)) {
    ua_help_check();
    return UA_EXIT_OK;
  }
  json_mode = argc == 2 && !strcmp(argv[1], "--json");
  if (argc > 1 && !json_mode) {
    ua_usage_error("check", "check takes no arguments but --json");
    return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
  }

  int missing = 0, root = geteuid() == 0;
  char cfs[PATH_MAX] = "", udc[64] = "", desc[PATH_MAX + 64];
  struct ua_gadget g;

  if (json_mode)
    printf("{");
  else
    printf(C_BOLD "USB Arsenal " UA_VERSION " - checking this system" C_RESET
                  "\n\n[MUST HAVE]\n");
  line("root", root, 1, "Root privileges", "Run as root (su)");
  missing += !root;

  int have_cfs = ua_find_configfs(cfs, sizeof(cfs)) == 0;
  snprintf(desc, sizeof(desc), "configfs USB gadget%s%s%s",
           have_cfs ? " (" : "", cfs, have_cfs ? ")" : "");
  line("configfs", have_cfs, 1, desc,
       "CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS. Stock 3.18 kernels ship the legacy android "
       "gadget instead and need a custom kernel.");
  missing += !have_cfs;

  /* Listed here rather than through ua_pick_udc(), whose errors would land
   * on stderr in the middle of this report */
  char names[16][64], list[512] = "";
  int nudc = ua_list_udcs(names, 16), have_udc = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < nudc; i++) {
    size_t len = strlen(list);
    snprintf(list + len, sizeof(list) - len, "%s%s", i ? ", " : "", names[i]);
    if (ua_udc_opt ? !strcmp(names[i], ua_udc_opt) : nudc == 1) {
      safe_strncpy(udc, names[i], sizeof(udc));
      have_udc = 1;
    }
  }
  snprintf(desc, sizeof(desc), "USB device controller%s%s%s", nudc ? " (" : "",
           have_udc ? udc : list, nudc ? ")" : "");
  /* A dual-role controller leaves /sys/class/udc while its port is a host:
   * dwc3 removes its gadget on the switch (__dwc3_set_mode) */
  char why[PATH_MAX];
  if (ua_udc_opt)
    snprintf(why, sizeof(why),
             "%s is not in /sys/class/udc now: a typo, or a dual-role port in "
             "host mode (OTG), which lists none until it is a device again",
             ua_udc_opt);
  else
    snprintf(why, sizeof(why), "%s",
             nudc > 1 ? "More than one controller; pick one with --udc"
                      : "No peripheral-mode controller in /sys/class/udc now. "
                        "A dual-role port in host mode (OTG) lists none, and "
                        "dummy_udc.* counts only when --udc names it; on a "
                        "Raspberry Pi: dtoverlay=dwc2");
  line("udc", have_udc, 1, desc, why);
  missing += !have_udc;

  int have_backend = have_cfs && have_udc && root && ua_gadget_open(&g) == 0;
  line("gadget", have_backend, 1, "Own USB gadget",
       missing ? "Needs the lines above first"
               : "Could not create a gadget; see the errors above");
  missing += !have_backend;

  if (!json_mode)
    printf("\n[FUNCTIONS]\n");
  if (have_backend) {
    /* A line that needs a function is reported only with that function; the
     * JSON keeps its key, as 0 */
    int ms = ua_probe_function(&g, "mass_storage", NULL);
    line("mass_storage", ms, 0, "mass_storage",
         "CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_MASS_STORAGE; needed by 'storage' (and CD-ROM)");
    if (ms > 0 || json_mode)
      line("cdrom",
           ms > 0 && ua_probe_function(&g, "mass_storage", "lun.0/cdrom"), 0,
           "CD-ROM emulation (mass_storage)",
           "Without lun.0/cdrom, non-hybrid ISOs (Windows) cannot boot");
    int hid = ua_probe_function(&g, "hid", NULL);
    line("hid", hid, 0, "hid", "CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_F_HID; needed by 'hid'");
    /* Known before HID runs, so a client never offers an interval the
     * kernel would ignore */
    if (hid > 0 || json_mode)
      line("hid_interval", hid > 0 && ua_probe_function(&g, "hid", "interval"),
           0, "HID poll interval (f_hid)",
           "Stock f_hid polls the keyboard every 1 ms; the f_hid patch in "
           "kernel-patches/ makes 'hid --interval' work");
    if (ua_ncm_unsafe())
      line("ncm", -1, 0,
           "ncm (unsafe on this Samsung kernel; tether uses rndis)",
           "Another NCM instance would make f_ncm destroy android0 and the "
           "kernel BUG. The kernel fix (docs/kernel-requirements.md) adds "
           "android0/ncm_instances, and NCM is used again once it is "
           "there.");
    else
      line("ncm", ua_probe_function(&g, "ncm", NULL), 0, "ncm",
           "CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_NCM; preferred by 'tether'");
    line("rndis", ua_probe_function(&g, "rndis", NULL), 0, "rndis",
         "CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_RNDIS; 'tether --rndis' fallback for Windows "
         "7 and older hosts");
    line("nat", ds_ipt4_nat_available(), 0, "NAT for tethering",
         "The iptables nat table and MASQUERADE target "
         "(CONFIG_IP_NF_NAT, CONFIG_IP_NF_TARGET_MASQUERADE)");
    line("nat6", ds_ipt6_available(), 0, "IPv6 NAT for tethering",
         "The ip6tables nat table and MASQUERADE target "
         "(CONFIG_IP6_NF_NAT, CONFIG_IP6_NF_TARGET_MASQUERADE); without "
         "them the host gets IPv4 only");
  } else if (json_mode) {
    /* Every key always present, so a reader never has to guess */
    static const char *const fkeys[] = {"mass_storage", "cdrom", "hid",
                                        "hid_interval", "ncm",   "rndis",
                                        "nat",          "nat6"};
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(fkeys) / sizeof(fkeys[0]); i++)
      ua_json_int(fkeys[i], 0, &json_first);
  } else {
    printf("  Skipped: needs every MUST HAVE line first.\n");
  }

  if (json_mode) {
    ua_json_str("version", UA_VERSION, &json_first);
    ua_json_str("udc_name", udc, &json_first);
    ua_json_int("requirements_met", !missing, &json_first);
    printf("}\n");
    return missing ? UA_EXIT_FAIL : UA_EXIT_OK;
  }

  printf("\n");
  if (missing)
    printf("  %d required feature(s) missing - USB Arsenal will not work\n",
           missing);
  else
    printf("  All required features found\n");
  if (!root)
    printf("\nRun '" UA_NAME " check' as root for an accurate report.\n");
  return missing ? UA_EXIT_FAIL : UA_EXIT_OK;
}

```

`src/config.c`:

```c
/*
 * USB Arsenal - composite USB gadget builder for Linux and Android
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
 *
 * Profiles: everything a user may want to change, from the IDs the host sees
 * to each command's defaults, in an editable key=value file. The format and
 * the loader follow Droidspaces' config.c: '#' comments, trimmed keys and
 * values, a bad value warned about and left at its default, atomic writes.
 *
 * One profile is active at a time: <workspace>/Gadget/identity.conf, a
 * symlink to the user's file.
 */

#include "usbarsenal.h"

#define PROFILE_LEAF "identity.conf"

#define F(field) offsetof(struct ua_config, field)
#define S(field) sizeof(((struct ua_config *)0)->field)

/* One table drives loading, validation, `generate` and `show`. setup.c has a
 * second table for the same machinery. */
static const struct ua_key keys[] = {
    {"id_vendor", K_HEX16, F(id_vendor), 0, 0, NULL, NULL},
    {"id_product", K_HEX16, F(id_product), 0, 0, NULL, NULL},
    {"bcd_device", K_HEX16, F(bcd_device), 0, 0, NULL, NULL},
    {"bcd_usb", K_HEX16, F(bcd_usb), 0, 0, NULL, NULL},
    {"manufacturer", K_STR, F(manufacturer), S(manufacturer), 126, NULL, NULL},
    {"product", K_STR, F(product), S(product), 126, NULL, NULL},
    {"serial", K_STR, F(serial), S(serial), 126, NULL,
     "empty: ro.serialno, or /etc/machine-id"},
    {"configuration", K_STR, F(configuration), S(configuration), 126, NULL,
     NULL},
    {"max_power", K_UINT, F(max_power), 0, 500, NULL, "mA, 0-500"},
    {"storage_inquiry", K_STR, F(storage_inquiry), S(storage_inquiry), 28, NULL,
     "vendor(8) product(16) revision(4); empty: kernel default"},
    {"tether_dev_mac", K_MAC, F(tether_dev_mac), S(tether_dev_mac), 0, NULL,
     "empty: derived, stable per device"},
    {"tether_host_mac", K_MAC, F(tether_host_mac), S(tether_host_mac), 0, NULL,
     "the MAC the host sees"},
    {"storage_mode", K_CHOICE, F(storage_mode), S(storage_mode), 0,
     "auto cdrom dvd disk rw", "auto | cdrom | dvd | disk | rw"},
    {"tether_function", K_CHOICE, F(tether_function), S(tether_function), 0,
     "ncm rndis", "ncm | rndis"},
    {"tether_address", K_CIDR, F(tether_address), S(tether_address), 0, NULL,
     "this side's address; the host gets the next one"},
    {"tether_dns", K_DNS, F(tether_dns), S(tether_dns), 0, NULL,
     "empty: 1.1.1.1,8.8.8.8"},
    {"tether_upstream", K_STR, F(tether_upstream), S(tether_upstream),
     IFNAMSIZ - 1, NULL, "empty: detect automatically"},
    {"hid_perm", K_OCTAL, F(hid_perm), 0, 0777, NULL, "octal"},
    {"hid_group", K_UINT, F(hid_group), 0, 0x7fffffff, NULL, "numeric gid"},
};

#define NKEYS (sizeof(keys) / sizeof(keys[0]))
#define FIRST_DEFAULT 12 /* keys from storage_mode on are command defaults */

static void ua_config_defaults(struct ua_config *c) {
  memset(c, 0, sizeof(*c));
  c->id_vendor = 0x1d6b; /* Linux Foundation multifunction composite */
  c->id_product = 0x0104;
  c->bcd_device = 0x0100;
  c->bcd_usb = 0x0200;
  safe_strncpy(c->manufacturer, "USB Arsenal", sizeof(c->manufacturer));
  safe_strncpy(c->product, "USB Arsenal", sizeof(c->product));
  safe_strncpy(c->configuration, "USB Arsenal", sizeof(c->configuration));
  c->max_power = 250;
  safe_strncpy(c->storage_mode, "auto", sizeof(c->storage_mode));
  safe_strncpy(c->tether_function, "ncm", sizeof(c->tether_function));
  safe_strncpy(c->tether_address, "192.168.42.129/24",
               sizeof(c->tether_address));
  c->hid_perm = 0660;
}

static char *trim(char *s) {
  while (isspace((unsigned char)*s))
    s++;
  char *end = s + strlen(s);
  while (end > s && isspace((unsigned char)end[-1]))
    *--end = '\0';
  return s;
}

static int valid_mac(const char *v) {
  unsigned b[6];
  char tail;
  return sscanf(v, "%2x:%2x:%2x:%2x:%2x:%2x%c", &b[0], &b[1], &b[2], &b[3],
                &b[4], &b[5], &tail) == 6 &&
         strlen(v) == 17 && !(b[0] & 1);
}

static int valid_cidr(const char *v) {
  char ip[32];
  const char *slash = strchr(v, '/');
  struct in_addr a;
  if (!slash || (size_t)(slash - v) >= sizeof(ip))
    return 0;
  memcpy(ip, v, (size_t)(slash - v));
  ip[slash - v] = '\0';
  char *end;
  long p = strtol(slash + 1, &end, 10);
  return inet_pton(AF_INET, ip, &a) == 1 && !*end && end != slash + 1 &&
         p >= 8 && p <= 30;
}

int ua_valid_dns(const char *v) {
  char tmp[128], *save = NULL;
  struct in_addr a;
  int n = 0;
  /* As long as the key's own field holds, or a list cut short here would be
   * checked and then stored shorter than it was given */
  if (strlen(v) >= sizeof(tmp))
    return 0;
  safe_strncpy(tmp, v, sizeof(tmp));
  for (char *t = strtok_r(tmp, ",", &save); t; t = strtok_r(NULL, ",", &save))
    if (inet_pton(AF_INET, trim(t), &a) != 1)
      return 0;
    else
      n++;
  return n > 0;
}

static int ua_in_choices(const char *v, const char *choices) {
  size_t n = strlen(v);
  for (const char *c = choices; n && (c = strstr(c, v)); c += n)
    if ((c == choices || c[-1] == ' ') && (c[n] == ' ' || !c[n]))
      return 1;
  return 0;
}

/* A setup LUN: MODE:PATH with an absolute path, or empty for no drive */
static int valid_lun(const char *v, size_t size) {
  const char *colon = strchr(v, ':');
  char mode[8];
  if (!colon || (size_t)(colon - v) >= sizeof(mode) || colon[1] != '/' ||
      strlen(v) >= size)
    return 0;
  memcpy(mode, v, (size_t)(colon - v));
  mode[colon - v] = '\0';
  return ua_in_choices(mode, "auto cdrom dvd disk rw");
}

/* Store val into the key's field. Empty clears a string (back to "derive
 * it"); a numeric key cannot be empty. 0 ok, -1 rejected. */
int ua_key_set(void *base, const struct ua_key *k, const char *val) {
  char *field = (char *)base + k->off;
  char *end;
  unsigned long v;
  switch (k->kind) {
  case K_HEX16:
    v = strtoul(val, &end, 0);
    if (!*val || *end || v > 0xffff)
      return -1;
    *(unsigned *)(void *)field = (unsigned)v;
    return 0;
  case K_UINT:
  case K_OCTAL:
    v = strtoul(val, &end, k->kind == K_OCTAL ? 8 : 10);
    if (!*val || *end || v > k->max)
      return -1;
    *(unsigned *)(void *)field = (unsigned)v;
    return 0;
  case K_STR:
    if (strlen(val) > k->max)
      return -1;
    for (const char *p = val; *p; p++)
      if (!isprint((unsigned char)*p))
        return -1;
    break;
  case K_MAC:
    if (*val && !valid_mac(val))
      return -1;
    break;
  case K_CHOICE:
    /* Empty means the default (the setup leaves it to the profile) */
    if (*val && !ua_in_choices(val, k->choices))
      return -1;
    break;
  case K_LUN:
    if (*val && !valid_lun(val, k->size))
      return -1;
    break;
  case K_CIDR:
    /* Empty: the setup leaves it to the profile, and a profile without one
     * gets the built-in address */
    if (*val && !valid_cidr(val))
      return -1;
    break;
  case K_DNS:
    if (*val && !ua_valid_dns(val))
      return -1;
    break;
  }
  safe_strncpy(field, val, k->size);
  return 0;
}

void ua_key_get(const void *base, const struct ua_key *k, char *out,
                size_t size) {
  const char *field = (const char *)base + k->off;
  unsigned v = (k->kind == K_HEX16 || k->kind == K_UINT || k->kind == K_OCTAL)
                   ? *(const unsigned *)(const void *)field
                   : 0;
  if (k->kind == K_HEX16)
    snprintf(out, size, "0x%04x", v);
  else if (k->kind == K_UINT)
    snprintf(out, size, "%u", v);
  else if (k->kind == K_OCTAL)
    snprintf(out, size, "0%o", v);
  else
    safe_strncpy(out, field, size);
}

/* Returns the number of lines that were not taken (bad value, unknown key,
 * no '='), or -1 when the file cannot be read. Everything else keeps what
 * base held before, normally the defaults. */
int ua_table_load(const char *path, const struct ua_key *table, size_t nkeys,
                  void *base) {
  FILE *f = fopen(path, "re");
  if (!f)
    return -1;
  char line[512];
  int n = 0, bad = 0;
  while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), f)) {
    n++;
    char *t = trim(line);
    if (!*t || *t == '#')
      continue;
    char *eq = strchr(t, '=');
    if (!eq) {
      ua_warn("%s:%d: not key=value, ignored", path, n);
      bad++;
      continue;
    }
    *eq = '\0';
    char *key = trim(t), *val = trim(eq + 1);
    /* An inline comment starts the value or follows whitespace, so a '#'
     * inside a string (a serial like "AB#12") stays part of it. A value
     * that is only a comment is empty: that is how `generate` writes them. */
    for (char *h = val; (h = strchr(h, '#')); h++)
      if (h == val || isspace((unsigned char)h[-1])) {
        *h = '\0';
        val = trim(val);
        break;
      }
    size_t i;
    for (i = 0; i < nkeys; i++)
      if (!strcmp(key, table[i].name))
        break;
    if (i == nkeys) {
      ua_warn("%s:%d: unknown key '%s', ignored", path, n, key);
      bad++;
    } else if (ua_key_set(base, &table[i], val) < 0) {
      ua_warn("%s:%d: bad value '%s' for %s, keeping the default", path, n, val,
              key);
      bad++;
    }
  }
  fclose(f);
  return bad;
}

static void active_path(char *out, size_t size) {
  ua_ws_path("Gadget", PROFILE_LEAF, out, size);
}

/* The profile in force: the user's file through the symlink.
 * No profile is fine and silent; one that has gone missing is reported. */
void ua_config_active(struct ua_config *c) {
  char p[PATH_MAX], target[PATH_MAX];
  struct stat st;
  ua_config_defaults(c);
  active_path(p, sizeof(p));
  if (lstat(p, &st) < 0)
    return;
  if (S_ISLNK(st.st_mode)) {
    ssize_t n = readlink(p, target, sizeof(target) - 1);
    target[n > 0 ? n : 0] = '\0';
    if (ua_table_load(p, keys, NKEYS, c) < 0) {
      ua_warn("Profile %s is gone; using the built-in defaults", target);
      ua_config_defaults(c);
      return;
    }
    safe_strncpy(c->source, target, sizeof(c->source));
    return;
  }
  /* A plain file: an older version's copy of a profile */
  if (ua_table_load(p, keys, NKEYS, c) == 0)
    safe_strncpy(c->source, p, sizeof(c->source));
}

/* mkstemp next to path, write, fsync, rename, fsync the directory: the
 * Droidspaces ds_config_save sequence. body(f, arg) writes the content. */
int ua_write_atomic(const char *path, mode_t mode,
                    void (*body)(FILE *, const void *), const void *arg) {
  char tmp[PATH_MAX + 8];
  snprintf(tmp, sizeof(tmp), "%s.XXXXXX", path);
  int fd = mkstemp(tmp);
  if (fd < 0)
    return -1;
  fchmod(fd, mode);
  FILE *f = fdopen(fd, "w");
  if (!f) {
    close(fd);
    unlink(tmp);
    return -1;
  }
  body(f, arg);
  int ok = fflush(f) == 0 && !ferror(f) &&
           (fsync(fileno(f)) == 0 || errno == EINVAL);
  if (fclose(f) != 0 || !ok || rename(tmp, path) < 0) {
    unlink(tmp);
    return -1;
  }
  char *slash = strrchr(tmp, '/');
  if (slash) {
    *slash = '\0';
    int dfd =
        open(slash == tmp ? "/" : tmp, O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC);
    if (dfd >= 0) {
      fsync(dfd);
      close(dfd);
    }
  }
  return 0;
}

static void template_body(FILE *f, const void *arg) {
  const struct ua_config *c = arg;
  fprintf(f, "# USB Arsenal profile. Make it the default with:\n"
             "#   " UA_NAME " identity set <this file>\n"
             "# A command-line option overrides the value here. An empty value "
             "means\n# \"derive it\" where the comment says so.\n\n"
             "# What the host sees\n");
  for (size_t i = 0; i < NKEYS; i++) {
    char v[160], line[200];
    if (i == FIRST_DEFAULT)
      fprintf(f, "\n# Defaults for commands\n");
    ua_key_get(c, &keys[i], v, sizeof(v));
    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%s=%s", keys[i].name, v);
    if (keys[i].comment)
      fprintf(f, "%-32s # %s\n", line, keys[i].comment);
    else
      fprintf(f, "%s\n", line);
  }
}

void ua_help_identity(void) {
  printf(
      "Usage: " UA_NAME " identity <action> [options] [FILE]\n\n"
      "Profiles: the IDs, strings and serial the host sees, plus the defaults\n"
      "of every command, in an editable key=value file. Keep as many as you\n"
      "like; one is active at a time.\n\n"
      "Actions:\n"
      "  generate FILE  Write a profile with every key and its default.\n"
      "                 Refuses an existing file unless --force.\n"
      "  set FILE       Make FILE the active profile. A live gadget re-plugs\n"
      "                 once so the host sees the change now.\n"
      "  show [FILE...] Print the values in force and where they come from;\n"
      "                 with FILEs, what each one gives, read as set reads\n"
      "                 it (a bad line keeps that key's default)\n"
      "  unset          Back to the built-in defaults\n\n"
      "Options:\n"
      "      --force    Let generate overwrite FILE\n"
      "      --json     show as JSON: {profile, missing, keys}, or with\n"
      "                 FILEs an array of {path, errors, keys}. A derived\n"
      "                 value is \"\"; errors is -1 for a FILE that cannot\n"
      "                 be read.\n"
      "  -h, --help     Show this help\n\n"
      "The active profile is a symlink at <workspace>/Gadget/identity.conf,\n"
      "so an edit of FILE counts from the next start. A profile that has\n"
      "gone missing is reported, and the built-in\n"
      "defaults are used.\n\n"
      "Examples:\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " identity generate ~/pixel.conf\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " identity set ~/pixel.conf\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " identity show\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " identity show --json ~/pixel.conf ~/other.conf\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " identity unset\n");
}

static int replug_if_live(void) {
  struct ua_gadget g;
  if (ua_gadget_open(&g) < 0)
    return 0;
  if (!ua_gadget_live(&g))
    return 0;
  ua_log("Re-plugging the gadget so the host sees the new identity");
  if (ua_gadget_begin(&g) < 0)
    return -1;
  return ua_gadget_commit(&g);
}

/* set: link to the user's file, by its canonical path */
static int do_set(const char *file) {
  char real[PATH_MAX], active[PATH_MAX], tmp[PATH_MAX + 8];
  struct ua_config c;

  if (geteuid() != 0) {
    ua_error("Must be run as root");
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  }
  if (!realpath(file, real)) {
    ua_error("%s: %s", file, strerror(errno));
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  }
  ua_config_defaults(&c);
  int bad = ua_table_load(real, keys, NKEYS, &c);
  if (bad != 0) {
    ua_error(bad < 0 ? "Cannot read %s" : "%s has errors (see above); not set",
             real);
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  }

  active_path(active, sizeof(active));
  snprintf(tmp, sizeof(tmp), "%s.new", active);
  unlink(tmp);
  if (symlink(real, tmp) < 0 || rename(tmp, active) < 0) {
    ua_error("Cannot link %s: %s", active, strerror(errno));
    unlink(tmp);
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  }
  ua_log("Active profile: %s", real);
  return replug_if_live() < 0 ? UA_EXIT_FAIL : UA_EXIT_OK;
}

/* c's values as ua_key_get prints them: a "keys" JSON object, or a line each
 */
static void print_keys(const struct ua_config *c, int json) {
  int first = 1;
  if (json)
    printf("\"keys\":{");
  for (size_t i = 0; i < NKEYS; i++) {
    char v[160];
    ua_key_get(c, &keys[i], v, sizeof(v));
    if (json)
      ua_json_str(keys[i].name, v, &first);
    else
      printf("  %-16s %s\n", keys[i].name, v[0] ? v : "(derived)");
  }
  if (json)
    printf("}");
}

/* The profile in force, or with FILEs each of them read through the same
 * loader `set` uses, so a client never has to parse a profile itself */
static int do_show(char **files, int nfiles, int json) {
  struct ua_config c;
  int ret = UA_EXIT_OK, first;
  if (!nfiles) {
    char p[PATH_MAX], missing[PATH_MAX] = "";
    struct stat st;
    ua_config_active(&c);
    /* A link to a deleted file reads as the built-in defaults; say which file
     * went, or the user only sees their profile silently ignored */
    active_path(p, sizeof(p));
    if (lstat(p, &st) == 0 && S_ISLNK(st.st_mode) && stat(p, &st) < 0 &&
        errno == ENOENT) {
      ssize_t n = readlink(p, missing, sizeof(missing) - 1);
      missing[n > 0 ? n : 0] = '\0';
    }
    if (json) {
      first = 1;
      printf("{");
      ua_json_str("profile", c.source, &first);
      ua_json_str("missing", missing, &first);
      printf(",");
      print_keys(&c, 1);
      printf("}\n");
    } else {
      if (missing[0])
        printf("Profile: %s (missing)\n", missing);
      else
        printf("Profile: %s\n", c.source[0] ? c.source : "built-in defaults");
      print_keys(&c, 0);
    }
    return UA_EXIT_OK;
  }
  if (json)
    printf("[");
  for (int i = 0; i < nfiles; i++) {
    char real[PATH_MAX];
    ua_config_defaults(&c);
    int bad = ua_table_load(files[i], keys, NKEYS, &c);
    if (bad < 0) {
      ua_error("Cannot read %s: %s", files[i], strerror(errno));
      ret = UA_EXIT_FAIL;
    }
    if (!realpath(files[i], real))
      safe_strncpy(real, files[i], sizeof(real));
    if (json) {
      first = 1;
      printf("%s{", i ? "," : "");
      ua_json_str("path", real, &first);
      ua_json_int("errors", bad, &first);
      printf(",");
      print_keys(&c, 1);
      printf("}");
    } else {
      printf("Profile: %s", real);
      if (bad)
        printf(bad < 0 ? " (cannot read)" : " (%d bad lines, defaults kept)",
               bad);
      printf("\n");
      print_keys(&c, 0);
    }
  }
  if (json)
    printf("]\n");
  return ret;
}

static int do_unset(void) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  if (geteuid() != 0) {
    ua_error("Must be run as root");
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  }
  active_path(p, sizeof(p));
  if (unlink(p) < 0 && errno != ENOENT) {
    ua_error("Cannot remove %s: %s", p, strerror(errno));
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  }
  ua_log("Back to the built-in defaults");
  return replug_if_live() < 0 ? UA_EXIT_FAIL : UA_EXIT_OK;
}

int ua_cmd_identity(int argc, char **argv) {
  enum { OPT_FORCE = 256, OPT_JSON };
  static const struct option opts[] = {
      {"force", no_argument, NULL, OPT_FORCE},
      {"json", no_argument, NULL, OPT_JSON},
      {"help", no_argument, NULL, 'h'},
      {NULL, 0, NULL, 0},
  };
  int force = 0, json = 0, c;
  if (argc < 2 || ua_want_help(argc, argv)) {
    ua_help_identity();
    return UA_EXIT_OK;
  }
  while ((c = getopt_long(argc, argv, ":h", opts, NULL)) != -1) {
    switch (c) {
    case OPT_FORCE:
      force = 1;
      break;
    case OPT_JSON:
      json = 1;
      break;
    case 'h':
      ua_help_identity();
      return UA_EXIT_OK;
    case ':':
      ua_usage_error("identity", "Option '%s' needs a value", argv[optind - 1]);
      return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
    default:
      ua_usage_error("identity", "Bad option '%s'", ua_bad_option(argv));
      return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
    }
  }
  int nargs = argc - optind;
  const char *action = nargs ? argv[optind] : "";
  const char *file = nargs > 1 ? argv[optind + 1] : NULL;
  if (json && strcmp(action, "show")) {
    ua_usage_error("identity", "--json goes with show");
    return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
  }
  if (!strcmp(action, "show"))
    return do_show(argv + optind + 1, nargs - 1, json);
  int want = !strcmp(action, "generate") || !strcmp(action, "set") ? 2 : 1;
  if (nargs != want) {
    ua_usage_error("identity", nargs < want ? "Missing FILE"
                                            : "Too many "
                                              "arguments");
    return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
  }
  if (!strcmp(action, "generate")) {
    struct ua_config d;
    ua_config_defaults(&d);
    if (!force && access(file, F_OK) == 0) {
      ua_error("%s exists; use --force to overwrite it", file);
      return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
    }
    if (ua_write_atomic(file, 0644, template_body, &d) < 0) {
      ua_error("Cannot write %s: %s", file, strerror(errno));
      return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
    }
    ua_log("Wrote %s; edit it, then: " UA_NAME " identity set %s", file, file);
    return UA_EXIT_OK;
  }
  if (!strcmp(action, "set"))
    return do_set(file);
  if (!strcmp(action, "unset"))
    return do_unset();
  ua_usage_error("identity", "Unknown action '%s'", action);
  return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
}

```

`src/gadget.c`:

```c
/*
 * USB Arsenal - composite USB gadget builder for Linux and Android
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
 *
 * The gadget core. Every subsystem goes through begin -> add -> commit, and
 * every failure after begin goes through teardown, which is the one path that
 * hands the controller back. See
 * docs/developer/research/02-android-usb-handoff.md.
 */

#include "usbarsenal.h"

const char *ua_udc_opt;

/* What we took from the previous owner, written before we touch anything so
 * `stop` can put it back after a crash or a kill -9. */
struct handoff {
  char udc[64];         /* the controller we took */
  char usb_config[128]; /* Android: sys.usb.config before we started */
  char boot[40];        /* boot_id: a handoff from an earlier boot is void */
  char g1_udc[64];      /* Android's g1 was bound to this before we took it */
};

static int handoff_load(struct handoff *h);

/* What tells one boot from the next. boot_id where the kernel offers it,
 * the boot time from /proc/stat where a restricted container hides it; an
 * empty marker would make every old handoff look current. */
void ua_boot_marker(char *out, size_t size) {
  char buf[4096], *bt;
  if (read_file("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id", out, size) > 0)
    return;
  if (read_file("/proc/stat", buf, sizeof(buf)) > 0 &&
      (bt = strstr(buf, "btime ")))
    snprintf(out, size, "btime-%ld", strtol(bt + 6, NULL, 10));
  else
    safe_strncpy(out, "unknown", size);
}

static void handoff_path(char *out, size_t size) {
  ua_ws_path("Gadget", "handoff", out, size);
}

int ua_gadget_taken(void) {
  struct handoff h;
  return handoff_load(&h) == 0;
}

static int handoff_save(const struct handoff *h) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  handoff_path(p, sizeof(p));
  int fd = open(p, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC, 0600);
  FILE *f = fd >= 0 ? fdopen(fd, "w") : NULL;
  if (!f) {
    if (fd >= 0)
      close(fd);
    return -1;
  }
  fprintf(f, "udc=%s\nusb_config=%s\nboot=%s\ng1_udc=%s\n", h->udc,
          h->usb_config, h->boot, h->g1_udc);
  /* The whole point of this file is surviving a crash, so it has to be on
   * disk before the controller changes hands */
  int ok = fflush(f) == 0 && fsync(fileno(f)) == 0;
  return (fclose(f) == 0 && ok) ? 0 : -1;
}

static int handoff_load(struct handoff *h) {
  char p[PATH_MAX], line[512];
  memset(h, 0, sizeof(*h));
  handoff_path(p, sizeof(p));
  FILE *f = fopen(p, "re");
  if (!f)
    return -1;
  while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), f)) {
    line[strcspn(line, "\r\n")] = '\0';
    char *v = strchr(line, '=');
    if (!v)
      continue;
    *v++ = '\0';
    if (!strcmp(line, "udc"))
      safe_strncpy(h->udc, v, sizeof(h->udc));
    else if (!strcmp(line, "usb_config"))
      safe_strncpy(h->usb_config, v, sizeof(h->usb_config));
    else if (!strcmp(line, "boot"))
      safe_strncpy(h->boot, v, sizeof(h->boot));
    else if (!strcmp(line, "g1_udc"))
      safe_strncpy(h->g1_udc, v, sizeof(h->g1_udc));
  }
  fclose(f);

  /* A reboot already gave the controller back. Android keeps this file in
   * /data across it, and acting on it would skip releasing Android's gadget. */
  char boot[40] = "";
  ua_boot_marker(boot, sizeof(boot));
  if (strcmp(boot, h->boot) != 0) {
    unlink(p);
    return -1;
  }
  return 0;
}

static void handoff_drop(void) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  handoff_path(p, sizeof(p));
  unlink(p);
}

/* Ctrl-C between unbinding Android and binding ours would leave the phone
 * with no USB at all, so the handoff runs with the usual stop signals held.
 * kill -9 still gets through; `stop` and the handoff file cover that. */
static int crit_depth, crit_lock = -1;
static sigset_t crit_old;

/* The critical section is also the only time this process holds the state
 * lock, so two commands run at once queue up instead of both deciding they
 * are first and overwriting each other's handoff. Released before a tether
 * daemon forks, so it never inherits the lock. */
void ua_crit_enter(void) {
  if (crit_depth++ == 0) {
    char p[PATH_MAX];
    ua_ws_path("Gadget", "lock", p, sizeof(p));
    crit_lock = open(p, O_RDWR | O_CREAT | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC, 0600);
    if (crit_lock >= 0)
      while (flock(crit_lock, LOCK_EX) < 0 && errno == EINTR)
        ;
    sigset_t s;
    sigemptyset(&s);
    sigaddset(&s, SIGINT);
    sigaddset(&s, SIGTERM);
    sigaddset(&s, SIGHUP);
    sigaddset(&s, SIGQUIT);
    sigprocmask(SIG_BLOCK, &s, &crit_old);
  }
}

void ua_crit_leave(void) {
  if (crit_depth > 0 && --crit_depth == 0) {
    if (crit_lock >= 0)
      close(crit_lock);
    crit_lock = -1;
    sigprocmask(SIG_SETMASK, &crit_old, NULL);
  }
}

static int pathf(char *out, size_t size, const char *fmt, ...)
    __attribute__((format(printf, 3, 4)));
static int pathf(char *out, size_t size, const char *fmt, ...) {
  va_list ap;
  va_start(ap, fmt);
  int n = vsnprintf(out, size, fmt, ap);
  va_end(ap);
  return (n < 0 || (size_t)n >= size) ? -1 : 0;
}

int ua_find_configfs(char *out, size_t size) {
  static const char *const roots[] = {"/sys/kernel/config", "/config"};
  for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt++) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(roots) / sizeof(roots[0]); i++) {
      char p[PATH_MAX];
      snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/usb_gadget", roots[i]);
      if (access(p, F_OK) == 0) {
        safe_strncpy(out, p, size);
        return 0;
      }
    }
    /* A plain Linux board often has configfs built but not mounted, and
     * libcomposite as a module. Android always has both ready. The mount
     * loads a modular configfs itself, and fails harmlessly without one. */
    if (attempt == 0)
      mount("none", "/sys/kernel/config", "configfs", 0, NULL);
    if (attempt == 1) {
      char *argv[] = {"modprobe", "libcomposite", NULL};
      run_command_quiet(argv);
    }
  }
  return -1;
}

/* GKI kernels build dummy_hcd in (CONFIG_USB_DUMMY_HCD=y in gki_defconfig),
 * so nearly every Android phone lists a dummy_udc.0 beside its real
 * controller, and it reaches no host. It is left out unless --udc names it
 * (tests/dummy_hcd.sh does): picked by itself whenever the real one is gone
 * (a dual-role port in host mode lists none), it would quietly serve nothing.
 */
static int is_dummy_udc(const char *name) {
  return !strncmp(name, "dummy_udc.", 10) &&
         !(ua_udc_opt && !strcmp(name, ua_udc_opt));
}

int ua_list_udcs(char names[][64], int max) {
  DIR *d = opendir("/sys/class/udc");
  if (!d)
    return 0;
  int n = 0;
  struct dirent *e;
  while ((e = readdir(d)) && n < max)
    if (e->d_name[0] != '.' && !is_dummy_udc(e->d_name))
      safe_strncpy(names[n++], e->d_name, 64);
  closedir(d);
  return n;
}

int ua_pick_udc(char *out, size_t size) {
  char names[16][64];
  int n = ua_list_udcs(names, 16);
  if (n == 0) {
    ua_error("No USB device controller in /sys/class/udc now");
    ua_log("A dual-role port in host mode (OTG) lists none until it is a "
           "device again, and dummy_udc.* counts only when --udc names it. "
           "Otherwise the kernel needs a peripheral-capable controller driver "
           "(on a Raspberry Pi: dtoverlay=dwc2).");
    return -1;
  }
  if (ua_udc_opt) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
      if (!strcmp(names[i], ua_udc_opt)) {
        safe_strncpy(out, names[i], size);
        return 0;
      }
    ua_error("No such UDC now: %s (a typo, or a dual-role port in host mode)",
             ua_udc_opt);
  } else if (n == 1) {
    safe_strncpy(out, names[0], size);
    return 0;
  } else {
    ua_error("More than one USB device controller; pick one with --udc");
  }
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
    ua_log("  %s", names[i]);
  return -1;
}

/* The first config of g1. Android names it b.1, but nothing guarantees it. */
/* Android's configfs gives every gadget an androidN device, all with devt 0,
 * and android_device_destroy() looks its device up by devt: dropping any
 * gadget destroys the oldest, android0, which belongs to g1. Android then
 * stops hearing USB state (no USB notification, tethering greyed out) until a
 * reboot. kernel-patches/ has the kernel fix for 4.9 to 6.6; meanwhile a gadget
 * we made stays, unbound and empty, instead of being removed. */
/* An empty write unbinds a gadget. "none" only does on Android's configfs,
 * which added it; mainline (a Pi, a PC under dummy_hcd) reads it as a
 * controller name and answers EBUSY, since the gadget is still bound. */
#define UNBIND "\n"

static int keep_gadget(void) {
  return access("/sys/class/android_usb", F_OK) == 0;
}

static int first_config(const char *gadget, char *out, size_t size) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  if (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/configs", gadget) < 0)
    return -1;
  DIR *d = opendir(p);
  if (!d)
    return -1;
  struct dirent *e;
  int ret = -1;
  while ((e = readdir(d)))
    if (e->d_name[0] != '.') {
      ret = pathf(out, size, "%s/%s", p, e->d_name);
      break;
    }
  closedir(d);
  return ret;
}

int ua_gadget_open(struct ua_gadget *g) {
  memset(g, 0, sizeof(*g));
  if (ua_find_configfs(g->cfs, sizeof(g->cfs)) < 0) {
    ua_error("configfs USB gadget support not found");
    ua_log("The kernel needs CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS. Run '" UA_NAME
           " check' for the full report.");
    return -1;
  }

  struct handoff h;
  int taken = handoff_load(&h) == 0;
  if (taken && h.udc[0]) {
    /* Stick to the controller we already hold, whatever --udc says now */
    safe_strncpy(g->udc, h.udc, sizeof(g->udc));
  } else if (ua_pick_udc(g->udc, sizeof(g->udc)) < 0) {
    return -1;
  }

  char own[PATH_MAX];
  if (pathf(own, sizeof(own), "%s/" UA_GADGET, g->cfs) < 0)
    return -1;

  /* Asked of the kernel, not of /system: inside a container on a phone (a
   * Droidspaces rootfs, a chroot) is_android() is false, but g1 and the
   * android_usb class are still there and Android still owns the UDC. */
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  g->android_gadget =
      is_android() ||
      (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/g1", g->cfs) == 0 && access(p, F_OK) == 0 &&
       access("/sys/class/android_usb", F_OK) == 0);

  /* Stock Samsung configfs names every gadget's uevent device android0, so a
   * second one fails in device_create() before anything is set up and the
   * mkdir returns ENOMEM. Nothing changes; it is the cheapest detector. The
   * gadget made here is kept (keep_gadget), so probes run inside it. Without
   * android_usb there is no such kernel, and a mkdir and rmdir on every
   * open would race a command's build_skeleton for `status`; begin makes it. */
  if (keep_gadget() && access(own, F_OK) != 0) {
    if (mkdir(own, 0755) < 0 && errno != EEXIST) {
      int err = errno;
      if (err == ENOMEM && g->android_gadget &&
          access("/sys/class/android_usb/android0/functions", F_OK) == 0) {
        ua_error("This is stock Samsung configfs, which cannot create a "
                 "second gadget next to Android's");
        ua_log("It needs the configfs patches in kernel-patches/4.14 or 4.19 "
               "(docs/kernel-requirements.md). Nothing was "
               "changed.");
      } else {
        ua_error("Cannot create a gadget in %s: %s", g->cfs, strerror(err));
      }
      return -1;
    }
  }

  safe_strncpy(g->path, own, sizeof(g->path));
  if (pathf(g->config, sizeof(g->config), "%s/configs/" UA_CONFIG, own) < 0)
    return -1;
  return 0;
}

/* Our functions carry the "ua" instance */
static int is_ours(const char *func) {
  const char *dot = strchr(func, '.');
  return dot && !strncmp(dot + 1, "ua", 2);
}

int ua_gadget_func_dir(const struct ua_gadget *g, const char *func, char *dir,
                       size_t size) {
  return pathf(dir, size, "%s/functions/%s", g->path, func);
}

int ua_gadget_has(const struct ua_gadget *g, const char *func) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  struct stat st;
  return pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/%s", g->config, func) == 0 &&
         lstat(p, &st) == 0;
}

/* A gadget directory whose UDC names a controller */
static int bound(const char *gadget) {
  char p[PATH_MAX], buf[64];
  return pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/UDC", gadget) == 0 &&
         read_file(p, buf, sizeof(buf)) > 0;
}

/* Bound to the controller right now, as far as this tool is concerned */
int ua_gadget_live(const struct ua_gadget *g) {
  return ua_gadget_taken() && bound(g->path);
}

static int build_skeleton(const struct ua_gadget *g) {
  char p[PATH_MAX], v[160];
  struct ua_config c;
  if (mkdir(g->path, 0755) < 0 && errno != EEXIST)
    return -1;
  /* The active profile, or the built-in identity. Written on every take and
   * every rebind, so `identity set` reaches the host at the next enumeration */
  ua_config_active(&c);
  snprintf(v, sizeof(v), "0x%04x", c.id_vendor);
  write_attr(g->path, "idVendor", v);
  snprintf(v, sizeof(v), "0x%04x", c.id_product);
  write_attr(g->path, "idProduct", v);
  snprintf(v, sizeof(v), "0x%04x", c.bcd_device);
  write_attr(g->path, "bcdDevice", v);
  snprintf(v, sizeof(v), "0x%04x", c.bcd_usb);
  write_attr(g->path, "bcdUSB", v);
  /* Misc/IAD: Windows only enumerates a composite with an RNDIS or NCM
   * function properly when the device says it uses interface associations */
  write_attr(g->path, "bDeviceClass", "0xEF");
  write_attr(g->path, "bDeviceSubClass", "0x02");
  write_attr(g->path, "bDeviceProtocol", "0x01");

  if (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/strings/0x409", g->path) < 0 ||
      mkdir_p(p, 0755) < 0)
    return -1;
  write_attr(p, "manufacturer", c.manufacturer);
  write_attr(p, "product", c.product);
  if (!c.serial[0])
    ua_device_seed(c.serial, sizeof(c.serial));
  write_attr(p, "serialnumber", c.serial);

  if (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/strings/0x409", g->config) < 0 ||
      mkdir_p(p, 0755) < 0)
    return -1;
  /* Samsung's configfs treats any configuration string other than "Conf 1" as
   * "symlink change mode" and binds links straight away. Harmless elsewhere. */
  write_attr(p, "configuration", c.configuration);
  snprintf(v, sizeof(v), "%u", c.max_power);
  write_attr(g->config, "MaxPower", v);
  return 0;
}

/* Off Android nobody hands the controller over politely. If another gadget
 * holds it, say who and stop: we do not unbind someone else's gadget. */
static int udc_owner(const struct ua_gadget *g, char *owner, size_t size) {
  DIR *d = opendir(g->cfs);
  if (!d)
    return 0;
  struct dirent *e;
  int found = 0;
  while (!found && (e = readdir(d))) {
    char p[PATH_MAX], buf[64];
    if (e->d_name[0] == '.' || !strcmp(e->d_name, UA_GADGET))
      continue;
    if (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/%s/UDC", g->cfs, e->d_name) == 0 &&
        read_file(p, buf, sizeof(buf)) > 0 && !strcmp(buf, g->udc)) {
      safe_strncpy(owner, e->d_name, size);
      found = 1;
    }
  }
  closedir(d);
  return found;
}

static void android_release(const struct ua_gadget *g) {
  char p[PATH_MAX], buf[64];
  /* Ask init first, so adbd and the HAL stand down instead of rebinding.
   * Without the property service (a container) there is nobody to ask. */
  if (is_android()) {
    ua_debug("setprop sys.usb.config none");
    ua_setprop("sys.usb.config", "none");
    if (ua_wait(ua_getprop, "sys.usb.state", "none", UA_HANDOFF_TIMEOUT_MS) < 0)
      ua_warn("Android did not report sys.usb.state=none in time");
  }
  /* A gadget HAL may not follow the property at all. Take it by hand. */
  if (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/g1/UDC", g->cfs) == 0 &&
      read_file(p, buf, sizeof(buf)) > 0) {
    ua_debug("g1 still bound to %s, unbinding it", buf);
    write_file(p, UNBIND);
  }
}

int ua_gadget_begin(struct ua_gadget *g) {
  ua_crit_enter();

  if (ua_gadget_taken()) {
    /* Already ours: unbind so functions can change. Attributes like the HID
     * report descriptor are locked while the function is in use. */
    if (ua_gadget_live(g))
      write_attr(g->path, "UDC", UNBIND);
    /* Idempotent, and covers a crash between saving the handoff and
     * building the gadget the first time round */
    if (build_skeleton(g) < 0) {
      ua_error("Cannot build the gadget in %s: %s", g->path, strerror(errno));
      ua_crit_leave();
      return -1;
    }
    return 0;
  }

  struct handoff h;
  memset(&h, 0, sizeof(h));
  safe_strncpy(h.udc, g->udc, sizeof(h.udc));
  ua_boot_marker(h.boot, sizeof(h.boot));

  /* Android's gadget but no Android userspace: a container or chroot. Unless
   * Android's workspace is bind-mounted over ours, a copy run from Android
   * (the app) keeps a second hand-back record for the same controller */
  if (g->android_gadget && !is_android())
    ua_warn("Running inside a container: the hand-back record is in %s. "
            "Bind-mount /data/local/USB-Arsenal there, or do not run USB "
            "Arsenal from Android at the same time (see docs/containers.md).",
            ua_workspace());

  char owner[256] = "";
  int owned = udc_owner(g, owner, sizeof(owner));
  if (owned && g->android_gadget && !strcmp(owner, "g1"))
    safe_strncpy(h.g1_udc, g->udc, sizeof(h.g1_udc));
  else if (owned) {
    /* Not Android's: we do not unbind someone else's gadget */
    ua_error("%s is in use by the gadget '%s'", g->udc, owner);
    ua_log("Unbind it first: echo none > %s/%s/UDC", g->cfs, owner);
    ua_crit_leave();
    return -1;
  }

  if (is_android()) {
    ua_getprop("sys.usb.config", h.usb_config, sizeof(h.usb_config));
    if (!h.usb_config[0] || !strcmp(h.usb_config, "none"))
      ua_getprop("persist.sys.usb.config", h.usb_config, sizeof(h.usb_config));
    if (!h.usb_config[0] || !strcmp(h.usb_config, "none"))
      safe_strncpy(h.usb_config, "mtp", sizeof(h.usb_config));
  }
  if (handoff_save(&h) < 0) {
    ua_error("Cannot write the handoff state in %s: %s", ua_workspace(),
             strerror(errno));
    ua_crit_leave();
    return -1;
  }

  if (g->android_gadget)
    android_release(g);
  if (build_skeleton(g) < 0) {
    ua_error("Cannot build the gadget in %s: %s", g->path, strerror(errno));
    ua_gadget_teardown(g);
    ua_crit_leave();
    return -1;
  }
  return 0;
}

int ua_gadget_add(struct ua_gadget *g, const char *func, char *dir,
                  size_t size) {
  if (ua_gadget_func_dir(g, func, dir, size) < 0)
    return -1;
  if (mkdir(dir, 0755) < 0 && errno != EEXIST) {
    int err = errno;
    ua_error("Cannot create function %s: %s", func, strerror(err));
    if (err == ENOENT || err == EINVAL)
      ua_log("The kernel was built without this function. Run '" UA_NAME
             " check'.");
    return -1;
  }
  return 0;
}

/* Out of the config but kept: some attributes (a new LUN, HID descriptors,
 * NCM addresses) can only change while nothing uses the function. Commit
 * links it back. */
void ua_gadget_unlink(struct ua_gadget *g, const char *func) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  if (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/%s", g->config, func) == 0 && unlink(p) < 0 &&
      errno != ENOENT)
    ua_warn("Cannot unlink %s: %s", p, strerror(errno));
}

/* Names of the entries of dir (no dot entries) that pass keep(), read in
 * full before the caller removes any: rmdir during readdir of the same
 * configfs directory may skip entries. */
#define MAX_ENTRIES 64
static int list_dir(const char *dir, char names[][NAME_MAX + 1],
                    int (*keep)(const char *dir, const struct dirent *e)) {
  DIR *d = opendir(dir);
  struct dirent *e;
  int n = 0;
  while (d && n < MAX_ENTRIES && (e = readdir(d)))
    if (e->d_name[0] != '.' && keep(dir, e))
      safe_strncpy(names[n++], e->d_name, NAME_MAX + 1);
  if (d)
    closedir(d);
  return d ? n : -1;
}

static int keep_dir(const char *dir, const struct dirent *e) {
  (void)dir;
  return e->d_type == DT_DIR;
}

static int keep_link(const char *dir, const struct dirent *e) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  struct stat st;
  return pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/%s", dir, e->d_name) == 0 &&
         lstat(p, &st) == 0 && S_ISLNK(st.st_mode);
}

static int keep_ours(const char *dir, const struct dirent *e) {
  (void)dir;
  return is_ours(e->d_name);
}

int ua_gadget_remove(struct ua_gadget *g, const char *func) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  ua_gadget_unlink(g, func);
  if (ua_gadget_func_dir(g, func, p, sizeof(p)) < 0)
    return -1;
  /* Groups made under the function (lun.1 and up) must go first. Its own
   * default groups (lun.0, os_desc) refuse rmdir, which is fine. */
  char names[MAX_ENTRIES][NAME_MAX + 1];
  int n = list_dir(p, names, keep_dir);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    char sub[PATH_MAX];
    if (pathf(sub, sizeof(sub), "%s/%s", p, names[i]) == 0)
      rmdir(sub);
  }
  if (rmdir(p) < 0 && errno != ENOENT) {
    ua_warn("Cannot remove %s: %s", p, strerror(errno));
    return -1;
  }
  return 0;
}

/* Link every function of ours that is not linked yet; returns how many are */
static int link_functions(struct ua_gadget *g) {
  char fdir[PATH_MAX];
  if (pathf(fdir, sizeof(fdir), "%s/functions", g->path) < 0)
    return -1;
  DIR *d = opendir(fdir);
  if (!d)
    return -1;
  int n = 0, failed = 0;
  struct dirent *e;
  while ((e = readdir(d))) {
    char src[PATH_MAX], dst[PATH_MAX];
    if (e->d_name[0] == '.' || !is_ours(e->d_name))
      continue;
    if (pathf(src, sizeof(src), "%s/%s", fdir, e->d_name) < 0 ||
        pathf(dst, sizeof(dst), "%s/%s", g->config, e->d_name) < 0)
      continue;
    if (symlink(src, dst) < 0 && errno != EEXIST) {
      ua_error("Cannot link %s: %s", e->d_name, strerror(errno));
      failed = 1;
      continue;
    }
    n++;
  }
  closedir(d);
  return failed ? -1 : n;
}

/* Android's udc core comments out the pullup after bind on some kernels
 * (the HACK), so the host sees nothing. soft_connect raises it, but its
 * "connect" calls usb_gadget_udc_start() unconditionally before the core
 * learned to track a started UDC (no "started" guard in 4.14). On a dwc3
 * that bind already started, dwc3_gadget_start() requests its IRQ, finds a
 * driver bound, and frees that IRQ on the way out while it is still in use;
 * the next unbind then panics the phone (seen on the S10 with the M62
 * kernel). So: leave it alone when the host is already enumerating us, and
 * otherwise use the balanced pair, disconnect (udc_stop) then connect
 * (udc_start), which never starts a started controller. */
static void pullup(const struct ua_gadget *g) {
  char p[PATH_MAX], st[64];
  if (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "/sys/class/udc/%s/state", g->udc) < 0)
    return;
  for (int waited = 0; waited < UA_PULLUP_WAIT_MS; waited += 100) {
    if (read_file(p, st, sizeof(st)) > 0 && strcmp(st, "not attached") != 0)
      return; /* the host is talking to us: the pullup is up */
    usleep(100000);
  }
  if (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "/sys/class/udc/%s/soft_connect", g->udc) < 0)
    return;
  ua_debug("no enumeration after bind, cycling soft_connect");
  if (write_file(p, "disconnect") < 0 || write_file(p, "connect") < 0)
    ua_debug("soft_connect: %s", strerror(errno));
}

static void wait_configured(const struct ua_gadget *g) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  if (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "/sys/class/udc/%s/state", g->udc) == 0 &&
      ua_wait(read_file, p, "configured", UA_ENUM_TIMEOUT_MS) < 0)
    ua_warn("The host has not configured the gadget yet (is the cable "
            "plugged into a computer?)");
}

int ua_gadget_commit(struct ua_gadget *g) {
  char udc[80];
  int n = link_functions(g);
  if (n < 0)
    goto fail;
  if (n == 0) {
    ua_gadget_teardown(g);
    ua_crit_leave();
    return 0;
  }
  snprintf(udc, sizeof(udc), "%s\n", g->udc);

  if (write_attr(g->path, "UDC", udc) < 0) {
    int err = errno;
    ua_error("Binding to %s failed: %s", g->udc, strerror(err));
    if (err == EINVAL)
      ua_log("Samsung configfs without the bring-up fix (kernel-patches/4.14 "
             "or 4.19) cannot bind a hand-built gadget.");
    else if (err == EBUSY)
      ua_log("Another gadget or a legacy g_* driver holds the controller.");
    goto fail;
  }
  pullup(g);
  wait_configured(g);
  /* Inside the section: a client hangup's SIGTERM must not land mid-chown */
  ua_hid_reapply(g);
  ua_crit_leave();
  return 0;

fail:
  ua_gadget_teardown(g);
  ua_crit_leave();
  return -1;
}

static int unlink_all(const char *dir) {
  char names[MAX_ENTRIES][NAME_MAX + 1], p[PATH_MAX];
  int n = list_dir(dir, names, keep_link);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
    if (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/%s", dir, names[i]) == 0)
      unlink(p);
  return n;
}

/* Our own gadget holds something: bound, or functions linked. A kept, empty
 * gadget (keep_gadget) does not count. */
int ua_gadget_in_use(const char *cfs) {
  char p[PATH_MAX], names[MAX_ENTRIES][NAME_MAX + 1];
  if (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/" UA_GADGET, cfs) == 0 && bound(p))
    return 1;
  return pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/" UA_GADGET "/configs/" UA_CONFIG, cfs) == 0 &&
         list_dir(p, names, keep_link) > 0;
}

static void remove_ours(struct ua_gadget *g) {
  char names[MAX_ENTRIES][NAME_MAX + 1], fdir[PATH_MAX];
  if (pathf(fdir, sizeof(fdir), "%s/functions", g->path) < 0)
    return;
  int n = list_dir(fdir, names, keep_ours);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
    ua_gadget_remove(g, names[i]);
}

/* g1's config has functions linked: Android has set up a mode, and binding
 * it now gives the user that mode instead of an empty device */
static int g1_ready(const struct ua_gadget *g) {
  char g1[PATH_MAX], cfg[PATH_MAX], names[MAX_ENTRIES][NAME_MAX + 1];
  return pathf(g1, sizeof(g1), "%s/g1", g->cfs) == 0 &&
         first_config(g1, cfg, sizeof(cfg)) == 0 &&
         list_dir(cfg, names, keep_link) > 0;
}

static int g1_bound(const struct ua_gadget *g) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  return pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/g1", g->cfs) == 0 && bound(p);
}

static void bind_g1(const struct ua_gadget *g) {
  char p[PATH_MAX], udc[80];
  snprintf(udc, sizeof(udc), "%s\n", g->udc);
  if (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/g1/UDC", g->cfs) == 0 && write_file(p, udc) == 0)
    pullup(g);
  else
    ua_error("Cannot rebind Android's g1 to %s: %s", g->udc, strerror(errno));
}

static void android_restore(const struct ua_gadget *g,
                            const struct handoff *h) {
  if (is_android() && h->usb_config[0]) {
    ua_debug("setprop sys.usb.config %s", h->usb_config);
    ua_setprop("sys.usb.config", h->usb_config);
    /* adb modes also wait for adbd to come back, which takes a while */
    if (ua_wait(ua_getprop, "sys.usb.state", h->usb_config,
                UA_RESTORE_TIMEOUT_MS) < 0)
      ua_debug("sys.usb.state did not reach %s in time", h->usb_config);
  }
  /* No property service (container), or a HAL that ignored it: bind g1
   * ourselves. Only once its functions are linked, or we would race init
   * while it is still relinking and leave g1 bound with nothing in it. */
  if ((h->g1_udc[0] || is_android()) && !g1_bound(g) && g1_ready(g)) {
    if (is_android())
      ua_warn("Android did not rebind g1, binding it by hand");
    bind_g1(g);
  }
}

void ua_gadget_teardown(struct ua_gadget *g) {
  struct handoff h;
  int have = handoff_load(&h) == 0, was_here = 0;
  char p[PATH_MAX];

  ua_crit_enter();
  /* Everything of ours goes, NCM included: its network side must not keep
   * serving an interface that is about to vanish */
  ua_tether_kill();
  if (access(g->path, F_OK) == 0) {
    if (bound(g->path)) {
      write_attr(g->path, "UDC", UNBIND);
      was_here = 1;
    }
    if (unlink_all(g->config) > 0)
      was_here = 1;
    if (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/os_desc", g->path) == 0)
      unlink_all(p);
    remove_ours(g);
    if (!keep_gadget()) {
      if (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/strings/0x409", g->config) == 0)
        rmdir(p);
      rmdir(g->config);
      if (pathf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/strings/0x409", g->path) == 0)
        rmdir(p);
      if (rmdir(g->path) < 0 && errno != ENOENT)
        ua_warn("Cannot remove %s: %s", g->path, strerror(errno));
    }
  }

  if (g->android_gadget) {
    if (have)
      android_restore(g, &h);
    /* Our gadget was there but the record of what we took is gone (a crash
     * between deleting it and finishing, an older version): Android's g1
     * with functions linked and nothing bound can only mean we left it so */
    else if (was_here && !g1_bound(g) && g1_ready(g))
      bind_g1(g);
  }

  /* The record goes only once the controller is really back. If g1 did not
   * come back, keeping it means the next `stop` tries again. */
  if (have && h.g1_udc[0] && !g1_bound(g))
    ua_error("Android's gadget is not bound yet; run '" UA_NAME " stop' again");
  else
    handoff_drop();
  /* Nothing of ours runs any more, whoever started it */
  ua_running_clear(UA_FN_ALL);
  ua_crit_leave();
}

```

`src/gadgets/hid.c`:

```c
/*
 * USB Arsenal - composite USB gadget builder for Linux and Android
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
 *
 * `hid`: a boot-protocol keyboard and mouse through f_hid. Our job ends at
 * /dev/hidgN existing with sane permissions; what gets written there is up
 * to whoever opens it. Descriptors:
 * docs/developer/references/hid-report-descriptors.txt
 */

#include "usbarsenal.h"
#include <grp.h>

#define KBD UA_F_KBD
#define MOUSE UA_F_MOUSE

/* Standard boot keyboard: modifiers, reserved, 6 keycodes, 5 LED outputs.
 * 8-byte input report. */
static const unsigned char kbd_desc[] = {
    0x05, 0x01, 0x09, 0x06, 0xa1, 0x01, 0x05, 0x07, 0x19, 0xe0, 0x29,
    0xe7, 0x15, 0x00, 0x25, 0x01, 0x75, 0x01, 0x95, 0x08, 0x81, 0x02,
    0x95, 0x01, 0x75, 0x08, 0x81, 0x03, 0x95, 0x05, 0x75, 0x01, 0x05,
    0x08, 0x19, 0x01, 0x29, 0x05, 0x91, 0x02, 0x95, 0x01, 0x75, 0x03,
    0x91, 0x03, 0x95, 0x06, 0x75, 0x08, 0x15, 0x00, 0x25, 0x65, 0x05,
    0x07, 0x19, 0x00, 0x29, 0x65, 0x81, 0x00, 0xc0,
};

/* Mouse: 5 buttons, relative X, Y and wheel. 4-byte input report. */
static const unsigned char mouse_desc[] = {
    0x05, 0x01, 0x09, 0x02, 0xa1, 0x01, 0x09, 0x01, 0xa1, 0x00, 0x05,
    0x09, 0x19, 0x01, 0x29, 0x05, 0x15, 0x00, 0x25, 0x01, 0x95, 0x05,
    0x75, 0x01, 0x81, 0x02, 0x95, 0x01, 0x75, 0x03, 0x81, 0x01, 0x05,
    0x01, 0x09, 0x30, 0x09, 0x31, 0x09, 0x38, 0x15, 0x81, 0x25, 0x7f,
    0x75, 0x08, 0x95, 0x03, 0x81, 0x06, 0xc0, 0xc0,
};

struct hid_fn {
  const char *func, *label, *protocol, *report_length;
  const unsigned char *desc;
  size_t desc_len;
};

static const struct hid_fn fns[] = {
    {KBD, "keyboard", "1", "8", kbd_desc, sizeof(kbd_desc)},
    {MOUSE, "mouse", "2", "4", mouse_desc, sizeof(mouse_desc)},
};

void ua_help_hid(void) {
  printf(
      "Usage: " UA_NAME " hid <action> [options]\n\n"
      "Add a USB keyboard and mouse to the gadget. The host sees real HID\n"
      "devices; this side gets two character devices to write reports to.\n"
      "What you write there is up to you.\n\n"
      "Actions:\n"
      "  start   Create the keyboard and mouse and print which /dev/hidgN\n"
      "          is which. --interval is saved as the setup (see `setup`);\n"
      "          without it, the saved one applies.\n"
      "  apply   Restart with the setup's interval if it changed, in one\n"
      "          replug; start if not running\n"
      "  stop    Remove them\n"
      "  write NODE SIZE\n"
      "          Copy reports of SIZE bytes (1 to 64) from stdin to NODE, a\n"
      "          /dev/hidgN, without ever blocking: while the host is not\n"
      "          reading, only the newest unsent report is kept, and it goes\n"
      "          out as soon as the host reads again. Exits 0 at the end of\n"
      "          stdin once the last report went out (a second at most),\n"
      "          non-zero when it did not or NODE fails (the host went "
      "away).\n\n"
      "Options:\n"
      "  -p, --perm MODE    Octal permissions for the nodes (default: 0660)\n"
      "  -g, --group GROUP  Group owning the nodes, name or GID (default:\n"
      "                     root). Anyone who can write a node can type on\n"
      "                     the host, so widen this deliberately.\n"
      "  -i, --interval N   Keyboard poll interval, 1 to 255 (needs the f_hid\n"
      "                     patch). Lower is faster: at high speed the period\n"
      "                     is 2^(N-1) x 125us, so 4 (the kernel default) is\n"
      "                     1 ms and 1 is 125us. Set at start; stop to "
      "change.\n"
      "  -h, --help         Show this help\n\n"
      "Reports:\n"
      "  keyboard  8 bytes: modifiers, 0, then up to 6 HID keycodes\n"
      "  mouse     4 bytes: buttons, X, Y, wheel (signed)\n\n"
      "Examples:\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " hid start\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " hid start --group input\n"
      "  # type 'a' on the host (press, then release):\n"
      "  printf '\\0\\0\\x04\\0\\0\\0\\0\\0' > /dev/hidg0\n"
      "  printf '\\0\\0\\0\\0\\0\\0\\0\\0' > /dev/hidg0\n"
      "  # move the mouse 10 px right:\n"
      "  printf '\\0\\x0a\\0\\0' > /dev/hidg1\n"
      "  # or keep one writer open for a stream of reports:\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " hid write /dev/hidg1 4 < reports\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " hid stop\n");
}

/* f_hid locks its attributes once the function is in a config, so this must
 * run before commit links it */
static int setup_fn(struct ua_gadget *g, const struct hid_fn *f, int *created,
                    unsigned interval) {
  char dir[PATH_MAX], ip[PATH_MAX];
  ua_gadget_func_dir(g, f->func, dir, sizeof(dir));
  snprintf(ip, sizeof(ip), "%s/interval", dir);
  /* No interval asked is the kernel's default, and only a fresh function has
   * it: one a crash left behind holds the last start's value, and no value
   * written means "default" everywhere (0 is our patch's default, but
   * mainline's own attribute takes it as bInterval 0, which hosts drop) */
  if (!interval && access(ip, F_OK) == 0)
    ua_gadget_remove(g, f->func);
  *created = access(dir, F_OK) != 0;
  if (ua_gadget_add(g, f->func, dir, sizeof(dir)) < 0)
    return -1;
  /* Already there and linked from an earlier start: out of the config for
   * the writes, commit puts it back */
  ua_gadget_unlink(g, f->func);
  if (write_attr_buf(dir, "protocol", f->protocol, 1) < 0 ||
      write_attr_buf(dir, "subclass", "1", 1) < 0 ||
      write_attr_buf(dir, "report_length", f->report_length, 1) < 0 ||
      write_attr_buf(dir, "report_desc", f->desc, f->desc_len) < 0) {
    ua_error("Cannot configure the %s: %s", f->label, strerror(errno));
    return -1;
  }
  /* The interrupt endpoint's bInterval is set by the kernel's f_hid, not the
   * report descriptor. Stock f_hid hardcodes it (1 ms at high speed); our patch
   * and mainline (6.x) add a writable "interval" attribute, so write it when
   * one was asked and it is there, and fall back with a note when it is not */
  if (!interval)
    return 0;
  if (access(ip, F_OK) != 0) {
    ua_warn("This kernel has no f_hid 'interval' control; --interval needs the "
            "USB Arsenal f_hid patch. Using the kernel default.");
  } else {
    char v[8];
    int n = snprintf(v, sizeof(v), "%u", interval);
    if (write_attr_buf(dir, "interval", v, (size_t)n) < 0) {
      ua_error("Cannot set the %s poll interval: %s", f->label,
               strerror(errno));
      return -1;
    }
  }
  return 0;
}

/* The function's "dev" attribute is major:minor; the node name is up to
 * ueventd/udev/devtmpfs, so find it by device number, not by guessing. */
static int find_node(const struct ua_gadget *g, const char *func, char *out,
                     size_t size, int tries) {
  char dir[PATH_MAX], p[PATH_MAX + 8], dev[32];
  unsigned int maj, min;
  ua_gadget_func_dir(g, func, dir, sizeof(dir));
  snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/dev", dir);
  if (read_file(p, dev, sizeof(dev)) <= 0 ||
      sscanf(dev, "%u:%u", &maj, &min) != 2)
    return -1;
  /* The node shows up a moment after bind, when the device manager has run;
   * a bind waits up to [tries] tenths of a second for it, a read looks once */
  while (tries-- > 0) {
    DIR *d = opendir("/dev");
    struct dirent *e;
    while (d && (e = readdir(d))) {
      struct stat st;
      if (strncmp(e->d_name, "hidg", 4) != 0)
        continue;
      snprintf(out, size, "/dev/%s", e->d_name);
      if (stat(out, &st) == 0 && S_ISCHR(st.st_mode) &&
          major(st.st_rdev) == maj && minor(st.st_rdev) == min) {
        closedir(d);
        return 0;
      }
    }
    if (d)
      closedir(d);
    if (tries)
      usleep(100000);
  }
  return -1;
}

static void perm_path(char *out, size_t size) {
  ua_ws_path("Gadget", "hid.perm", out, size);
}

/* Only a --perm or --group given to a start is saved: a bare start (the
 * app's, an apply) must not put the profile's back over it. Without a saved
 * one, the profile's applies. The file goes with the HID function
 * (ua_running_clear). */
static void save_perm(mode_t perm, gid_t gid) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  perm_path(p, sizeof(p));
  int fd = open(p, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC, 0600);
  if (fd < 0)
    return;
  dprintf(fd, "%o %u\n", (unsigned)perm, (unsigned)gid);
  close(fd);
}

/* The access in force: what a start was given, else the profile's */
static void load_perm(unsigned *perm, unsigned *gid) {
  char p[PATH_MAX], buf[64];
  struct ua_config c;
  ua_config_active(&c);
  *perm = c.hid_perm;
  *gid = c.hid_group;
  perm_path(p, sizeof(p));
  if (read_file(p, buf, sizeof(buf)) > 0)
    sscanf(buf, "%o %u", perm, gid);
}

/* Every unbind destroys /dev/hidgN and every bind makes it again, as
 * 0600 root, so the requested access is re-applied after each commit, not
 * only by `hid start` */
static int apply_perm(const struct ua_gadget *g, int report) {
  unsigned perm, gid;
  int ret = 0;
  /* Every commit comes here; only one with HID needs the profile read */
  if (!ua_gadget_has(g, KBD) && !ua_gadget_has(g, MOUSE))
    return 0;
  load_perm(&perm, &gid);
  for (size_t i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
    char node[PATH_MAX];
    if (!ua_gadget_has(g, fns[i].func))
      continue;
    if (find_node(g, fns[i].func, node, sizeof(node), 20) < 0) {
      ua_warn("The %s is bound but its /dev/hidgN node did not appear",
              fns[i].label);
      ret = -1;
      continue;
    }
    if (chown(node, 0, (gid_t)gid) < 0 || chmod(node, (mode_t)perm) < 0)
      ua_warn("Cannot set permissions on %s: %s", node, strerror(errno));
    if (report)
      ua_log("%-8s %s", fns[i].label, node);
  }
  return ret;
}

void ua_hid_reapply(const struct ua_gadget *g) { apply_perm(g, 0); }

static gid_t parse_group(const char *s, int *ok) {
  char *end;
  long v = strtol(s, &end, 10);
  *ok = 1;
  if (*s && !*end && v >= 0)
    return (gid_t)v;
  /* By name through /etc/group; Android has none, so numbers only there */
  struct group *gr = getgrnam(s);
  *ok = gr != NULL;
  return gr ? gr->gr_gid : 0;
}

static int do_start(mode_t perm, gid_t gid, int perm_given, unsigned interval) {
  struct ua_gadget g;
  if (ua_gadget_open(&g) < 0 || ua_check_requirements(&g, UA_NEED_HID) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;

  /* Saved before commit, which re-applies it after the bind */
  if (perm_given)
    save_perm(perm, gid);
  if (!(ua_gadget_has(&g, KBD) && ua_gadget_has(&g, MOUSE) &&
        ua_gadget_live(&g))) {
    int created[2] = {0, 0};
    if (ua_gadget_begin(&g) < 0)
      return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
    /* The interval is about typing speed, so it rides on the keyboard only. */
    for (size_t i = 0; i < 2; i++)
      if (setup_fn(&g, &fns[i], &created[i], i == 0 ? interval : 0) < 0) {
        /* Undo only what this call made */
        for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; j++)
          if (created[j])
            ua_gadget_remove(&g, fns[j].func);
        ua_gadget_commit(&g);
        return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
      }
    if (ua_gadget_commit(&g) < 0)
      return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  } else if (interval) {
    /* Already running: the interval only changes with a restart, so a start
     * that asked for another one has not done what it was asked. The app
     * reads the exit code, not the warning. */
    char dir[PATH_MAX], p[PATH_MAX + 16], v[16] = "";
    ua_gadget_func_dir(&g, KBD, dir, sizeof(dir));
    snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/interval", dir);
    if (read_file(p, v, sizeof(v)) > 0 && strtoul(v, NULL, 10) != interval) {
      ua_error("HID is already running with interval %s; '" UA_NAME
               " hid apply' restarts it with %u",
               v, interval);
      return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
    }
  }
  if (apply_perm(&g, 1) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  ua_running_take(UA_FN_HID, 0);
  return UA_EXIT_OK;
}

static int do_stop(void) {
  struct ua_gadget g;
  if (ua_gadget_open(&g) < 0 || ua_check_requirements(&g, 0) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  if (!ua_gadget_has(&g, KBD) && !ua_gadget_has(&g, MOUSE)) {
    ua_log("HID is not running");
    return UA_EXIT_OK;
  }
  if (ua_gadget_begin(&g) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  ua_gadget_remove(&g, KBD);
  ua_gadget_remove(&g, MOUSE);
  if (ua_gadget_commit(&g) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  ua_log("HID removed");
  ua_running_clear(UA_FN_HID);
  return UA_EXIT_OK;
}

/* Bring HID to its setup: nothing when it runs unchanged, a swap inside one
 * critical section when the interval changed (one replug of the whole
 * gadget, as configfs swaps a function only unbound, but the port never goes
 * back to Android), a start when it is not running */
static int do_apply(mode_t perm, gid_t gid, int perm_given, unsigned interval) {
  struct ua_setup s, r;
  struct ua_gadget g;
  ua_setup_load(&s);
  ua_running_load(&r);
  if (ua_gadget_open(&g) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  if (!(ua_gadget_has(&g, KBD) && ua_gadget_live(&g)))
    return do_start(perm, gid, perm_given, interval);
  if (!ua_setup_pending(UA_FN_HID, &s, &r)) {
    ua_log("HID already runs its setup");
    return UA_EXIT_OK;
  }
  if (ua_gadget_begin(&g) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  ua_gadget_remove(&g, KBD);
  ua_gadget_remove(&g, MOUSE);
  int ret = do_start(perm, gid, perm_given, interval);
  if (ua_gadget_live(&g))
    ua_crit_leave();
  else
    ua_gadget_commit(&g);
  return ret;
}

/* JSON: the elements of an array, one object per live node */
void ua_status_hid(const struct ua_gadget *g, int json) {
  int sep = 0;
  for (size_t i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
    char node[PATH_MAX];
    if (!ua_gadget_has(g, fns[i].func))
      continue;
    if (find_node(g, fns[i].func, node, sizeof(node), 1) < 0)
      node[0] = '\0';
