```c
    if (json) {
      /* The poll interval the function runs with: what the patched f_hid's
       * attribute holds (0 for its default, 1 ms), or -1 where the kernel
       * has no control for it (stock f_hid), so a client shows what the host
       * gets */
      char dir[PATH_MAX], p[PATH_MAX + 16], v[16] = "";
      long interval = -1;
      if (ua_gadget_func_dir(g, fns[i].func, dir, sizeof(dir)) == 0) {
        snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/interval", dir);
        if (read_file(p, v, sizeof(v)) > 0)
          interval = strtol(v, NULL, 10);
      }
      int first = 1;
      printf("%s{", sep++ ? "," : "");
      ua_json_str("function", fns[i].label, &first);
      ua_json_str("node", node, &first);
      ua_json_int("interval", interval, &first);
      printf("}");
    } else {
      printf("HID:        %-8s %s\n", fns[i].label,
             node[0] ? node : "(no node)");
    }
  }
}

/* 1 sent, 0 the host has not taken the last report yet, -1 failed */
static int send_report(int fd, const unsigned char *r, size_t size) {
  ssize_t n;
  while ((n = write(fd, r, size)) < 0 && errno == EINTR)
    ;
  return n >= 0 ? 1 : errno == EAGAIN ? 0 : -1;
}

/* hid write NODE SIZE: the reports on stdin, SIZE bytes each, onto NODE.
 * f_hid sends one report per write and, opened non-blocking, answers EAGAIN
 * while the host has not taken the one before. Nothing queues here: an unsent
 * report is replaced by the next, so while the writer runs the host ends in
 * the latest state (a release is not lost behind a press), and a host waking
 * from sleep gets no backlog replayed. No lock: it only writes a node the
 * caller can open. */
static int do_write(const char *node, const char *size_arg) {
  unsigned char rep[64], pend[64];
  struct stat st;
  char *end;
  unsigned long size = strtoul(size_arg, &end, 10);
  int fd, pending = 0, eof = 0, r;
  if (!*size_arg || *end || size < 1 || size > sizeof(rep)) {
    ua_usage_error("hid", "write takes a report SIZE of 1 to 64 bytes");
    return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
  }
  /* Asked before the open, which has side effects on some devices */
  if (stat(node, &st) == 0 && !S_ISCHR(st.st_mode)) {
    ua_error("%s is not a character device", node);
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  }
  if ((fd = open(node, O_WRONLY | O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC)) < 0) {
    ua_error("%s: %s", node, strerror(errno));
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  }
  while (!eof) {
    struct pollfd p[2] = {{STDIN_FILENO, POLLIN, 0}, {fd, POLLOUT, 0}};
    if (poll(p, pending ? 2 : 1, -1) < 0) {
      if (errno == EINTR)
        continue;
      goto fail;
    }
    if (p[0].revents) {
      size_t got = 0;
      ssize_t n;
      while (got < size) {
        if ((n = read(STDIN_FILENO, rep + got, size - got)) < 0 &&
            errno == EINTR)
          continue;
        if (n <= 0) {
          eof = 1; /* a report cut short by the end is dropped */
          break;
        }
        got += (size_t)n;
      }
      if (got == size) {
        memcpy(pend, rep, size);
        pending = 1;
      }
    }
    if (pending && (r = send_report(fd, pend, size)) < 0)
      goto fail;
    if (pending)
      pending = r == 0;
  }
  /* stdin is done: the newest report still goes, a second at most. A host
   * that takes nothing that long never gets it (a release among them), which
   * is a failure, not a clean end */
  if (pending) {
    struct pollfd p = {fd, POLLOUT, 0};
    poll(&p, 1, 1000);
    if ((r = send_report(fd, pend, size)) < 0)
      goto fail;
    if (r == 0) {
      ua_error("%s: the host did not take the last report", node);
      close(fd);
      return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
    }
  }
  close(fd);
  return UA_EXIT_OK;

fail:
  ua_error("%s: %s", node, strerror(errno));
  close(fd);
  return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
}

int ua_cmd_hid(int argc, char **argv) {
  static const struct option opts[] = {
      {"perm", required_argument, NULL, 'p'},
      {"group", required_argument, NULL, 'g'},
      {"interval", required_argument, NULL, 'i'},
      {"help", no_argument, NULL, 'h'},
      {NULL, 0, NULL, 0},
  };
  struct ua_setup s;
  int c, ok, edited = 0, perm_given = 0;
  unsigned cur_perm, cur_gid;
  char *end;
  if (argc < 2 || ua_want_help(argc, argv)) {
    ua_help_hid();
    return UA_EXIT_OK;
  }
  if (!strcmp(argv[1], "write")) {
    if (argc != 4) {
      ua_usage_error("hid", "write takes NODE and SIZE");
      return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
    }
    return do_write(argv[2], argv[3]);
  }
  ua_setup_load(&s);
  /* A --perm alone keeps the group in force, and the other way round */
  load_perm(&cur_perm, &cur_gid);
  mode_t perm = (mode_t)cur_perm;
  gid_t gid = (gid_t)cur_gid;
  while ((c = getopt_long(argc, argv, ":p:g:i:h", opts, NULL)) != -1) {
    switch (c) {
    case 'p':
      perm = (mode_t)strtoul(optarg, &end, 8);
      if (!*optarg || *end || perm > 0777) {
        ua_usage_error("hid", "--perm takes an octal mode like 0660");
        return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
      }
      perm_given = 1;
      break;
    case 'i': {
      unsigned long v = strtoul(optarg, &end, 10);
      if (!*optarg || *end || v < 1 || v > 255) {
        ua_usage_error(
            "hid", "--interval takes 1 to 255 (the HID poll interval; at high "
                   "speed the period is 2^(N-1) x 125us, so 1 is 125us)");
        return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
      }
      /* Saved as the setup, so a bare start keeps it */
      s.hid_interval = (unsigned)v;
      edited = 1;
      break;
    }
    case 'g':
      gid = parse_group(optarg, &ok);
      if (!ok) {
        ua_usage_error("hid", "Unknown group '%s'", optarg);
        return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
      }
      perm_given = 1;
      break;
    case 'h':
      ua_help_hid();
      return UA_EXIT_OK;
    case ':':
      ua_usage_error("hid", "Option '%s' needs a value", argv[optind - 1]);
      return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
    default:
      ua_usage_error("hid", "Bad option '%s'", ua_bad_option(argv));
      return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
    }
  }
  if (argc - optind != 1) {
    ua_usage_error("hid",
                   argc - optind ? "Too many arguments" : "Missing action");
    return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
  }
  if (edited && ua_setup_save(&s) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  unsigned interval = s.hid_interval; /* 0 = leave the kernel's default */
  if (!strcmp(argv[optind], "start"))
    return do_start(perm, gid, perm_given, interval);
  if (!strcmp(argv[optind], "apply"))
    return do_apply(perm, gid, perm_given, interval);
  if (!strcmp(argv[optind], "stop"))
    return do_stop();
  ua_usage_error("hid", "Unknown action '%s'", argv[optind]);
  return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
}
```

`src/gadgets/storage.c`:

```c
/*
 * USB Arsenal - composite USB gadget builder for Linux and Android
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
 *
 * `storage`: f_mass_storage LUNs. Booting an ISO is entirely the kernel's
 * job; we only pick between CD-ROM and disk mode and write the attributes in
 * the order the kernel accepts. See
 * docs/developer/research/03-mass-storage-cdrom.md.
 */

#include "usbarsenal.h"
#include <linux/loop.h>
#include <sys/xattr.h>

#define FUNC UA_F_STORAGE

/* The profile's SCSI inquiry string, empty for the kernel's own */
static char inquiry[32];

/* storage_common.c clamps a CD-ROM to 256*60*75-1 frames of 2048 bytes on
 * every kernel we support, and only logs it. Past this the host reads a
 * silently truncated disc. */
#define CDROM_MAX_BYTES ((long long)(256 * 60 * 75 - 1) * 2048)
#define CDROM_MIN_BYTES (300LL * 2048)

enum mode { MODE_AUTO, MODE_CDROM, MODE_DVD, MODE_DISK, MODE_RW };
static const char *const mode_names[] = {"auto", "cdrom", "dvd", "disk", "rw"};
#define NMODES (int)(sizeof(mode_names) / sizeof(mode_names[0]))

static int mode_of(const char *name) {
  for (int i = 0; i < NMODES; i++)
    if (!strcmp(name, mode_names[i]))
      return i;
  return -1;
}

#ifndef LOOP_SET_BLOCK_SIZE
#define LOOP_SET_BLOCK_SIZE 0x4C09
#endif

void ua_help_storage(void) {
  printf(
      "Usage: " UA_NAME " storage <action> [options] [IMAGE]\n"
      "       " UA_NAME " storage start [--lun N] [--mode MODE] IMAGE "
      "[[--lun N] [--mode MODE] IMAGE ...]\n\n"
      "Present an image file or block device to the host as a USB drive.\n"
      "A bootable ISO boots on the host like a real USB stick or DVD.\n\n"
      "Actions:\n"
      "  start [IMAGE] Insert IMAGE. If the LUN already holds an image, swap\n"
      "                it in place without the host re-enumerating the "
      "device.\n"
      "                The IMAGEs given are saved as the setup (see `setup`);\n"
      "                with none, the saved setup starts.\n"
      "  apply         Bring the drives to the setup: eject what it dropped,\n"
      "                load what it changed or added, leave the rest alone\n"
      "  eject         Take the medium out; the host sees an empty drive\n"
      "  stop          Remove the USB drive from the gadget entirely\n\n"
      "Options:\n"
      "  -m, --mode MODE  How the host sees the image (default: auto)\n"
      "                     auto   disk if the image has an MBR or GPT\n"
      "                            (isohybrid Linux ISOs, USB images),\n"
      "                            CD-ROM otherwise, dvd past the CD-ROM\n"
      "                            limit (Windows ISOs)\n"
      "                     cdrom  read-only CD-ROM, boots plain ISO9660/UDF\n"
      "                            via El Torito. Limit: about 2.36 GB.\n"
      "                     dvd    read-only disk with 2048-byte sectors, for\n"
      "                            plain ISOs of any size. UEFI boots it via\n"
      "                            El Torito and Windows reads its UDF.\n"
      "                            Needs kernel 4.14+ (loop block size).\n"
      "                     disk   read-only disk\n"
      "                     rw     writable disk: a pen drive the host can\n"
      "                            write to. Never use on a mounted image.\n"
      "  -l, --lun N      LUN to use, 0-7 (default: 0). Each LUN is a\n"
      "                   separate drive on the host.\n"
      "                   start takes up to eight IMAGEs at once, each\n"
      "                   after its own --lun and --mode, and the host\n"
      "                   sees all of them in one replug. An IMAGE with\n"
      "                   no --lun takes the LUN after the one before.\n"
      "  -h, --help       Show this help\n\n"
      "Examples:\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " storage start ubuntu-24.04.iso\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " storage start --mode dvd Win11.iso\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " storage start --mode rw /data/local/tmp/pendrive.img\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " storage start --lun 1 --mode disk rescue.img\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " storage start Win11.iso --mode rw pendrive.img\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " storage start fedora.iso     # swaps the live image\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " storage start                # what `setup show` lists\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " storage eject\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " storage stop\n\n"
      "Make a blank 4 GB pen drive image:\n"
      "  truncate -s 4G pendrive.img\n");
}

/* An MBR or GPT means the image boots as a disk: isohybrid ISOs carry one
 * for exactly that reason. A plain ISO9660 image starts with 32 KB of zeros,
 * so it gets CD-ROM mode, the only way it can boot. */
static enum mode detect_mode(int fd) {
  unsigned char buf[1024];
  if (pread(fd, buf, sizeof(buf), 0) != (ssize_t)sizeof(buf))
    return MODE_CDROM;
  if (buf[510] == 0x55 && buf[511] == 0xAA)
    return MODE_DISK;
  if (!memcmp(buf + 512, "EFI PART", 8))
    return MODE_DISK;
  return MODE_CDROM;
}

static int open_image(const char *image, enum mode mode);

static int lun_dir(const char *fdir, int lun, char *out, size_t size) {
  int n = snprintf(out, size, "%s/lun.%d", fdir, lun);
  return (n < 0 || (size_t)n >= size) ? -1 : 0;
}

/* A dvd LUN holds a loop device rather than the image itself */
static int is_loop(const char *file) {
  const char *base = strrchr(file, '/');
  return base && !strncmp(base + 1, "loop", 4);
}

/* Eject. "\n" rather than "": a zero-length write never reaches the store
 * function. forced_eject (6.6+) also clears a host's medium lock. */
static int lun_eject(const char *ldir) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/forced_eject", ldir);
  if (access(p, F_OK) == 0)
    return write_file(p, "1");
  return write_attr(ldir, "file", "\n");
}

/* Tenths of a second that every eject wait of one command shares. A host's
 * medium lock lets go once the kernel has processed the disconnect, which
 * every LUN sees at once; eight locked LUNs waiting in turn would add up past
 * the app's 30 s timeout, whose kill lands mid-commit. */
static int eject_budget = 50;

/* Eject, retrying while EBUSY as long as the budget lasts */
static int lun_eject_wait(const char *ldir) {
  int r;
  while ((r = lun_eject(ldir)) < 0 && errno == EBUSY && eject_budget > 0) {
    eject_budget--;
    usleep(100000);
  }
  return r;
}

/* Write order matters: cdrom and ro return EBUSY while a file is open, so
 * the medium goes out first and the new one goes in last. */
/* Returns -EBUSY, quietly, when the host holds a medium lock: the caller
 * decides whether a rebind (which clears it) is the way out. With wait set
 * the eject is retried while the kernel processes that disconnect. A medium
 * the kernel refuses puts the old one back. */
static int lun_load(const char *ldir, const char *path, enum mode mode,
                    int wait) {
  char cur[PATH_MAX] = "", file[PATH_MAX + 2], ro[4] = "", cdrom[4] = "";
  int old = -1, r = -1;
  snprintf(file, sizeof(file), "%s/file", ldir);
  if (read_file(file, cur, sizeof(cur)) > 0) {
    /* Held across the swap so it can go back in: a dvd LUN's loop device
     * would detach on eject (autoclear) with nobody else holding it */
    snprintf(file, sizeof(file), "%s/ro", ldir);
    read_file(file, ro, sizeof(ro));
    snprintf(file, sizeof(file), "%s/cdrom", ldir);
    read_file(file, cdrom, sizeof(cdrom));
    old = open(cur, (ro[0] == '0' ? O_RDWR : O_RDONLY) | O_CLOEXEC);
    if ((wait ? lun_eject_wait(ldir) : lun_eject(ldir)) < 0) {
      r = errno == EBUSY ? -EBUSY : -1;
      goto out;
    }
  }
  write_attr(ldir, "removable", "1");
  if (inquiry[0])
    write_attr(ldir, "inquiry_string", inquiry);
  if (write_attr(ldir, "cdrom", mode == MODE_CDROM ? "1" : "0") < 0 &&
      mode == MODE_CDROM) {
    ua_error("This kernel cannot emulate a CD-ROM (no lun.N/cdrom)");
    goto restore;
  }
  write_attr(ldir, "ro", mode == MODE_RW ? "0" : "1");

  snprintf(file, sizeof(file), "%s\n", path);
  if (write_attr(ldir, "file", file) < 0) {
    ua_error("The kernel refused %s: %s", path, strerror(errno));
    goto restore;
  }
  r = 0;
  goto out;

restore:
  if (old >= 0) {
    if (cdrom[0])
      write_attr(ldir, "cdrom", cdrom);
    if (ro[0])
      write_attr(ldir, "ro", ro);
    snprintf(file, sizeof(file), "/proc/self/fd/%d\n", old);
    if (write_attr(ldir, "file", file) == 0)
      ua_log("Put %s back", cur);
    else
      ua_warn("Cannot put %s back: %s", cur, strerror(errno));
  }
out:
  if (old >= 0)
    close(old);
  return r;
}

/* f_mass_storage reads the image from a kernel thread, so SELinux checks the
 * kernel's domain against the image's label, not ours. Android's policy lets
 * it at user storage (/sdcard, /data) but not at tmpfs or an unlabeled
 * filesystem such as a container's rootfs: the host then gets "unrecovered
 * read error" on every sector, and the only log is a dontaudit nobody sees.
 * So ask the policy itself, on any distro, instead of trusting a label list. */
#define UA_STORAGE_LABEL "u:object_r:media_rw_data_file:s0"

/* The kernel's own context, from kthreadd (kernel_t on Fedora, kernel on
 * Android). In a PID namespace /proc/2 is someone else; Android's name is
 * then the only safe guess, and elsewhere we do not ask. */
static int kernel_context(char *out, size_t size, int android) {
  char comm[32] = "";
  if (read_file("/proc/2/comm", comm, sizeof(comm)) > 0 &&
      !strncmp(comm, "kthreadd", 8) &&
      read_file("/proc/2/attr/current", out, size) > 0) {
    out[strcspn(out, "\n")] = '\0';
    return 0;
  }
  if (!android)
    return -1;
  safe_strncpy(out, "u:r:kernel:s0", size);
  return 0;
}

static int perm_bit(const char *cls, const char *perm) {
  char p[96], v[16];
  snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "/sys/fs/selinux/class/%s/perms/%s", cls, perm);
  return read_file(p, v, sizeof(v)) > 0 ? atoi(v) : 0;
}

/* May the kernel read (and with rw, write) what fd is, as class cls ("file",
 * "blk_file")? 1 when it may or when there is nothing to ask. label gets the
 * object's label for the caller's message. */
static int kernel_may(int fd, const char *cls, int rw, int android, char *label,
                      size_t lsize) {
  char kctx[256], q[600], ans[96], v[16], p[96];
  label[0] = '\0';
  /* The policy answers the same in permissive mode, so a denial only counts
   * when it is enforced: not with SELinux permissive, nor in a permissive
   * domain (the reply's flags). Labels can outlive SELinux (a kernel booted
   * with it off still reads them from disk), so ask whether it is running,
   * not whether a file has one. */
  if (read_file("/sys/fs/selinux/enforce", v, sizeof(v)) <= 0 || v[0] == '0')
    return 1;
  ssize_t n = fgetxattr(fd, "security.selinux", label, lsize - 1);
  if (n <= 0)
    return 1;
  label[n] = '\0';
  snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "/sys/fs/selinux/class/%s/index", cls);
  int idx = read_file(p, v, sizeof(v)) > 0 ? atoi(v) : 0;
  int rd = perm_bit(cls, "read"), wr = perm_bit(cls, "write");
  if (idx <= 0 || rd <= 0 || kernel_context(kctx, sizeof(kctx), android) < 0)
    return 1;
  int afd = open("/sys/fs/selinux/access", O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC);
  if (afd < 0)
    return 1;
  int len = snprintf(q, sizeof(q), "%s %s %d", kctx, label, idx), ok = 1;
  if (write(afd, q, len) == len && (n = read(afd, ans, sizeof(ans) - 1)) > 0) {
    unsigned long allowed = 0, flags = 0;
    ans[n] = '\0';
    /* allowed decided auditallow auditdeny seqno flags */
    sscanf(ans, "%lx %*x %*x %*x %*u %lx", &allowed, &flags);
    ok = (allowed >> (rd - 1)) & 1;
    if (rw && wr > 0)
      ok = ok && ((allowed >> (wr - 1)) & 1);
    if (flags & 1) /* AVD_FLAGS_PERMISSIVE */
      ok = 1;
  }
  close(afd);
  return ok;
}

static void selinux_fix(int fd, const char *path, int rw, int android) {
  char label[256];
  if (kernel_may(fd, "file", rw, android, label, sizeof(label)))
    return;
  /* Android has one label every policy lets the kernel at; other distros do
   * not, so there it is the user's call */
  if (android && fsetxattr(fd, "security.selinux", UA_STORAGE_LABEL,
                           sizeof(UA_STORAGE_LABEL), 0) == 0)
    ua_log("Relabelled %s (%s -> %s) so the kernel may read it", path, label,
           UA_STORAGE_LABEL);
  else if (android)
    ua_warn("%s is labelled %s, which Android's SELinux policy does not let "
            "the kernel read; the host will see read errors (%s). Move it to "
            "/sdcard or /data.",
            path, label, strerror(errno));
  else
    ua_warn("SELinux does not let the kernel read %s (labelled %s); the host "
            "will see read errors. Relabel it (chcon) or move it.",
            path, label);
}

/* A loop device node: ueventd (or udev) makes it a moment after the kernel
 * creates the device, so wait for it before making one ourselves. The minor
 * comes from sysfs, since loop.max_part spaces them out. */
static int loop_open(int n, char *dev, size_t size) {
  for (int tries = 0; tries < 20; tries++) {
    snprintf(dev, size, "/dev/block/loop%d", n);
    if (access(dev, F_OK) != 0)
      snprintf(dev, size, "/dev/loop%d", n);
    int fd = open(dev, O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC);
    if (fd >= 0 || errno != ENOENT)
      return fd;
    usleep(50000);
  }
  char p[64], v[32];
  unsigned maj, min;
  snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "/sys/block/loop%d/dev", n);
  if (read_file(p, v, sizeof(v)) <= 0 || sscanf(v, "%u:%u", &maj, &min) != 2)
    return -1;
  snprintf(
      dev, size,
      access("/dev/block", F_OK) == 0 ? "/dev/block/loop%d" : "/dev/loop%d", n);
  mknod(dev, S_IFBLK | 0600, makedev(maj, min));
  return open(dev, O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC);
}

/* dvd mode: the image behind a read-only loop device with 2048-byte blocks.
 * f_mass_storage then reports 2048-byte sectors, the geometry a plain ISO's
 * UDF is laid out for, and disk mode has no CD-ROM size clamp. Autoclear
 * detaches the loop when its last user lets go: us right after the kernel
 * opens it, then the kernel on eject, swap or stop. */
static int loop_attach(int fd, const char *name, char *dev, size_t size) {
  int ctl = open("/dev/loop-control", O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC);
  if (ctl < 0) {
    ua_error("dvd mode needs loop devices: /dev/loop-control: %s",
             strerror(errno));
    return -1;
  }
  for (int tries = 0; tries < 3; tries++) {
    int n = ioctl(ctl, LOOP_CTL_GET_FREE);
    int lfd = n < 0 ? -1 : loop_open(n, dev, size);
    if (lfd < 0)
      break;
    if (ioctl(lfd, LOOP_SET_FD, fd) < 0) {
      close(lfd);
      if (errno == EBUSY)
        continue; /* someone took it between GET_FREE and here */
      break;
    }
    struct loop_info64 li;
    memset(&li, 0, sizeof(li));
    li.lo_flags = LO_FLAGS_AUTOCLEAR;
    safe_strncpy((char *)li.lo_file_name, name, sizeof(li.lo_file_name));
    if (ioctl(lfd, LOOP_SET_STATUS64, &li) < 0 ||
        ioctl(lfd, LOOP_SET_BLOCK_SIZE, 2048UL) < 0) {
      ua_error("Cannot give %s 2048-byte blocks: %s%s", dev, strerror(errno),
               errno == EINVAL ? " (needs kernel 4.14 or newer)" : "");
      ioctl(lfd, LOOP_CLR_FD, 0);
      close(lfd);
      close(ctl);
      return -1;
    }
    close(ctl);
    return lfd;
  }
  ua_error("Cannot set up a loop device for %s: %s", name, strerror(errno));
  close(ctl);
  return -1;
}

/* One LUN of a start: its image, open, and what the kernel will be given.
 * loop_fd is the loop device behind a dvd LUN, closed once the kernel holds
 * it. */
struct load {
  int fd, loop_fd, lun;
  enum mode mode;
  char name[PATH_MAX], path[64];
};

/* Everything about one image before the gadget changes: its mode, the size
 * checks, SELinux, the loop device behind dvd. The image arrives open. The
 * kernel gets /proc/self/fd/N: it follows the magic link to the file we
 * opened, wherever that lives in our mount namespace. name is only for
 * messages. */
static int prepare(struct load *l, int android_gadget) {
  snprintf(l->path, sizeof(l->path), "/proc/self/fd/%d", l->fd);
  /* lseek works for block devices too, no BLKGETSIZE64 needed */
  long long size = (long long)lseek(l->fd, 0, SEEK_END);
  if (l->mode == MODE_AUTO) {
    l->mode = detect_mode(l->fd);
    if (l->mode == MODE_CDROM && size > CDROM_MAX_BYTES)
      l->mode = MODE_DVD;
  }

  if (l->mode == MODE_CDROM && size >= 0 && size < CDROM_MIN_BYTES) {
    ua_error("%s is too small for a CD-ROM (minimum 600 KB)", l->name);
    return -1;
  }
  if (l->mode == MODE_CDROM && size > CDROM_MAX_BYTES)
    ua_warn("%s is %.2f GB, but the kernel's CD-ROM emulation stops at 2.36 "
            "GB unless it carries the DVD patch (kernel-patches/). "
            "Otherwise the host reads a truncated disc; --mode dvd has no "
            "limit.",
            l->name, (double)size / 1e9);

  struct stat st;
  int have_st = fstat(l->fd, &st) == 0;
  if (have_st && S_ISREG(st.st_mode))
    selinux_fix(l->fd, l->name, l->mode == MODE_RW, android_gadget);

  /* A block device served as is: the kernel thread reads it under the node's
   * label, and no label is readable on every policy, so it cannot be fixed by
   * relabelling the way a file can. Say why before the host sees a dead disk.
   * Whether to serve it at all, mounted or not, is the user's call. */
  char blabel[256];
  if (have_st && S_ISBLK(st.st_mode) &&
      !kernel_may(l->fd, "blk_file", l->mode == MODE_RW, android_gadget, blabel,
                  sizeof(blabel))) {
    ua_error("SELinux does not let the kernel %s %s (%s), so the host would "
             "see only read errors",
             l->mode == MODE_RW ? "read and write" : "read", l->name, blabel);
    ua_log("To serve it anyway, set SELinux permissive by hand first: "
           "setenforce 0");
    return -1;
  }

  if (l->mode == MODE_DVD) {
    char dev[32];
    if ((l->loop_fd = loop_attach(l->fd, l->name, dev, sizeof(dev))) < 0)
      return -1;
    /* Fail closed: an unreadable LUN looks like a dead disk on the host */
    char label[256];
    if (!kernel_may(l->loop_fd, "blk_file", 0, android_gadget, label,
                    sizeof(label))) {
      ua_error("SELinux does not let the kernel read loop devices (%s), so "
               "the host would see only read errors",
               label);
      if (android_gadget)
        ua_log("The USB Arsenal module loads the rule at boot; without it, "
               "run: ksud sepolicy patch \"allow kernel loop_device blk_file "
               "{ open read getattr ioctl }\" (Magisk: magiskpolicy --live)");
      return -1;
    }
    ua_debug("%s is %s with 2048-byte blocks", l->name, dev);
    snprintf(l->path, sizeof(l->path), "/proc/self/fd/%d", l->loop_fd);
  }
  return 0;
}

/* One file behind two LUNs, either of them writable: the host caches each
 * drive on its own, so a write through one corrupts what the other shows,
 * and two writers corrupt the file. Live LUNs this call replaces do not
 * count. A dvd LUN's loop device is skipped; it is read-only anyway. */
static int shared_rw(const struct load *ls, int n, const char *fdir) {
  struct stat a, b;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (fstat(ls[i].fd, &a) < 0)
      continue;
    for (int j = 0; j < i; j++)
      if (fstat(ls[j].fd, &b) == 0 && a.st_dev == b.st_dev &&
          a.st_ino == b.st_ino &&
          (ls[i].mode == MODE_RW || ls[j].mode == MODE_RW)) {
        ua_error("%s is given for LUN %d and LUN %d; a writable LUN cannot "
                 "share its file",
                 ls[i].name, ls[j].lun, ls[i].lun);
        return -1;
      }
    for (int lun = 0; lun < 8; lun++) {
      char ldir[PATH_MAX], p[PATH_MAX + 8], file[PATH_MAX] = "", ro[4] = "";
      int ours = 0;
      for (int j = 0; j < n; j++)
        ours |= ls[j].lun == lun;
      if (ours || lun_dir(fdir, lun, ldir, sizeof(ldir)) < 0)
        continue;
      snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/file", ldir);
      if (read_file(p, file, sizeof(file)) <= 0 || is_loop(file) ||
          stat(file, &b) < 0 || a.st_dev != b.st_dev || a.st_ino != b.st_ino)
        continue;
      snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/ro", ldir);
      read_file(p, ro, sizeof(ro));
      if (ls[i].mode == MODE_RW || ro[0] == '0') {
        ua_error("%s is already on LUN %d; a writable LUN cannot share its "
                 "file",
                 ls[i].name, lun);
        return -1;
      }
    }
  }
  return 0;
}

/* Whether the LUN already serves this very file in this mode: then there is
 * nothing to write, and the host keeps its medium. Ejecting and reloading
 * the same disc would be a medium change, and a locked drive a replug. */
static int serving(const char *ldir, const struct load *l) {
  char p[PATH_MAX + 16], file[PATH_MAX] = "", backing[PATH_MAX] = "", ro[4];
  snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/file", ldir);
  if (read_file(p, file, sizeof(file)) <= 0)
    return 0;
  if (is_loop(file)) {
    snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "/sys/block/%s/loop/backing_file",
             strrchr(file, '/') + 1);
    read_file(p, backing, sizeof(backing));
  }
  snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/ro", ldir);
  return strcmp(backing[0] ? backing : file, l->name) == 0 &&
         read_file(p, ro, sizeof(ro)) > 0 &&
         (ro[0] == '0') == (l->mode == MODE_RW);
}

/* Every image is prepared first, so a bad one fails before the host sees
 * anything; then all of them load in one begin/commit, one replug however
 * many LUNs. Other LUNs already on the bus stay as they are. */
static int do_start(struct load *ls, int n) {
  struct ua_gadget g;
  if (ua_gadget_open(&g) < 0 || ua_check_requirements(&g, UA_NEED_STORAGE) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
    if (prepare(&ls[i], g.android_gadget) < 0)
      return UA_EXIT_FAIL;

  char fdir[PATH_MAX], ldir[UA_LUNS][PATH_MAX];
  if (ua_gadget_func_dir(&g, FUNC, fdir, sizeof(fdir)) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
    if (lun_dir(fdir, ls[i].lun, ldir[i], sizeof(ldir[i])) < 0)
      return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  if (shared_rw(ls, n, fdir) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;

  /* Images for LUNs already on the bus, each in the same mode as its LUN: a
   * medium change is all the host needs to see, like swapping a disc in a
   * real drive. Disk vs CD-ROM is a different SCSI device type, which a host
   * only reads when it enumerates, and a host lock blocks the eject; both
   * take the rebind below, whose disconnect also clears the lock. dvd and
   * disk differ in sector size, which the host also only reads when it sees
   * a new medium, so a loaded one is swapped the same way. */
  int inplace = ua_gadget_live(&g) && ua_gadget_has(&g, FUNC);
  for (int i = 0; inplace && i < n; i++) {
    char cdrom[PATH_MAX + 8], cur[PATH_MAX + 8], v[8] = "";
    snprintf(cdrom, sizeof(cdrom), "%s/cdrom", ldir[i]);
    snprintf(cur, sizeof(cur), "%s/file", ldir[i]);
    inplace = read_file(cdrom, v, sizeof(v)) > 0 &&
              (v[0] == '1') == (ls[i].mode == MODE_CDROM) &&
              (read_file(cur, cur, sizeof(cur)) <= 0 ||
               is_loop(cur) == (ls[i].mode == MODE_DVD));
  }
  if (inplace) {
    /* The lock, so a command run meanwhile queues up behind the swap */
    int r = 0;
    ua_crit_enter();
    for (int i = 0; i < n && r == 0; i++) {
      if (serving(ldir[i], &ls[i])) {
        ua_log("LUN %d already holds %s (%s)", ls[i].lun, ls[i].name,
               mode_names[ls[i].mode]);
        continue;
      }
      r = lun_load(ldir[i], ls[i].path, ls[i].mode, 0);
      if (r == 0)
        ua_log("LUN %d now holds %s (%s)", ls[i].lun, ls[i].name,
               mode_names[ls[i].mode]);
    }
    ua_crit_leave();
    if (r == 0)
      return UA_EXIT_OK;
    if (r != -EBUSY)
      return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
    ua_debug("host holds the medium lock, rebinding to release it");
  }

  int existed = access(fdir, F_OK) == 0, made[UA_LUNS] = {0}, unlinked = 0,
      reached = 0, failed = -1;
  if (ua_gadget_begin(&g) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  if (ua_gadget_add(&g, FUNC, fdir, sizeof(fdir)) < 0)
    goto fail;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    /* lun.0 comes with the function; the rest are made on demand, and only
     * while the function is out of every config (EBUSY otherwise) */
    if (ls[i].lun > 0 && access(ldir[i], F_OK) != 0) {
      if (!unlinked++)
        ua_gadget_unlink(&g, FUNC);
      if (mkdir(ldir[i], 0755) < 0) {
        ua_error("Cannot create LUN %d: %s", ls[i].lun, strerror(errno));
        goto fail;
      }
      made[i] = 1;
    }
    reached = i + 1;
    int r = lun_load(ldir[i], ls[i].path, ls[i].mode, 1);
    if (r < 0) {
      if (r == -EBUSY)
        ua_error("The host still holds the drive locked (EBUSY)");
      failed = i;
      goto fail;
    }
  }
  if (ua_gadget_commit(&g) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
    ua_log("Serving %s as a %s on LUN %d", ls[i].name,
           ls[i].mode == MODE_CDROM ? "CD-ROM"
           : ls[i].mode == MODE_DVD ? "read-only disk with 2048-byte sectors"
           : ls[i].mode == MODE_RW  ? "writable disk"
                                    : "read-only disk",
           ls[i].lun);
  return UA_EXIT_OK;

fail:
  /* Leave nothing of this call behind: LUNs it made go, LUNs it loaded
   * that were already there come back empty, their old medium having gone
   * out first. The one that failed kept or got back its old medium
   * (lun_load). Other LUNs and functions stay live. */
  if (!existed)
    ua_gadget_remove(&g, FUNC);
  else
    for (int i = reached - 1; i >= 0; i--)
      if (made[i])
        rmdir(ldir[i]);
      else if (i != failed)
        lun_eject(ldir[i]);
  ua_gadget_commit(&g);
  return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
}

/* Eject every LUN in mask. Those a host has locked all go out in one
 * rebind, not one each. */
static int do_eject(unsigned mask) {
  struct ua_gadget g;
  char fdir[PATH_MAX], ldir[PATH_MAX];
  unsigned locked = 0;
  if (ua_gadget_open(&g) < 0 || ua_check_requirements(&g, 0) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  if (!ua_gadget_has(&g, FUNC)) {
    ua_error("Mass storage is not running");
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  }
  ua_gadget_func_dir(&g, FUNC, fdir, sizeof(fdir));
  for (int lun = 0; lun < UA_LUNS; lun++) {
    if (!(mask & (1u << lun)))
      continue;
    if (lun_dir(fdir, lun, ldir, sizeof(ldir)) < 0) {
      ua_error("Eject failed: %s", strerror(errno));
      return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
    }
    if (lun_eject(ldir) == 0) {
      ua_log("LUN %d ejected", lun);
      ua_running_clear_lun(lun);
      continue;
    }
    /* Before 6.6 there is no forced_eject, and a host's medium lock makes
     * the eject EBUSY. The disconnect of a rebind releases it, as start does
     * for a swap; the eject is retried while the kernel processes it. */
    if (errno != EBUSY || !ua_gadget_live(&g)) {
      ua_error("Eject failed: %s", strerror(errno));
      return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
    }
    locked |= 1u << lun;
  }
  if (!locked)
    return UA_EXIT_OK;
  ua_debug("host holds the medium lock, rebinding to release it");
  if (ua_gadget_begin(&g) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  int ret = UA_EXIT_OK;
  for (int lun = 0; lun < UA_LUNS; lun++) {
    if (!(locked & (1u << lun)) || lun_dir(fdir, lun, ldir, sizeof(ldir)) < 0)
      continue;
    if (lun_eject_wait(ldir) < 0) {
      ua_error("Eject of LUN %d failed: %s%s", lun, strerror(errno),
               errno == EBUSY ? " (the host still holds the drive locked)"
                              : "");
      ret = UA_EXIT_FAIL;
      continue;
    }
    ua_log("LUN %d ejected (the host had it locked, so it was replugged)", lun);
    ua_running_clear_lun(lun);
  }
  if (ua_gadget_commit(&g) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  return ret;
}

static int do_stop(void) {
  struct ua_gadget g;
  if (ua_gadget_open(&g) < 0 || ua_check_requirements(&g, 0) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  if (!ua_gadget_has(&g, FUNC)) {
    ua_log("Mass storage is not running");
    return UA_EXIT_OK;
  }
  if (ua_gadget_begin(&g) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  ua_gadget_remove(&g, FUNC);
  if (ua_gadget_commit(&g) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  ua_log("Mass storage removed");
  ua_running_clear(UA_FN_STORAGE);
  return UA_EXIT_OK;
}

/* A LUN of the setup, opened and named as an IMAGE operand would be */
static int load_from_spec(struct load *l, int lun, const char *spec) {
  char mode[8], path[PATH_MAX];
  int m;
  if (sscanf(spec, "%7[^:]:%4095[^\n]", mode, path) != 2 ||
      (m = mode_of(mode)) < 0) {
    ua_error("Bad setup for LUN %d: '%s'", lun, spec);
    return -1;
  }
  l->lun = lun;
  l->mode = (enum mode)m;
  l->loop_fd = -1;
  if ((l->fd = open_image(path, l->mode)) < 0) {
    ua_error("%s: %s", path, strerror(errno));
    return -1;
  }
  if (!realpath(path, l->name))
    safe_strncpy(l->name, path, sizeof(l->name));
  return 0;
}

static void close_loads(struct load *ls, int n) {
  /* The kernel holds its own references by now; a loop is autoclear, so it
   * lives as long as its LUN */
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    close(ls[i].fd);
    if (ls[i].loop_fd >= 0)
      close(ls[i].loop_fd);
  }
}

/* Start what was opened, and record the LUNs that now run */
static int start_loads(struct load *ls, int n) {
  int r = do_start(ls, n);
  close_loads(ls, n);
  if (r == UA_EXIT_OK) {
    unsigned mask = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
      mask |= 1u << ls[i].lun;
    ua_running_take(UA_FN_STORAGE, mask);
  }
  return r;
}

/* Bring the drives to the setup, deciding against the kernel: a LUN the
 * setup dropped is ejected in place, one whose setup changed since it started
 * (or that the host emptied) is loaded, the rest are left alone. With nothing
 * set up, storage stops. */
static int do_apply(void) {
  struct ua_setup s, r;
  struct ua_gadget g;
  struct load ls[UA_LUNS];
  char fdir[PATH_MAX];
  int any = 0, n = 0;
  unsigned eject = 0;
  ua_setup_load(&s);
  ua_running_load(&r);
  for (int lun = 0; lun < UA_LUNS; lun++)
    any |= s.lun[lun][0] != '\0';
  if (ua_gadget_open(&g) < 0)
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  int linked = ua_gadget_has(&g, FUNC) && ua_gadget_live(&g);
  if (!any) {
    if (linked)
      return do_stop();
    ua_log("Nothing set up for storage");
    return UA_EXIT_OK;
  }
  if (linked)
    ua_gadget_func_dir(&g, FUNC, fdir, sizeof(fdir));
  for (int lun = 0; lun < UA_LUNS; lun++) {
    char ldir[PATH_MAX], p[PATH_MAX + 8], file[PATH_MAX] = "";
    int loaded = linked && lun_dir(fdir, lun, ldir, sizeof(ldir)) == 0 &&
                 (snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/file", ldir),
                  read_file(p, file, sizeof(file)) > 0);
    if (!s.lun[lun][0]) {
      if (loaded)
        eject |= 1u << lun;
      else if (r.lun[lun][0])
        ua_running_clear_lun(lun);
      continue;
    }
    if (loaded && !strcmp(s.lun[lun], r.lun[lun]))
      continue;
    if (n == UA_LUNS)
      break;
    if (load_from_spec(&ls[n], lun, s.lun[lun]) < 0) {
      close_loads(ls, n);
      return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
    }
    n++;
  }
  /* Every image opened first, so a missing one fails before any eject */
  if (eject && do_eject(eject) != UA_EXIT_OK) {
    close_loads(ls, n);
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  }
  if (!n) {
    ua_log(eject ? "Storage now runs its setup"
                 : "Storage already runs its setup");
    return UA_EXIT_OK;
  }
  return start_loads(ls, n);
}

/* JSON: the elements of an array, one object per LUN; an ejected LUN has an
 * empty file, mode and access */
void ua_status_storage(const struct ua_gadget *g, int json) {
  char fdir[PATH_MAX];
  int sep = 0;
  if (!ua_gadget_has(g, FUNC) ||
      ua_gadget_func_dir(g, FUNC, fdir, sizeof(fdir)) < 0)
    return;
  for (int lun = 0; lun < 16; lun++) {
    char ldir[PATH_MAX], p[PATH_MAX + 8], file[PATH_MAX] = "", v[8] = "";
    if (lun_dir(fdir, lun, ldir, sizeof(ldir)) < 0 || access(ldir, F_OK) != 0)
      continue;
    snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/file", ldir);
    read_file(p, file, sizeof(file));
    snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/cdrom", ldir);
    int cdrom = read_file(p, v, sizeof(v)) > 0 && v[0] == '1';
    snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/ro", ldir);
    int ro = read_file(p, v, sizeof(v)) > 0 && v[0] == '1';
    /* Name the image behind a dvd LUN's loop device */
    char backing[PATH_MAX] = "";
    if (is_loop(file)) {
      snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "/sys/block/%s/loop/backing_file",
               strrchr(file, '/') + 1);
      read_file(p, backing, sizeof(backing));
    }
    const char *mode = !file[0]     ? ""
                       : cdrom      ? "cdrom"
                       : backing[0] ? "dvd"
                       : ro         ? "disk"
                                    : "rw";
    if (json) {
      int first = 1;
      printf("%s{", sep++ ? "," : "");
      ua_json_int("lun", lun, &first);
      ua_json_str("file", backing[0] ? backing : file, &first);
      ua_json_str("mode", mode, &first);
      ua_json_str("access",
                  !file[0]             ? ""
                  : strcmp(mode, "rw") ? "ro"
                                       : "rw",
                  &first);
      printf("}");
      continue;
    }
    printf("Storage:    LUN %d: %s%s\n", lun,
           backing[0] ? backing
           : file[0]  ? file
                      : "(empty)",
           !file[0]     ? ""
           : cdrom      ? " [cdrom]"
           : backing[0] ? " [dvd]"
           : ro         ? " [disk, read-only]"
                        : " [disk, writable]");
  }
}

/* One IMAGE of a start: its argv index */
struct simg {
  int lun, image, mode_set;
  enum mode mode;
};

struct sargs {
  int lun, nimg; /* lun: the last --lun, for eject */
  const char *action;
  struct simg img[UA_LUNS];
};

/* An IMAGE takes the --lun and --mode given since the one before it; with
 * no --lun, the LUN after that one's */
static int add_image(struct sargs *a, int image, int *lun, int *mode) {
  if (a->nimg == UA_LUNS) {
    ua_usage_error("storage", "start takes at most %d IMAGEs", UA_LUNS);
    return -1;
  }
  struct simg *m = &a->img[a->nimg];
  m->lun = *lun >= 0 ? *lun : a->nimg ? a->img[a->nimg - 1].lun + 1 : 0;
  m->mode_set = *mode >= 0;
  m->mode = m->mode_set ? (enum mode) * mode : MODE_AUTO;
  m->image = image;
  for (int i = 0; i < a->nimg; i++)
    if (a->img[i].lun == m->lun) {
      ua_usage_error("storage", "LUN %d is given twice", m->lun);
      return -1;
    }
  if (m->lun > 7) {
    /* only reachable without --lun: it was checked when it was read */
    ua_usage_error("storage",
                   "An IMAGE would take LUN 8, past the last; give it a "
                   "--lun");
    return -1;
  }
  a->nimg++;
  *lun = *mode = -1;
  return 0;
}

/* A word that is not an option: the action first, then IMAGEs, which only
 * start takes */
static int operand(struct sargs *a, int i, char **argv, int *lun, int *mode) {
  if (!a->action[0]) {
    a->action = argv[i];
    return 0;
  }
  if (strcmp(a->action, "start")) {
    ua_usage_error("storage", "Too many arguments");
    return -1;
  }
  return add_image(a, i, lun, mode);
}

/* Returns -1 to go on, else an exit code. Options are read in order ("-" in
 * the option string), so each one applies to the IMAGE after it. */
static int parse(int argc, char **argv, struct sargs *a) {
  static const struct option opts[] = {
      {"mode", required_argument, NULL, 'm'},
      {"lun", required_argument, NULL, 'l'},
      {"help", no_argument, NULL, 'h'},
      {NULL, 0, NULL, 0},
  };
  int c, lun = -1, mode = -1;
  char *end;
  memset(a, 0, sizeof(*a));
  a->action = "";
  optind = 0;
  while ((c = getopt_long(argc, argv, "-:m:l:h", opts, NULL)) != -1) {
    switch (c) {
    case 1: /* not an option: the action, then IMAGEs */
      if (operand(a, optind - 1, argv, &lun, &mode) < 0)
        return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
      break;
    case 'm':
      if ((mode = mode_of(optarg)) < 0) {
        ua_usage_error("storage", "Unknown mode '%s'", optarg);
        return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
      }
      break;
    case 'l': {
      long v = strtol(optarg, &end, 10);
      if (*optarg == '\0' || *end || v < 0 || v > 7) {
        ua_usage_error("storage", "--lun takes a number from 0 to 7");
        return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
      }
      lun = a->lun = (int)v;
      break;
    }
    case 'h':
      ua_help_storage();
      return UA_EXIT_OK;
    case ':':
      ua_usage_error("storage", "Option '%s' needs a value", argv[optind - 1]);
      return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
    default:
      ua_usage_error("storage", "Bad option '%s'", ua_bad_option(argv));
      return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
    }
  }
  /* getopt stops at "--"; what follows it is operands, so an IMAGE whose
   * name starts with '-' can still be given */
  for (; optind < argc; optind++)
    if (operand(a, optind, argv, &lun, &mode) < 0)
      return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
  if (!a->action[0]) {
    ua_usage_error("storage", "Missing action");
    return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
  }
  if (strcmp(a->action, "start"))
    return -1;
  /* Options after the last IMAGE: with one IMAGE they are its own, as they
   * always were; with several there is no telling which they meant */
  if (a->nimg && (lun >= 0 || mode >= 0)) {
    if (a->nimg > 1) {
      ua_usage_error("storage",
                     "--lun and --mode go before the IMAGE they are for");
      return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
    }
    if (lun >= 0)
      a->img[0].lun = lun;
    if (mode >= 0)
      a->img[0].mode = (enum mode)mode, a->img[0].mode_set = 1;
  }
  return -1;
}

static int open_image(const char *image, enum mode mode) {
  return open(image, (mode == MODE_RW ? O_RDWR : O_RDONLY) | O_CLOEXEC);
}

int ua_cmd_storage(int argc, char **argv) {
  struct sargs a;
  if (argc < 2 || ua_want_help(argc, argv)) {
    ua_help_storage();
    return UA_EXIT_OK;
  }
  int r = parse(argc, argv, &a);
  if (r != -1)
    return r;
  struct ua_config cfg;
  ua_config_active(&cfg);
  safe_strncpy(inquiry, cfg.storage_inquiry, sizeof(inquiry));
  if (!strcmp(a.action, "start")) {
    struct load ls[UA_LUNS];
    struct ua_setup s;
    int n = 0;
    ua_setup_load(&s);
    if (!a.nimg) {
      /* A bare start runs the setup */
      for (int lun = 0; lun < UA_LUNS; lun++) {
        if (!s.lun[lun][0])
          continue;
        if (load_from_spec(&ls[n], lun, s.lun[lun]) < 0) {
          close_loads(ls, n);
          return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
        }
        n++;
      }
      if (!n) {
        ua_error("Nothing set up for storage");
        ua_log("Give an IMAGE, or: " UA_NAME
               " setup set storage_lun0=auto:/path/to/image.iso");
        return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
      }
      return start_loads(ls, n);
    }
    for (; n < a.nimg; n++) {
      struct simg *m = &a.img[n];
      struct load *l = &ls[n];
      const char *image = argv[m->image];
      l->lun = m->lun;
      l->loop_fd = -1;
      l->mode = m->mode;
      if (!m->mode_set && mode_of(cfg.storage_mode) >= 0)
        l->mode = (enum mode)mode_of(cfg.storage_mode);
      if ((l->fd = open_image(image, l->mode)) < 0) {
        ua_error("%s: %s", image, strerror(errno));
        close_loads(ls, n);
        return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
      }
      if (!realpath(image, l->name))
        safe_strncpy(l->name, image, sizeof(l->name));
    }
    /* The IMAGEs given become the setup, as Droidspaces saves a start's
     * flags, so a later bare start needs nothing. A name that means nothing
     * where a later start runs (a container's private path, started again
     * from Android) fails that start, naming it. */
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
      snprintf(s.lun[ls[i].lun], UA_LUN_SPEC, "%s:%s", mode_names[ls[i].mode],
               ls[i].name);
    if (ua_setup_save(&s) < 0) {
      close_loads(ls, n);
      return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
    }
    return start_loads(ls, n);
  }
  if (!strcmp(a.action, "apply"))
    return do_apply();
  if (!strcmp(a.action, "eject")) {
    r = do_eject(1u << a.lun);
    if (r == UA_EXIT_OK) {
      /* An eject from the command line is an edit of the setup too */
      struct ua_setup s;
      ua_setup_load(&s);
      s.lun[a.lun][0] = '\0';
      ua_setup_save(&s);
    }
    return r;
  }
  if (!strcmp(a.action, "stop"))
    return do_stop();
  ua_usage_error("storage", "Unknown action '%s'", a.action);
  return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
}

```

`src/gadgets/tether.c`:

```c
/*
 * USB Arsenal - composite USB gadget builder for Linux and Android
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
 *
 * `tether`: an f_ncm (or f_rndis) network function, plus a small daemon
 * that gives the host an address, NAT and a route out. The networking is
 * Droidspaces' (src/net/); this file only wires it to the gadget's
 * interface. See docs/developer/research/04-tethering.md.
 */

#include "../net/net.h"
#include "usbarsenal.h"
#include <linux/rtnetlink.h>
#include <sys/signalfd.h>

#define NCM UA_F_NCM
#define RNDIS UA_F_RNDIS

/* Below Android's VPN rules (10000+) so tethered traffic never gets pulled
 * into a VPN, above the OEM reserved range (< 1000). Same values Droidspaces
 * uses; the selectors are our own subnet, so the two never collide. */
#define RULE_PRIO_TO 6090
#define RULE_PRIO_FROM 6100

/* Droidspaces' route monitor heartbeat: covers kernels with broken netlink
 * notifications, a gateway container restarting in another namespace (no
 * event reaches us from there), and forwarding that someone switched off */
#define HEARTBEAT_MS 1500

/* NAT66 hands the host a ULA /64. Our own, not Droidspaces' fd64:7370::/48,
 * so a container's network and the USB link can run side by side. */
#define NAT6_PREFIX "fd75:7361::"
#define NAT6_CIDR "fd75:7361::/64"
#define NAT6_GW_LL "fe80::1" /* the source of every RA ds_ra_build() sends */

struct tether {
  const char *upstream;           /* --upstream, or NULL for automatic */
  const char *dns;                /* --dns, or NULL */
  const char *dev_mac, *host_mac; /* the profile's, "" for stable_macs() */
  char iface[IFNAMSIZ];
  uint32_t ip_be, net_be, mask_be, offer_be;
  uint8_t prefix;
  char cidr[32]; /* our subnet, for the NAT rules */
  int table;     /* uplink routing table the FROM rule points at, 0 = none */
  char uplink[IFNAMSIZ];
  int nat6;   /* IPv6 NAT is up, and the DHCP thread sends RAs */
  int table6; /* uplink IPv6 table the IPv6 FROM rule points at, 0 = none */
  struct in6_addr prefix6;
  unsigned ifindex; /* of the netdev we configured; a new one means rebind */
  /* gateway mode: a container (OpenWrt) serves the host instead of us */
  int gateway;
  const char *gw_name, *gw_path, *gw_iface;
  pid_t gw_pid;
  ino_t gw_ino; /* the netns the cable is plugged into, 0 = none */
};

/* Gateway topology, after Droidspaces' gateway mode: usb0 never leaves our
 * namespace. It sits on a bridge with no address, and one veth runs from
 * that bridge into the container, its far end born there under its final
 * name. A container restart only takes the far end with it, and a gadget
 * rebind only gives usb0 a new identity; both are re-plugged each tick. */
#define GW_BRIDGE "ua-usb"
#define GW_VETH "ua-gw"

void ua_help_tether(void) {
  printf(
      "Usage: " UA_NAME " tether <action> [options]\n\n"
      "Share this device's internet connection with the host over USB.\n"
      "The host gets a network adapter, an address by DHCP, and a route out\n"
      "through whatever connection this device is using.\n\n"
      "Actions:\n"
      "  start   Add the network function and start sharing. The options\n"
      "          given are saved as the setup (see `setup`); with none, the\n"
      "          saved setup starts.\n"
      "  apply   Restart with the setup if it changed since the start, in\n"
      "          one replug; start if not running\n"
      "  stop    Stop sharing and remove the network function\n\n"
      "Options:\n"
      "      --rndis            Use RNDIS instead of NCM. NCM works out of\n"
      "                         the box on Windows 11, macOS and Linux;\n"
      "                         RNDIS is for Windows 7/8 and older hosts.\n"
      "                         Picked automatically if NCM is missing.\n"
      "      --ncm              Use NCM even if the profile says RNDIS\n"
      "  -u, --upstream IFACE   Share this interface instead of the one\n"
      "                         detected automatically (wlan0, rmnet_data0)\n"
      "  -a, --address CIDR     This side's address (default:\n"
      "                         192.168.42.129/24). The host is offered the\n"
      "                         next address.\n"
      "  -d, --dns IP[,IP]      DNS servers handed to the host (default:\n"
      "                         1.1.1.1,8.8.8.8)\n"
      "      --no-net           Only add the network function: no address,\n"
      "                         DHCP or NAT. For bringing your own setup.\n"
      "                         Forgets a saved gateway.\n"
      "  -f, --foreground       Stay in the foreground instead of running\n"
      "                         the network side as a daemon\n"
      "  -G, --gateway NAME     Gateway mode: hand the link to a Droidspaces\n"
      "                         container (OpenWrt) instead of serving it\n"
      "                         here. No DHCP or NAT from us; the container\n"
      "                         provides them on its end of the cable.\n"
      "      --gateway-pid PID  Same, for any container with this init pid\n"
      "      --gateway-netns PATH  Same, given a network namespace file\n"
      "      --gateway-iface IFACE  Name of the cable inside the container\n"
      "                         (default: usb0)\n"
      "  -h, --help             Show this help\n\n"
      "Examples:\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " tether start\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " tether start --upstream wlan0 --dns 9.9.9.9\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " tether start --rndis\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " tether start --no-net\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " tether start --gateway OpenWrt\n"
      "  " UA_NAME " tether stop\n");
}

static void pid_path(char *out, size_t size) {
  ua_ws_path("Pids", "tether.pid", out, size);
}

static void info_path(char *out, size_t size) {
  ua_ws_path("Net", "tether.info", out, size);
}

/* The pid file names a live daemon only if that pid is still ours: a pid
 * reused by something else after a reboot must never get our SIGTERM */
static pid_t daemon_pid(void) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  pid_path(p, sizeof(p));
  return ua_read_our_pid(p);
}

void ua_tether_kill(void) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  pid_t pid = daemon_pid();
  if (pid > 0 && kill(pid, SIGTERM) == 0) {
    /* It removes its NAT rules on the way out; give it time to */
    for (int i = 0; i < 50 && kill(pid, 0) == 0; i++)
      usleep(100000);
    if (kill(pid, 0) == 0) {
      ua_warn("Tether daemon %d did not exit, killing it", (int)pid);
      kill(pid, SIGKILL);
    }
  }
  pid_path(p, sizeof(p));
  unlink(p);
  info_path(p, sizeof(p));
  unlink(p);
}

static int parse_address(const char *s, struct tether *t) {
  char ip[32];
  const char *slash = strchr(s, '/');
  size_t n = slash ? (size_t)(slash - s) : strlen(s);
  char *end = NULL;
  long prefix = slash ? strtol(slash + 1, &end, 10) : 24;
  if (slash && (end == slash + 1 || *end))
    return -1;
  struct in_addr a;
  if (n >= sizeof(ip) || prefix < 8 || prefix > 30)
    return -1;
  memcpy(ip, s, n);
  ip[n] = '\0';
  if (inet_pton(AF_INET, ip, &a) != 1)
    return -1;

  uint32_t ip_h = ntohl(a.s_addr);
  uint32_t mask_h = 0xffffffffu << (32 - prefix);
  uint32_t net_h = ip_h & mask_h, bcast_h = net_h | ~mask_h;
  if (ip_h == net_h || ip_h == bcast_h)
    return -1;
  uint32_t offer_h = ip_h + 1 < bcast_h ? ip_h + 1 : ip_h - 1;
  if (offer_h == net_h)
    return -1;

  t->ip_be = a.s_addr;
  t->mask_be = htonl(mask_h);
  t->net_be = htonl(net_h);
  t->offer_be = htonl(offer_h);
  t->prefix = (uint8_t)prefix;
  struct in_addr na = {t->net_be};
  snprintf(t->cidr, sizeof(t->cidr), "%s/%ld", inet_ntoa(na), prefix);
  return 0;
}

/* A locally administered 02:55 MAC, FNV-1a hashed from key */
static void gw_mac(const char *key, uint8_t mac[6]) {
  uint32_t h = 2166136261u;
  for (const char *k = key; *k; k++)
    h = (h ^ (uint8_t)*k) * 16777619u;
  mac[0] = 0x02;
  mac[1] = 0x55;
  mac[2] = (uint8_t)(h >> 24);
  mac[3] = (uint8_t)(h >> 16);
  mac[4] = (uint8_t)(h >> 8);
  mac[5] = (uint8_t)h;
}

/* Fixed MACs per device: random ones make Windows add "Ethernet 7, 8, 9..."
 * every time tethering starts. Locally administered, derived from something
 * stable on this machine. */
static void stable_macs(char *dev, char *host, size_t size) {
  char seed[128];
  uint8_t m[6];
  ua_device_seed(seed, sizeof(seed));
  gw_mac(seed, m);
  snprintf(dev, size, "02:55:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x", m[2], m[3], m[4], m[5]);
  snprintf(host, size, "02:48:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x", m[2], m[3], m[4], m[5]);
}

/* Windows only loads its RNDIS driver unprompted when the device answers the
 * Microsoft OS descriptor request with compatible ID "RNDIS" */
static void rndis_os_desc(const struct ua_gadget *g, const char *fdir) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/os_desc", g->path);
  write_attr(p, "use", "1");
  write_attr(p, "b_vendor_code", "0xcd");
  write_attr(p, "qw_sign", "MSFT100");
  snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/os_desc/interface.rndis", fdir);
  write_attr(p, "compatible_id", "RNDIS");
  write_attr(p, "sub_compatible_id", "5162001");
  snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/os_desc/" UA_CONFIG, g->path);
  if (symlink(g->config, p) < 0 && errno != EEXIST)
    ua_debug("os_desc link: %s", strerror(errno));
}

static const char *live_func(const struct ua_gadget *g) {
  return ua_gadget_has(g, NCM) ? NCM : ua_gadget_has(g, RNDIS) ? RNDIS : NULL;
}

static int read_ifname(const struct ua_gadget *g, const char *func, char *out) {
  char dir[PATH_MAX], p[PATH_MAX + 8], buf[64];
  ua_gadget_func_dir(g, func, dir, sizeof(dir));
  snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/ifname", dir);
  /* Old kernels say "(unnamed net_device)" until the function is bound */
  if (read_file(p, buf, sizeof(buf)) <= 0 || buf[0] == '(' ||
      strlen(buf) >= IFNAMSIZ)
    return -1;
  safe_strncpy(out, buf, IFNAMSIZ);
  return 0;
}

/* What the running daemon is doing, as key=value lines: status prints them as
 * text or JSON. A key with no value is left out. */
static void write_info(const struct tether *t) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  struct in_addr a = {t->ip_be};
  info_path(p, sizeof(p));
  FILE *f = fopen(p, "we");
  if (!f)
    return;
  fprintf(f, "iface=%s\n", t->iface);
  if (t->gateway) {
    fprintf(f, "gateway=%s\ngateway_iface=%s\ngateway_waiting=%d\n",
            t->gw_name ? t->gw_name : "", t->gw_iface, !t->gw_ino);
  } else {
    fprintf(f, "address=%s/%u\n", inet_ntoa(a), t->prefix);
    if (t->nat6)
      fprintf(f, "ipv6=" NAT6_CIDR "\n");
    if (t->uplink[0])
      fprintf(f, "upstream=%s\n", t->uplink);
  }
  fclose(f);
}

/* One value from tether.info, "" when the key is not there */
static void info_get(const char *info, const char *key, char *out,
                     size_t size) {
  size_t len = strlen(key);
  out[0] = '\0';
  for (const char *l = info; *l;) {
    const char *end = strchrnul(l, '\n');
    if ((size_t)(end - l) > len && !strncmp(l, key, len) && l[len] == '=') {
      snprintf(out, size, "%.*s", (int)(end - l - len - 1), l + len + 1);
      return;
    }
    l = *end ? end + 1 : end;
  }
}

static void no_ipv6(const char *ifname) {
  char p[128];
  /* Android leaves accept_ra=2 everywhere: a port with no address would
   * pick up one, and a default route, from the container's RAs */
  snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/%s/disable_ipv6", ifname);
  write_file(p, "1");
}

/* Android answers a fresh link's first master or up with a transient EPERM;
 * VirtualAP's six tries 300 ms apart cover it */
static int plug(ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx, const char *ifname, const char *master) {
  for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
    if ((!master || ds_nl_set_master(ctx, ifname, master) == 0) &&
        ds_nl_link_up(ctx, ifname) == 0)
      return 0;
    usleep(300000);
  }
  return -1;
}

static int usb_on_bridge(const struct tether *t) {
  char p[128], target[PATH_MAX];
  snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "/sys/class/net/%s/master", t->iface);
  ssize_t n = readlink(p, target, sizeof(target) - 1);
  if (n <= 0)
    return 0;
  target[n] = '\0';
  const char *b = strrchr(target, '/');
  return !strcmp(b ? b + 1 : target, GW_BRIDGE);
}

/* With no daemon alive, a host end of the cable is a leftover; dropping it
 * takes its far end with it, so what the container still holds is not ours */
static void drop_host_end(void) {
  ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx = ds_nl_open();
  if (!ctx)
    return;
  if (ds_nl_link_exists(ctx, GW_VETH))
    ds_nl_del_link(ctx, GW_VETH);
  ds_nl_close(ctx);
}

/* Keep the cable plugged into the container's current namespace. A host end
 * whose far end lives in another (dead) namespace is deleted: it would pin
 * that namespace and lead nowhere. */
static void gw_wire(struct tether *t, int quiet) {
  char path[64];
  struct stat st;
  if (ua_container_netns(t->gw_name, t->gw_pid, t->gw_path, path,
                         sizeof(path)) < 0 ||
      stat(path, &st) < 0) {
    if (!quiet || t->gw_ino)
      ua_warn("[NET] The gateway container is not running; the cable goes in "
              "when it starts");
    t->gw_ino = 0;
    write_info(t);
    return;
  }
  ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx = ds_nl_open();
  if (!ctx)
    return;
  int have = ds_nl_link_exists(ctx, GW_VETH);
  if (have && st.st_ino == t->gw_ino && ds_netns_has_link(path, t->gw_iface)) {
    ds_nl_close(ctx);
    return;
  }
  if (have)
    ds_nl_del_link(ctx, GW_VETH);

  uint8_t mac[6];
  gw_mac(t->gw_iface, mac);
  int fd = ds_open_container_netns(path);
  int r = fd >= 0 ? ds_nl_create_veth_in(ctx, GW_VETH, t->gw_iface, fd, mac)
                  : -errno;
  if (fd >= 0)
    close(fd);
  if (r < 0) {
    ua_warn("[NET] Cannot plug %s into the container: %s%s", t->gw_iface,
            strerror(-r),
            r == -EEXIST ? " (an interface by that name already exists "
                           "there; pick another with --gateway-iface)"
                         : "");
    t->gw_ino = 0;
  } else {
    no_ipv6(GW_VETH);
    if (plug(ctx, GW_VETH, GW_BRIDGE) < 0 ||
        ds_netns_link_up(path, t->gw_iface) < 0)
      ua_warn("[NET] The cable is in but not up yet");
    t->gw_ino = st.st_ino;
    ua_log("Plugged %s into the container as %s", t->iface, t->gw_iface);
  }
  ds_nl_close(ctx);
  write_info(t);
}

static int gw_up(struct tether *t) {
  ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx = ds_nl_open();
  if (!ctx) {
    ua_error("Cannot open a netlink socket: %s", strerror(errno));
    return -1;
  }
  uint8_t mac[6];
  int r = ds_nl_create_bridge(ctx, GW_BRIDGE);
  if (r < 0) {
    ua_error("Cannot create bridge " GW_BRIDGE ": %s", strerror(-r));
    ds_nl_close(ctx);
    return -1;
  }
  /* A bridge with no address borrows its lowest port MAC, so it would
   * change whenever the container restarts and the far side's ARP goes
   * stale. A MAC set by us is exempt. */
  gw_mac(GW_BRIDGE, mac);
  ds_nl_set_mac(ctx, GW_BRIDGE, mac);
  no_ipv6(GW_BRIDGE);
  write_file("/sys/class/net/" GW_BRIDGE "/bridge/nf_call_iptables", "0");
  write_file("/sys/class/net/" GW_BRIDGE "/bridge/nf_call_ip6tables", "0");
  no_ipv6(t->iface);
  if (plug(ctx, GW_BRIDGE, NULL) < 0 || plug(ctx, t->iface, GW_BRIDGE) < 0) {
    ua_error("Cannot put %s on bridge " GW_BRIDGE, t->iface);
    ds_nl_close(ctx);
    return -1;
  }
  ds_nl_close(ctx);
  gw_wire(t, 0);
  return 0;
}

static void gw_tick(struct tether *t) {
  /* M62-style kernels free usb0 on unbind and make a new one on bind */
  if (!usb_on_bridge(t)) {
    ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx = ds_nl_open();
    if (ctx) {
      no_ipv6(t->iface);
      if (plug(ctx, t->iface, GW_BRIDGE) == 0)
        ua_log("[NET] %s back on " GW_BRIDGE, t->iface);
      ds_nl_close(ctx);
    }
  }
  gw_wire(t, 1);
}

static void gw_down(void) {
  ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx = ds_nl_open();
  if (!ctx)
    return;
  /* The host end goes first: it pins the container's namespace */
  ds_nl_del_link(ctx, GW_VETH);
  ds_nl_del_link(ctx, GW_BRIDGE);
  ds_nl_close(ctx);
}

/* Point "from our subnet" at the uplink's routing table. Android only: there
 * every network has its own table and nothing routes our subnet by default.
 * On plain Linux the main table already does. */
/* The IPv6 half of sync_uplink(). On an IPv6-only carrier the IPv4 uplink
 * is the CLAT device v4-rmnetX, whose IPv6 routes live in the table of the
 * rmnetX underneath. An uplink with no IPv6 table clears the rule, and the
 * host falls back to IPv4 at once instead of waiting on a dead route. */
static void sync_uplink6(struct tether *t, const char *iface) {
  if (!t->nat6 || !is_android())
    return;
  ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx = ds_nl_open();
  if (!ctx)
    return;
  int table = 0;
  if (!strncmp(iface, "v4-", 3))
    iface += 3;
  ds_nl_get_iface_table(ctx, AF_INET6, iface, &table);
  if (table != t->table6) {
    if (t->table6 > 0)
      ds_nl_rule6(ctx, 0, &t->prefix6, 64, 1, t->table6, RULE_PRIO_FROM);
    if (table > 0 &&
        ds_nl_rule6(ctx, 1, &t->prefix6, 64, 1, table, RULE_PRIO_FROM) < 0)
      ua_warn("[NET] Cannot add the IPv6 route rule for table %d", table);
    t->table6 = table;
  }
  ds_nl_close(ctx);
}

static void sync_uplink(struct tether *t, int quiet) {
  char iface[IFNAMSIZ];
  int table = 0;
  const char *how = ua_find_uplink(t->upstream, iface, &table, t->nat6);
  if (!how) {
    /* Once per loss, not every tick: this goes to the log */
    if (!quiet || t->uplink[0])
      ua_warn("[NET] No internet connection to share yet; the host gets a "
              "link but no route out until one comes up");
    t->uplink[0] = '\0';
    iface[0] = '\0';
    /* Automatic mode keeps the rule through a transient loss. A pinned
     * uplink that is gone loses it, so the host's traffic never leaks out
     * of a table the kernel may recycle for another network. */
    table = t->upstream ? 0 : t->table;
  }
  if (strcmp(iface, t->uplink) != 0 && how) {
    ua_log("Sharing %s (%s)", iface, how);
    safe_strncpy(t->uplink, iface, sizeof(t->uplink));
  }
  if (how || t->upstream)
    sync_uplink6(t, iface);
  if (!is_android() || table == t->table) {
    write_info(t);
    return;
  }

  ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx = ds_nl_open();
  if (!ctx)
    return;
  if (t->table > 0)
    ds_nl_del_rule4(ctx, t->net_be, t->prefix, 0, 0, t->table, RULE_PRIO_FROM);
  if (table > 0 && ds_nl_add_rule4(ctx, t->net_be, t->prefix, 0, 0, table,
                                   RULE_PRIO_FROM) < 0)
    ua_warn("[NET] Cannot add the route rule for table %d", table);
  t->table = table;
  ds_nl_close(ctx);
  write_info(t);
}

/* Android routes nothing to or from our subnets by default: replies to the
 * host must find our connected route in main, and the host's traffic must
 * find the uplink's table. Re-run by the monitor, because netd flushes every
 * rule when it restarts; adding a rule that exists is a no-op. */
static void install_policy_rules(struct tether *t) {
  if (!is_android())
    return;
  ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx = ds_nl_open();
  if (!ctx)
    return;
  int ret = ds_nl_add_rule4(ctx, 0, 0, t->net_be, t->prefix, RT_TABLE_MAIN,
                            RULE_PRIO_TO);
  if (t->table > 0 && ds_nl_add_rule4(ctx, t->net_be, t->prefix, 0, 0, t->table,
                                      RULE_PRIO_FROM) < 0)
    ret = -1;
  if (t->nat6 &&
      ds_nl_rule6(ctx, 1, &t->prefix6, 64, 0, RT_TABLE_MAIN, RULE_PRIO_TO) < 0)
    ret = -1;
  if (t->table6 > 0 &&
      ds_nl_rule6(ctx, 1, &t->prefix6, 64, 1, t->table6, RULE_PRIO_FROM) < 0)
    ret = -1;
  if (ret < 0)
    ua_warn("[NET] One or more route rules failed to install");
  ds_nl_close(ctx);
}

/* One family's firewall rules. Fails on MASQUERADE or FORWARD, the two
 * without which that family has no connectivity at all. A mobile uplink's
 * MTU is often below the 1500 the host assumes, hence the clamp. */
static int install_family_rules(int family, const char *cidr,
                                const char *iface) {
  ds_ipt_ensure_input_accept(family, iface);
  int ret = ds_ipt_ensure_masquerade(family, cidr) < 0 ||
                    ds_ipt_ensure_forward_accept(family, iface) < 0
                ? -1
                : 0;
  ds_ipt_ensure_mss_clamp(family);
  return ret;
}

/* The per-interface half of NAT66, redone whenever the netdev is re-created.
 * Our end is a router: IPv6 on even where the default is off, and never
 * autoconfigured from what the host sends. accept_ra_rt_table exists only on
 * Android, whose default files connected routes in a private per-interface
 * table; 0 keeps them in main, where the TO rule sends replies. The prefix
 * route goes in by hand too, for a netdev that existed before the knob. */
static int nat6_iface(ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx, struct tether *t) {
  static const char *const knobs[][2] = {{"disable_ipv6", "0"},
                                         {"accept_ra", "0"},
                                         {"autoconf", "0"},
                                         {"accept_ra_rt_table", "0"}};
  for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(knobs) / sizeof(knobs[0]); i++) {
    char p[128];
    snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/%s/%s", t->iface,
             knobs[i][0]);
    write_file(p, knobs[i][1]);
  }
  struct in6_addr ll, gw = t->prefix6;
  inet_pton(AF_INET6, NAT6_GW_LL, &ll);
  gw.s6_addr[15] = 1;
  int err = ds_nl_add_addr6(ctx, t->iface, &ll, 64);
  if (err == 0)
    err = ds_nl_add_addr6(ctx, t->iface, &gw, 64);
  if (err == 0)
    err = ds_nl_add_route6(ctx, &t->prefix6, 64,
                           ds_nl_get_ifindex(ctx, t->iface));
  return err;
}

/* Turning on IPv6 forwarding makes the kernel ignore RAs on every interface
 * at accept_ra=1, so a machine that got its own address by SLAAC would lose
 * its default route when the current one expires. 2 means "accept even while
 * forwarding". Android already runs its uplinks at 2, and if forwarding is
 * already on, whoever turned it on has dealt with this. */
static void keep_host_slaac(void) {
  char val[4] = {0};
  if (read_file("/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding", val, sizeof(val)) >
          0 &&
      val[0] == '1')
    return;
  DIR *d = opendir("/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf");
  if (!d)
    return;
  struct dirent *e;
  while ((e = readdir(d))) {
    if (e->d_name[0] == '.' || !strcmp(e->d_name, "all") ||
        !strcmp(e->d_name, "lo"))
      continue;
    char p[PATH_MAX];
    snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/%s/accept_ra", e->d_name);
    if (read_file(p, val, sizeof(val)) > 0 && val[0] == '1')
      write_file(p, "2");
  }
  closedir(d);
}

/* NAT66, after Droidspaces' setup_nat6_host (itself after LXC's lxc-net): a
 * ULA /64 on the link, one MASQUERADE rule, forwarding, and RAs from the DHCP
 * thread. Anything missing leaves the host on IPv4 only, as it was before. */
static void nat6_up(struct tether *t) {
  if (access("/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding", F_OK) != 0)
    return;
  /* Not a warning: stock GKI has no IPv6 nat table; `check` reports it */
  if (!ds_ipt6_available()) {
    ua_log("[NET] No IPv6 NAT in this kernel; the host gets IPv4 only");
    return;
  }
  ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx = ds_nl_open();
  if (!ctx)
    return;
  inet_pton(AF_INET6, NAT6_PREFIX, &t->prefix6);
  int err = nat6_iface(ctx, t);
  ds_nl_close(ctx);
  /* Fail closed: an address and a default route with no MASQUERADE behind
   * them make every IPv6 connection hang instead of falling back to IPv4 */
  if (err < 0 || install_family_rules(AF_INET6, NAT6_CIDR, t->iface) < 0) {
    ua_warn("[NET] IPv6 setup on %s failed; the host gets IPv4 only", t->iface);
    ds_ipt_remove_nat_rules(AF_INET6, NAT6_CIDR, t->iface);
    return;
  }
  keep_host_slaac();
  write_file("/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding", "1");
  t->nat6 = 1;
  ua_log("[NET] IPv6: advertising " NAT6_CIDR " to the host");
}

static int net_up(struct tether *t) {
  ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx = ds_nl_open();
  if (!ctx) {
    ua_error("Cannot open a netlink socket: %s", strerror(errno));
    return -1;
  }
  int ret = ds_nl_link_up(ctx, t->iface);
  int addr = ds_nl_add_addr4(ctx, t->iface, t->ip_be, t->prefix);
  if (ret < 0 || (addr < 0 && addr != -EEXIST)) {
    ua_error("Cannot bring up %s: %s", t->iface,
             strerror(-(ret < 0 ? ret : addr)));
    ds_nl_close(ctx);
    return -1;
  }
  ds_nl_close(ctx);

  write_file("/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward", "1");
  if (install_family_rules(AF_INET, t->cidr, t->iface) < 0) {
    ua_error("Cannot install the NAT rules for %s", t->cidr);
    return -1;
  }

  nat6_up(t);
  install_policy_rules(t);
  sync_uplink(t, 0);
  ds_dhcp_server_start(t->dns, t->iface, t->offer_be, t->ip_be, t->mask_be,
                       t->nat6 ? &t->prefix6 : NULL);
  t->ifindex = if_nametoindex(t->iface);
  return 0;
}

/* Kernels with Samsung's UEVENT configfs (M62 4.14) free the netdev when the
 * gadget unbinds and make a new one at bind, so any other function starting
 * or stopping hands us a fresh rndis0/usb0: no address, down, and a DHCP
 * socket still bound to the dead ifindex. Spot the new index and redo the
 * per-interface half. The NAT rules match by name and subnet, so they hold. */
static void follow_netdev(struct tether *t) {
  unsigned idx = if_nametoindex(t->iface);
  if (!idx || idx == t->ifindex)
    return;
  ua_log("[NET] %s was re-created by a rebind, configuring it again", t->iface);
  ds_dhcp_server_stop();
  ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx = ds_nl_open();
  if (ctx) {
    int r = ds_nl_link_up(ctx, t->iface);
    int a = ds_nl_add_addr4(ctx, t->iface, t->ip_be, t->prefix);
    if (r < 0 || (a < 0 && a != -EEXIST))
      ua_warn("[NET] Cannot bring up the new %s", t->iface);
    if (t->nat6 && nat6_iface(ctx, t) < 0)
      ua_warn("[NET] Cannot give the new %s its IPv6 addresses", t->iface);
    ds_nl_close(ctx);
  }
  ds_dhcp_server_start(t->dns, t->iface, t->offer_be, t->ip_be, t->mask_be,
                       t->nat6 ? &t->prefix6 : NULL);
  t->ifindex = idx;
}

static void net_down(struct tether *t) {
  ds_dhcp_server_stop();
  ds_ipt_remove_nat_rules(AF_INET, t->cidr, t->iface);
  if (t->nat6)
    ds_ipt_remove_nat_rules(AF_INET6, NAT6_CIDR, t->iface);
  if (is_android()) {
    ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx = ds_nl_open();
    if (ctx) {
      ds_nl_del_rule4(ctx, 0, 0, t->net_be, t->prefix, RT_TABLE_MAIN,
                      RULE_PRIO_TO);
      if (t->table > 0)
        ds_nl_del_rule4(ctx, t->net_be, t->prefix, 0, 0, t->table,
                        RULE_PRIO_FROM);
      if (t->nat6)
        ds_nl_rule6(ctx, 0, &t->prefix6, 64, 0, RT_TABLE_MAIN, RULE_PRIO_TO);
      if (t->table6 > 0)
        ds_nl_rule6(ctx, 0, &t->prefix6, 64, 1, t->table6, RULE_PRIO_FROM);
      ds_nl_close(ctx);
    }
  }
  /* Forwarding stays on: a Droidspaces container or Android's own tethering
   * may be routing through it by now, and turning it off would cut them */
}

/* Re-apply what someone else may have removed, then follow the uplink.
 * Droidspaces' do_uplink_reprobe(), with our subnets and interface. */
static void reprobe(struct tether *t) {
  if (t->gateway) {
    gw_tick(t);
    return;
  }
  follow_netdev(t);
  install_policy_rules(t);
  /* Only 0 means a rule is missing; -1 is "tables unreadable", where a
   * blind reinstall through the iptables binary would stack duplicates */
  if (ds_ipt_host_rules_present(AF_INET, t->iface, t->cidr, 0) == 0 ||
      (t->nat6 &&
       ds_ipt_host_rules_present(AF_INET6, t->iface, NAT6_CIDR, 0) == 0)) {
    ua_warn("[NET] The tether firewall rules are gone (netd restart or a "
            "firewall app?); reinstalling");
    install_family_rules(AF_INET, t->cidr, t->iface);
    if (t->nat6)
      install_family_rules(AF_INET6, NAT6_CIDR, t->iface);
  }
  sync_uplink(t, 1);
}

/* netd resets forwarding on Android, and on Linux any tool restoring its own
 * saved value on exit does the same. /proc/sys raises no event, so poll. */
static void keep_forwarding(const struct tether *t) {
  char val[4];
  if (!t->gateway && (t->table > 0 || !is_android()) &&
      read_file("/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward", val, sizeof(val)) > 0 &&
      val[0] == '0') {
    ua_log("[NET] ip_forward was switched off; switching it back on");
    write_file("/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward", "1");
  }
  if (t->nat6 &&
      read_file("/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding", val, sizeof(val)) >
          0 &&
      val[0] == '0')
    write_file("/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding", "1");
}

static int monitor_socket(const struct tether *t) {
  int sock = socket(AF_NETLINK, SOCK_RAW | SOCK_CLOEXEC, NETLINK_ROUTE);
  if (sock < 0)
    return -1;
  struct sockaddr_nl sa;
  memset(&sa, 0, sizeof(sa));
  sa.nl_family = AF_NETLINK;
  /* Rule changes are netd swapping the default network, the Wi-Fi <-> mobile
   * handoff itself. No RTMGRP_ macro exists for rule groups. */
  sa.nl_groups = RTMGRP_LINK | RTMGRP_IPV4_IFADDR | RTMGRP_IPV4_ROUTE |
                 (1u << (RTNLGRP_IPV4_RULE - 1));
  if (t->nat6)
    sa.nl_groups |= RTMGRP_IPV6_ROUTE | (1u << (RTNLGRP_IPV6_RULE - 1));
  if (bind(sock, (struct sockaddr *)&sa, sizeof(sa)) < 0) {
    close(sock);
    return -1;
  }
  return sock;
}

/* An event on an interface that still exists and is not loopback or our own
 * bridge and veth (ua-*). The USB interface counts: a re-created one is what
 * follow_netdev() is waiting for. */
static int real_iface(int ifindex) {
  char name[IFNAMSIZ] = {0};
  if (ifindex <= 0 || !if_indextoname((unsigned)ifindex, name))
    return 0;
  return strncmp(name, "ua-", 3) != 0 && strcmp(name, "lo") != 0;
}

static int wants_reprobe(uint8_t *buf, ssize_t len) {
  for (struct nlmsghdr *h = (struct nlmsghdr *)buf; NLMSG_OK(h, (uint32_t)len);
       h = NLMSG_NEXT(h, len)) {
    if (h->nlmsg_type == NLMSG_DONE || h->nlmsg_type == NLMSG_ERROR)
      break;
    if (h->nlmsg_type == RTM_NEWRULE || h->nlmsg_type == RTM_DELRULE)
      return 1; /* our own rule echoes settle in one no-op pass */
    if (h->nlmsg_type == RTM_NEWLINK || h->nlmsg_type == RTM_DELLINK) {
      if (real_iface(((struct ifinfomsg *)NLMSG_DATA(h))->ifi_index))
        return 1;
    } else if (h->nlmsg_type == RTM_NEWADDR || h->nlmsg_type == RTM_DELADDR) {
      struct ifaddrmsg *ifa = NLMSG_DATA(h);
      if (ifa->ifa_family == AF_INET && real_iface((int)ifa->ifa_index))
        return 1;
    } else if (h->nlmsg_type == RTM_NEWROUTE || h->nlmsg_type == RTM_DELROUTE) {
      /* IPv6 also announces every /64, neighbour and cached clone; only a
       * route as short as uplink detection accepts can move the uplink */
      struct rtmsg *rtm = NLMSG_DATA(h);
      if (rtm->rtm_family != AF_INET &&
          !(rtm->rtm_family == AF_INET6 && rtm->rtm_dst_len < 8))
        continue;
      int oif = 0, rlen = (int)RTM_PAYLOAD(h);
      for (struct rtattr *rta = RTM_RTA(rtm); RTA_OK(rta, rlen);
           rta = RTA_NEXT(rta, rlen))
        if (rta->rta_type == RTA_OIF && RTA_PAYLOAD(rta) >= (int)sizeof(int))
          oif = *(int *)RTA_DATA(rta);
      /* No output interface (a blackhole, say) still counts */
      if (oif <= 0 || real_iface(oif))
        return 1;
    }
  }
  return 0;
}

/* The network side lives as long as this loop: Droidspaces' route monitor,
 * event driven over rtnetlink with a heartbeat behind it. It follows the
 * uplink between Wi-Fi and mobile data, puts back the rules and forwarding
 * that Android (or anyone) removes, and re-configures a re-created netdev. */
static int serve(struct tether *t, int ready_fd) {
  sigset_t set;
  sigemptyset(&set);
  sigaddset(&set, SIGTERM);
  sigaddset(&set, SIGINT);
  sigaddset(&set, SIGHUP);
  sigprocmask(SIG_BLOCK, &set, NULL);
  int sfd = signalfd(-1, &set, SFD_CLOEXEC);

  int ok = sfd >= 0 && (t->gateway ? gw_up(t) : net_up(t)) == 0;
  if (ready_fd >= 0) {
    char c = ok ? '1' : '0';
    if (write(ready_fd, &c, 1) < 0)
      ua_debug("ready pipe: %s", strerror(errno));
    close(ready_fd);
  }
  if (!ok) {
    if (sfd < 0)
      ua_error("signalfd: %s", strerror(errno));
    else if (t->gateway)
      gw_down();
    else
      net_down(t);
    return -1;
  }

  int sock = monitor_socket(t);
  if (sock < 0)
    ua_warn("[NET] No rtnetlink socket (%s); following changes on the "
            "heartbeat only",
            strerror(errno));
  uint8_t buf[8192];
  for (;;) {
    keep_forwarding(t);
    struct pollfd pfd[2] = {{sfd, POLLIN, 0}, {sock, POLLIN, 0}};
    int pr = poll(pfd, sock >= 0 ? 2 : 1, HEARTBEAT_MS);
    if (pr < 0 && errno == EINTR)
      continue;
    if (pr < 0 || (pfd[0].revents & POLLIN))
      break;
    if (pr == 0) {
      reprobe(t);
      continue;
    }
    ssize_t len = recv(sock, buf, sizeof(buf), 0);
    if (len < 0 && errno == ENOBUFS) {
      /* An event burst overflowed the socket: resync and keep going */
      reprobe(t);
      continue;
    }
    if (len < 0 && errno != EINTR && errno != EAGAIN) {
      ua_warn("[NET] rtnetlink: %s; following changes on the heartbeat only",
              strerror(errno));
      close(sock);
      sock = -1;
    }
    if (len <= 0 || !wants_reprobe(buf, len))
      continue;
    /* A handoff is a burst of rule, route and address events: let it settle
     * into one reprobe instead of one per event */
    while (poll(&pfd[1], 1, 200) > 0 && recv(sock, buf, sizeof(buf), 0) > 0)
      ;
    reprobe(t);
  }
  if (sock >= 0)
    close(sock);
  close(sfd);
  ua_log("[NET] Stopping tethering on %s", t->iface);
  if (t->gateway)
    gw_down();
  else
```
