`src/net/uplink.c`:

```c
/*
 * USB Arsenal - lifted from Droidspaces (src/net/network.c) by the same author
 *
 * Finds the interface and routing table that currently reach the internet,
 * so tethered traffic can be pointed at it. Android keeps one routing table
 * per network and a netd rule naming the default one; plain Linux has a
 * default route in the main table.
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
 */

#include "net.h"
#include "usbarsenal.h"
#include <fnmatch.h>
#include <linux/rtnetlink.h>

/* The only interface families that terminate internet access, highest
 * precedence first: Wi-Fi STA, ethernet, CLAT (464xlat), Qualcomm and MTK
 * mobile data. */
static const char *const k_uplink_patterns[] = {
    "wlan*", "eth*", "end*", "enp*", "v4-*", "rmnet*", "*ccmni*",
};

/* Never an uplink: downstream devices that share connectivity out (ours
 * included, usb0/ncm0/rndis0 are exactly what we create), VPN tunnels,
 * loopback and placeholders. */
static const char *const k_uplink_excludes[] = {
    "ds-*",   "lo",   "dummy*", "swlan*", "ap*",  "usb*",
    "rndis*", "ncm*", "p2p*",   "tun*",   "ppp*", "bt-pan",
};

static int iface_is_running(const char *ifname) {
  int fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0);
  if (fd < 0)
    return 0;
  struct ifreq ifr;
  memset(&ifr, 0, sizeof(ifr));
  safe_strncpy(ifr.ifr_name, ifname, IFNAMSIZ);
  int ret = 0;
  if (ioctl(fd, SIOCGIFFLAGS, &ifr) == 0)
    ret = (ifr.ifr_flags & (IFF_UP | IFF_RUNNING)) == (IFF_UP | IFF_RUNNING);
  close(fd);
  return ret;
}

static int uplink_candidate_ok(const char *ifname) {
  if (!ifname[0])
    return 0;
  for (size_t i = 0;
       i < sizeof(k_uplink_excludes) / sizeof(k_uplink_excludes[0]); i++)
    if (fnmatch(k_uplink_excludes[i], ifname, 0) == 0)
      return 0;
  return iface_is_running(ifname);
}

static int scan_uplink_whitelist(ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx, char *iface_out,
                                 int *table_out) {
  char all[64][IFNAMSIZ];
  int count = ds_nl_list_ifaces(ctx, all, 64);
  for (size_t p = 0;
       p < sizeof(k_uplink_patterns) / sizeof(k_uplink_patterns[0]); p++)
    for (int j = 0; j < count; j++) {
      int tbl = 0;
      if (fnmatch(k_uplink_patterns[p], all[j], 0) != 0 ||
          !uplink_candidate_ok(all[j]) ||
          ds_nl_get_iface_table(ctx, AF_INET, all[j], &tbl) != 0)
        continue;
      safe_strncpy(iface_out, all[j], IFNAMSIZ);
      *table_out = tbl;
      return 0;
    }
  return -ENOENT;
}

/* A pinned --upstream is taken as given: the user picked it deliberately, so
 * none of the exclude heuristics apply, only "is it up and routed". */
static int resolve_pinned(ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx, int family, const char *pin,
                          char *iface_out, int *table_out) {
  int tbl = RT_TABLE_MAIN;
  if (!iface_is_running(pin))
    return -ENOENT;
  if (is_android() && ds_nl_get_iface_table(ctx, family, pin, &tbl) != 0)
    return -ENOENT;
  safe_strncpy(iface_out, pin, IFNAMSIZ);
  *table_out = tbl;
  return 0;
}

/* First hit wins: a pinned interface, Android's netd default-network rule,
 * the main table's default route, then a name scan. */
static const char *probe(ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx, int family, const char *pin,
                         char *iface_out, int *table_out) {
  iface_out[0] = '\0';
  *table_out = 0;
  if (pin && pin[0])
    return resolve_pinned(ctx, family, pin, iface_out, table_out) == 0
               ? "pinned"
               : NULL;
  if (is_android() &&
      ds_nl_get_android_default(ctx, family, iface_out, table_out) == 0 &&
      uplink_candidate_ok(iface_out))
    return "netd rule";
  iface_out[0] = '\0';
  *table_out = RT_TABLE_MAIN;
  if (ds_nl_get_table_default_oif(ctx, family, RT_TABLE_MAIN, iface_out) == 0 &&
      uplink_candidate_ok(iface_out))
    return "main table";
  /* IPv4 only: a name match is a guess, and the IMS bearer fits it (an
   * always-up IPv6 rmnetX with its own default route), so an IPv6 scan would
   * send the host's traffic out through the carrier's voice network */
  iface_out[0] = '\0';
  if (family == AF_INET &&
      scan_uplink_whitelist(ctx, iface_out, table_out) == 0)
    return "interface scan";
  return NULL;
}

/* IPv4 goes through every step first, so dual-stack and CLAT networks resolve
 * as they always did. Only with v6 set and nothing carrying IPv4 is an
 * IPv6-only uplink taken, and then *table_out is 0: there is no IPv4 table to
 * point at. Returns how the uplink was found, or NULL when there is none. */
const char *ua_find_uplink(const char *pin, char *iface_out, int *table_out,
                           int v6) {
  ds_nl_ctx_t *ctx = ds_nl_open();
  if (!ctx)
    return NULL;
  const char *how = probe(ctx, AF_INET, pin, iface_out, table_out);
  if (!how && v6 && (how = probe(ctx, AF_INET6, pin, iface_out, table_out)))
    *table_out = 0;
  ds_nl_close(ctx);
  return how;
}

```

`src/setup.c`:

```c
/*
 * USB Arsenal - composite USB gadget builder for Linux and Android
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
 *
 * The setup: what each function starts with, in the workspace, so the app
 * and the CLI share one record and a cleared app loses nothing. Two files
 * with the same keys, Droidspaces' container.config idea:
 *   Gadget/setup.conf    the draft; `setup set` and a start with arguments edit
 * it Gadget/running.conf  what the last successful start used; the backend
 *                        writes it, whoever started the function
 * A bare `start` runs the draft; `apply` brings what runs to the draft;
 * `status --json` reports both and whether they differ. The format and the
 * loader are config.c's.
 */

#include "usbarsenal.h"

#define SETUP_LEAF "setup.conf"
#define RUNNING_LEAF "running.conf"

#define F(field) offsetof(struct ua_setup, field)
#define S(field) sizeof(((struct ua_setup *)0)->field)
#define LUN(n)                                                                 \
  {"storage_lun" #n,                                                           \
   K_LUN,                                                                      \
   F(lun[n]),                                                                  \
   S(lun[n]),                                                                  \
   0,                                                                          \
   NULL,                                                                       \
   n == 0 ? "MODE:PATH; mode auto | cdrom | dvd | disk | rw" : NULL}

static const struct ua_key keys[] = {
    {"udc", K_STR, F(udc), S(udc), 63, NULL,
     "controller; empty: the only one in /sys/class/udc"},
    LUN(0),
    LUN(1),
    LUN(2),
    LUN(3),
    LUN(4),
    LUN(5),
    LUN(6),
    LUN(7),
    {"tether_function", K_CHOICE, F(tether_function), S(tether_function), 0,
     "ncm rndis", "ncm | rndis; empty: the profile's"},
    {"tether_gateway", K_STR, F(tether_gateway), S(tether_gateway), 255, NULL,
     "a container's name; empty: no gateway"},
    {"tether_gateway_iface", K_STR, F(tether_gateway_iface),
     S(tether_gateway_iface), IFNAMSIZ - 1, NULL, "empty: usb0"},
    {"tether_net", K_UINT, F(tether_net), 0, 1, NULL, "0: --no-net"},
    {"tether_address", K_CIDR, F(tether_address), S(tether_address), 0, NULL,
     "empty: the profile's"},
    {"tether_dns", K_DNS, F(tether_dns), S(tether_dns), 0, NULL,
     "empty: the profile's"},
    {"tether_upstream", K_STR, F(tether_upstream), S(tether_upstream),
     IFNAMSIZ - 1, NULL, "empty: the profile's"},
    {"hid_interval", K_UINT, F(hid_interval), 0, 255, NULL,
     "1-255; 0: the kernel's default"},
};

#define NKEYS (sizeof(keys) / sizeof(keys[0]))

/* Which function a key belongs to; the UDC goes with every start */
static enum ua_fn key_fn(size_t i) {
  const char *n = keys[i].name;
  if (!strncmp(n, "storage_", 8))
    return UA_FN_STORAGE;
  if (!strncmp(n, "tether_", 7))
    return UA_FN_TETHER;
  if (!strncmp(n, "hid_", 4))
    return UA_FN_HID;
  return UA_FN_ALL;
}

static void ua_setup_defaults(struct ua_setup *s) {
  memset(s, 0, sizeof(*s));
  s->tether_net = 1;
}

static void load(const char *leaf, struct ua_setup *s) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  ua_setup_defaults(s);
  ua_ws_path("Gadget", leaf, p, sizeof(p));
  ua_table_load(p, keys, NKEYS, s);
}

void ua_setup_load(struct ua_setup *s) { load(SETUP_LEAF, s); }
/* Running carries the boot it was written in, as the handoff does: after a
 * reboot nothing of ours runs, whatever the file says */
void ua_running_load(struct ua_setup *s) {
  char p[PATH_MAX], line[80] = "", boot[40];
  ua_setup_defaults(s);
  ua_ws_path("Gadget", RUNNING_LEAF, p, sizeof(p));
  FILE *f = fopen(p, "re");
  if (!f)
    return;
  if (fgets(line, sizeof(line), f))
    line[strcspn(line, "\n")] = '\0';
  fclose(f);
  ua_boot_marker(boot, sizeof(boot));
  if (strncmp(line, "# boot ", 7) || strcmp(line + 7, boot)) {
    unlink(p);
    return;
  }
  ua_table_load(p, keys, NKEYS, s);
}

struct body_arg {
  const struct ua_setup *s;
  int running;
};

static void body(FILE *f, const void *arg) {
  const struct body_arg *a = arg;
  if (a->running) {
    char boot[40];
    ua_boot_marker(boot, sizeof(boot));
    fprintf(f,
            "# boot %s\n# What the last successful start of each function "
            "used. Written by\n# " UA_NAME "; `" UA_NAME
            " setup show` reads it.\n\n",
            boot);
  } else
    fprintf(f,
            "# USB Arsenal setup: what each function starts with. Change "
            "it with\n#   " UA_NAME " setup set KEY=VALUE ...\n# An empty "
            "value means the active profile's default, or the kernel's.\n\n");
  for (size_t i = 0; i < NKEYS; i++) {
    char v[UA_LUN_SPEC], line[UA_LUN_SPEC + 40];
    ua_key_get(a->s, &keys[i], v, sizeof(v));
    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%s=%s", keys[i].name, v);
    if (keys[i].comment && !a->running)
      fprintf(f, "%-32s # %s\n", line, keys[i].comment);
    else
      fprintf(f, "%s\n", line);
  }
}

static int save(const char *leaf, const struct ua_setup *s, int running) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  struct body_arg a = {s, running};
  ua_ws_path("Gadget", leaf, p, sizeof(p));
  if (ua_write_atomic(p, 0644, body, &a) < 0) {
    ua_error("Cannot write %s: %s", p, strerror(errno));
    return -1;
  }
  return 0;
}

int ua_setup_save(const struct ua_setup *s) { return save(SETUP_LEAF, s, 0); }

/* "key=value" into the draft, validated as the file would be */
int ua_setup_set(struct ua_setup *s, const char *assignment) {
  char key[64];
  const char *eq = strchr(assignment, '=');
  if (!eq || eq == assignment || (size_t)(eq - assignment) >= sizeof(key)) {
    ua_error("'%s' is not KEY=VALUE", assignment);
    return -1;
  }
  memcpy(key, assignment, (size_t)(eq - assignment));
  key[eq - assignment] = '\0';
  for (size_t i = 0; i < NKEYS; i++)
    if (!strcmp(key, keys[i].name)) {
      if (ua_key_set(s, &keys[i], eq + 1) == 0)
        return 0;
      ua_error("Bad value '%s' for %s%s%s", eq + 1, key,
               keys[i].comment ? ": " : "",
               keys[i].comment ? keys[i].comment : "");
      return -1;
    }
  ua_error("No such setup key: %s", key);
  return -1;
}

/* Copy fn's keys (UA_FN_ALL: every key) from one setup to another; for
 * storage only the LUNs whose bit is in mask. The controller belongs to no
 * function, so only UA_FN_ALL takes it: `setup reset hid` must not drop it */
static void copy_fn(struct ua_setup *to, const struct ua_setup *from,
                    enum ua_fn fn, unsigned mask) {
  for (size_t i = 0; i < NKEYS; i++) {
    enum ua_fn kf = key_fn(i);
    if (fn != UA_FN_ALL && kf != fn)
      continue;
    if (kf == UA_FN_STORAGE && !(mask & (1u << (keys[i].name[11] - '0'))))
      continue;
    memcpy((char *)to + keys[i].off, (const char *)from + keys[i].off,
           keys[i].kind == K_UINT ? sizeof(unsigned) : keys[i].size);
  }
}

int ua_running_take(enum ua_fn fn, unsigned mask) {
  struct ua_setup s, r;
  ua_setup_load(&s);
  ua_running_load(&r);
  copy_fn(&r, &s, fn, mask);
  /* Every start runs on the setup's controller */
  safe_strncpy(r.udc, s.udc, sizeof(r.udc));
  return save(RUNNING_LEAF, &r, 1);
}

int ua_running_clear(enum ua_fn fn) {
  struct ua_setup r, d;
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  /* A --perm or --group given to `hid start` lasts as long as that HID
   * (hid.c save_perm); the next one starts from the profile's */
  if (fn == UA_FN_ALL || fn == UA_FN_HID) {
    ua_ws_path("Gadget", "hid.perm", p, sizeof(p));
    unlink(p);
  }
  if (fn == UA_FN_ALL) {
    ua_ws_path("Gadget", RUNNING_LEAF, p, sizeof(p));
    return unlink(p) < 0 && errno != ENOENT ? -1 : 0;
  }
  ua_running_load(&r);
  ua_setup_defaults(&d);
  copy_fn(&r, &d, fn, ~0u);
  return save(RUNNING_LEAF, &r, 1);
}

int ua_running_clear_lun(int lun) {
  struct ua_setup r;
  ua_running_load(&r);
  r.lun[lun][0] = '\0';
  return save(RUNNING_LEAF, &r, 1);
}

/* An empty value means the profile's (or usb0 for the cable's name), so two
 * setups are compared as a start would read them: picking the function the
 * profile already gives is no change, and a profile switch changes nothing
 * either, since both sides resolve against the same profile */
static void resolved(const struct ua_setup *s, const struct ua_config *cfg,
                     size_t i, char *out, size_t size) {
  ua_key_get(s, &keys[i], out, size);
  if (out[0])
    return;
  const char *n = keys[i].name;
  if (!strcmp(n, "tether_function"))
    safe_strncpy(out, cfg->tether_function, size);
  else if (!strcmp(n, "tether_address"))
    safe_strncpy(out, cfg->tether_address, size);
  else if (!strcmp(n, "tether_dns"))
    safe_strncpy(out, cfg->tether_dns, size);
  else if (!strcmp(n, "tether_upstream"))
    safe_strncpy(out, cfg->tether_upstream, size);
  else if (!strcmp(n, "tether_gateway_iface"))
    safe_strncpy(out, "usb0", size);
}

int ua_setup_pending(enum ua_fn fn, const struct ua_setup *setup,
                     const struct ua_setup *running) {
  struct ua_config cfg;
  ua_config_active(&cfg);
  for (size_t i = 0; i < NKEYS; i++) {
    if (key_fn(i) != fn)
      continue;
    char a[UA_LUN_SPEC], b[UA_LUN_SPEC];
    resolved(setup, &cfg, i, a, sizeof(a));
    resolved(running, &cfg, i, b, sizeof(b));
    if (strcmp(a, b))
      return 1;
  }
  return 0;
}

int ua_fn_linked(const struct ua_gadget *g, enum ua_fn fn) {
  switch (fn) {
  case UA_FN_STORAGE:
    return ua_gadget_has(g, UA_F_STORAGE);
  case UA_FN_TETHER:
    return ua_gadget_has(g, UA_F_NCM) || ua_gadget_has(g, UA_F_RNDIS);
  case UA_FN_HID:
    return ua_gadget_has(g, UA_F_KBD);
  default:
    return 0;
  }
}

static void json_table(const char *name, const struct ua_setup *s, int *first) {
  int f = 1;
  printf("%s\"%s\":{", *first ? "" : ",", name);
  *first = 0;
  for (size_t i = 0; i < NKEYS; i++) {
    char v[UA_LUN_SPEC];
    ua_key_get(s, &keys[i], v, sizeof(v));
    ua_json_str(keys[i].name, v, &f);
  }
  printf("}");
}

/* The status --json tail: boot_id, setup, running and pending. Pending is
 * "the function is linked and its draft differs from what started it". */
void ua_setup_json(const struct ua_gadget *g, int live, int *first) {
  struct ua_setup s, r;
  char boot[40];
  ua_setup_load(&s);
  ua_running_load(&r);
  ua_boot_marker(boot, sizeof(boot));
  ua_json_str("boot_id", boot, first);
  json_table("setup", &s, first);
  json_table("running", &r, first);
  printf(",\"pending\":{");
  static const char *const names[] = {"storage", "tether", "hid"};
  int f = 1;
  for (enum ua_fn fn = UA_FN_STORAGE; fn <= UA_FN_HID; fn++)
    ua_json_int(names[fn],
                live && ua_fn_linked(g, fn) && ua_setup_pending(fn, &s, &r),
                &f);
  printf("}");
}

void ua_help_setup(void) {
  printf(
      "Usage: " UA_NAME " setup <action> [KEY=VALUE ...]\n\n"
      "What each function starts with, kept in the workspace so the app and\n"
      "the command line share it. A `start` with arguments saves them here;\n"
      "a bare `start` runs what is saved; `<function> apply` brings what\n"
      "runs to it.\n\n"
      "Actions:\n"
      "  show [--json]  Every key: the setup, and what the last start used\n"
      "  set KEY=VALUE  Change the setup. A bad value changes nothing.\n"
      "  reset [FN]     Back to the defaults (storage, tether or hid; all\n"
      "                 without one)\n"
      "  revert [FN]    Back to what runs (what Discard does in the app)\n\n"
      "Keys:\n");
  for (size_t i = 0; i < NKEYS; i++)
    printf("  %-22s %s\n", keys[i].name,
           keys[i].comment ? keys[i].comment : "");
  printf("\nThe files are <workspace>/Gadget/setup.conf and running.conf.\n\n"
         "Examples:\n"
         "  " UA_NAME
         " setup set storage_lun0=auto:/sdcard/USB-Arsenal/Disks/win.iso\n"
         "  " UA_NAME " setup set tether_function=rndis tether_dns=9.9.9.9\n"
         "  " UA_NAME " storage start\n"
         "  " UA_NAME " setup show\n");
}

static int fn_of(const char *name, enum ua_fn *fn) {
  if (!name)
    *fn = UA_FN_ALL;
  else if (!strcmp(name, "storage"))
    *fn = UA_FN_STORAGE;
  else if (!strcmp(name, "tether"))
    *fn = UA_FN_TETHER;
  else if (!strcmp(name, "hid"))
    *fn = UA_FN_HID;
  else
    return -1;
  return 0;
}

static int do_show(int json) {
  struct ua_setup s, r;
  ua_setup_load(&s);
  ua_running_load(&r);
  if (json) {
    int first = 1;
    printf("{");
    json_table("setup", &s, &first);
    json_table("running", &r, &first);
    printf("}\n");
    return UA_EXIT_OK;
  }
  printf("%-22s %-40s %s\n", "key", "setup", "running");
  for (size_t i = 0; i < NKEYS; i++) {
    char a[UA_LUN_SPEC], b[UA_LUN_SPEC];
    ua_key_get(&s, &keys[i], a, sizeof(a));
    ua_key_get(&r, &keys[i], b, sizeof(b));
    printf("%-22s %-40s %s\n", keys[i].name, a[0] ? a : "-", b[0] ? b : "-");
  }
  return UA_EXIT_OK;
}

int ua_cmd_setup(int argc, char **argv) {
  if (argc < 2 || ua_want_help(argc, argv)) {
    ua_help_setup();
    return UA_EXIT_OK;
  }
  const char *action = argv[1];
  if (!strcmp(action, "show")) {
    int json = argc == 3 && !strcmp(argv[2], "--json");
    if (argc > 2 && !json) {
      ua_usage_error("setup", "show takes no arguments but --json");
      return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
    }
    return do_show(json);
  }
  if (geteuid() != 0) {
    ua_error("Must be run as root");
    return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
  }
  if (!strcmp(action, "set")) {
    struct ua_setup s;
    if (argc < 3) {
      ua_usage_error("setup", "set takes KEY=VALUE");
      return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
    }
    ua_setup_load(&s);
    for (int i = 2; i < argc; i++)
      if (ua_setup_set(&s, argv[i]) < 0)
        return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
    return ua_setup_save(&s) < 0 ? UA_EXIT_FAIL : UA_EXIT_OK;
  }
  if (!strcmp(action, "reset") || !strcmp(action, "revert")) {
    struct ua_setup s, from;
    enum ua_fn fn;
    if (argc > 3 || fn_of(argc == 3 ? argv[2] : NULL, &fn) < 0) {
      ua_usage_error("setup", "%s takes storage, tether, hid or nothing",
                     action);
      return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
    }
    ua_setup_load(&s);
    if (action[2] == 's')
      ua_setup_defaults(&from);
    else
      ua_running_load(&from);
    copy_fn(&s, &from, fn, ~0u);
    if (ua_setup_save(&s) < 0)
      return UA_EXIT_FAIL;
    ua_log("Setup %s%s%s", action[2] == 's' ? "reset" : "reverted to what runs",
           argc == 3 ? " for " : "", argc == 3 ? argv[2] : "");
    return UA_EXIT_OK;
  }
  ua_usage_error("setup", "Unknown action '%s'", action);
  return UA_EXIT_USAGE;
}

```

`src/utils.c`:

```c
/*
 * USB Arsenal - composite USB gadget builder for Linux and Android
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 ravindu644 <droidcasts@protonmail.com>
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
 *
 * The file, process and logging helpers are lifted from Droidspaces
 * (src/utils.c, src/android/android.c) by the same author.
 */

#include "usbarsenal.h"

int ua_verbose;

/* One log for every run, the app's or a shell's, and the tether daemon's:
 * Logs/usb-arsenal.log, a timestamped line per message, tagged ones too.
 * Each line is one open, write and close: O_APPEND lands it whole beside
 * another process's, and the daemon follows a rotation by opening the
 * path afresh. ponytail: two runs rotating in the same instant may lose the
 * old file; a lock is not worth a log */
static char log_path[PATH_MAX];
static char log_who[32];

static void log_line(const char *prefix, const char *msg) {
  char line[4096 + 96], stamp[32];
  struct timespec ts;
  struct tm tm;
  if (!log_path[0])
    return;
  /* UTC, marked: a static binary has no zone data, the app shows local time */
  clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &ts);
  gmtime_r(&ts.tv_sec, &tm);
  strftime(stamp, sizeof(stamp), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S", &tm);
  int n = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%s.%03ldZ %s[%d] [%s] %s\n", stamp,
                   ts.tv_nsec / 1000000, log_who, (int)getpid(), prefix, msg);
  int fd = open(log_path, O_WRONLY | O_APPEND | O_CREAT | O_CLOEXEC, 0600);
  if (fd < 0)
    return;
  if (n > 0 && write(fd, line, (size_t)n) < 0)
    log_path[0] = '\0';
  close(fd);
}

void ua_log_open(const char *who, const char *invocation) {
  char old[PATH_MAX];
  struct stat st;
  if (geteuid() != 0)
    return;
  ua_ws_path("Logs", "usb-arsenal.log", log_path, sizeof(log_path));
  /* Past 1 MiB the file steps aside; one old file stays */
  if (stat(log_path, &st) == 0 && st.st_size > 1024 * 1024) {
    ua_ws_path("Logs", "usb-arsenal.log.1", old, sizeof(old));
    rename(log_path, old);
  }
  safe_strncpy(log_who, who, sizeof(log_who));
  /* The command line as a prompt line, in the file only: whoever typed it
   * has it on screen already */
  log_line("$", invocation);
}

void ua_log_internal(const char *prefix, const char *color, int is_err,
                     const char *fmt, ...) {
  char msg[4096];
  va_list ap;
  va_start(ap, fmt);
  vsnprintf(msg, sizeof(msg), fmt, ap);
  va_end(ap);

  log_line(prefix, msg);
  if (!is_err && !ua_verbose && msg[0] == '[' &&
      (strncmp(msg, "[DEBUG]", 7) == 0 || strncmp(msg, "[IPT]", 5) == 0 ||
       strncmp(msg, "[NET]", 5) == 0 || strncmp(msg, "[DHCP]", 6) == 0))
    return;

  /* Always coloured, as in Droidspaces: the app reads it through a pipe and
   * strips the codes itself */
  FILE *out = is_err ? stderr : stdout;
  fprintf(out, "[%s%s" C_RESET "] %s\n", color, prefix, msg);
  fflush(out);
}

/* Droidspaces' JSON encoder (src/status.c): flat objects of strings and ints
 * are all `check --json` needs */
void ua_json_str(const char *key, const char *val, int *first) {
  printf("%s\"%s\":\"", *first ? "" : ",", key);
  *first = 0;
  for (const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)val; val && *p; p++) {
    if (*p == '"' || *p == '\\')
      printf("\\%c", *p);
    else if (*p < 0x20)
      printf("\\u%04x", *p);
    else
      putchar(*p);
  }
  putchar('"');
}

void ua_json_int(const char *key, long long val, int *first) {
  printf("%s\"%s\":%lld", *first ? "" : ",", key, val);
  *first = 0;
}

void safe_strncpy(char *dst, const char *src, size_t size) {
  if (!dst || size == 0)
    return;
  snprintf(dst, size, "%s", src ? src : "");
}

int mkdir_p(const char *path, mode_t mode) {
  char tmp[PATH_MAX];
  int r = snprintf(tmp, sizeof(tmp), "%s", path);
  if (r < 0 || (size_t)r >= sizeof(tmp)) {
    errno = ENAMETOOLONG;
    return -1;
  }
  for (char *p = tmp + 1; *p; p++) {
    if (*p == '/') {
      *p = '\0';
      if (mkdir(tmp, mode) < 0 && errno != EEXIST)
        return -1;
      *p = '/';
    }
  }
  if (mkdir(tmp, mode) < 0 && errno != EEXIST)
    return -1;
  return 0;
}

ssize_t write_all(int fd, const void *buf, size_t count) {
  const char *p = buf;
  size_t remaining = count;
  while (remaining > 0) {
    ssize_t w = write(fd, p, remaining);
    if (w < 0) {
      if (errno == EINTR)
        continue;
      return -1;
    }
    p += w;
    remaining -= (size_t)w;
  }
  return (ssize_t)count;
}

/* No O_CREAT: every write here lands on a configfs or sysfs attribute, and a
 * typo in a path must fail with ENOENT, not create a stray file. State files
 * go through stdio instead. errno is kept for callers that care which
 * configfs check rejected the write. */
static int write_path(const char *path, const void *buf, size_t len) {
  int fd = open(path, O_WRONLY | O_TRUNC | O_CLOEXEC);
  if (fd < 0)
    return -1;
  ssize_t w = write_all(fd, buf, len);
  int saved = errno;
  close(fd);
  errno = saved;
  return w == (ssize_t)len ? 0 : -1;
}

int write_file(const char *path, const char *content) {
  return write_path(path, content, strlen(content));
}

/* <dir>/<attr>, for the binary attributes f_hid takes */
int write_attr_buf(const char *dir, const char *attr, const void *buf,
                   size_t len) {
  char p[PATH_MAX];
  int n = snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "%s/%s", dir, attr);
  if (n < 0 || (size_t)n >= sizeof(p)) {
    errno = ENAMETOOLONG;
    return -1;
  }
  return write_path(p, buf, len);
}

/* Logged with -v when the kernel refuses it; errno survives the log, since
 * callers tell EBUSY (a host's medium lock) from the rest */
int write_attr(const char *dir, const char *attr, const char *val) {
  if (write_attr_buf(dir, attr, val, strlen(val)) == 0)
    return 0;
  int saved = errno;
  ua_debug("write %s/%s <- %s: %s", dir, attr, val, strerror(saved));
  errno = saved;
  return -1;
}

int read_file(const char *path, char *buf, size_t size) {
  if (size == 0)
    return -1;
  int fd = open(path, O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC);
  if (fd < 0)
    return -1;
  ssize_t total = 0, r = 1;
  while ((size_t)total < size - 1 &&
         (r = read(fd, buf + total, size - 1 - (size_t)total)) > 0)
    total += r;
  close(fd);
  if (r < 0)
    return -1;
  buf[total] = '\0';
  while (total > 0 && (buf[total - 1] == '\n' || buf[total - 1] == '\r'))
    buf[--total] = '\0';
  return (int)total;
}

static int wait_exit(pid_t pid) {
  int status;
  while (waitpid(pid, &status, 0) < 0)
    if (errno != EINTR)
      return -1;
  return WIFEXITED(status) ? WEXITSTATUS(status) : -1;
}

static int internal_run(char *const argv[], int quiet) {
  pid_t pid = fork();
  if (pid < 0)
    return -1;
  if (pid == 0) {
    if (quiet) {
      int devnull = open("/dev/null", O_RDWR);
      if (devnull >= 0) {
        dup2(devnull, 1);
        dup2(devnull, 2);
        close(devnull);
      }
    }
    execvp(argv[0], argv);
    _exit(127);
  }
  return wait_exit(pid);
}

int run_command_quiet(char *const argv[]) { return internal_run(argv, 1); }

/* stdout of argv into out, trailing newlines stripped. musl's popen() runs
 * /bin/sh, which Android does not have, so fork and exec it ourselves. */
int run_capture(char *const argv[], char *out, size_t size) {
  int pfd[2];
  if (size == 0 || pipe(pfd) < 0)
    return -1;
  pid_t pid = fork();
  if (pid < 0) {
    close(pfd[0]);
    close(pfd[1]);
    return -1;
  }
  if (pid == 0) {
    close(pfd[0]);
    dup2(pfd[1], STDOUT_FILENO);
    close(pfd[1]);
    int devnull = open("/dev/null", O_WRONLY);
    if (devnull >= 0) {
      dup2(devnull, STDERR_FILENO);
      close(devnull);
    }
    execvp(argv[0], argv);
    _exit(127);
  }
  close(pfd[1]);
  size_t total = 0;
  ssize_t r;
  while (total < size - 1 &&
         (r = read(pfd[0], out + total, size - 1 - total)) != 0) {
    if (r < 0) {
      if (errno == EINTR)
        continue;
      break;
    }
    total += (size_t)r;
  }
  close(pfd[0]);
  out[total] = '\0';
  while (total > 0 && (out[total - 1] == '\n' || out[total - 1] == '\r'))
    out[--total] = '\0';
  return wait_exit(pid);
}

/* run_command_log: stderr and stdout of argv go to the [IPT] debug log, so an
 * iptables failure is visible with -v without cluttering normal runs. */
int run_command_log(char *const argv[]) {
  int pfd[2];
  if (pipe(pfd) < 0)
    return internal_run(argv, 0);
  pid_t pid = fork();
  if (pid < 0) {
    close(pfd[0]);
    close(pfd[1]);
    return -1;
  }
  if (pid == 0) {
    close(pfd[0]);
    dup2(pfd[1], STDOUT_FILENO);
    dup2(pfd[1], STDERR_FILENO);
    close(pfd[1]);
    execvp(argv[0], argv);
    _exit(127);
  }
  close(pfd[1]);
  char buf[512];
  FILE *f = fdopen(pfd[0], "r");
  if (f) {
    while (fgets(buf, sizeof(buf), f)) {
      buf[strcspn(buf, "\r\n")] = '\0';
      if (buf[0])
        ua_log("[IPT] %s", buf);
    }
    fclose(f);
  } else {
    close(pfd[0]);
  }
  return wait_exit(pid);
}

int ds_thread_create(pthread_t *tid, void *(*fn)(void *), void *arg) {
  sigset_t all, old;
  sigfillset(&all);
  pthread_sigmask(SIG_BLOCK, &all, &old);
  int ret = pthread_create(tid, NULL, fn, arg);
  pthread_sigmask(SIG_SETMASK, &old, NULL);
  return ret;
}

int is_android(void) {
  static int cached = -1;
  if (cached != -1)
    return cached;
  /* Recovery (TWRP) has /system mounted at times but no init USB HAL to hand
   * the controller back to, so treat it as plain Linux */
  if (access("/system/bin/recovery", F_OK) == 0)
    cached = 0;
  else
    cached = access("/system/build.prop", F_OK) == 0 ||
             access("/system/bin/app_process", F_OK) == 0;
  return cached;
}

/* argv wants char *, our callers hold const strings: copy, do not cast */
int ua_getprop(const char *name, char *out, size_t size) {
  char n[128];
  safe_strncpy(n, name, sizeof(n));
  char *argv[] = {"getprop", n, NULL};
  out[0] = '\0';
  return run_capture(argv, out, size) == 0 ? 0 : -1;
}

int ua_setprop(const char *name, const char *value) {
  char n[128], v[256];
  safe_strncpy(n, name, sizeof(n));
  safe_strncpy(v, value, sizeof(v));
  char *argv[] = {"setprop", n, v, NULL};
  return run_command_quiet(argv) == 0 ? 0 : -1;
}

static void sleep_ms(int ms) {
  struct timespec ts = {ms / 1000, (long)(ms % 1000) * 1000000L};
  while (nanosleep(&ts, &ts) < 0 && errno == EINTR)
    ;
}

/* Poll until get(key) reads want, or the timeout runs out. 0 on match. get is
 * read_file or ua_getprop. */
int ua_wait(int (*get)(const char *, char *, size_t), const char *key,
            const char *want, int timeout_ms) {
  char buf[256];
  for (int waited = 0;; waited += 100) {
    if (get(key, buf, sizeof(buf)) >= 0 && strcmp(buf, want) == 0)
      return 0;
    if (waited >= timeout_ms)
      return -1;
    sleep_ms(100);
  }
}

/* One workspace, laid out like Droidspaces' /data/local/Droidspaces: Logs,
 * Pids, Net, plus Gadget (handoff, lock, setup). A container gets the Linux
 * path, where Android's is best bind-mounted, so both share one handoff.
 * Persistent on both; a stale handoff is voided by its boot marker. */
const char *ua_workspace(void) {
  return is_android() ? UA_WORKSPACE_ANDROID : UA_WORKSPACE_LINUX;
}

/* Root writes the handoff here. If anyone else owned the workspace, or could
 * write to it, they could plant a symlink for root to follow; refuse instead.
 * Runs before anything changes hands. */
static void ensure_workspace(void) {
  static int done;
  struct stat st;
  const char *ws = ua_workspace();
  if (done)
    return;
  mkdir_p(ws, 0755);
  if (lstat(ws, &st) < 0 || !S_ISDIR(st.st_mode) || st.st_uid != 0 ||
      (st.st_mode & 022)) {
    ua_error("Unsafe workspace %s (not a directory owned by root, or "
             "writable by others)",
             ws);
    exit(UA_EXIT_FAIL);
  }
  done = 1;
}

/* <workspace>/<sub>/<leaf>, sub may be NULL. As root the directories are
 * made on the way; anyone else (a client in the usb-arsenal group) only gets
 * the path. */
void ua_ws_path(const char *sub, const char *leaf, char *out, size_t size) {
  if (geteuid() == 0) {
    ensure_workspace();
    if (sub) {
      snprintf(out, size, "%s/%s", ua_workspace(), sub);
      mkdir(out, 0755);
    }
  }
  if (sub)
    snprintf(out, size, "%s/%s/%s", ua_workspace(), sub, leaf);
  else
    snprintf(out, size, "%s/%s", ua_workspace(), leaf);
}

/* The pid in pidfile, if that process is still one of ours. Matched by
 * program name, not inode: replacing the binary while the tether process
 * runs (adb push, an update) leaves its exe as "... (deleted)", and a stop may
 * come from a different copy than the start. A pid reused by something else
 * after a reboot must never get our signal. */
pid_t ua_read_our_pid(const char *pidfile) {
  char p[PATH_MAX], buf[32], exe[PATH_MAX], self[PATH_MAX];
  if (read_file(pidfile, buf, sizeof(buf)) <= 0)
    return 0;
  pid_t pid = (pid_t)strtol(buf, NULL, 10);
  if (pid <= 0)
    return 0;
  snprintf(p, sizeof(p), "/proc/%d/exe", (int)pid);
  ssize_t a = readlink(p, exe, sizeof(exe) - 1);
  ssize_t b = readlink("/proc/self/exe", self, sizeof(self) - 1);
  if (a <= 0 || b <= 0)
    return 0;
  exe[a] = self[b] = '\0';
  char *del = strstr(exe, " (deleted)");
  if (del)
    *del = '\0';
  const char *x = strrchr(exe, '/'), *y = strrchr(self, '/');
  return strcmp(x ? x + 1 : exe, y ? y + 1 : self) == 0 ? pid : 0;
}

/* Something stable and unique to this machine: the phone's serial, else the
 * machine id. The default USB serial and the tether MACs come from it, so a
 * host keeps recognising the device and two of them never collide. */
void ua_device_seed(char *out, size_t size) {
  out[0] = '\0';
  if (is_android())
    ua_getprop("ro.serialno", out, size);
  if (!out[0])
    read_file("/etc/machine-id", out, size);
  if (!out[0])
    safe_strncpy(out, UA_NAME, size);
}

```

`tests/device.sh`:

```sh
#!/system/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#
# On-device test of USB Arsenal: every backend command the app sends, then the app itself,
# driven by the text its screens show. It needs the app and its backend installed, and the
# phone plugged into a computer. adbd stops while the gadget holds the port, so it runs as
# root in the background:
#
#   adb push tests/device.sh /data/local/tmp/
#   adb shell "su -c 'nohup sh /data/local/tmp/device.sh [CONTAINER [IFACE]] >/dev/null 2>&1 &'"
#   adb shell cat /data/local/tmp/uatest/log    # once it ends in DONE
#
# CONTAINER names a running Droidspaces container to test the tether gateway with (IFACE:
# the cable's name inside it, default usb0); without one the gateway steps are skipped.
# Screenshots land beside the log. The setup, the animation scale and the screen timeout
# are put back at the end, and the port is handed back.

UA=/data/local/USB-Arsenal/bin/usb-arsenal
GS=/data/local/USB-Arsenal/Gadget
APP=com.usbarsenal.app
D=/data/local/tmp/uatest
GW=${1:-}
GWIF=${2:-usb0}
rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D
# Blank images of our own, so nothing of the user's is ever served
IMG=$D
dd if=/dev/zero of=$IMG/cd.img bs=1048576 count=8 2>/dev/null
dd if=/dev/zero of=$IMG/disk.img bs=1048576 count=8 2>/dev/null
exec >$D/log 2>&1

pass=0; fail=0; failed=""
ok() { pass=$((pass + 1)); echo "  PASS $*"; }
no() { fail=$((fail + 1)); failed="$failed
  $*"; echo "  FAIL $*"; }
check() { # NAME COMMAND...: pass when the command succeeds
  n=$1; shift
  if "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "$n"; else no "$n"; fi
}
section() { echo; echo "== $*"; }

# The kernel complains before it panics: any new warning fails the step that caused it
KPAT='WARNING:|BUG:|Oops|Call trace|Unable to handle|panic'
kbase=$(dmesg | grep -cE "$KPAT")
kernel() {
  now=$(dmesg | grep -cE "$KPAT")
  if [ "$now" -gt "$kbase" ]; then
    no "dmesg after $1: $(dmesg | grep -E "$KPAT" | tail -3)"
    kbase=$now
  fi
}

st() { $UA status --json 2>/dev/null; }
has() { st | grep -q "$1"; }
wait_for() { # PATTERN SECONDS: until status --json has it
  i=0
  while [ $i -lt "$2" ]; do has "$1" && return 0; sleep 1; i=$((i + 1)); done
  return 1
}
setupval() { grep "^$1=" $GS/setup.conf | sed 's/ *#.*//; s/^[^=]*=//; s/ *$//'; }
# What runs; with nothing run since boot there is no file, and revert falls back to the
# default, which is 0 for the only key read here
runval() {
  [ -f $GS/running.conf ] || { echo 0; return; }
  grep "^$1=" $GS/running.conf | sed 's/ *#.*//; s/^[^=]*=//; s/ *$//'
}

# UI: uiautomator's tree, one node a line; a control is found by its text or content-desc
dump() {
  i=0
  while [ $i -lt 4 ]; do
    uiautomator dump $D/raw.xml >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
    sleep 1; i=$((i + 1))
  done
  sed 's/<node /\n<node /g' $D/raw.xml >$D/ui.txt
}
center() { # TEXT [N]: the Nth node with exactly that text or description
  grep -F -e "text=\"$1\"" -e "content-desc=\"$1\"" $D/ui.txt | sed -n "${2:-1}p" |
    sed 's/.*bounds="\[\([0-9]*\),\([0-9]*\)\]\[\([0-9]*\),\([0-9]*\)\]".*/\1 \2 \3 \4/' |
    awk 'NF==4{print int(($1+$3)/2), int(($2+$4)/2)}'
}
focused() { dumpsys window | grep mCurrentFocus | grep -q "$APP"; }
tap() { # TEXT [N]
  focused || { no "tap '$1': the app is not in front"; return 1; }
  dump
  xy=$(center "$1" "$2")
  [ -n "$xy" ] || { no "tap '$1': not on screen"; return 1; }
  input tap $xy
}
back() { focused && input keyevent KEYCODE_BACK; }
sees() { dump; grep -qiF "$1" $D/ui.txt; }
shot() { screencap -p $D/$1.png; }
screen() { # NAME OPEN-TEXT [N] EXPECT: opens a screen from Home, checks it, comes back
  tap "$2" "$3" && sleep 2
  if sees "$4"; then ok "$1 opens"; else no "$1 opens (no '$4')"; fi
  shot "$1"
  back; sleep 1.5
  if sees "SETTINGS"; then ok "$1 Back returns Home"; else no "$1 Back returns Home"; fi
}

cleanup() {
  section "cleanup"
  $UA stop
  if [ -f $D/setup.conf.bak ]; then cp $D/setup.conf.bak $GS/setup.conf; else rm -f $GS/setup.conf; fi
  settings put global animator_duration_scale "$anim"
  settings put system screen_off_timeout "$tmo"
  echo
  echo "RESULT: $pass passed, $fail failed$failed"
  echo DONE
}

section "preflight"
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo "needs root"; echo DONE; exit 1; }
$UA version
if has '"bound":1'; then echo "the gadget is bound; stop it first"; echo DONE; exit 1; fi
[ -f $GS/setup.conf ] && cp $GS/setup.conf $D/setup.conf.bak
anim=$(settings get global animator_duration_scale)
tmo=$(settings get system screen_off_timeout)
trap cleanup EXIT
# Still screens: uiautomator waits for an idle frame, and the app rests its loops without motion
settings put global animator_duration_scale 0
settings put system screen_off_timeout 600000
input keyevent KEYCODE_WAKEUP
gw=0
if [ -n "$GW" ]; then
  if /data/local/Droidspaces/bin/droidspaces show --json 2>/dev/null | grep -qF "\"name\":\"$GW\""; then gw=1; else no "container $GW is not running"; fi
fi

section "backend: reads"
check "check --json" sh -c "$UA check --json | grep -q '{'"
check "status --json" sh -c "$UA status --json | grep -q '\"pending\"'"
check "identity show --json" sh -c "$UA identity show --json | grep -q '{'"
check "setup show" $UA setup show

section "backend: setup"
$UA setup set hid_interval=4
check "setup set" test "$(setupval hid_interval)" = 4
$UA setup revert hid
check "setup revert" test "$(setupval hid_interval)" = "$(runval hid_interval)"

section "backend: storage"
$UA setup set storage_lun0=cdrom:$IMG/cd.img storage_lun1= hid_interval=0
check "storage start" $UA storage start
check "storage lun0 served" has '"lun":0'
check "bound" has '"bound":1'
kernel "storage start"
$UA setup set storage_lun1=disk:$IMG/disk.img
check "storage pending after setup set" has '"storage":1'
check "storage apply" $UA storage apply
check "storage lun1 served" has '"lun":1'
check "storage not pending" has '"storage":0'
check "storage eject --lun 1" $UA storage eject --lun 1
kernel "storage apply"

section "backend: hid"
check "hid start" $UA hid start
check "hid nodes" sh -c 'ls /dev/hidg*'
kb=$(st | grep -o '{[^}]*"keyboard"[^}]*}' | grep -o '"node":"[^"]*"' | sed 's/"node":"//; s/"//')
[ -n "$kb" ] && check "hid write (empty report)" sh -c "printf '\0\0\0\0\0\0\0\0' | $UA hid write $kb 8"
$UA setup set hid_interval=2
check "hid pending" has '"hid":1'
check "hid apply" $UA hid apply
check "hid running interval 2" test "$(runval hid_interval)" = 2
check "storage kept through hid apply" has '"lun":0'
kernel "hid"

section "backend: tether"
if [ $gw = 1 ]; then
  $UA setup set "tether_gateway=$GW" "tether_gateway_iface=$GWIF" tether_net=1
  check "tether start (gateway)" $UA tether start
  check "gateway up" has '"gateway":1'
  check "network side runs" has '"running":1'
  check "tether stop" $UA tether stop
  kernel "tether gateway"
  # A gateway wins over tether_net=0 (the bug this session left on the phone)
  $UA setup set tether_net=0
  $UA tether start
  check "gateway wins over tether_net=0" has '"gateway":1'
  $UA tether stop
fi
$UA setup set tether_gateway= tether_net=0
check "tether start (no network side)" $UA tether start
check "tether function up" has '"iface":"usb'
check "tether stop" $UA tether stop
kernel "tether"

section "backend: stop"
check "stop" $UA stop
check "handed back" wait_for '"bound":0' 10
kernel "stop"

section "app: screens"
am force-stop $APP
monkey -p $APP -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1 >/dev/null 2>&1
sleep 4
check "app in front" focused
if sees "SETTINGS"; then ok "Home"; else no "Home"; fi
shot home
screen storage Storage 1 MODE
screen tether Tether 1 CONFIGURE
screen hid HID 1 INTERVAL
screen log LOG 1 "COPY LOGS"
tap SETTINGS && sleep 2
if sees BACKEND; then ok "settings opens"; else no "settings opens"; fi
shot settings
tap PROFILE && sleep 2
if sees PROFILES; then ok "identity opens"; else no "identity opens"; fi
shot identity
back; sleep 1.5; back; sleep 1.5
if sees "SETTINGS"; then ok "Identity and Settings Back to Home"; else no "Identity and Settings Back to Home"; fi

section "app: HID switch, Not applied sheet"
$UA setup set hid_interval=1
sleep 3
tap HID 2
if wait_for '"function":"keyboard"' 20; then ok "HID switch starts hid"; else no "HID switch starts hid"; fi
sleep 3
kernel "app hid start"
# The bug: Back a beat after an edit, once it was sent and before a status read, left unasked
tap HID 1 && sleep 2
tap "Longer interval"; sleep 1
back; sleep 1
if sees "not applied"; then ok "Back 1s after an edit asks"; else no "Back 1s after an edit asks"; fi
shot hid-sheet-fast
tap DISCARD; sleep 4
check "Discard leaves nothing pending" has '"hid":0'
check "Discard puts the setup back" test "$(setupval hid_interval)" = "$(runval hid_interval)"
if sees "SETTINGS"; then ok "Discard leaves for Home"; else no "Discard leaves for Home"; fi
# Slow Back, then Apply
tap HID 1 && sleep 2
tap "Longer interval"; sleep 4
back; sleep 1
if sees "not applied"; then ok "Back 4s after an edit asks"; else no "Back 4s after an edit asks"; fi
tap APPLY
if wait_for '"hid":0' 20; then ok "Apply leaves nothing pending"; else no "Apply leaves nothing pending"; fi
check "Apply runs the new interval" test "$(runval hid_interval)" = 2
kernel "app hid apply"
sleep 3
tap HID 1 && sleep 2
back; sleep 1
if sees "not applied"; then no "Back with no edit asks"; else ok "Back with no edit leaves"; fi

section "app: storage"
tap Storage 2
if wait_for '"lun":0' 20; then ok "Storage switch starts storage"; else no "Storage switch starts storage"; fi
sleep 3
tap Storage 1 && sleep 2
tap DVD; sleep 1
back; sleep 1
if sees "not applied"; then ok "Storage: Back after a mode change asks"; else no "Storage: Back after a mode change asks"; fi
shot storage-sheet
tap DISCARD; sleep 4
check "Storage: nothing pending" has '"storage":0'
kernel "app storage"

if [ $gw = 1 ]; then
  section "app: tether gateway"
  $UA setup set "tether_gateway=$GW" "tether_gateway_iface=$GWIF" tether_net=1
  sleep 3
  tap Tether 2
  if wait_for '"gateway":1' 25; then ok "Tether switch starts the gateway"; else no "Tether switch starts the gateway"; fi
  sleep 3
  tap Tether 1 && sleep 2
  if sees "virtual cable"; then ok "Tether chain shows the gateway"; else no "Tether chain shows the gateway"; fi
  shot tether-gateway
  tap RNDIS; sleep 1
  back; sleep 1
  if sees "not applied"; then ok "Tether: Back after an edit asks"; else no "Tether: Back after an edit asks"; fi
  tap DISCARD; sleep 4
  check "Tether: nothing pending" has '"tether":0'
  kernel "app tether"
fi

section "app: log, stop all"
tap LOG && sleep 2
if sees "# usb-arsenal"; then ok "Log shows the commands"; else no "Log shows the commands"; fi
shot log-after
back; sleep 1.5
tap "STOP ALL"
if wait_for '"bound":0' 20; then ok "Stop all hands back"; else no "Stop all hands back"; fi
sleep 3
if sees "PORT WITH ANDROID"; then ok "Home says the port is Android's"; else no "Home says the port is Android's"; fi
shot home-after
kernel "stop all"
```

`tests/dummy_hcd.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#
# End-to-end check of the gadget core on a Linux PC, no phone needed.
# dummy_hcd gives this machine a virtual device controller whose host side is
# this same machine, so every gadget we bind shows up here as a USB device.
#
#   sudo tests/dummy_hcd.sh [path/to/usb-arsenal]
#
# Leaves nothing behind on success: the last step is `stop`, and the script
# checks that it really removed the gadget.

set -eu
B=${1:-output/usb-arsenal}
UDC=dummy_udc.0
G=/sys/kernel/config/usb_gadget/usb_arsenal
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
pass=0

ok() { pass=$((pass + 1)); echo "ok $pass - $1"; }
die() { echo "FAIL: $1"; "$B" stop >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; exit 1; }
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || die "run as root"
# A clean slate: a run that failed halfway can leave the gadget bound, the
# dummy host's port stuck, and setup, running or identity values that would
# change this run. modprobe keeps a loaded module, so reload it
[ -e /sys/class/udc/$UDC ] && { "$B" --udc $UDC stop >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }
modprobe -r dummy_hcd 2>/dev/null || true
modprobe dummy_hcd
modprobe libcomposite
[ -e /sys/class/udc/$UDC ] || die "dummy_hcd gave no $UDC"
# A dummy controller is never picked by itself, so it is always named
A="--udc $UDC"
"$B" $A setup reset >/dev/null || die "setup reset"
"$B" $A identity unset >/dev/null || die "identity unset"
rm -f /var/lib/USB-Arsenal/Gadget/running.conf
# dummy_udc sets its state file to configured but never resets it on a
# disconnect, so it cannot say whether the host still sees us: ask the host.
# Its side of dummy_hcd is the root hub whose product names it
HUB=$(grep -l "Dummy host" /sys/bus/usb/devices/usb*/product | head -n 1)
DEV=/sys/bus/usb/devices/$(basename "$(dirname "$HUB")" | sed 's/^usb//')-1
configured() {
  for i in $(seq 50); do
    [ "$(cat "$DEV/bConfigurationValue" 2>/dev/null)" = 1 ] && return 0
    sleep 0.1
  done
  echo "# the host does not see the gadget configured; the kernel says:"
  dmesg | tail -n 30 | sed 's/^/#   /'
  return 1
}

"$B" $A check >/dev/null || die "check reports missing MUST HAVE features"
ok "check passes"

# A 2 MB "disk": an MBR signature is all auto mode looks at
truncate -s 2M "$TMP/disk.img"
printf '\125\252' | dd of="$TMP/disk.img" bs=1 seek=510 conv=notrunc 2>/dev/null
"$B" $A storage start "$TMP/disk.img" || die "storage start"
configured || die "host did not configure the gadget"
grep -q 1 $G/functions/mass_storage.ua/lun.0/ro || die "auto mode should pick a read-only disk"
grep -q 0 $G/functions/mass_storage.ua/lun.0/cdrom || die "MBR image must not be a CD-ROM"
ok "storage start: bound, configured, disk mode"

# No MBR: auto mode must fall back to CD-ROM. A mode change rebinds, by design.
truncate -s 2M "$TMP/plain.iso"
"$B" $A storage start "$TMP/plain.iso" || die "storage hot-swap"
grep -q 1 $G/functions/mass_storage.ua/lun.0/cdrom || die "plain image should be a CD-ROM"
grep -q "$TMP/plain.iso" $G/functions/mass_storage.ua/lun.0/file || die "swap did not load the new image"
configured || die "the host did not configure the gadget after the mode change"
ok "storage switch to CD-ROM mode"

# Same mode: a medium change in place (or a rebind if the host locked it)
cp "$TMP/plain.iso" "$TMP/plain2.iso"
"$B" $A storage start "$TMP/plain2.iso" || die "same-mode swap"
grep -q "$TMP/plain2.iso" $G/functions/mass_storage.ua/lun.0/file || die "same-mode swap did not load"
configured || die "gadget not configured after swap"
ok "storage same-mode swap"

"$B" $A hid start || die "hid start"
[ -L $G/configs/c.1/hid.ua_kbd ] && [ -L $G/configs/c.1/hid.ua_mouse ] || die "hid functions not linked"
grep -q "$TMP/plain2.iso" $G/functions/mass_storage.ua/lun.0/file || die "storage lost its image across the rebind"
configured || die "the host did not configure the gadget with HID"
ok "hid start alongside storage"

# --perm given once lasts while HID runs: a bare start must not reset it
KBD=$("$B" $A status --json | sed -n 's/.*"function":"keyboard","node":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
[ -c "$KBD" ] || die "status --json names no keyboard node"
"$B" $A hid start --perm 0600 >/dev/null || die "hid start --perm"
"$B" $A hid start >/dev/null || die "bare hid start on a running HID"
[ "$(stat -c %a "$KBD")" = 600 ] || die "a bare hid start reset --perm"
"$B" $A status --json | grep -q '"speed":"[a-z-]*speed"' || die "status --json has no speed while bound"
# The non-blocking writer: an all-zero report is no key at all, so the host
# (this PC) sees nothing; it must exit 0 at the end of stdin. f_hid answers
# ESHUTDOWN while the host has not configured the interface
configured || die "the host lost the gadget before hid write"
printf '\0\0\0\0\0\0\0\0' | "$B" $A hid write "$KBD" 8 || die "hid write"
"$B" $A hid write "$TMP/disk.img" 8 2>/dev/null && die "hid write must refuse a regular file"
ok "hid: --perm kept, speed in status, hid write"

"$B" $A tether start --no-net || die "tether start --no-net"
[ -L $G/configs/c.1/ncm.ua ] || die "ncm not linked"
ok "tether --no-net adds NCM"

# The setup: a start saves its arguments, `setup set` edits them, `apply`
# brings the kernel to them LUN by LUN, and status says when they differ
"$B" $A setup show | grep -q "storage_lun0 *auto:$TMP/plain2.iso" || die "start did not save its image as the setup"
"$B" $A status --json | grep -q '"pending":{"storage":0,"tether":0,"hid":0}' || die "nothing should be pending after a start"
truncate -s 2M "$TMP/second.img"
"$B" $A setup set storage_lun1=rw:$TMP/second.img || die "setup set"
"$B" $A setup set storage_lun1=bogus:$TMP/second.img 2>/dev/null && die "setup set must refuse a bad mode"
"$B" $A status --json | grep -q '"pending":{"storage":1,' || die "a changed setup should read as pending"
"$B" $A storage apply || die "storage apply"
grep -q "$TMP/second.img" $G/functions/mass_storage.ua/lun.1/file || die "apply did not add LUN 1"
grep -q "$TMP/plain2.iso" $G/functions/mass_storage.ua/lun.0/file || die "apply touched LUN 0"
"$B" $A storage apply | grep -q "already runs" || die "a second apply should change nothing"
"$B" $A setup set storage_lun1= || die "setup set (clear)"
"$B" $A storage apply || die "storage apply (eject)"
[ -z "$(cat $G/functions/mass_storage.ua/lun.1/file)" ] || die "apply did not eject LUN 1"
"$B" $A setup set hid_interval=3 || die "setup set hid_interval"
"$B" $A status --json | grep -q '"hid":1}' || die "a changed interval should read as pending"
"$B" $A hid apply || die "hid apply"
configured || die "gadget not configured after hid apply"
"$B" $A status --json | grep -q '"hid":0}' || die "hid apply should clear pending"
"$B" $A setup set hid_interval=5 && "$B" $A setup revert hid || die "setup revert"
"$B" $A setup show | grep -q "^hid_interval *3 " || die "revert did not take the running value"
ok "setup: saved by start, applied LUN by LUN, pending in status"

"$B" $A status | grep -q "LUN 0" || die "status does not show storage"
ok "status"

"$B" $A hid stop || die "hid stop"
[ ! -e $G/functions/hid.ua_kbd ] || die "hid stop left the function behind"
[ ! -e /var/lib/USB-Arsenal/Gadget/hid.perm ] || die "hid stop kept the --perm of the HID it removed"
configured || die "gadget did not come back after hid stop"
ok "hid stop rebinds the rest"

"$B" $A stop || die "stop"
[ ! -e $G ] || die "stop left $G behind"
[ -z "$(cat /sys/class/udc/$UDC/function 2>/dev/null)" ] || die "UDC still bound after stop"
"$B" $A stop >/dev/null || die "a second stop must be a no-op"
"$B" $A status --json | grep -q '"speed":""' || die "speed should be empty while not bound"
[ ! -e $G ] || die "status created $G"
ok "stop tears down, and is idempotent; status creates nothing"

# A bare start runs the setup the earlier starts saved; stop forgets what ran
"$B" $A setup show | grep -q "^storage_lun0 *auto:$TMP/plain2.iso *-" || die "stop should clear what runs, not the setup"
"$B" $A storage start || die "bare start from the setup"
grep -q "$TMP/plain2.iso" $G/functions/mass_storage.ua/lun.0/file || die "bare start did not load the setup"
"$B" $A stop || die "stop after the bare start"
"$B" $A setup reset || die "setup reset"
ok "a bare start runs the setup"

# Profiles read through the C loader, and a profile whose file went is named
printf ' id_product = 0104 \nbogus=1\n' > "$TMP/p.conf"
"$B" $A identity show --json "$TMP/p.conf" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '"errors":1,"keys":{"id_vendor":"0x1d6b","id_product":"0x0044"' || die "identity show FILE --json"
"$B" $A identity set "$TMP/p.conf" >/dev/null 2>&1 && die "identity set must refuse a file with errors"
printf 'product=Gone\n' > "$TMP/gone.conf"
"$B" $A identity set "$TMP/gone.conf" >/dev/null || die "identity set"
rm "$TMP/gone.conf"
"$B" $A identity show 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^Profile: $TMP/gone.conf (missing)" || die "identity show does not name the missing profile"
"$B" $A identity show --json 2>/dev/null | grep -q "\"missing\":\"$TMP/gone.conf\"" || die "identity show --json has no missing"
"$B" $A identity unset >/dev/null || die "identity unset"
ok "identity show: FILEs through the loader, a missing profile named"

echo "all $pass checks passed"

```
